short_description.id: Al Basty adalah roh perempuan jahat dalam cerita rakyat Turkik dan Kaukasus yang muncul dalam mimpi dan menindih dada orang yang tidur.
short_description.en: Al Basty is an evil female spirit of Turkic folklore and the Caucasus who appears in dreams and presses on sleepers' chests.

long_description.id: Al Basty atau Al Kardai adalah roh perempuan kuno, personifikasi rasa bersalah, dalam cerita rakyat Pegunungan Kaukasus dan bangsa-bangsa Turkik. Namanya berarti "tekanan merah": al berarti merah dan bastı berarti menekan. Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai perempuan telanjang buruk rupa berambut kuning panjang yang muncul dalam mimpi dan mencekik dengan menekan dada.
long_description.en: Al Basty, also called Al Kardai, is an old female spirit who personifies guilt and is known across the Caucasus and among the Turkic peoples. Her name means "red pressing": al is red and bastı is pressing. She is usually pictured as an ugly naked woman with long yellow hair who appears in dreams and smothers people by pressing on the chest.

long_description.id: Satu versi mitosnya ditarik hingga zaman Sumeria sebagai salah satu nama Lilith. Dalam cerita rakyat Turkik ia sering dikacaukan dengan mare dan sukubus, tetapi berbeda dari keduanya karena ia bukan roh seksual.
long_description.en: One variant of her myth is traced to Sumerian times as a name of Lilith. In Turkic folklore she is often confused with the mare and the succubus, but unlike them she is not a sexual spirit.

short_description.id: Naga Slavia adalah sebutan untuk naga mana pun dalam mitologi Slavia, seperti zmei dari Rusia atau żmij dari Polandia, yang sering digambarkan sebagai ular bersayap.
short_description.en: Slavic dragon is the name for any dragon in Slavic mythology, such as the Russian zmei or the Polish żmij, often pictured as a winged serpent.

long_description.id: Naga Slavia mencakup semua naga dalam mitologi Slavia, termasuk żmij dari Polandia, zmei dari Rusia, dan padanannya di budaya Slavia lain. Istilah-istilah itu berasal dari kata Proto-Slavia *zmьjь, dan kebanyakan merupakan bentuk maskulin dari kata Slavia untuk "ular". Wujudnya memadukan naga klasik dan ular, sebagai ular bersayap, dan kadang digambarkan berkaki dua atau berkepala lebih dari satu.
long_description.en: The Slavic dragon covers every dragon of Slavic mythology, including the Polish żmij, the Russian zmei and their counterparts in other Slavic cultures. These terms descend from Proto-Slavic *zmьjь, and most are masculine forms of the Slavic word for "snake". In shape it blends the classical dragon with a snake, as a winged serpent, and is sometimes shown with two legs or several heads.

long_description.id: Zmei bisa berwujud binatang atau mirip manusia: berwujud naga di udara dan manusia di darat, kadang merayu perempuan, tetapi dalam sastra Rusia sering menjadi musuh utama. Motif umum tentang naga Slavia antara lain perannya sebagai penguasa cuaca atau sumber air, asal-usulnya sebagai ular, dan kisah cinta naga jantan maupun betina dengan manusia. Dalam kepercayaan Rusia, ular, kadal, ayam jantan, atau ikan mas yang mencapai umur tertentu dapat berubah menjadi zmei terbang.
long_description.en: A zmei may be beast-like or human-like, taking dragon form in the air and human form on the ground; it sometimes woos women but in Russian literature often plays the chief villain. Common motifs include its role as master of weather or water sources, its beginning as a snake, and love affairs between humans and male or female dragons. In Russian lore a snake, lizard, rooster or carp that reaches a certain age may turn into a flying zmei.

long_description.id: Di Balkan, zmei pada umumnya dianggap baik, sebagai naga roh penjaga yang melawan naga jahat seperti lamia. Di Bulgaria ia kadang digambarkan bersisik dengan empat kaki dan sayap kelelawar, kadang setengah manusia setengah ular dengan ekor seperti ikan. Sebaliknya, di Slovenia naga biasanya dianggap jahat, walaupun naga Ljubljana justru melindungi kota itu dan tampil di lambang kotanya.
long_description.en: In the Balkans the zmei is generally seen as benevolent, a guardian-spirit dragon set against evil dragons such as the lamia. In Bulgaria it is sometimes described as scaly, four-legged and bat-winged, sometimes as half man, half snake with a fish-like tail. In Slovenia, by contrast, dragons are usually held to be evil, though the Ljubljana dragon protects that city and appears on its coat of arms.

long_description.id: Bentuk-bentuk khusus naga Slavia antara lain Zmey Gorynych dari legenda Rusia dan Ukraina, yang berkepala tiga sampai dua belas (satu sumber menyebutnya berkepala tiga, hijau, dan dapat menyemburkan api), serta smok dari Polandia, Ukraina, dan Belarus, misalnya Naga Wawel dari Kraków. Ada pula gagasan, yang diduga diilhami angin puting beliung, tentang naga yang mencelupkan ekornya ke sungai atau danau dan menyedot airnya hingga menimbulkan banjir.
long_description.en: Particular forms include Zmey Gorynych of Russian and Ukrainian legend, with three to twelve heads (one source makes him three-headed, green and fire-breathing), and the Polish, Ukrainian or Belarusian smok, such as the Wawel Dragon of Kraków. There is also a notion, thought to be inspired by tornadoes, of a dragon that dips its tail into a river or lake and sucks up the water to cause floods.

literal_meaning.en: (masculine form of the word for) snake

short_description.id: Naga Wawel (Smok Wawelski) adalah naga terkenal dalam legenda Polandia yang tinggal di gua di bawah Bukit Wawel dan meneror kota Kraków sampai dibunuh dengan umpan berisi belerang.
short_description.en: The Wawel Dragon (Smok Wawelski) is a famous dragon of Polish legend who lived in a cave beneath Wawel Hill and plagued Kraków until killed with a sulfur-filled bait.

long_description.id: Naga Wawel adalah naga terkenal dalam legenda Polandia. Kisah tertua tentangnya berasal dari abad ke-13, dalam karya yang dikaitkan dengan Wincenty Kadłubek. Menurut catatan itu, naga pemakan manusia tersebut mengganggu kota Kraków yang didirikan Raja Krak, dan ditenangkan dengan jatah ternak setiap minggu.
long_description.en: The Wawel Dragon is a famous dragon of Polish legend. The oldest known telling dates from the 13th century, in a work attributed to Wincenty Kadłubek. In that account the man-eating beast troubled the city of Kraków founded by King Krak and was kept calm with a weekly share of cattle.

long_description.id: Dalam versi tertua, putra-putra raja mengalahkannya dengan memberinya kulit sapi berisi belerang yang membara sehingga naga mati terbakar; lalu putra yang lebih muda membunuh kakaknya agar mendapat pujian sendirian, dan akhirnya diusir. Kronik abad ke-15 karya Jan Długosz menukar peran kedua pangeran dan menyebut Raja Krak sendiri sebagai perancang siasat; naga itu menyemburkan api sesaat sebelum mati.
long_description.en: In the oldest version the king's sons defeat it by feeding it a cattle skin packed with smouldering sulfur, so the dragon dies in flames; the younger son then kills his brother to take all the credit and is later banished. Jan Długosz's 15th-century chronicle swaps the princes' roles and credits King Krak himself with the plan; the dragon breathes fire just before it dies.

long_description.id: Kronika Polska karya Marcin Bielski (1597) memberi jasa itu kepada Skub atau Skuba, seorang tukang sepatu. Dalam versi ini naga tidak dapat menelan umpan belerang dan terus minum air sampai mati, lalu si tukang sepatu diberi hadiah besar. Versi populer lain menyebut seorang magang tukang sepatu bernama Dratewka yang mengisi bangkai domba dengan belerang; naga minum di Sungai Vistula sampai perutnya pecah, dan Dratewka menikahi putri raja.
long_description.en: Marcin Bielski's Kronika Polska (1597) gives the credit to Skub or Skuba, a cobbler. In this version the dragon cannot swallow the sulfur bait and drinks water until it dies, and the shoemaker is richly rewarded. Another popular version names a young shoemaker's apprentice, Dratewka, who stuffs a dead lamb with sulfur; the dragon drinks from the Vistula until its belly bursts, and Dratewka marries the king's daughter.

long_description.id: Naga itu dikatakan tinggal di Smocza Jama, gua naga di bawah Bukit Wawel di tepi Sungai Vistula. Dalam kebanyakan versi populer, ia lebih suka memangsa gadis muda dan hanya bisa ditenangkan dengan persembahan seorang gadis setiap bulan. Pada tahun 1970 sebuah patung logam naga ini karya Bronisław Chromy dipasang di depan gua; patung itu menyemburkan api dari lubang hidungnya.
long_description.en: The dragon is said to have lived in Smocza Jama, the dragon's cave beneath Wawel Hill on the banks of the Vistula. In most popular versions it preferred to eat young girls and could only be soothed by a monthly offering of a girl. In 1970 a metal sculpture of the dragon by Bronisław Chromy was set up before the cave; it breathes fire from its nostrils.

short_description.id: Susulu adalah makhluk air dalam mitologi Turkik yang berwujud setengah perempuan setengah ikan. Kehadirannya dianggap pertanda sial yang dapat meramalkan dan memicu bencana.
short_description.en: The Susulu is a water being of Turkic mythology with the form of half woman and half fish. Its appearance is held to be an unlucky omen that can both foretell and cause disaster.

long_description.id: Susulu, juga disebut Susuna, Susona, Suna, atau Sona, adalah makhluk air dalam mitologi Turkik. Tubuh bagian atasnya berwujud perempuan, sedangkan bagian bawahnya berupa ekor ikan, dan ia disebut sebagai putri Raja Laut. Kamus mitos Turkik menggolongkannya sebagai makhluk setengah perempuan setengah ikan dan mencatat nama padanan seperti Sisili dan Suvkiz.
long_description.en: The Susulu, also called Susuna, Susona, Suna or Sona, is a water being of Turkic mythology. Its upper body is that of a woman while its lower part is a fish tail, and it is said to be the daughter of the Sea King. The dictionary of Turkic myth classes it as half woman and half fish and records related names such as Sisili and Suvkiz.

long_description.id: Susulu digambarkan sebagai makhluk betina yang sangat cantik dengan rambut panjang tergerai. Ia dikatakan tinggal di danau dan sungai, dan dapat berenang ke hulu hingga danau air tawar; kamus menambahkan bahwa mereka hidup di laut dan perairan, di sebuah istana di bawah batu besar di dasar air.
long_description.en: The Susulu is pictured as a very beautiful female being with long, flowing hair. It is said to dwell in lakes and rivers and to be able to swim upstream to freshwater lakes; the dictionary adds that these beings live in the sea and other waters, in a palace beneath a great rock deep under the water.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, kemunculan Susulu dianggap membawa sial: ia meramalkan bencana sekaligus menimbulkannya. Setelah gelap mereka terlihat menari di bawah cahaya bulan, memanggil nama para pemuda, lalu memikat mereka ke air dan menenggelamkannya; menurut kamus, mereka memperdaya laki-laki dan membawanya ke negeri bawah air. Kamus juga menasihati agar orang tidak menatap matanya.
long_description.en: In folklore, the Susulu's appearance is unlucky: it foretells disaster and also brings it about. After dark these beings are seen dancing in the moonlight, calling young men by name, then drawing them to the water and drowning them; according to the dictionary, they trick men and carry them off to an underwater land. The dictionary also warns against looking into its eyes.

long_description.id: Sumber-sumber tidak seragam tentang asal-usulnya. Artikel pertama menyebut Susulu putri Raja Laut, tetapi juga mengatakan bahwa mereka biasanya arwah perempuan muda yang mati tenggelam atau secara tidak wajar. Kamus menyebut bahwa bila keluar dari air, Susulu mati atau ekornya berubah menjadi kaki sehingga ia menjadi manusia; namanya dijelaskan sebagai yang bergantung pada air dan hidup di air.
long_description.en: The sources are not uniform about its origin. The first article calls the Susulu the daughter of the Sea King, yet also says these beings are usually the ghosts of young women who drowned or died untimely deaths. The dictionary says that if a Susulu leaves the water it either dies or its tail turns into legs and it becomes human; its name is explained as one dependent on water and living in it.

short_description.id: Elang berkepala tiga adalah elang mitologis dan heraldik yang muncul dalam kitab apokrif Ezra, dongeng Chechnya, cerita rakyat Yakut, dan heraldik.
short_description.en: The three-headed eagle is a mythological and heraldic eagle found in the apocryphal Ezra, a Chechen fairy tale, Yakut folklore and heraldry.

long_description.id: Elang berkepala tiga adalah elang mitologis atau heraldik, semacam versi tambahan dari elang berkepala dua. Dalam kitab apokrif Ezra Latin, imam besar Ezra memimpikan elang dengan dua belas sayap dan tiga kepala yang naik dari laut. Dalam dongeng Chechnya ia lawan mengerikan yang dibunuh sang pahlawan, dan dalam cerita rakyat Yakut serta Dolgan dikenal elang berkepala dua atau tiga bernama Öksökö.
long_description.en: The three-headed eagle is a mythological or heraldic eagle, an augmented double-headed eagle. In the apocryphal Latin Ezra, the high priest Ezra dreams of an eagle with twelve wings and three heads rising from the sea. In a Chechen fairy tale it is a monstrous foe slain by the hero, and Yakut and Dolgan folklore know a two- or three-headed eagle named Öksökö.

long_description.en: In heraldry it is a rare charge: it serves as the arms of Reinmar von Zweter in the Codex Manesse (c. 1300), and one adorned the sceptre of Tsar Michael I of Russia.

short_description.id: Korbolko adalah burung api dalam mitologi Turk yang dipercaya membawa api ke bumi dan mengajari manusia menyalakannya; menurut sebagian legenda ia diutus oleh Tanrı Ülgen.
short_description.en: Korbolko is a fire bird of Turkic mythology believed to have brought fire to the earth and taught people to kindle it; in some legends it is sent by Tanrı Ülgen.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turk, Korbolko adalah burung yang tubuhnya dari api. Ia dipercaya menghadirkan api di bumi dan mengajarkan manusia cara membuatnya. Menurut kamus kedua, Tanrı Ülgen mengutus burung ini membawa api, atau dalam sebagian legenda membawa batu api untuk menyalakannya.
long_description.en: In Turkic mythology, Korbolko is a bird whose body is fire. It is credited with giving the earth fire and showing humans how to make it. According to the second source, Tanrı Ülgen sent the bird with fire, or in some legends with the flints needed to light it.

long_description.id: Ada juga cerita bahwa Tanrı Ülgen sendiri menyamar sebagai burung itu dan membawa batu-batu tersebut. Satu batu berwarna putih dan yang lain hitam, dan bila keduanya digosokkan akan keluar percikan api.
long_description.en: Another account says that Tanrı Ülgen himself took on the bird's form and carried the stones. One stone is white and the other black, and rubbing them together throws off sparks.

long_description.id: Korbolko dilukiskan sebagai burung besar berbulu indah yang bersinar merah dan kuning, menyerupai api unggun yang nyalanya mulai tenang. Dalam dongeng, ia biasanya menjadi tujuan pencarian yang berat, yang kerap dimulai ketika seseorang menemukan sehelai bulu ekornya.
long_description.en: Korbolko is portrayed as a big bird with splendid feathers shining red and yellow, much like a campfire whose blaze has started to settle. In folk tales it is usually the goal of a hard search, which often starts when someone comes upon one of its tail feathers.

long_description.id: Dalam satu versi, burung itu mencuri apel ajaib milik penguasa dan dikejar para abdinya. Seorang Khan menyuruh tiga putranya menangkap burung yang terus turun memakan apelnya; mereka gagal, tetapi mendapat sehelai bulu yang bercahaya dan mampu menerangi ruangan gelap.
long_description.en: In one version the bird steals a ruler's magic apples and is chased by his servants. A Khan sends his three sons to catch the bird that keeps swooping down on his apples; they fail, but obtain one feather that shines and can light up a dark room.

short_description.id: Sockburn Worm adalah wyvern ganas dalam cerita rakyat Northumbria yang menghancurkan desa Sockburn di Durham sampai dibunuh oleh John Conyers.
short_description.en: The Sockburn Worm is a ferocious wyvern of Northumbrian folklore that laid waste to the village of Sockburn in Durham until John Conyers slew it.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Northumbria, Sockburn Worm adalah wyvern ganas yang memporak-porandakan desa Sockburn di Durham, meneror penduduk dan melahap ternak. Kata worm di sini berarti wyvern, yaitu naga bersayap berkaki dua dengan ujung ekor berbentuk mata panah. Pidato upacara menyebutnya 'cacing, naga, atau ular terbang berapi' yang membinasakan laki-laki, perempuan, dan anak-anak, sedangkan buku heraldik awal abad ke-17 menyebutnya wyvern berbisa yang menelan banyak orang.
long_description.en: In Northumbrian folklore the Sockburn Worm was a savage wyvern that ravaged the village of Sockburn in Durham, terrorising locals and devouring livestock. Worm here means a wyvern, a winged two-legged dragon with an arrow-tipped tail. The ceremonial speech calls it a 'worm, dragon or fiery flying serpent' that destroyed man, woman and child, while an early seventeenth-century heraldry book calls it a venomous wyvern that devoured many people.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, pada tahun 1063 Sir John Conyers, kepala keluarganya, membunuh naga itu. Satu versi ringkas menyebut naga itu telah menghantui wilayah tersebut selama tujuh tahun; setelah berdoa di kapel terdekat, Sir John membunuh ular berbau busuk itu dengan falchion-nya, membiarkan tubuhnya di Sungai Tees, dan mengubur sisanya di bawah Grey Stone yang masih terlihat sampai sekarang.
long_description.en: According to legend, in 1063 Sir John Conyers, head of his family, killed the dragon. One summarised version says the dragon had haunted the region for seven years; Sir John, having first prayed in a chapel close by, killed the evil-smelling serpent with his falchion, let its body lie in the River Tees, and buried the remains beneath the Grey Stone, which can still be seen.

long_description.id: Legenda ini melekat pada upacara Conyers Falchion: setiap Uskup Durham yang baru, saat pertama kali menyeberangi Sungai Tees di Croft-on-Tees, diberi pedang abad pertengahan itu disertai pidato tradisional. Kebiasaan itu terhenti pada 1771, pedangnya diserahkan ke Katedral Durham pada 1947, dan upacaranya dihidupkan kembali pada 1984 dengan Wali Kota Darlington sebagai penyerah pedang.
long_description.en: The legend is bound to the ceremony of the Conyers Falchion: each newly appointed Bishop of Durham, on first crossing the River Tees at Croft-on-Tees, was presented with the medieval sword along with a traditional speech. The custom lapsed in 1771, the sword was given to Durham Cathedral in 1947, and the ceremony was revived in 1984 with the Mayor of Darlington presenting the sword.

long_description.id: Ada dugaan bahwa kisah ini terilhami kapal panjang Viking yang haluannya diukir kepala worm (Ormr), tetapi ada yang mencatat bahwa dugaan itu mengabaikan banyaknya naga dalam cerita rakyat Jermanik. Kisah Sockburn Worm juga hampir pasti mengilhami puisi Jabberwocky karya Lewis Carroll, yang tinggal di Croft-on-Tees.
long_description.en: It has been suggested that the tale was inspired by Viking longships with worm heads (Ormr) carved on their bows, though others note this ignores how common dragons are in Germanic folklore. The Sockburn Worm story was also almost certainly the inspiration for Lewis Carroll's poem Jabberwocky, Carroll having lived in Croft-on-Tees.

cultural_context.id: Nama baik dan garis keturunan keluarga Conyers bertumpu pada naga yang dibunuh leluhur mereka. Di masa pergolakan agama dan sosial, kisah Sockburn Worm paling menonjol di antara cerita naga setempat, dan kisah ini menjadi bagian upacara kepemilikan tanah di Palatinate Durham.
cultural_context.en: The Conyers family's standing and lineage rested on the dragon slain by their forebear. In a time of religious and social upheaval the Sockburn Worm story stood above the other local dragon tales, and it was woven into the ceremonial tenure ritual of the Palatinate of Durham.

claims.quote: In the folklore of Northumbria, the Sockburn Worm was a ferocious wyvern that laid waste to the village of Sockburn in Durham. It was said that the beast was finally slain by John Conyers.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Northumbria, Sockburn Worm adalah wyvern ganas yang menghancurkan desa Sockburn di Durham, dan dikatakan akhirnya dibunuh oleh John Conyers.
statement.en: In Northumbrian folklore the Sockburn Worm was a ferocious wyvern that laid waste to the village of Sockburn in Durham, said to have finally been slain by John Conyers.

claims.quote: The tale is said to be the inspiration for Lewis Carroll's poem Jabberwocky which he wrote while in Croft-on-Tees and Whitburn.

statement.id: Kisah ini dikatakan mengilhami puisi Jabberwocky karya Lewis Carroll, yang ditulisnya saat berada di Croft-on-Tees dan Whitburn.
statement.en: The tale is said to have inspired Lewis Carroll's poem Jabberwocky, written while he was in Croft-on-Tees and Whitburn.

claims.quote: The tale of the worm may be inspired by the longships of marauding Vikings, who carved the heads of Worms (Ormr) on the bow

statement.id: Kisah worm ini mungkin terilhami kapal panjang Viking yang mengukir kepala worm (Ormr) di haluannya.
statement.en: The tale of the worm may be inspired by the longships of marauding Vikings, who carved worm heads (Ormr) on the bow.

claims.quote: however, this does not take into account the commonness of dragons in Germanic folklore including that of Northumbria (see the Laidly and Lambton Worms as well as the Worm of Linton).

statement.id: Namun dugaan itu tidak memperhitungkan banyaknya naga dalam cerita rakyat Jermanik, termasuk Northumbria (seperti Laidly Worm, Lambton Worm, dan Worm of Linton).
statement.en: However, this does not account for the commonness of dragons in Germanic folklore including Northumbria (see the Laidly and Lambton Worms and the Worm of Linton).

claims.quote: The tradition lapsed from 1771 and the sword was given to Durham Cathedral in 1947. The ceremony was revived by bishop David Jenkins in 1984

statement.id: Tradisi itu terhenti sejak 1771, pedangnya diserahkan ke Katedral Durham pada 1947, dan upacaranya dihidupkan kembali oleh Uskup David Jenkins pada 1984.
statement.en: The tradition lapsed from 1771, the sword was given to Durham Cathedral in 1947, and the ceremony was revived by Bishop David Jenkins in 1984.

claims.quote: The Sockburn Worm, with the falchion embedded in it, appears on the district badge of the local Darlington & District Scout Association.

statement.id: Sockburn Worm dengan falchion tertancap padanya muncul di lencana distrik Darlington & District Scout Association.
statement.en: The Sockburn Worm, with the falchion embedded in it, appears on the district badge of the Darlington & District Scout Association.

claims.quote: According to legend, this was because in 1063 the head of the family, Sir John Conyers, had killed a fearsome dragon which had been terrorising the area, known as the Sockburn Worm.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, pada 1063 kepala keluarga, Sir John Conyers, membunuh naga menakutkan yang meneror wilayah itu, yang dikenal sebagai Sockburn Worm.
statement.en: According to legend, in 1063 the head of the family, Sir John Conyers, killed a fearsome dragon terrorising the area, known as the Sockburn Worm.

claims.quote: My Lord Bishop. I hereby present you with the falchion wherewith the champion Conyers slew the worm, dragon or fiery flying serpent which destroyed man, woman and child; in memory of which the king then reigning gave him the manor of Sockburn

statement.id: Pidato upacara: falchion ini dipakai sang juara Conyers membunuh worm, naga, atau ular terbang berapi yang membinasakan laki-laki, perempuan, dan anak-anak; untuk mengenangnya raja memberinya manor Sockburn.
statement.en: The ceremonial speech: this falchion is the one with which the champion Conyers slew the worm, dragon or fiery flying serpent that destroyed man, woman and child; in memory of which the king gave him the manor of Sockburn.

claims.quote: The custom fell out of use in 1771, and the sword was given to the Cathedral in 1947. The tenure ceremony was revived in 1984, the sword now being presented to the Bishop by the Mayor of Darlington

statement.id: Kebiasaan itu terhenti pada 1771, pedangnya diserahkan ke katedral pada 1947, dan upacara dihidupkan kembali pada 1984 dengan Wali Kota (Mayor) Darlington sebagai penyerah pedang kepada Uskup.
statement.en: The custom fell out of use in 1771, the sword was given to the Cathedral in 1947, and the ceremony was revived in 1984, with the Mayor of Darlington now presenting the sword to the Bishop.

claims.quote: The story of the Sockburn Worm was almost certainly the inspiration for Lewis Carroll’s famous nonsense poem ‘Jabberwocky’. Carroll lived in nearby Croft-on-Tees as a boy

statement.id: Kisah Sockburn Worm hampir pasti mengilhami puisi nonsens Jabberwocky karya Lewis Carroll, yang semasa kecil tinggal di Croft-on-Tees.
statement.en: The Sockburn Worm story was almost certainly the inspiration for Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem Jabberwocky; Carroll lived in Croft-on-Tees as a boy.

claims.quote: In the poem, the hero wields a ‘vorpal blade’ to kill the monster, a weapon probably based on the falchion.

statement.id: Dalam puisi itu sang pahlawan memakai 'vorpal blade' untuk membunuh monster, senjata yang mungkin terilhami falchion.
statement.en: In the poem the hero wields a vorpal blade to kill the monster, a weapon probably based on the falchion.

claims.quote: telling the story of a young knight named Sir. John Conyers, who fought to save his lands from a great dragon who had haunted the region for seven years.

statement.id: Kisahnya tentang ksatria muda Sir John Conyers yang bertarung menyelamatkan tanahnya dari naga besar yang telah menghantui wilayah itu selama tujuh tahun.
statement.en: The story tells of a young knight, Sir John Conyers, who fought to save his lands from a great dragon that had haunted the region for seven years.

claims.quote: After offering his prayers at a nearby chapel, Sir John slew the foul-breathed serpent with his trusty falchion, letting its decimated body rest in the River Tees. He buried what was left of the beast under the great ‘Grey Stone’ still visible today

statement.id: Setelah berdoa di kapel terdekat, Sir John membunuh ular berbau busuk itu dengan falchion-nya, membiarkan tubuhnya di Sungai Tees, dan mengubur sisanya di bawah Grey Stone yang masih terlihat sekarang.
statement.en: After praying at a nearby chapel, Sir John slew the foul-breathed serpent with his falchion, left its body in the River Tees, and buried what remained under the Grey Stone still visible today.

claims.quote: Sr. Jo. Conyers of Storkburn [sic] Knt who slew [th]e monstrous venoms and poysons wiverns Ask or worme which overthrew and Devourd many people in fight
claims.locator: quotation from an early seventeenth-century heraldry book

statement.id: Buku heraldik: Sir John Conyers dari Sockburn (ditulis Storkburn) membunuh wyvern (wiverns) atau worme yang mengerikan, berbisa (venoms), dan beracun, yang menjatuhkan dan melahap (Devourd) banyak orang.
statement.en: Heraldry book: Sir John Conyers of Storkburn slew the monstrous, venomous (venoms) and poisonous wyvern (wiverns) or worme that overthrew and devoured (Devourd) many people.

claims.quote: A book of heraldry dating from the early seventeenth century recalls the legend

statement.id: Sebuah buku heraldik dari awal abad ke-17 mencatat legenda ini.
statement.en: A book of heraldry dating from the early seventeenth century recalls the legend.

claims.quote: In the North East, tales of dragons (known as ‘worms’) seem to have dominated the popular imagination, with at least twenty separate stories recorded in Northumbria, Co. Durham and Yorkshire alone.

statement.id: Di Timur Laut, kisah naga (disebut worms) tampaknya mendominasi imajinasi rakyat, dengan sedikitnya dua puluh kisah tercatat di Northumbria, Co. Durham, dan Yorkshire.
statement.en: In the North East, tales of dragons (known as worms) seem to have dominated the popular imagination, with at least twenty separate stories recorded in Northumbria, Co. Durham and Yorkshire alone.

claims.quote: During these tumultuous times of religious and social upheaval, the story of the Sockburn Worm reigned supreme
claims.locator: paragraph comparing the Lambton and Sockburn Worms

statement.id: Pada masa pergolakan agama dan sosial itu, kisah Sockburn Worm paling unggul (reigned supreme).
statement.en: During these tumultuous times of religious and social upheaval, the story of the Sockburn Worm reigned supreme.

claims.quote: Bishop Cosin records the pomp and excitement associated with the ceremony in 1661

statement.id: Uskup Cosin mencatat kemeriahan dan kegembiraan upacara itu pada 1661.
statement.en: Bishop Cosin records the pomp and excitement of the ceremony in 1661.

claims.quote: Sockburn was a village under siege from the ferocious Sockburn Worm, who terrorised locals, devoured livestock and lay waste to the land.

statement.id: Sockburn adalah desa yang dikepung Sockburn Worm yang ganas, yang meneror penduduk, melahap ternak, dan menghancurkan tanah.
statement.en: Sockburn was a village under siege from the ferocious Sockburn Worm, which terrorised locals, devoured livestock and laid waste to the land.

claims.quote: A worm is the name given to a wyvern, a winged dragon sporting a tail with an arrow-shaped tip and has two legs instead of four.

statement.id: Worm adalah sebutan untuk wyvern, naga bersayap dengan ekor berujung mata panah dan dua kaki, bukan empat.
statement.en: A worm is the name given to a wyvern, a winged dragon with an arrow-tipped tail and two legs instead of four.

claims.quote: From that time on to the present day, whenever a new Bishop of Durham enters the Diocese for the first time by crossing the River Tees at Croft on Tees, a welcoming ceremony is conducted on the bridge.

statement.id: Sejak saat itu hingga kini, setiap Uskup Durham baru yang pertama kali memasuki keuskupan dengan menyeberangi Sungai Tees di Croft on Tees disambut dengan upacara di jembatan.

claims.quote: The reputation and pedigree of the Conyers family was firmly linked to the dragon their ancestor had slayed. The Sockburn Worm was tied to the ceremonial ritual of the Palatinate.

statement.id: Reputasi dan silsilah keluarga Conyers terikat erat pada naga yang dibunuh leluhurnya, dan Sockburn Worm terikat pada ritual upacara Palatinate.
statement.en: The reputation and pedigree of the Conyers family was firmly linked to the dragon their ancestor slew, and the Sockburn Worm was tied to the ceremonial ritual of the Palatinate.

claims.quote: and received the lands of Sockburn for his efforts from the Bishop of Durham.

short_description.id: Rusalka adalah makhluk perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Slavia yang erat dengan air dan sering memusuhi manusia, biasanya arwah perempuan muda yang mati tenggelam.
short_description.en: The rusalka is a female being of Slavic folklore, closely tied to water and often hostile to people, usually the spirit of a young woman who drowned.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Slavia, rusalka adalah sosok perempuan yang sering berbuat jahat kepada manusia dan biasanya dikaitkan dengan air. Padanannya di Eropa lain antara lain Melusine dari Prancis dan Nixie dari dunia Jermanik. Di Rusia utara ia punya banyak sebutan seperti vodyanitsa, sedangkan di Ukraina ia disebut mavka.
long_description.en: In Slavic folklore the rusalka is a female figure, frequently harmful to people and usually associated with water. Her counterparts elsewhere in Europe include the French Melusine and the Germanic Nixie. In northern Russia she had many names, such as vodyanitsa, while in Ukraine she was called a mavka.

long_description.id: Menurut kebanyakan cerita, arwah perempuan muda yang mati di atau dekat sungai atau danau kembali menghantui perairan itu. Ia tidak selalu jahat dan dapat beristirahat dengan tenang bila kematiannya dibalas, tetapi tujuan utamanya memikat pemuda dengan rupa atau suaranya, lalu menjerat kaki mereka dengan rambut panjangnya dan menenggelamkan mereka. Dalam sebagian cerita, korban dibunuh dengan digelitik sampai mati atau dipaksa ikut tarian yang liar. Rambutnya selalu terurai dan bisa pirang, hitam, kehijauan, atau hijau sama sekali.
long_description.en: In most stories the soul of a young woman who died in or near a river or lake returns to haunt those waters. She is not always malevolent and may rest in peace once her death is avenged, but her chief aim is to lure young men with her looks or voice, bind their feet with her long hair and drag them under. In some tales victims were tickled to death or forced to join a frenzied dance. Her hair is always loose and may be fair, black, greenish or entirely green.

long_description.id: Gambaran rusalka berbeda menurut daerah. Di Ukraina ia lebih sering dikaitkan dengan air, di Belarus dengan hutan dan ladang; biasanya ia digambarkan sebagai gadis cantik tanpa busana, tetapi di beberapa tempat sebagai makhluk buruk rupa dan berbulu. Rusalka dipercaya paling berbahaya pada Pekan Rusalka di awal Juni, ketika mereka keluar dari air untuk berayun di dahan pohon birch dan willow pada malam hari, sehingga berenang saat itu dilarang keras.
long_description.en: Images of the rusalka varied by region. In Ukraine she was more often tied to water, in Belarus to forest and field; she was usually a beautiful naked maiden, but in some areas a hideous, hairy creature. Rusalki were thought most dangerous during Rusalka Week in early June, when they left the water to swing on birch and willow branches at night, so swimming then was strictly forbidden.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari rusalija, yang masuk ke bahasa Slavia lewat bahasa Yunani Bizantium dari kata Latin Rosālia, nama untuk Pentakosta dan hari-hari di sekitarnya. Menurut Vladimir Propp, bangsa Slavia pagan semula mengaitkan rusalka dengan kesuburan: mereka keluar dari air pada musim semi untuk membawa kelembapan ke ladang dan tidak dianggap jahat sebelum abad ke-19. Dalam versi abad ke-19, rusalka menjadi makhluk mati yang gelisah dan berbahaya.
long_description.en: Her name comes from rusalija, which reached the Slavic languages through Byzantine Greek from the Latin Rosālia, a name for Pentecost and the days around it. According to Vladimir Propp, pagan Slavs first linked rusalki with fertility: they rose from the water in spring to bring moisture to the fields and were not thought evil before the 19th century. In 19th-century versions the rusalka became a restless, dangerous dead being.

statement.id: Dalam versi abad ke-19, rusalka adalah makhluk yang sudah mati, gelisah, dan berbahaya, yang dikaitkan dengan roh najis.
statement.en: In 19th-century versions the rusalka is a restless, dangerous being no longer alive, associated with the unclean spirit.

claims.quote: It is accounted by most stories that the soul of a young woman who had died in or near a river or a lake would come back to haunt that waterway. This undead rusalka is not invariably malevolent, and would be allowed to die in peace if her death is avenged.

statement.id: Menurut kebanyakan cerita, arwah perempuan muda yang mati di atau dekat sungai atau danau kembali menghantui perairan itu; rusalka mayat hidup ini tidak selalu jahat dan dapat mati dengan tenang bila kematiannya dibalas.
statement.en: Most stories say the soul of a young woman who died in or near a river or lake returns to haunt it; this undead rusalka is not always malevolent and may die in peace if her death is avenged.

claims.quote: Her main purpose is, however, to lure young men, seduced by either her looks or her voice, into the depths of said waterways where she would entangle their feet with her long hair and submerge them.

statement.id: Tujuan utamanya adalah memikat pemuda dengan rupa atau suaranya ke kedalaman perairan, lalu menjerat kaki mereka dengan rambut panjangnya dan menenggelamkan mereka.
statement.en: Her main purpose is to lure young men with her looks or voice into the depths, entangle their feet in her long hair and drown them.

claims.quote: They killed their victims by tickling them to death or forcing them to participate in a frenzied dance.

statement.id: Mereka membunuh korban dengan menggelitikinya sampai mati atau memaksanya ikut serta dalam tarian yang liar.
statement.en: They killed their victims by tickling them to death or forcing them into a frenzied dance.

claims.quote: In stories from Ukraine, they were often linked with water. In Belarus they were linked with the forest and field. They were usually pictured as beautiful naked maidens, but in some areas they were imagined as hideous and hairy.

statement.id: Dalam cerita dari Ukraina rusalka sering dikaitkan dengan air, di Belarus dengan hutan dan ladang; biasanya mereka digambarkan sebagai gadis cantik tanpa busana, tetapi di beberapa daerah sebagai makhluk buruk rupa dan berbulu.
statement.en: In Ukrainian stories rusalki were often linked with water, in Belarus with forest and field; usually pictured as beautiful naked maidens, in some areas they were hideous and hairy.

claims.quote: The rusalki were believed to be at their most dangerous during the 'Rusalka week' ... in early June. At this time, they were supposed to have left their watery depths in order to swing on branches of birch and willow trees by night.

statement.id: Rusalka dipercaya paling berbahaya pada Pekan Rusalka di awal Juni, ketika mereka keluar dari air untuk berayun di dahan pohon birch dan willow pada malam hari.
statement.en: Rusalki were believed most dangerous during Rusalka Week in early June, when they left the water to swing on birch and willow branches at night.

claims.quote: Swimming during this week was strictly forbidden, lest mermaids drag a swimmer down to the river bed.

statement.id: Selama pekan itu berenang dilarang keras, agar perenang tidak diseret ke dasar sungai.
statement.en: Swimming that week was strictly forbidden, lest a swimmer be dragged to the river bed.

claims.quote: the currently dominant presents her as something like a mermaid, though she is pictured as having legs rather than a fish tail ... In the past, her image was more complex and she more closely resembled a nature spirit, found not only near water but in fields, forests, and mountains, rather like the vila

statement.id: Menurut seorang ahli folklor, gambaran yang kini dominan menyerupai putri duyung tetapi berkaki, bukan berekor ikan; dulu gambarannya lebih rumit dan lebih mirip roh alam yang ditemukan di dekat air, ladang, hutan, dan gunung.
statement.en: According to a folklorist, the dominant image today is mermaid-like but with legs rather than a fish tail; formerly she was more complex, closer to a nature spirit found by water, in fields, forests and mountains.

statement.id: Menurut sebagian besar tradisi, rusalka adalah perempuan ikan yang tinggal di dasar sungai dan berasal dari perempuan yang meninggal di sungai.
statement.en: In most traditions the rusalka is a fish-woman living on the river bed, arising from women who died in the river.

claims.quote: Rusalka tidak bisa tinggal lama di atas permukaan, tetapi sisir mereka bisa mengeluarkan air untuk membasahi rambut mereka, jika rambutnya kering maka rusalka akan mati.

statement.id: Rusalka tidak bisa lama di atas permukaan air, tetapi sisirnya dapat mengeluarkan air untuk membasahi rambutnya; jika rambutnya kering, rusalka akan mati.
statement.en: The rusalka cannot stay long above water, but her comb can produce water to wet her hair; if her hair dries, she dies.

claims.quote: In most beliefs rusalki always have loose hair ... The hair of the rusalka can be fair, black, greenish or completely green.

statement.id: Dalam kebanyakan kepercayaan rambut rusalka selalu terurai, dan warnanya bisa pirang, hitam, kehijauan, atau hijau sepenuhnya.
statement.en: In most beliefs rusalki always have loose hair, which can be fair, black, greenish or completely green.

short_description.id: Turul adalah burung pemangsa mitologis dalam tradisi Hungaria dan Turk, umumnya digambarkan sebagai falkon, dan menjadi lambang nasional bangsa Hungaria.
short_description.en: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey of Hungarian and Turkic tradition, usually shown as a falcon, and a national symbol of the Hungarians.

long_description.id: Turul adalah burung pemangsa mitologis dalam tradisi Hungaria dan Turk yang umumnya digambarkan sebagai falkon, dan kini menjadi lambang nasional bangsa Hungaria. Burung ini kemungkinan besar didasarkan pada falkon besar. Dalam bahasa Hungaria, turul adalah sebutan untuk satu jenis falkon, dan asal katanya kini dianggap paling mungkin dari bahasa Turk, dengan bentuk toġrïl atau toğrul yang berarti burung pemangsa sedang hingga besar dari famili Accipitridae.
long_description.en: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey of Hungarian and Turkic tradition, usually pictured as a falcon, and today a national symbol of the Hungarians. It is probably modelled on a large falcon. In Hungarian, turul named one kind of falcon, and the word is now thought most likely to be of Turkic origin, from toġrïl or toğrul, a medium to large bird of prey of the family Accipitridae.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda Emese yang tercatat dalam Gesta Hungarorum dan Chronicon Pictum, turul muncul dalam mimpi Emese ketika ia sudah hamil. Peran turul di sini adalah roh pelindung yang menjaga bayi Álmos dari bahaya, motif yang sangat mirip dengan peran Simurgh dalam epos Iran Shahnameh. Dalam mimpi kedua pemimpin suku Hungaria, elang-elang lambang bangsa Pecheneg menyerang kuda mereka, lalu turul datang menyelamatkannya.
long_description.en: Both the Gesta Hungarorum and the Chronicon Pictum preserve the tale of Emese, who sees the turul in a dream while already carrying her child. Its role there is that of a guardian spirit shielding the infant Álmos from harm, a motif very close to the Simurgh's role in the Iranian epic Shahnameh. In a second dream of the Hungarian tribal leader, eagles, the emblem of the Pechenegs, attacked their horses and the turul came to rescue them.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Hungaria, turul bermula sebagai lambang klan wangsa Árpád yang berkuasa pada abad ke-9 dan ke-10. Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum menyebut wangsa itu keturunan klan Turul, dan Gesta Hungarorum mencatat turul sebagai leluhur totemik Árpád. Sepasang cakram perak bermotif turul ditemukan di Rakamaz dari pemakaman Hungaria abad ke-10.
long_description.en: In Hungarian tradition the turul began as the clan emblem of the ruling Árpád dynasty in the 9th and 10th centuries. The Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum says the dynasty descended from the Turul clan, and the Gesta Hungarorum records the turul as Árpád's totemic ancestor. A pair of silver discs with a turul motif was found at Rakamaz in a 10th-century Hungarian cemetery.

long_description.id: Kini turul menjadi unsur utama lambang Angkatan Bersenjata Hungaria: burung bersayap terbentang yang mencengkeram pedang Raja Santo Stefanus. Patung turul di sebuah gunung dekat Tatabánya disebut patung burung terbesar di Eropa.
long_description.en: Today the turul is the centrepiece of the Hungarian Defence Forces emblem: a bird with outspread wings gripping the sword of King Saint Stephen. The turul statue on a mountain near Tatabánya is described as the largest bird statue in Europe.

statement.en: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey, mostly depicted as a falcon, in Hungarian and Turkic tradition, and a national symbol of Hungarians.

statement.en: The Turul is probably based on a large falcon; the Hungarian word turul meant one kind of falcon, and its origin is now thought most likely Turkic.

statement.en: In the legend of Emese, recorded in the Gesta Hungarorum and the Chronicon Pictum, the turul appears in Emese's dream when she was already pregnant.

claims.quote: The Turul's role is one of a protector spirit that protects the infant Álmos from harm. This is a very similar motif to the role of the Simurgh in the Iranian epic Shahnameh.

statement.id: Peran turul adalah roh pelindung yang menjaga bayi Álmos dari bahaya, motif yang sangat mirip dengan peran Simurgh dalam epos Iran Shahnameh.
statement.en: The Turul's role is a protector spirit shielding the infant Álmos from harm, a motif very similar to the Simurgh's role in the Iranian epic Shahnameh.

claims.quote: In Hungarian tradition, it originated as the clan symbol used in the 9th and 10th centuries by the ruling Árpád dynasty.

statement.id: Dalam tradisi Hungaria, turul bermula sebagai lambang klan yang dipakai wangsa Árpád yang berkuasa pada abad ke-9 dan ke-10.
statement.en: In Hungarian tradition it originated as the clan symbol of the ruling Árpád dynasty in the 9th and 10th centuries.

claims.quote: The Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum mentioned that the Árpád dynasty descended from the gens (clan) Turul, and the Gesta Hungarorum recorded that the Árpád's totemic ancestor was the Turul.

statement.id: Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum menyebut wangsa Árpád keturunan klan Turul, dan Gesta Hungarorum mencatat bahwa leluhur totemik Árpád adalah turul.
statement.en: The Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum says the Árpád dynasty descended from the Turul clan, and the Gesta Hungarorum records the Turul as Árpád's totemic ancestor.

claims.quote: a divine vision appeared to his mother in a dream in the form of a falcon that, as if coming to her, impregnated her and made known to her that from her womb a torrent would come forth and from her loins glorious kings be generated

statement.id: Menurut Gesta Hungarorum, penampakan ilahi berwujud falkon muncul dalam mimpi ibu Álmos, seakan mendatangi dan membuahinya, serta memberitahukan bahwa dari rahimnya akan mengalir arus deras dan lahir raja-raja mulia.
statement.en: According to the Gesta Hungarorum, a divine vision in the form of a falcon appeared in a dream to Álmos's mother, as if coming to her and impregnating her, and revealed that a torrent would come from her womb and glorious kings from her loins.

short_description.id: Xiuhcōātl adalah ular api dalam agama Aztek, wujud roh dewa api Xiuhtecuhtli dan senjata Huitzilopochtli; namanya berarti "ular pirus".
short_description.en: Xiuhcōātl is the fire serpent of Aztec religion, the spirit form of the fire god Xiuhtecuhtli and a weapon of Huitzilopochtli; its name means "turquoise serpent".

long_description.id: Dalam agama Aztek, Xiuhcōātl adalah ular mitologis, wujud roh dewa api Xiuhtecuhtli, yang kadang digambarkan sebagai atlatl atau senjata Huitzilopochtli. Namanya dalam bahasa Nahuatl berarti "ular pirus" dan secara simbolis "ular api". Ia ditafsirkan sebagai perwujudan musim kemarau dan senjata matahari; dalam kisah kelahiran Huitzilopochtli, sang dewa bertempur dengan perisai, tombak lempar, dan Xiuhcoatl.
long_description.en: In Aztec religion Xiuhcōātl was a mythological serpent, the spirit form of the fire god Xiuhtecuhtli, sometimes shown as an atlatl or weapon of Huitzilopochtli. Its Nahuatl name means "turquoise serpent" and symbolically "fire serpent". It is read as the embodiment of the dry season and the weapon of the sun; in the birth story of Huitzilopochtli, the god fights with shield, darts and Xiuhcoatl.

long_description.id: Xiuhcoatl sering muncul dalam seni dan kodeks Aztek, biasanya dengan moncong melengkung ke belakang dan tubuh beruas-ruas yang dililit pita kertas bersimpul, lambang persembahan darah. Ia juga menjadi hiasan punggung pada gambar Xiuhtecuhtli dan Huitzilopochtli, dan mahkota kaisar Aztek tampaknya melambangkan ekornya.
long_description.en: Xiuhcoatl was common in Aztec art and codices, usually with a back-turned snout and a segmented body wrapped in knotted paper strips, a sign of blood offering. It appears as a back ornament on images of Xiuhtecuhtli and Huitzilopochtli, and the Aztec emperors' diadem apparently represented its tail.

short_description.id: El Sombrerón adalah tokoh legenda paling terkenal di Guatemala, lelaki bertopi besar yang mengepang rambut kuda dan perempuan muda serta menyanyikan serenade.
short_description.en: El Sombrerón is one of Guatemala's best-known legendary figures, a man in a huge hat who braids horses' and young women's hair and sings serenades.

long_description.id: El Sombrerón adalah tokoh legenda dan salah satu legenda paling terkenal di Guatemala, juga sosok penakut anak di Meksiko; ia dikenal pula sebagai Tzipitio atau Tzizimite. Ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki berpakaian hitam dengan sabuk tebal mengilap, topi hitam besar, dan sepatu bot yang berisik. Ia suka menunggang kuda dan mengepang ekor serta surainya, atau bulu anjing bila tak ada kuda. Ia mengejar gadis berambut panjang dan bermata besar, mengepang rambutnya dan bernyanyi dengan gitar peraknya, tetapi menaruh tanah di piringnya hingga gadis itu tak bisa makan atau tidur.
long_description.en: El Sombrerón is a legendary figure and among the most famous legends of Guatemala, and a bogeyman in Mexico as well; he also goes by Tzipitio or Tzizimite. He is pictured as a man in black with a thick shining belt, a great black hat and noisy boots. He loves riding horses and plaiting their tails and manes, or dogs' hair when no horse is at hand. He pursues girls with long hair and big eyes, braiding their hair and playing his silver guitar for them, yet he puts earth in the girl's food so she can neither eat nor sleep.

long_description.id: Ia muncul saat senja sambil menggiring kawanan bagal pengangkut arang. Dalam kisahnya, gadis bernama Susana di lingkungan La Recolección tak bisa tidur atau makan karenanya, sampai orang tuanya memotong rambutnya dan membawanya ke gereja untuk diberkati. Miguel Ángel Asturias menulis "Legend of El Sombrerón" dalam Legends of Guatemala (1930), dan pada 1950 ia menjadi subjek film. Artikel es menggambarkannya sebagai kurcaci bertopi besar yang mengepang rambut perempuan di malam hari.
long_description.en: He shows up at dusk driving a string of mules loaded with coal. In the tale, a girl named Susana in La Recolección could neither sleep nor eat because of him until her parents cut her hair and took it to church to be blessed. Miguel Ángel Asturias wrote 'Legend of El Sombrerón' in his 1930 Legends of Guatemala, and in 1950 he was the subject of a film. The es article describes him as a dwarf in an enormous hat who braids women's hair at night.

short_description.id: Maelor Gawr adalah raja Kelt awal sekaligus raksasa dalam mitologi Wales yang tinggal di Castell Maelor dan kisahnya dicatat bersama tiga putranya dalam teks akhir abad ke-16.
short_description.en: Maelor Gawr, a giant and early Celtic king in Welsh mythology, lived at Castell Maelor; his tale, with his three sons, is preserved in a Welsh text of the late 1500s.

long_description.id: Maelor Gawr dikenal sebagai raja Kelt awal dan raksasa dalam mitologi Wales. Kisahnya bersama tiga putranya, Cornippyn, Crygyn, dan Bwba, tercatat dalam teks Wales akhir abad ke-16; teks itu mengejanya Maylor Gawr dan menempatkannya di Aberteifi sebelum kedatangan Brutus.
long_description.en: Maelor Gawr is known as an early Celtic king and giant of Welsh mythology. His tale with his three sons, Cornippyn, Crygyn and Bwba, is recorded in a late sixteenth-century Welsh text; that text spells him Maylor Gawr and places him in Aberteifi before the coming of Brutus.

long_description.id: Menurut teks itu, Maylor ditawan di Cyfeilog, sekitar dua belas mil dari kastilnya, dan sebelum dihukum mati ia diizinkan meniup tanduknya tiga kali. Tiupan pertama merontokkan rambut dan jenggotnya, tiupan kedua merontokkan semua kukunya, dan pada tiupan ketiga tanduk itu pecah berkeping-keping.
long_description.en: According to the text, Maylor was taken prisoner at Cyfeilog, about twelve miles from his castle, and before being put to death was allowed to blow his horn three times. The first blast made his hair and beard fall out, the second his nails, and at the third the horn shattered into small pieces.

long_description.id: Cornippin, putranya, mendengar bunyi tanduk itu dan memacu kudanya demikian cepat hingga kepala anjing pemburunya terlepas; kudanya melompati Sungai Ystwyth dalam satu lompatan. Setelah bertarung, ia terbunuh. Dua putra lain, Crygyn dan Bwba, membunuh siapa pun yang mendekati benteng mereka.
long_description.en: His son Cornippin heard the horn and rode so fast that his hound's head was torn off; his horse cleared the Ystwyth River in a single bound. After fighting he was killed. The other two sons, Crygyn and Bwba, killed anyone who came near their strongholds.

long_description.id: Cerita masa kini di Penparcau masih mengisahkan anjing tanpa kepala milik putra Raja Maelor.
long_description.en: Present-day stories in Penparcau still tell of the headless dog of King Maelor's son.

short_description.id: Nuberu, "Si Pembuat Awan", adalah roh atau dewa awan dan badai dalam mitologi Asturias, Cantabria, Galisia, dan León yang merusak panen dengan hujan es dan petir tetapi baik kepada penolongnya.
short_description.en: Nuberu, 'The Clouder', is a spirit or god of clouds and storms in Asturian, Cantabrian, Galician and Leonese mythology who wrecks harvests with hail and lightning but is kind to those who help him.

long_description.id: Nuberu atau Nubeiro, "Si Pembuat Awan", adalah dewa awan dan badai dari Asturias, Cantabria, Galisia, dan León. Di Asturias ia satu sosok tua berjanggut berpakaian kulit binatang gelap dan bertopi besar, naik kereta yang ditarik serigala, dan bermata satu; di Cantabria nuberu adalah banyak makhluk kecil gemuk bersayap hitam, dan di Galisia lelaki kecil berbulu berekor atau raksasa yang menempa petir di bengkel pegunungan. Wajahnya buruk dengan mata seperti bara.
long_description.en: Nuberu or Nubeiro, 'The Clouder', is a god of clouds and storms of Asturias, Cantabria, Galicia and León. In Asturias he is a single old bearded being in dark pelts and a big hat who rides a wolf-drawn chariot and has one eye; in Cantabria the Nuberus are many small chubby black-winged creatures, and in Galicia small hairy tailed men or a giant who forges lightning in a mountain workshop. His face is ugly with ember-like eyes.

long_description.id: Ia merusak ladang dan dipersalahkan nelayan atas angin kencang Laut Cantabria, tetapi baik kepada yang menolongnya: petani yang menampungnya diberi hujan dan panen, lalu dibawa menunggang awan dari Mesir pulang tepat waktu untuk menggagalkan pernikahan istrinya. Ia tinggal di Orito, Mesir, dan dianggap sisa dewa Taranis, serupa Entiznáu dari Extremadura, dan dibandingkan dengan Odin.
long_description.en: He damages fields and fishermen blame him for the Cantabrian Sea's gales, but he is kind to helpers: the peasant who sheltered him got rain and harvests and was later carried on the clouds from Egypt in time to stop his wife's wedding. He lives in Orito, Egypt, and is seen as a remnant of Taranis, akin to the Entiznáu of Extremadura, and compared with Odin.

claims.quote: Nubero (Castilian) or Nubeiro (Galician) -literally "The Clouder"- is a character of Asturian, Cantabrian, Galician and Leonese mythology.

statement.id: Nuberu, Nubero (Kastilia), atau Nubeiro (Galisia), harfiah "Si Pembuat Awan", adalah tokoh mitologi Asturias, Cantabria, Galisia, dan León.
statement.en: Nuberu, Nubero (Castilian) or Nubeiro (Galician), literally 'The Clouder', is a figure of Asturian, Cantabrian, Galician and Leonese mythology.

claims.quote: According to Asturian mythology, the Nuberu (also known in Western Asturias as Reñubeiru or Xuan Cabritu) is the divinity of clouds and storms.

statement.id: Menurut mitologi Asturias, Nuberu (di Asturias barat juga Reñubeiru atau Xuan Cabritu) adalah dewa awan dan badai.
statement.en: In Asturian mythology the Nuberu (in western Asturias also Reñubeiru or Xuan Cabritu) is the god of clouds and storms.

claims.quote: In some stories, he is an individual; in others, the Nuberu is a species of dwarf-like beings with the power to control the weather. Sometimes, he is represented as a man with a thick beard, who wears goat leathers and a big hat.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian cerita ia satu sosok, dalam cerita lain sejenis makhluk mirip kurcaci yang dapat mengendalikan cuaca, dan kadang ia digambarkan lelaki berjanggut lebat berpakaian kulit kambing dan bertopi besar.
statement.en: In some stories he is one being, in others a species of dwarf-like weather-controlling beings, and sometimes a thick-bearded man in goatskins and a big hat.

claims.quote: When he is treated as a single entity, Nuberu is said to dress with dark pelts and leather, travel in a chariot pulled by wolves, and wear a patch to cover an injured or missing eye.

statement.id: Sebagai satu sosok, Nuberu berpakaian kulit binatang gelap, naik kereta yang ditarik serigala, dan memakai penutup mata untuk mata yang terluka atau hilang.
statement.en: As a single being, Nuberu wears dark pelts, rides a wolf-drawn chariot and wears a patch over an injured or missing eye.

claims.quote: He, or they, can be terribly cruel to people, damaging fields and pastures, although he can also be very kind to those who had helped him before. The myth tells us that he lives in the city of Orito, in Egypt.

statement.id: Ia bisa sangat kejam, merusak ladang dan padang rumput, tetapi baik kepada orang yang pernah menolongnya, dan menurut mitos ia tinggal di kota Orito di Mesir.
statement.en: He can be terribly cruel, damaging fields and pastures, but kind to those who once helped him, and by myth he lives in the city of Orito in Egypt.

claims.quote: Folklorists think that Nuberu is an Asturian remnant of the ancient god Taranis, who also ruled over the skies and was worshipped in Asturias until the Middle Ages.

statement.id: Para folklorist menganggap Nuberu sisa dewa kuno Taranis, penguasa langit yang dipuja di Asturias sampai Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: Folklorists see Nuberu as an Asturian remnant of the ancient sky god Taranis, worshipped in Asturias until the Middle Ages.

claims.quote: Within Spain, their closest parallel is the Entiznáu from Extremadura, another evil weather creature with dark appearance and power over storms, who shares description and clothing with Nuberu, but differs in size.

statement.id: Padanan terdekatnya di Spanyol adalah Entiznáu dari Extremadura, makhluk cuaca jahat yang serupa wujud dan pakaiannya tetapi berbeda ukuran.
statement.en: Its closest Spanish parallel is the Entiznáu of Extremadura, an evil weather creature of similar look and dress but different size.

claims.quote: In appreciation for his help, Nuberu irrigated his fields, and gave him good harvests, and has continued to provide rain to the people of the region.

statement.id: Konon Nuberu jatuh dari awan dan hanya seorang petani yang mau menampungnya; sebagai terima kasih, Nuberu mengairi ladangnya, memberinya panen baik, dan terus memberi hujan kepada penduduk daerah itu.
statement.en: Nuberu once fell from a cloud and only one peasant would shelter him; in thanks, Nuberu watered his fields, gave him good harvests and still brings rain to the region.

claims.quote: The peasant then asked Nuberu for help and together they travel back to Asturias riding the clouds and they arrive in time to prevent the wedding.

statement.id: Bertahun-tahun kemudian petani itu di Mesir mendengar istrinya akan menikah lagi; ia meminta tolong Nuberu, dan mereka menunggang awan kembali ke Asturias tepat waktu untuk menggagalkan pernikahan.
statement.en: Years later the peasant, in Egypt, heard his wife was to remarry; he asked Nuberu for help, and they rode the clouds back to Asturias in time to stop the wedding.

claims.quote: Fishermen fear the Nuberu because they blame him for the strong north-western winds of the Cantabrian Sea, which forces them to return hurriedly to port, where worried people await them.

statement.id: Para nelayan takut pada Nuberu karena menyalahkannya atas angin barat laut kencang di Laut Cantabria yang memaksa mereka bergegas pulang ke pelabuhan.
statement.en: Fishermen fear the Nuberu, blaming him for the strong north-westerly winds of the Cantabrian Sea that drive them hurriedly back to port.

claims.quote: In Cantabrian mythology, the Nuberus are often a multitude of little creatures, not a single one. They are described as small, chubby and mischievous, with devilish grins in their demonic faces and little black wings.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Cantabria, nuberu sering berupa banyak makhluk kecil yang gemuk dan nakal, berwajah iblis menyeringai dan bersayap hitam kecil.
statement.en: In Cantabrian mythology the Nuberus are often many little creatures, small, chubby and mischievous, with devilish grins and little black wings.

claims.quote: In Southern Galicia, Nubeiros have the appearance of small hairy men with a long and twisted tail. They fly on grey clouds and cause dry summer storms, lightning, and similar disasters.

statement.id: Di Galisia selatan, nubeiro berupa lelaki kecil berbulu berekor panjang dan berpilin yang terbang di atas awan kelabu dan menimbulkan badai kering musim panas dan petir.
statement.en: In southern Galicia Nubeiros are small hairy men with long twisted tails who fly on grey clouds and cause dry summer storms and lightning.

claims.quote: Nuberu forges lightning by himself in his iron workshop in the mountains, and when he has made enough he goes out and rides through the sky to cause storms and throw his creations around.

statement.id: Di bagian lain Galisia, Nuberu menempa petir sendiri di bengkel besinya di pegunungan, lalu menunggang langit untuk menimbulkan badai dan melemparkan petir-petirnya.
statement.en: Elsewhere in Galicia, Nuberu forges lightning himself in his mountain ironworks, then rides the sky to cause storms and hurl his creations.

claims.quote: Su apariencia varía dependiendo del lugar, pero casi siempre se describen como seres antropomorfos, envejecidos, extremadamente feos, de tez oscura, con boca y orejas grandes y barba poblada. Sus ojos hundidos lucen como brasas rojas.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, wujud mereka berbeda menurut daerah, tetapi hampir selalu mirip manusia, tua, sangat buruk rupa, berkulit gelap, bermulut dan bertelinga besar, berjanggut lebat, dengan mata cekung menyala seperti bara merah.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, their look varies by place but they are almost always humanlike, aged, extremely ugly and dark-skinned, with big mouths and ears, thick beards and sunken eyes glowing like red embers.

claims.quote: Также сравнивается с Одином и Зевсом по схожим причинам.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Rusia juga membandingkannya dengan Odin dan Zeus.
statement.en: The Russian article also compares him with Odin and Zeus.

short_description.id: Suur Tõll atau Tõll yang Agung adalah pahlawan raksasa dalam mitologi Estonia yang tinggal di Pulau Saaremaa dan melempar batu-batu besar ke arah musuhnya.
short_description.en: Suur Tõll, Toell the Great, is a giant hero of Estonian mythology who lived on the island of Saaremaa and hurled huge rocks at his enemies.

long_description.id: Suur Tõll, yang berarti Tõll yang Agung, adalah raksasa dalam mitologi Estonia dari Pulau Saaremaa. Karena kesaksian yang andal tentang mitologi Estonia kurang, kisahnya bersandar pada tradisi lisan. Ia hidup bersama istrinya, Piret, di desa pesisir Tõlluste, dan melemparkan batu raksasa ke segala arah, terutama ke arah musuh bebuyutannya Vanatühi atau Vanapagan, sosok yang mewakili kejahatan.
long_description.en: Suur Tõll, meaning Toell the Great, is a giant of Estonian mythology from the island of Saaremaa. Since reliable evidence on Estonian mythology is lacking, his story rests on oral tradition. He lived with his wife Piret in the coastal village of Tõlluste and flung huge rocks in all directions, chiefly at his archenemy Vanatühi or Vanapagan, a figure standing for the diabolical.

long_description.id: Walaupun menjadi raja Saaremaa, Tõll hidup seperti petani biasa. Ia sering mengunjungi saudaranya, Leiger, di pulau tetangga Hiiumaa, dan tubuhnya begitu tinggi sehingga ia nyaris dapat berjalan kaki ke sana; tongkatnya sebatang pohon cemara. Ia selalu baik hati dan suka menolong, tetapi mudah marah, dan gemar makan kubis, minum bir, serta mandi sauna.
long_description.en: Though he was king of Saaremaa, Tõll lived like an ordinary farmer. He often visited his brother Leiger on neighbouring Hiiumaa, and was so tall that he could nearly walk there; his walking stick was a spruce trunk. He was always kind and helpful but quick to anger, and he loved cabbage, beer and the sauna.

long_description.id: Ketika seorang musuh memenggal kepalanya, Tõll meletakkan kepala itu di atas pedangnya dan berjalan sendiri ke kuburnya, yang konon berada di Tõlluste. Ia berjanji bangkit untuk menolong rakyat bila terjadi perang, tetapi anak-anak nakal mempermainkannya dengan seruan palsu tentang perang; Tõll bangkit, marah, lalu kembali ke kubur dan bersumpah tak akan kembali lagi.
long_description.en: When an enemy cut off his head, Tõll set it on his sword and walked to his own grave, said to lie somewhere in Tõlluste. He promised to rise and help the people in time of war, but naughty children tricked him with a false call to war; Tõll rose, grew angry, went back to his grave and swore never to return.

long_description.id: Ada dugaan bahwa kisah Tõll berakar pada tokoh sejarah, mungkin penguasa kuno Saaremaa yang juga sangat tinggi, dan asal namanya belum jelas; mungkin pelesetan Estonia dari nama keluarga bangsawan Jerman-Baltik von Toll. Tõll tetap hidup dalam budaya modern: dua kincir angin tua di desa Ninase dibentuk menyerupai Tõll dan Piret dan dikunjungi pengantin baru, dan kisahnya mengilhami film kartun Suur Tõll (1980). Pada 2002 pematung Tauno Kangro juga membuat monumen untuk sang raksasa dan istrinya di Kuressaare.
long_description.en: Some suppose that the Tõll stories rest on a historical figure, perhaps an ancient and very tall ruler of Saaremaa, and the origin of the name is unclear; it may be an Estonian corruption of the name of the Baltic German noble family von Toll. Tõll lives on in modern culture: two old windmills in Ninase village are shaped like Tõll and Piret and visited by newlyweds, and his tale inspired the cartoon film Suur Tõll (1980). In 2002 the sculptor Tauno Kangro also made a monument to the giant and his wife in Kuressaare.

short_description.id: Vitore adalah ular ilahi penjaga rumah dalam mitologi Albania, terkait dengan nasib, keberuntungan, jiwa leluhur, dan pemujaan perapian.
short_description.en: Vitore is the divine household serpent of Albanian mythology, linked with fate, good fortune, the ancestors' souls and the cult of the hearth.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, Vitore adalah ular ilahi penjaga rumah yang terkait dengan nasib manusia, keberuntungan, dan jiwa para leluhur. Ia erat dengan pemujaan perapian dan terutama dianggap pelindung keluarga dan rumah. Namanya ditafsirkan berasal dari kata untuk alat tenun, sehingga berarti "perempuan pemintal", terkait dengan menenun nasib.
long_description.en: In Albanian mythology and folklore Vitore is a divine household serpent linked with human destiny, good fortune and the souls of the ancestors. She is closely tied to the cult of the hearth and is above all the guardian of family and house. Her name is interpreted as coming from the word for a loom, meaning "a woman who spins", linked to the weaving of fate.

long_description.id: Vitorja biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular kecil berwarna-warni bertanduk emas yang baik hati, tetapi dalam sebagian tradisi sebagai perempuan tua. Bila ia tinggal di dinding rumah, ia membawa keberuntungan dan dihormati penghuni, dan desisannya menandakan peristiwa penting keluarga. Ular adalah totem hewan orang Albania, dan siluet ular diukir di dinding dan pintu rumah untuk keberuntungan.
long_description.en: Vitorja is usually described as a small, colourful, benign golden-horned serpent, but in some traditions as an old woman. When she lives in a house's walls she brings luck and is respected by the household, and her whispering announces important family events. The serpent is an animal totem of the Albanians, and snake silhouettes are carved on walls and doors for good fortune.

cultural_context.en: Vitore reflects the belief that ancestral souls take form in household serpents, tied to the cult of the hearth; snake silhouettes are carved on houses against the evil eye.

short_description.en: The volkolak is the werewolf of Slavic mythology: a sorcerer who becomes a wolf at will, a person born or cursed to shapeshift, or a victim of witchcraft.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, manusia serigala atau volkolak adalah manusia yang untuk sementara berwujud serigala; ia tampak seperti serigala biasa, tetap berakal manusia, tetapi tidak dapat berbicara. Kepercayaan ini kuno dan dikenal di semua bangsa Slavia, paling rinci di Belarus, Polandia, dan Ukraina; di Rusia istilah volkolak hanya tercatat di selatan, dan Slavia Selatan mencampurnya dengan vampir.
long_description.en: In Slavic mythology the werewolf or volkolak is a person who temporarily becomes a wolf; it looks like an ordinary wolf and keeps a human mind but cannot speak. The belief is ancient and known to all Slavic peoples, most fully among Belarusians, Poles and Ukrainians; among Russians the word volkolak is recorded only in the south, and South Slavic beliefs merge it with the vampire.

long_description.id: Penyihir menjadi serigala dengan mantra dan dengan melompati atau berguling melewati benda bertuah, misalnya pisau yang ditancapkan ke tanah, lalu kembali dengan mengulang secara terbalik. Ada pula yang terlahir atau dikutuk berubah wujud berkala, tidak terkendali dan menyerang ternak serta orang. Korban sihir, seperti rombongan pernikahan dalam kisah populer, menderita dan merindukan hidup manusia.
long_description.en: Sorcerers become wolves by spells and by leaping or tumbling over charmed objects such as knives stuck in the ground, returning by doing it in reverse. Others are born or cursed to change periodically, uncontrolled and attacking livestock and people. Victims of witchcraft, like the wedding party of a popular tale, suffer and long for human life.

claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, a werewolf is a human-shapeshifter who temporarily takes the form of a wolf. Werewolves were often described as ordinary wolves, though some accounts noted peculiarities in appearance or behavior that hinted at their human origin. Werewolves retain human intelligence but cannot speak.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, manusia serigala adalah manusia pengubah wujud yang untuk sementara berwujud serigala; ia sering digambarkan seperti serigala biasa dengan beberapa keanehan yang menandakan asal manusianya, tetap berakal manusia tetapi tidak dapat berbicara.
statement.en: In Slavic mythology a werewolf is a human shapeshifter who temporarily takes wolf form; often described as an ordinary wolf with some oddities betraying its human origin, it keeps human intelligence but cannot speak.

claims.quote: The concept is ancient and appears to varying degrees among all Slavic peoples, with the most detailed accounts among Belarusians, Poles, and Ukrainians. In Russian folklore, the character is often simply called a shapeshifter, sharing clear similarities with the werewolf.

statement.id: Konsep ini kuno dan dikenal di semua bangsa Slavia, paling rinci di kalangan orang Belarus, Polandia, dan Ukraina; dalam cerita rakyat Rusia tokoh ini sering disebut pengubah wujud saja.
statement.en: The idea is ancient and found among all Slavic peoples, most fully among Belarusians, Poles and Ukrainians; in Russian folklore the figure is often simply called a shapeshifter.

claims.quote: It was believed that sorcerers could transform into wolves by reciting spells and performing actions such as leaping, stepping over, tumbling through, or passing through magically imbued objects, or draping them over themselves.

statement.id: Penyihir dipercaya dapat menjadi serigala dengan membaca mantra lalu melompati, melangkahi, berguling melewati, atau menerobos benda bertuah, atau menyampirkannya ke tubuh.
statement.en: Sorcerers were believed to turn into wolves by reciting spells and leaping over, stepping over, tumbling through or passing through charmed objects, or draping them over themselves.

claims.quote: To revert to human form, sorcerers typically needed to repeat the actions in reverse. Sorcerers voluntarily became werewolves to cause harm to others.

statement.id: Untuk kembali menjadi manusia, penyihir mengulang tindakan itu secara terbalik; mereka menjadi manusia serigala dengan sengaja untuk mencelakai orang lain.
statement.en: To turn back into humans, sorcerers repeated the actions in reverse; they became werewolves on purpose to harm others.

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan Belarus, perubahan sukarela dilakukan dengan berjungkir balik melewati pisau yang ditancapkan ke tanah dengan ujung ke atas, berjumlah antara 1 dan 12 menurut versinya (1, 5, 7, 12).
statement.en: In Belarusian belief, a willed change is made by somersaulting over knives stuck point-up in the ground, from one to twelve in different tales (1, 5, 7, 12).

claims.quote: Some beliefs described people born with a predisposition to periodic shapeshifting due to their parents' actions or as punishment for their own sins. Such werewolves were thought to exhibit zoomorphic traits in human form, such as hair resembling wolf fur.

statement.id: Sebagian kepercayaan menyebut orang yang sejak lahir cenderung berubah wujud secara berkala karena perbuatan orang tuanya atau sebagai hukuman atas dosanya sendiri; dalam wujud manusia mereka punya ciri hewan seperti rambut mirip bulu serigala.
statement.en: Some beliefs told of people born prone to periodic shapeshifting because of their parents' deeds or as punishment for their own sins; in human form they showed animal traits such as wolf-like hair.

claims.quote: These werewolves were believed to lack control in wolf form, attacking livestock and even humans, including loved ones, and were sometimes associated with cannibalism. Ancient beliefs linked werewolves to celestial events like eclipses.

statement.id: Manusia serigala jenis ini dipercaya tidak dapat mengendalikan diri dalam wujud serigala, menyerang ternak bahkan manusia, termasuk orang terkasih, dan kadang dikaitkan dengan kanibalisme; kepercayaan kuno juga mengaitkannya dengan gerhana.
statement.en: Such werewolves were thought to lose control in wolf form, attacking livestock and even people, loved ones included, and were sometimes tied to cannibalism; ancient beliefs also linked them with eclipses.

claims.quote: Folk beliefs also held that sorcerers or witches could transform a person into a wolf, often as an act of revenge, by casting spells on a wolf skin, belt, or enchanted door, among other methods. A popular narrative involved transforming an entire wedding party into wolves.

statement.id: Penyihir laki-laki atau perempuan juga dipercaya dapat mengubah seseorang menjadi serigala, sering sebagai balas dendam, dengan memantrai kulit serigala, sabuk, atau pintu; kisah populer menceritakan seluruh rombongan pernikahan diubah menjadi serigala.
statement.en: Sorcerers or witches were also believed able to turn a person into a wolf, often in revenge, by bewitching a wolf skin, a belt or a door; a popular tale has a whole wedding party turned into wolves.

claims.quote: Involuntary werewolves suffered fear and despair, longing for human life and avoiding true wolves. They were thought to avoid carrion and raw meat, subsisting on foraged food or stolen human provisions.

statement.id: Manusia serigala yang terpaksa menderita ketakutan dan putus asa, merindukan hidup sebagai manusia, menjauhi serigala sejati, dan menghindari bangkai serta daging mentah.
statement.en: Involuntary werewolves suffered fear and despair, longed for human life, avoided real wolves and shunned carrion and raw meat.

claims.quote: The myth likely originated from ancient totemic beliefs and rites of youthful initiation. The werewolf image may have been influenced by observations of people with physical or mental disorders or of old and sick wolves.

statement.id: Mitos ini kemungkinan berasal dari kepercayaan totem kuno dan ritus inisiasi pemuda, dan citranya mungkin dipengaruhi pengamatan terhadap orang dengan gangguan fisik atau jiwa atau serigala tua dan sakit.
statement.en: The myth probably grew from ancient totemic beliefs and youth initiation rites, and its image may reflect observations of people with physical or mental disorders or of old, sick wolves.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, kepercayaan Slavia Selatan mencampuradukkan volkolak dengan upir (vampir).
statement.en: According to the Russian article, South Slavic beliefs conflate volkolaks with upirs (vampires).

short_description.id: Wulver adalah makhluk berkepala serigala dari cerita rakyat Shetland yang baik hati, suka memancing, dan meninggalkan ikan bagi orang miskin, meski asal-usulnya diperdebatkan.
short_description.en: The wulver is a kindly wolf-headed being of Shetland folklore who loves fishing and leaves fish for the poor, though its origin is disputed.

long_description.id: Wulver adalah makhluk Kepulauan Shetland berwujud lelaki berkepala serigala dan berbulu cokelat pendek, yang tinggal di gua di lereng bukit. Menurut Jessie Saxby ia baik hati, ramah kepada warga, dan memancing berjam-jam dari batu yang disebut Wulver's Stane, lalu meninggalkan ikan di jendela orang miskin; kisah lain menyebutnya buas bila diusik.
long_description.en: The wulver is a being of the Shetland Islands, a man with a wolf's head and short brown hair who lives in a cave on a hillside. According to Jessie Saxby it is kindly and friendly to locals, fishing for hours from a rock called the Wulver's Stane and leaving fish on poor people's windowsills; other accounts say it turns violent if provoked.

long_description.id: Asal-usulnya diperdebatkan: Susan Schoon Eberly menduga kisah ini berasal dari orang dengan penyakit seperti sindrom Hunter, sedangkan Brian Smith dari Shetland Museum menganggapnya rekaan Saxby sendiri.
long_description.en: Its origin is disputed: Susan Schoon Eberly suggests the tale arose from people with conditions such as Hunter syndrome, while Brian Smith of the Shetland Museum considers it Saxby's own invention.

role.en: Gives fish to the poor.

famous_for.en: The Wulver's Stane.
