claims.quote: The wulver or wullver is a kind of wolf-like humanoid creature in the folklore of the Shetland Islands of Scotland.  In modern times, the origin of the wulver has been disputed.

statement.id: Wulver atau wullver adalah makhluk mirip manusia berwujud serigala dalam cerita rakyat Kepulauan Shetland, Skotlandia, yang asal-usulnya kini diperdebatkan.
statement.en: The wulver or wullver is a wolf-like humanoid of the folklore of the Shetland Islands of Scotland, whose origin is now disputed.

claims.quote: The wulver is said by the Shetland folklorist Jessie Saxby to be benevolent, although later accounts state that they became violent if provoked. They were generally friendly to locals, however, and were known to share the fish they caught with them.

statement.id: Menurut folkloris Shetland Jessie Saxby, wulver baik hati, meski kisah lain menyebutnya menjadi buas bila diusik; mereka umumnya ramah kepada warga dan berbagi ikan tangkapannya.
statement.en: The Shetland folklorist Jessie Saxby calls the wulver benevolent, though later accounts say it turned violent if provoked; wulvers were usually friendly to locals and shared the fish they caught.

claims.quote: The Wulver was a creature like a man with a wolf's head. He had short brown hair all over him. His home was a cave dug out of the side of a steep knowe, half-way up a hill.

statement.id: Saxby menulis bahwa wulver seperti lelaki berkepala serigala, berbulu cokelat pendek di seluruh tubuh, dan tinggal di gua di lereng bukit yang curam.
statement.en: Saxby wrote that the wulver was like a man with a wolf's head, covered in short brown hair, living in a cave dug into a steep knoll halfway up a hill.

claims.quote: He was fond of catching and eating fish, and had a small rock in the deep water which is known to this day as the "Wulver's Stane". There he would sit fishing sillaks and piltaks for hour after hour. He was reported to have frequently left a few fish on the window-sill of some poor body.

statement.id: Ia suka menangkap dan memakan ikan dari batu kecil di air dalam yang sampai kini disebut Wulver's Stane, dan sering meninggalkan beberapa ekor ikan di ambang jendela orang miskin.
statement.en: He liked catching and eating fish from a little rock in deep water still called the Wulver's Stane, and often left a few fish on a poor person's windowsill.

claims.quote: Susan Schoon Eberly, has speculated that the tale of the wulver may have its basis in humans suffering a medical condition; possibly Hunter syndrome or lycanthropy, she suggests.

statement.id: Susan Schoon Eberly menduga kisah wulver mungkin berasal dari manusia yang menderita penyakit, mungkin sindrom Hunter atau likantropi.
statement.en: Susan Schoon Eberly has speculated the wulver tale may come from people with a medical condition, perhaps Hunter syndrome or lycanthropy.

claims.quote: Others, such as the Shetland Museum archivist Brian Smith, argue that the wulver is an entirely fictitious creation that was never part of Shetland folklore, contending the creature is solely the creation of Saxby.

statement.id: Yang lain, seperti arsiparis Shetland Museum Brian Smith, berpendapat wulver sepenuhnya rekaan Saxby dan tidak pernah menjadi bagian cerita rakyat Shetland.
statement.en: Others, such as the Shetland Museum archivist Brian Smith, argue the wulver is wholly Saxby's invention and was never part of Shetland folklore.

statement.en: The Catalan article also calls the wulver a humanoid wolf creature of the folklore of the Shetland Islands off Scotland.

short_description.id: Zmei ("ular") adalah bentuk naga dalam dongeng dan epos Rusia, kadang tokoh mirip manusia bersifat naga; yang terkenal antara lain Gorynych dan Tugarin.
short_description.en: Zmei ("serpent") is a form of dragon in Russian folk tales and epics, sometimes a human-like figure with dragon traits; famous ones include Gorynych and Tugarin.

long_description.id: Zmei (laki-laki) dan zmeya (perempuan), yang berarti "ular", adalah bentuk naga dalam dongeng dan epos Rusia, kadang tokoh mirip manusia yang bersifat naga. Dua zmei paling terkenal adalah Gorynych dan Tugarin, lawan para bogatyr Dobrynya Nikitich dan Alyosha Popovich. Walau berarti ular, istilah zmei untuk naga di seluruh Rusia selalu merujuk pada jenis yang terbang.
long_description.en: Zmei (masculine) and zmeya (feminine), "serpent", name a kind of dragon in Russian tales and epic songs, at times a human-like figure with dragonish traits. The best known are Gorynych and Tugarin, foes of the bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich and Alyosha Popovich. Though the word means serpent, across Russia zmei used of dragons always implies the flying kind.

long_description.id: Zmey Gorynych adalah naga cerita rakyat Rusia yang menculik perempuan. Ia biasanya tinggal di pegunungan, sering dekat sungai api, dan menjaga Jembatan Kalinov menuju alam orang mati. Kepala yang banyak adalah ciri tetapnya, biasanya kelipatan tiga seperti 3, 6, 9, atau 12; ia paling sering berkepala tiga, dan umumnya dapat terbang walau sayapnya jarang disebut.
long_description.en: Zmey Gorynych is a dragon of Russian folklore who carries off women. He usually lives in the mountains, often by a fiery river, and guards the Kalinov Bridge to the land of the dead. Many heads are his constant feature, usually a multiple of three such as 3, 6, 9 or 12; he is most often three-headed, and generally flies though his wings are seldom mentioned.

short_description.id: Bannik adalah roh rumah mandi uap (banya) dalam mitologi Slavia, biasanya digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua kecil berjanggut panjang yang bisa meramalkan masa depan.
short_description.en: The bannik is the spirit of the bathhouse (banya) in Slavic mythology, usually pictured as a small old man with a long beard who can foretell the future.

long_description.id: Bannik adalah roh rumah mandi uap atau banya dalam mitologi Slavia, terutama di Rusia dan Ukraina. Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua kecil tanpa pakaian, berjanggut panjang, dengan tubuh tertutup daun birch dari sapu mandi. Menurut sumber lain, ia tinggal di belakang atau di bawah tungku, biasanya tak kasatmata, dan kadang tampil sebagai lelaki tua yang kotor berambut panjang dengan tangan besar.
long_description.en: The bannik is the spirit of the steam bathhouse, or banya, in Slavic mythology, especially in Russia and Ukraine. He is usually pictured as a small, unclothed old man with a long beard, his body covered in birch leaves from bath brooms. Another source says he lives behind or under the stove, is normally invisible and sometimes looks like a dirty old man with long hair and big hands.

long_description.id: Banyak kisah menyebut bannik pandai berubah wujud: ia bisa tampil sebagai warga setempat, sebagai batu atau arang di tungku, atau sebagai kucing, anjing, kelinci, dan katak. Karena banya dianggap tempat gelap yang berpotensi berbahaya, bannik dipandang sebagai makhluk usil yang kadang mencelakai. Bila diganggu saat mandi, ia bisa menyiram penyusup dengan air mendidih atau bahkan mencekiknya.
long_description.en: Many accounts say the bannik is a shapeshifter, appearing as a local person, as a stone or coal in the stove, or as a cat, dog, hare or frog. Because the banya was seen as a dark, potentially dangerous place, the bannik was viewed as a mischievous and sometimes harmful being. If disturbed while bathing, he might scald an intruder with boiling water or even strangle him.

long_description.id: Giliran pemanasan ketiga atau keempat disediakan bagi bannik, yang suka mengundang setan dan roh hutan untuk mandi bersamanya, sehingga gambar Kristen tidak boleh dipasang. Orang meninggalkan sesaji berupa ranting cemara, air, dan sabun sambil mengucapkan terima kasih. Saat banya dibangun kembali, seekor ayam hitam dikubur di bawah ambangnya untuk menenangkan bannik. Ibu dan bayi yang baru lahir dijaga ketat karena bannik dipercaya mencoba menculik anak yang belum dibaptis, padahal ia baru benar-benar puas bila ada anak lahir di wilayahnya.
long_description.en: The third or fourth firing was set aside for the bannik, who liked to invite demons and forest spirits to bathe with him, so no Christian images were allowed. People left offerings of fir branches, water and soap along with spoken thanks. When a banya was rebuilt, a black hen was buried beneath its threshold to calm him. Mothers and newborns were closely guarded, since he was believed to try to carry off unbaptized children, yet he was only truly content once a child had been born in his domain.

long_description.id: Bannik juga dipercaya mampu meramalkan masa depan. Orang yang ingin bertanya berdiri dengan punggung terbuka di pintu banya yang setengah terbuka: belaian lembut berarti pertanda baik, sedangkan cakaran berarti kemalangan akan datang.
long_description.en: The bannik was also believed able to foretell the future. A person seeking an answer stood with bare back in the half-open bathhouse door: a gentle stroke meant good fortune, while a scratch of his claws meant trouble ahead.

short_description.id: Dormarch adalah anjing pemburu dalam mitologi Welsh, milik Gwynn ap Nudd dan tergolong Cŵn Annwn, kawanan anjing yang membantu mengumpulkan arwah prajurit yang gugur.
short_description.en: Dormarch is a hound of Welsh mythology belonging to Gwynn ap Nudd and counted among the Cŵn Annwn, the hounds that help gather the souls of fallen warriors.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Welsh, Dormarch (mungkin juga Dormarth) adalah seekor anjing pemburu. Tuannya adalah Gwynn ap Nudd, walaupun sebelumnya anjing ini dimiliki Maelgwn Gwynedd, raja Gwynedd pada abad ke-6. Gwynn ap Nudd dikenal sebagai raja Tylwyth Teg, bangsa peri, dan penguasa Annwn.
long_description.en: In Welsh mythology Dormarch (possibly also Dormarth) is a hound. Its master is Gwynn ap Nudd, although it was formerly owned by Maelgwn Gwynedd, a 6th-century king of Gwynedd. Gwynn ap Nudd is known as king of the Tylwyth Teg, the fairy folk, and ruler of Annwn.

long_description.id: Dormarch muncul dalam dialog antara Gwyn ap Nudd dan Gwyddno Garanhir yang tersimpan dalam Black Book of Carmarthen. Di sana Gwyn menggambarkan perannya dalam Wild Hunt, mengumpulkan arwah prajurit Britania yang gugur dengan bantuan anjing-anjingnya, sehingga Dormarch tergolong Cŵn Annwn atau 'Anjing-Anjing Annwn'. Dalam terjemahan Skene, Gwyn memuji anjingnya sebagai yang tampan, bertubuh bulat, dan terbaik, dahulu milik Maelgwn, serta menyebutnya berhidung kemerahan.
long_description.en: Dormarch appears in the dialogue between Gwyn ap Nudd and Gwyddno Garanhir preserved in the Black Book of Carmarthen. There Gwyn describes his role in the Wild Hunt, gathering the souls of fallen British warriors with his hounds, which makes Dormarch one of the Cŵn Annwn, the 'Hounds of Annwn'. In Skene's translation Gwyn praises the dog as handsome, round-bodied and the best of dogs, once Maelgwn's, and calls it the one with the ruddy nose.

long_description.id: Wujud Dormarch tidak lazim untuk seekor anjing: berkepala satu dan berkaki depan dua, sedangkan tubuhnya cepat menyempit dari dada dan berakhir pada tiga ekor mirip ekor ikan. Evans membandingkannya dengan Cerberus yang berkepala tiga dan berekor ular, dan melukiskan ekornya bercabang dengan ujung seperti kipas. Tempat hidupnya disebut 'ar wybir', yaitu menunggang awan yang menyelimuti puncak gunung.
long_description.en: Dormarch's form is unusual for a dog: it has one head and two front legs, while its body narrows quickly from the chest and ends in three fish-like tails. Evans compares it with the three-headed, serpent-tailed Cerberus and describes its tail as forked with fan-like ends. Its dwelling is called 'ar wybir', riding on the clouds that haunt the mountain peaks.

long_description.id: Gambar Dormarch terdapat di halaman 97 edisi Black Book of Carmarthen karya Evans, dalam bentuk yang dikristenkan: ciri anjingnya dikurangi dan mengambil pengaruh paus dari kisah Alkitab, terutama kisah Yunus. Bentuk dan arti namanya tidak pasti, karena penyalin menulis Dormarch dua kali tetapi huruf r-nya kemudian dihapus.
long_description.en: Evans' edition of the Black Book of Carmarthen carries a drawing of Dormarch on page 97. There the hound appears Christianised: less dog-like, and shaped instead by the whales of Biblical stories, above all Jonah's. The form and meaning of its name are uncertain, because the scribe wrote Dormarch twice but the r was later erased.

short_description.id: Finfolk adalah ras penyihir dan pengubah wujud dari laut dalam cerita rakyat Orkney, yang menculik manusia dekat pantai untuk dijadikan pasangan.
short_description.en: The Finfolk are a race of sorcerous shapeshifters of the sea in Orkney folklore, who abduct humans near the shore to serve as spouses.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Orkney, Finfolk adalah pengubah wujud penyihir dari laut, ras gelap dan misterius yang berasal dari Finfolkaheem. Sumber kedua menyebut mereka khas bagi Orkney dan Shetland dan menggambarkan mereka sebagai bangsa laut amfibi yang bisa keluar dari air ke darat sesuka hati.
long_description.en: In Orkney folklore the Finfolk are sorcerous shapeshifters of the sea, a dark and mysterious race from Finfolkaheem. The second source calls them unique to Orkney and Shetland and describes an amphibious sea people who can step from the water onto land at will.

long_description.id: Finman digambarkan punya banyak kekuatan gaib, misalnya mendayung antara Norwegia dan Orkney dalam tujuh kayuhan, membuat kapalnya tak terlihat, dan menciptakan armada perahu hantu. Finwife memulai hidup sebagai putri duyung cantik yang bertekad mendapatkan suami manusia, dan anak perempuan Fin dikatakan lahir dengan ekor ikan yang terbelah menjadi kaki saat dewasa.
long_description.en: The Finman is credited with numerous magical abilities: crossing between Norway and Orkney in only seven strokes of the oar, hiding his boat from sight, and conjuring ghostly fleets. The Finwife begins life as a beautiful mermaid bent on acquiring a human husband, and daughters are said to be born with a fish tail that splits into legs at maturity.

long_description.id: Nelayan yang lengah dan anak muda yang bermain dekat pantai direnggut Finfolk dan dipaksa menikah seumur hidup. Mereka dikatakan memiliki dua tempat tinggal: Finfolkaheem di bawah laut tempat mereka tinggal pada musim dingin, dan pulau Hildaland.
long_description.en: Fishermen off guard and young people at play near the shore are snatched by the Finfolk and forced into a lifelong marriage. They were said to have two homes: Finfolkaheem under the sea, where they lived in winter, and the island of Hildaland.

long_description.id: Kelemahan mereka antara lain perak dan tanda salib: menurut legenda koin perak yang dilempar menjauh dapat membantu orang lolos dari penculikan, dan Finman kadang dapat dihalau dengan salib yang digambar di dasar perahu memakai kapur atau ter.
long_description.en: Their weaknesses include silver and the cross: according to legend, silver coins tossed away can help a person escape abduction, and the Finman may sometimes be deterred by a cross drawn on the bottom of a boat with chalk or tar.

description.id: Fin Folk dikenal sebagai penyihir ampuh yang dapat mengendalikan cuaca, memberi laut tenang atau badai.
description.en: Fin Folk are known as powerful sorcerers who can control the weather, giving calm seas or storms.

description.en: Finfolk are weak for silver; tossing silver coins away can help a victim escape abduction.

description.en: A paradisiacal island said to be invisible, hidden just underwater, or surrounded by magical fog.

statement.en: Besides their lust for humans, Finfolk have a weakness for silver; according to legend, a way to escape abduction is to toss silver coins away from oneself.

claims.quote: One mythological race of beings which embodies all of the influences discussed above is the Fin Folk, who are unique to Orkney and Shetland.

statement.id: Fin Folk disebut sebagai ras mitologis yang khas bagi Orkney dan Shetland.
statement.en: The Fin Folk are described as a mythological race unique to Orkney and Shetland.

claims.quote: their race is that of an amphibious sea people who can step out of the water onto land as they choose, and live comfortably between the two worlds. They are both threatening and benevolent.

statement.id: Fin Folk adalah bangsa laut amfibi yang dapat keluar dari air ke darat sesuka hati, dan digambarkan sekaligus mengancam dan baik hati.
statement.en: The Fin Folk are an amphibious sea people who can step from the water onto land at will, and are described as both threatening and benevolent.

claims.quote: Known as powerful sorcerers, Fin Folk can control the weather. They may reward fishermen with pleasant sea waters, or punish them with treacherous storms.

statement.id: Dikenal sebagai penyihir ampuh, Fin Folk dapat mengendalikan cuaca; mereka bisa memberi nelayan laut yang tenang atau menghukum dengan badai berbahaya.
statement.en: Known as powerful sorcerers, Fin Folk can control the weather; they may reward fishermen with pleasant seas or punish them with treacherous storms.

claims.quote: But never silver, for Fin Folk value silver greatly and are loathe parting with it.

statement.id: Fin Folk sangat menghargai perak dan enggan melepaskannya.
statement.en: Fin Folk value silver greatly and are loath to part with it.

claims.quote: Female Fin children, however, are born with the fish tail of a mermaid, which they wear until they reach maturity when their tail will split into legs.

statement.id: Anak perempuan Fin lahir dengan ekor ikan putri duyung, yang mereka pakai sampai dewasa ketika ekor itu terbelah menjadi kaki.
statement.en: Female Fin children are born with the fish tail of a mermaid, which they wear until maturity when the tail splits into legs.

topic.en: The Fin Folk's disposition toward humans

summary.en: The first article portrays them as abductors of humans.

summary.id: Artikel kedua menyebut mereka sekaligus mengancam dan baik hati, dan dapat memberi atau menghukum nelayan lewat cuaca.

short_description.id: Lutin adalah makhluk kecil jenaka sejenis hobgoblin dalam cerita rakyat Prancis, yang perannya mirip roh rumah tangga dan kepercayaannya juga menyebar ke Quebec.
short_description.en: The lutin is a small, mischievous hobgoblin of French folklore, similar to a household spirit, whose belief also spread to Quebec.

long_description.id: Lutin adalah sejenis hobgoblin jenaka dalam cerita rakyat dan dongeng Prancis: makhluk kecil mirip manusia yang aktif di malam hari, terutama dikenal di Berry, Normandia, dan Picardie. Di Normandia perannya mirip roh rumah tangga di Inggris, Jerman, dan Skandinavia, sedangkan Ardennes dan Wallonia mengenal roh serupa bernama nuton.
long_description.en: The lutin is a mischievous hobgoblin of French folklore and fairy tales: a small nocturnal humanoid known especially in Berry, Normandy and Picardy. In Normandy it plays a role like the household spirits of England, Germany and Scandinavia, while the Ardennes and Wallonia know a similar spirit called the nuton.

long_description.id: Lutin kadang menjelma kuda berpelana yang disebut Le Cheval Bayard, dan suka menjalin rambut orang atau kuda hingga kusut. Dalam dongeng Le Prince Lutin karya Marie Catherine d'Aulnoy (1697), lutin dapat menjadi tak terlihat sesuka hati dan melintasi alam semesta dalam sekejap.
long_description.en: The lutin sometimes becomes a saddled horse called Le Cheval Bayard and likes to tangle the hair of people or horses. In Marie Catherine d'Aulnoy's fairy tale Le Prince Lutin (1697), the lutin can become invisible at will and cross the universe in a moment.

long_description.id: Namanya tercatat sebagai netun sekitar 1176–1181 dalam karya Chrétien de Troyes dan berasal dari Neptunus, nama dewa laut Romawi. Kepercayaan pada lutin juga menyebar ke Quebec, Kanada, tempat lutin dipercaya berwujud hewan peliharaan; kucing yang seluruhnya putih terutama dicurigai sebagai lutin.
long_description.en: The name is attested as netun around 1176–1181 in Chrétien de Troyes and comes from Neptunus, the Roman sea god's name. Belief in lutins also spread to Quebec, Canada, where they were thought to take the form of pets; completely white cats were especially suspected of being lutins.

short_description.id: Merfolk adalah makhluk legendaris berwujud setengah manusia dan setengah ikan yang hidup di perairan dalam berbagai mitologi dunia.
short_description.en: Merfolk are legendary water-dwelling beings combining human and fish-like traits attested in mythologies worldwide.

long_description.id: Merfolk, yang mencakup mermaids untuk sosok perempuan dan mermen untuk laki-laki, merupakan entitas air legendaris berwujud separuh manusia dan separuh ikan. Dalam tradisi sastra kuno di China mereka dikenal sebagai rényú atau manusia-ikan, sedangkan dalam tradisi Japanese dinamai ningyo yang tercatat sejak zaman abad pertengahan hingga Edo Period.
long_description.en: Merfolk, encompassing mermaids for females and mermen for males, are legendary aquatic entities appearing half-human and half-fish. In Chinese accounts they are known as rényú or human-fish, while in Japanese records they are called ningyo, documented from medieval times through the Edo Period.

long_description.id: Di kawasan Taga-Dagat, makhluk perairan ini dikenal dengan sebutan Bantay Tubig, dengan wujud perempuan bernama Sirena dan padanan laki-laki bernama Sireno. Cerita rakyat melukiskannya memiliki suara memikat yang dapat memikat pelaut, serta dipandang sebagai penjaga perairan.
long_description.en: Among Taga-Dagat beliefs, these aquatic beings are known as Bantay Tubig, featuring the female Sirena and male Sireno. Folklore describes them as having alluring voices and guarding aquatic realms.

who.id: Makhluk perairan bertubuh bagian atas manusia dan berekor ikan.
who.en: Aquatic beings with human upper bodies and fish tails.

origin.id: Mitos dan cerita rakyat lintas budaya di berbagai belahan dunia.
origin.en: Cross-cultural myths and folklore across various world regions.

role.id: Penghuni kedalaman air dan penjaga alam perairan.
role.en: Inhabitants of deep waters and guardians of aquatic realms.

famous_for.id: Wujud hibrida manusia-ikan serta suara nyanyian pemikat pelaut.
famous_for.en: Hybrid human-fish form and alluring voices captivating sailors.

did_you_know.id: Dalam tradisi mitolohiyang Pilipino, merfolk dikenal sebagai Bantay Tubig atau Sirena yang dipercaya menjaga wilayah perairan.
did_you_know.en: In Pilipino folklore, merfolk are called Bantay Tubig or Sirena and believed to guard bodies of water.

description.id: Sosok merfolk perempuan berwujud separuh wanita dan separuh ikan.
description.en: Female merfolk figure with upper female body and fish tail.

learning_questions.en: How did the concept of human-fish hybrid beings evolve across diverse maritime cultures around the world?

claims.quote: Merfolk, Mercreatures, Mermen or Merpeople are legendary water-dwelling, human-like beings.

statement.id: Merfolk atau Merpeople adalah makhluk mirip manusia legendaris yang mendiami perairan.
statement.en: Merfolk, Mercreatures, Mermen or Merpeople are legendary water-dwelling, human-like beings.

claims.quote: In English, female merfolk are called mermaids, although in a strict sense, mermaids are confined to beings who are half-woman and half-fish in appearance; male merfolk are called mermen.

statement.id: Merfolk perempuan disebut mermaids yang berwujud setengah wanita setengah ikan, sedangkan laki-laki disebut mermen.

short_description.id: Ravana adalah raja rakshasa Lanka yang lazim digambarkan berkepala sepuluh.
short_description.en: Ravana is the rakshasa king of Lanka traditionally depicted with ten heads.

long_description.id: Ravana adalah raja rakshasa Lanka yang lazim digambarkan berkepala sepuluh. Ia disebut putra Vishrava dan Kaikasi.
long_description.en: Ravana is the rakshasa king of Lanka traditionally depicted with ten heads. He is described as the son of Vishrava and Kaikasi.

long_description.id: Ia menculik Sita dan menahannya di Ashoka Vatika. Rama melawannya dengan dukungan Sugriva dan pasukan vanara lalu membunuhnya. Kekalahannya diperingati dengan pembakaran patung Ravana pada Dussehra. Ravana dipandang sebagai pemuja Shiva. Ia juga hadir dalam Lankavatara Sutra, Jataka Buddha, dan Ramayana Jain. Nama Ravana diterangkan berarti mengaum. Gelar Dashanana berarti yang berkepala sepuluh. Nama lainnya mencakup Lankapati dan Lankeshwara. Brahma memberinya anugerah kebal terhadap ciptaannya kecuali manusia dalam cerita. Anugerah Brahma juga mencakup senjata, kereta, dan kemampuan berganti wujud. Mandodari, putri Maya, disebut sebagai ratu utamanya. Mackenzie menggambarkan Rama sebagai pembunuh Ravana yang menindas manusia dalam Ramayana. Adegan koleksi Museum Carlos menggambarkan Ravana membawa Sita dari pertapaannya di hutan.
long_description.en: He abducts Sita and holds her in Ashoka Vatika. Rama fights him with Sugriva and the vanara army's support and kills him. His defeat is commemorated by burning Ravana effigies at Dussehra. Ravana is regarded as a devotee of Shiva. He also appears in the Lankavatara Sutra, Buddhist Jatakas, and Jain Ramayanas. The name Ravana is explained as meaning roaring. The epithet Dashanana means the one with ten heads. His other names include Lankapati and Lankeshwara. Brahma grants him immunity against his creations except humans in the story. Brahma's gifts also include weapons, a chariot, and shapeshifting. Mandodari, Maya's daughter, is described as his chief queen. Mackenzie describes Rama as the slayer of Ravana who oppresses humans in the Ramayana. The Carlos Museum collection scene depicts Ravana carrying Sita from her forest hermitage.

cultural_context.en: His defeat is commemorated at Dussehra.

short_description.id: Sirin adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, berkepala perempuan cantik dan bertubuh burung, yang nyanyiannya bisa membuat orang melupakan segalanya.
short_description.en: The Sirin is a legendary creature of Russian folklore with a beautiful woman's head and a bird's body, whose song can make people forget everything.

long_description.id: Sirin adalah makhluk legenda dari cerita rakyat Rusia. Ia berkepala perempuan cantik dan bertubuh burung, biasanya burung hantu, dan sering disamakan dengan siren dalam mitologi Yunani. Menurut mitos, Sirin tinggal di Iriy atau di sekitar Sungai Efrat. Satu sumber menyebut legendanya mungkin berasal dari Persia.
long_description.en: The Sirin is a legendary creature of Russian folklore. She is pictured as a bird, usually an owl, bearing a lovely woman's head, and is often equated with the sirens of Greek mythology. Myth places her home in Iriy or near the Euphrates River. One source suggests her legend may be of Persian origin.

long_description.id: Berbeda dari siren yang memikat pelaut menuju maut, Sirin memakai suaranya untuk mengganjar orang saleh. Ia menyanyikan lagu indah bagi para santo dan meramalkan kebahagiaan yang akan datang. Namun bagi manusia biasa ia berbahaya: laki-laki yang mendengarnya melupakan segala hal duniawi, mengikutinya, dan akhirnya mati. Orang berusaha mengusirnya dengan tembakan meriam, dentang lonceng, dan bunyi keras lainnya.
long_description.en: Unlike the sirens who lure sailors to death, the Sirin uses her voice to reward the virtuous. She sang lovely songs to the saints, foretelling joys to come. To ordinary mortals, however, she was dangerous: men who heard her forgot everything earthly, followed her and finally died. People tried to drive her off with cannon fire, ringing bells and other loud noises.

long_description.id: Sumber berbeda pendapat tentang sifatnya. Satu sumber menyebut Sirin burung kebahagiaan dan Alkonost burung kesedihan, sedangkan sumber lain justru menyebut Sirin burung duka yang cenderung berniat buruk kepada manusia, sementara Alkonost adalah burung kebahagiaan. Pada abad ke-17 hingga ke-18, citranya berubah menjadi lambang keselarasan dunia, dan orang percaya hanya orang bahagia yang dapat mendengarnya.
long_description.en: Sources disagree about her nature. One calls the Sirin the bird of happiness and the Alkonost the bird of sorrow, while another makes the Sirin the bird of grief, rather ill-disposed to humans, and the Alkonost the bird of happiness. In the 17th–18th centuries her image shifted to a symbol of world harmony, and people believed only the happy could hear her.

long_description.id: Sirin kadang dipandang sebagai kiasan firman Tuhan yang masuk ke jiwa manusia, kadang sebagai kiasan bidah yang menggoda orang lemah. Dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, Sirin dicampuradukkan dengan penulis religius Ephrem the Syrian, sehingga penyair petani memakai nama Sirin sebagai sinonim untuk penyair. Bersama Alkonost dan Gamayun, ia termasuk burung peramal dalam cerita rakyat Rusia. Pengarang Vladimir Nabokov pun pernah memakai Sirin sebagai nama samaran.
long_description.en: The Sirin is sometimes read as a metaphor for God's word entering a person's soul, and sometimes for heretics tempting the weak. In Russian folklore she became mixed up with the religious writer Ephrem the Syrian, so peasant poets used Sirin as another word for poet. With the Alkonost and Gamayun she is one of the prophetic birds of Russian folklore. The author Vladimir Nabokov even wrote under the pen name Sirin.

short_description.id: Strzyga biasanya adalah iblis perempuan mirip vampir dalam mitologi Slavia, terutama dalam cerita rakyat Polandia dan Silesia, yang berasal dari Strix Romawi dan Yunani kuno.
short_description.en: The strzyga is usually a female vampire-like demon of Slavic mythology, chiefly in Polish and Silesian folklore, stemming from the Strix of ancient Rome and Greece.

long_description.id: Strzyga (jamak strzygi, laki-laki strzygoń) biasanya iblis perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia yang berasal dari Strix dalam mitologi Romawi dan Yunani kuno. Ia mirip vampir dan terutama ditemukan dalam cerita rakyat Polandia dan Silesia. Menurut Aleksander Brückner, kata ini berasal dari strix, burung hantu dalam bahasa Latin, makhluk mirip burung yang memakan daging dan darah manusia.
long_description.en: The strzyga (plural strzygi, male strzygoń) is usually a female demon of Slavic myth derived from the Strix of Roman and Greek antiquity. Vampire-like, she belongs mostly to Polish and Silesian folklore. Aleksander Brückner traced the word to strix, Latin for an owl, a bird-like being that fed on human flesh and blood.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan Silesia, strzyga lahir sebagai strzyga: semasa hidup ia punya dua hati, dua jiwa, dan dua baris gigi. Setelah ia mati, satu jiwa meninggalkan tubuh, sementara jiwa lain tetap hidup di dalam jasad di peti. Agar ia tidak mencelakai orang, makamnya digali dan jantungnya ditusuk pasak kayu ek, atau kepalanya dipenggal; orang yang dicurigai akan menjadi strzyga dikuburkan telungkup dengan batu di bawah bibirnya. Strzyga kadang juga digambarkan sebagai burung hantu yang tinggal di hutan gelap.
long_description.en: Silesian belief held that a strzyga is born one: in life she has two hearts, two souls and two rows of teeth. When she dies one soul leaves while the other lives on in the body in the coffin. To stop her harming people, the grave was opened and her heart pierced with an oak stake, or her head cut off; someone suspected of becoming a strzyga was buried face down with a stone under the lips. Strzygi were also sometimes pictured as owls living in dark forests.

long_description.id: Strzyga tetap populer dalam cerita rakyat pedesaan Polandia hingga akhir abad ke-19 dan awal abad ke-20, seperti tampak dalam novel Chłopi karya Władysław Reymont. Setelah abad ke-18 dibedakan antara strzyga, yang lebih terkait dengan sihir, dan upiór, makhluk vampir yang terbang.
long_description.en: The strzyga stayed popular in rural Polish folklore into the late 19th and early 20th century, as Władysław Reymont's novel Chłopi shows. After the 18th century a line was drawn between the strzyga, tied more to witchcraft, and the upiór, a flying vampire.

short_description.id: Vanapagan atau Vanatühi adalah iblis raksasa dalam cerita rakyat Estonia, seorang petani yang lebih bodoh daripada jahat dan selalu diakali pelayannya, Kaval Ants.
short_description.en: Vanapagan or Vanatühi is the giant devil of Estonian folklore, a farmer more stupid than wicked who is always outwitted by his servant Kaval Ants.

long_description.id: Vanapagan atau Vanatühi adalah iblis atau dewa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Estonia, digambarkan sebagai petani raksasa yang lebih bodoh daripada jahat dengan ciri setan Kristen. Dalam dongeng "raksasa bodoh" ia selalu diakali pelayannya Kaval Ants; ia juga mencuri alat musik dewa petir Pikne dan menjadi musuh terbesar raksasa Suur Tõll dari Saaremaa. Topinya dari kuku membuatnya tak terlihat.
long_description.en: Vanapagan or Vanatühi is a devil or underworld god of Estonian mythology, pictured as a giant farmer more stupid than wicked with traits of the Christian Satan. In the 'stupid ogre' tales he is always outwitted by his servant Kaval Ants; he also steals the thunder god Pikne's instrument and is the worst enemy of the giant Suur Tõll of Saaremaa. His hat of fingernails makes him invisible.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah lain banyak vanapaganad tinggal di rawa, hutan, dan gua dan mengunjungi desa saat pesta. Vanapagan juga membentuk gunung dan danau dan memindahkan batu besar, tetapi kota dan jembatan yang ia bangun selalu tak selesai; ia takut pada serigala dan badai petir. Matthias Johann Eisen mempopulerkannya kembali.
long_description.en: In other tales many vanapaganad live in bogs, woods and caves and visit villages at feasts. Vanapagan also shapes mountains and lakes and moves great stones, but the towns and bridges he builds are never finished; he fears wolves and thunderstorms. Matthias Johann Eisen repopularised him.

short_description.id: Vodyanoy adalah roh air dalam mitologi Slavia, biasanya lelaki tua berjanggut hijau yang bisa menenggelamkan orang, tetapi juga dapat memberi tangkapan ikan berlimpah.
short_description.en: The vodyanoy is a water spirit of Slavic mythology, usually an old man with a green beard who may drown people but can also grant rich catches of fish.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, vodyanoy (secara harfiah "yang dari air") adalah roh air. Dalam dongeng Ceko dan Slowakia ia disebut vodník, dan dalam dongeng Ukraina vodyanyk; di Rusia ia kadang dijuluki dedushka vodyanoy, "Kakek Air". Ia dikatakan tinggal di lubuk atau pusaran sungai, kolam, atau danau, dan terutama suka hidup di dekat kincir air.
long_description.en: In Slavic mythology the vodyanoy (literally "he from the water") is a water spirit. Czech and Slovak fairy tales call him vodník, Ukrainian ones vodyanyk; in Russia he is sometimes called dedushka vodyanoy, "Water-Grandfather". He is said to live in a deep pool or whirlpool of a river, pond or lake, and to favour spots near a watermill.

long_description.id: Rupanya digambarkan berbeda-beda: lelaki telanjang berperut buncit dan berkepala botak bertopi dan bersabuk alang-alang, lelaki tua berambut dan berjanggut hijau, atau katak yang menyerupai manusia; perbedaan ini dijelaskan oleh kemampuannya berubah wujud. Janggut hijaunya memutih saat bulan menyusut, karena ia yang abadi menua atau menjadi muda lagi mengikuti fase bulan. Ia dapat muncul sebagai ikan raksasa berlumut, sebatang kayu, bahkan batang pohon bersayap kecil yang terbang di atas air.
long_description.en: Accounts of his looks differ: a naked, pot-bellied, bald man with a hat and belt of reeds, an old man with green hair and beard, or a man-like frog; the variety is put down to his shapeshifting. His green beard whitens as the moon wanes, since the immortal vodyanoy ages or grows young with the moon's phases. He may appear as a huge mossy fish, a log, or even a small-winged flying tree trunk skimming the water.

long_description.id: Saat marah ia menjebol bendungan, menghanyutkan kincir air, dan menenggelamkan manusia serta hewan, sehingga nelayan, penggiling, dan peternak lebah memberinya persembahan; kadang ia menyeret orang ke rumahnya di bawah air untuk dijadikan budak. Ketika kincir air dibangun, harus dikorbankan babi, sapi, domba, bahkan manusia atau ayam untuk menenangkannya. Sebaliknya, nelayan bisa mendapat tangkapan berlimpah darinya, misalnya setelah mengembalikan seorang anak yang tak sengaja terjaring.
long_description.en: When angry he breaks dams, washes away mills and drowns people and animals, so fishermen, millers and bee-keepers offer him sacrifices; at times he drags people to his underwater home as slaves. When a watermill was built, a pig, cattle, a sheep, even a human or a chicken had to be sacrificed to calm him. Fishermen, on the other hand, could receive bountiful catches from him, for instance after returning a child caught by accident in their nets.

long_description.id: Vodyanoy menguasai semua ikan dan makhluk air, dan ia memilih ikan lele besar sebagai tunggangan. Ia mengambil istri dari peri air atau gadis-gadis malang yang tenggelam, termasuk rusalka menurut Afanasyev. Ada pula penguasa para vodyanoy, Tsar Vodyanik, lelaki tua bersenjata gada yang bisa naik ke langit di atas awan hitam dan menciptakan sungai serta danau baru.
long_description.en: The vodyanoy owns all fish and water creatures and chooses the wels catfish as his mount. He takes wives from water-nymphs or drowned, unhappy girls, including the rusalka according to Afanasyev. The vodyanoys also have a ruler, the Tsar Vodyanik, an old man with a club who can rise to the sky on a black cloud and create new rivers and lakes.

claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, vodyanoy (Russian: водяной , IPA ... lit. '[he] from the water' or 'watery') is a water spirit. In Czech and Slovak fairy tales, he is called vodník (or in Germanized form: Hastrman ), and often referred to as Wassermann in German sources. In Ukrainian fairy tales, he is called “водяник“ (vodyanyk).

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, vodyanoy (водяной, harfiah "yang dari air" atau "berair") adalah roh air; dalam dongeng Ceko dan Slowakia ia disebut vodník (Hastrman), dan dalam dongeng Ukraina vodyanyk.
statement.en: In Slavic mythology the vodyanoy (водяной, literally "he from the water" or "watery") is a water spirit; Czech and Slovak tales call him vodník (Hastrman), Ukrainian tales vodyanyk.

claims.quote: He may appear to be a naked man with a pot belly (and bald-headed) wearing a hat and belt of reeds and rushes, conflicting with other accounts ascribing him green hair and a long green beard, while many depictions restore him as an anthropormophic frog. statement.en: He may appear as a naked, pot-bellied, bald man with a hat and belt of reeds, while other accounts give him green hair and a long green beard and many depictions show him as a man-like frog; the variety is attributed to his shape-shifting.

short_description.id: Water horse (kuda air) adalah makhluk mitos yang muncul dalam berbagai bentuk dalam cerita rakyat Kelt dan Nordik, seperti kelpie, each-uisge, dan bäckahästen.
short_description.en: The water horse is a mythical creature found in many forms in Celtic and Nordic folklore, such as the kelpie, each-uisge and bäckahästen.

long_description.id: Water horse (juga waterhorse) adalah makhluk mitos yang muncul dalam berbagai bentuk dalam cerita rakyat Kelt (Celtic) dan Nordik (Nordic). Wujud dalam tradisi Kelt antara lain Ceffyl Dŵr dari Wales (Welsh), each uisce dari Irlandia (Irish), serta each-uisge dan kelpie dari Skotlandia (Scottish). Dalam cerita rakyat Nordik, kuda air adalah wujud yang diambil nixie, yang dalam bahasa Swedia (Swedish) disebut bäckahästen ("kuda sungai kecil") dan dalam bahasa Faroe (Faroese) nykur.
long_description.en: The water horse (also waterhorse) is a mythical being appearing in many guises in Celtic and Nordic folklore. Celtic forms include the Welsh Ceffyl Dŵr, the Irish each uisce, and the Scottish each-uisge and kelpie. In Nordic lore the water horse is a shape the nixie takes, called bäckahästen ('the brook horse') in Swedish and nykur in Faroese.

long_description.id: Istilah "water horse" mulanya nama bagi kelpie, dan juga dipakai sebagai julukan monster danau seperti Ogopogo dan Nessie. Penggunaan "water horse" dan "kelpie" sering membingungkan: sebagian menganggapnya sinonim, sementara yang lain membedakan kuda air sebagai penghuni danau (loch) dan kelpie sebagai penghuni air deras seperti sungai, arungan, dan air terjun. Menurut artikel de, kuda air dikenal dari berbagai budaya dan zaman, termasuk Denmark, Yunani, Irlandia, dan Portugal, dan gagasan roh sungai berwujud kuda mungkin berasal dari kurban kuda di perairan.
long_description.en: 'Water horse' was first a name for the kelpie and has also served as a nickname for lake monsters such as Ogopogo and Nessie. The terms 'water horse' and 'kelpie' are easily confused: some treat them as the same, while others make the water horse a dweller of lochs and the kelpie a creature of rough water such as rivers, fords and waterfalls. According to the de article water horses are known from many cultures and eras, including Denmark, Greece, Ireland and Portugal, and the idea of horse-shaped river spirits may go back to sacrificing horses in water.

short_description.id: Naga putih (Y Ddraig Wen) adalah lambang dalam mitologi Wales yang dikaitkan dengan bangsa Anglo-Saxon, musuh naga merah bangsa Briton.
short_description.en: The white dragon (Y Ddraig Wen) is a symbol of Welsh myth associated with the Anglo-Saxons, foe of the red dragon of the Britons.

long_description.id: Naga putih (Wales/Welsh: Y Ddraig Wen) adalah lambang dalam mitologi Wales yang dikaitkan dengan bangsa Anglo-Saxon. Penggunaan tertuanya sebagai lambang Anglo-Saxon terdapat dalam Historia Brittonum: di Dinas Emrys, raja Briton Vortigern mencoba membangun benteng, tetapi setiap malam temboknya runtuh. Seorang anak tanpa ayah memberi tahu raja tentang dua naga di bawah bukit; setelah digali, keduanya bertarung dan naga merah akhirnya mengalahkan naga putih. Anak itu menjelaskan bahwa naga putih melambangkan bangsa Saxon dan naga merah bangsa Briton (Celtic Britons).
long_description.en: The white dragon (Welsh Y Ddraig Wen) is a symbol in Welsh myth tied to the Anglo-Saxons. Its earliest use as their emblem is in the Historia Brittonum: at Dinas Emrys the British king Vortigern tries to build a fort, but every night its walls fall down. A fatherless boy tells the king of two dragons under the hill; once dug up they fight, and the red dragon finally defeats the white. The boy explains that the white dragon stands for the Saxons and the red for the Celtic Britons.

long_description.id: Kisah ini diulang dalam History of the Kings of Britain karya Geoffrey of Monmouth (sekitar 1136), yang menjadikan anak itu Merlin muda; Historia Brittonum dan karya Geoffrey adalah satu-satunya teks abad pertengahan yang memakai naga putih sebagai lambang bangsa Inggris. Kisah serupa naga putih dan merah juga ada dalam Lludd and Llefelys, tanpa makna Briton atau Saxon. Dalam terjemahan Giles atas Geoffrey (Old English Chronicles, Gutenberg), Merlin bernubuat: "celakalah naga merah", karena sarangnya akan direbut naga putih, "yang melambangkan bangsa Saxon".
long_description.en: The story is retold in Geoffrey of Monmouth's History of the Kings of Britain (c. 1136), where the boy becomes the young Merlin; the Historia Brittonum and Geoffrey are the only medieval texts using the white dragon as a symbol of the English. A similar tale of white and red dragons appears in Lludd and Llefelys, without the Briton or Saxon meaning. In Giles's translation of Geoffrey (Old English Chronicles, Gutenberg), Merlin prophesies 'woe to the red dragon', whose lairs the white dragon, 'which signifies the Saxons', will seize.

claims.quote: The white dragon (Welsh: Y Ddraig Wen ) is a symbol associated in Welsh mythology with the Anglo-Saxons. Origin of tradition [edit] The earliest usage of the white dragon as a symbol of the Anglo-Saxons is found in the Historia Brittonum.

statement.id: Naga putih (Wales/Welsh: Y Ddraig Wen) lambang mitologi Wales untuk Anglo-Saxon; tertua dalam Historia Brittonum; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: The white dragon (Welsh Y Ddraig Wen) is a Welsh symbol of the Anglo-Saxons; earliest in the Historia Brittonum.

claims.quote: The boy tells the king of the two dragons. Vortigern excavates the hill, freeing the dragons. They continue their fight and the red dragon finally defeats the white dragon. The boy tells Vortigern that the white dragon symbolises the Saxons and that the red dragon symbolises the Celtic Britons.

statement.id: Di Dinas Emrys, Vortigern (raja Briton, Britons) menggali bukit; naga merah (Welsh dragon) mengalahkan naga putih; putih = Saxon (Saxons), merah = Briton (Celtic Britons).
statement.en: At Dinas Emrys Vortigern digs up the hill; the red dragon defeats the white; white = Saxons, red = Celtic Britons.

claims.quote: The story is repeated in Geoffrey of Monmouth's fictional History of the Kings of Britain (c. 1136). In this telling the boy is identified as the young Merlin. The Historia Brittonum and History of the Kings of Britain are the only medieval texts to use the white dragon as a symbol of the English.

statement.id: Diulang Geoffrey of Monmouth (History of the Kings of Britain, sekitar 1136), anak itu Merlin; satu-satunya teks abad pertengahan, lambang bangsa Inggris (English).
statement.en: Retold by Geoffrey of Monmouth (History of the Kings of Britain, c. 1136) with the boy as Merlin; the only medieval texts using it for the English.

claims.quote: A similar story of white and red dragons fighting is found in the medieval romance Lludd and Llefelys, although in this case the dragons are not used to symbolize Britons or Saxons.

statement.id: Kisah serupa dalam Lludd and Llefelys, tanpa makna Briton (Britons) atau Saxon (Saxons).
statement.en: A similar story in Lludd and Llefelys, without Briton or Saxon meaning.

claims.quote: the two serpents are two dragons; the red serpent is your dragon, but the white serpent is the dragon of the people who occupy several provinces and districts of Britain, even almost from sea to sea

statement.id: Terjemahan Giles atas Nennius: ular putih naga bangsa yang menduduki Britania (Britain); ular merah naga raja.
statement.en: Giles's translation of Nennius: the white serpent is the dragon of the people occupying Britain; the red is the king's.

claims.quote: "Woe to the red dragon, for his banishment hasteneth on. His lurking holes shall be seized by the white dragon, which signifies the Saxons whom you invited over; but the red denotes the British nation, which shall be oppressed by the white.

statement.id: Nubuat Merlin (Old English Chronicles, Gutenberg; Giles): celakalah naga merah (Woe to the red dragon); naga putih melambangkan Saxon (Saxons).
statement.en: Merlin's prophecy (Giles): woe to the red dragon; the white dragon signifies the Saxons.

short_description.id: Zmeu adalah makhluk fantastis dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Rumania, mirip naga tetapi bersifat manusia, yang menculik gadis-gadis dan hampir selalu dikalahkan pangeran pemberani.
short_description.en: The zmeu is a fantastic creature of Romanian folklore and mythology, dragon-like yet human-like, who kidnaps young girls and is almost always defeated by a daring prince.

long_description.id: Zmeu (jamak zmei, perempuan zmeoaică) adalah makhluk fantastis dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Rumania. Walau sebagian sumber menyebutnya naga, zmeu berbeda karena biasanya jelas bersifat manusia: berkaki dan berlengan, membuat dan memakai senjata, menunggang kuda, dan ingin menikahi gadis muda. Ada pengulas yang menggolongkannya sebagai raksasa (setara ogre), iblis, bahkan vampir.
long_description.en: The zmeu (plural zmei, feminine zmeoaică) is a fantastic being of Romanian folk tales and myth. Some sources call it a dragon, yet it differs in being plainly human-like: it has arms and legs, makes and wields weapons, rides horses and wants to wed young girls. Commentators variously class it as a giant (an ogre), a devil or even a vampire.

long_description.id: Dalam beberapa cerita zmeu muncul di langit dan menyemburkan api atau dapat berubah wujud; dalam cerita lain ia punya batu permata ajaib di kepalanya yang bersinar seperti matahari. Ia menyukai gadis muda yang cantik dan menculiknya, biasanya untuk dinikahi, tetapi hampir selalu dikalahkan oleh pangeran atau kesatria pemberani. Dalam mitologi Rumania ia juga raksasa berkekuatan gaib, perwujudan kejahatan yang selalu kalah oleh kekuatan baik.
long_description.en: In some tales the zmeu appears in the sky spitting fire or can change shape; in others it bears a magic jewel on its head that shines like the sun. It loves beautiful young girls and carries them off, usually to marry them, but is almost always beaten by a bold prince or knight-errant. Romanian myth also makes it a giant with supernatural powers, the embodiment of evil, always overcome by the forces of good.

long_description.id: Kebanyakan sarjana sepakat istilah Rumania zmeu berasal dari kata Slavia zmey. Dalam bahasa Rumania kata zmeu juga berarti layang-layang.
long_description.en: Most scholars agree that the Romanian term zmeu comes from Slavic zmey. In Romanian the word zmeu also means a kite.

short_description.id: Azhdahak adalah raja-naga dalam mitologi Armenia, bentuk Armenia dari nama iblis Avesta Azhi Dahaka.
short_description.en: Azhdahak is a dragon-king of Armenian myth whose name is the Armenian version of Azhi Dahaka, a demon of the Avesta.

long_description.id: Azhdahak adalah bentuk Armenia dari nama iblis Avesta Azhi Dahaka, dan dalam mitologi Armenia ia raja-naga, manusia-vishap. Para vishap, golongan naga tempat Azhdahak berada, hidup di gunung tinggi, danau besar, langit, dan awan; ketika naik ke langit atau turun ke danau, raungan mereka menakutkan penduduk. Gerakan azhdahak di bawah tanah dipercaya menyebabkan gempa, dan vishap yang hidup sampai seribu tahun dapat menelan seluruh dunia.
long_description.en: Azhdahak takes his name from Azhi Dahaka, a demon of the Avesta, and in Armenian myth he is a dragon-king, a man-vishap. The vishaps, the class of dragons Azhdahak belongs to, live in high mountains, great lakes, the sky and clouds; when they rise to the sky or come down to lakes, their roar terrifies people. The movement of azhdahaks underground was believed to cause earthquakes, and a vishap that lives to a thousand years can swallow the whole world.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Iran ia dipenjara di Gunung Damavand dan pada akhir zaman akan lepas, lalu akhirnya dikalahkan Fereydun. Dalam Sejarah Armenia, Movses Khorenatsi menyamakan Azhdahak dengan raja Media, Astyages; dalam epos Armenia kuno Vipasank ia raja bangsa Mar (Media) yang dikalahkan raja Armenia Tigran I. Bentuk Armenia Azhdahak dipinjam dari bahasa Parthia.
long_description.en: In Iranian mythology he is imprisoned in Mount Damavand and will break out at the end of time, to be finally defeated by Fereydun. In his History of Armenia, Movses Khorenatsi identified Azhdahak with the Median king Astyages; in the ancient Armenian epic Vipasank he is king of the Mars (Medes), defeated by the Armenian king Tigran I. The Armenian form Azhdahak was borrowed from Parthian.

short_description.id: Dunnie adalah makhluk kecil sejenis Brownie dari cerita rakyat Northumberland yang gemar menyamar sebagai kuda lalu menghilang, dan sering dianggap hantu seorang perampok perbatasan.
short_description.en: The Dunnie is a small Brownie-type being of Northumberland folklore who likes to pose as a horse and then vanish, and is often thought to be the ghost of a border reiver.

long_description.id: Dunnie adalah makhluk kecil mirip Brownie dalam cerita rakyat perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia, khususnya Northumberland. Yang paling terkenal adalah Dunnie dari Hazlerigg (dalam catatan Henderson ditulis Haselrigg) di paroki Chatton. Henderson menulis bahwa seperti makhluk sejenisnya, Dunnie sangat gemar melakukan tipu daya yang jahil dan merepotkan.
long_description.en: Folklore of the Anglo-Scottish borders, Northumberland in particular, tells of the Dunnie, a little creature much like a Brownie. The best known is the Dunnie of Hazlerigg (spelled Haselrigg by Henderson) in the parish of Chatton. Henderson says that, as with the rest of its kind, the Dunnie loves playing troublesome pranks.

long_description.id: Tipuan khasnya adalah menyamar sebagai kuda. Ketika seorang petani hendak menjemput bidan, Dunnie mengambil wujud kudanya, membawa keduanya dengan selamat, lalu tiba-tiba lenyap di bagian jalan paling berlumpur. Ia juga menyamar sebagai kuda bajak: begitu dipasangi tali kekang, tali itu jatuh ke tanah dan sang kuda berlari kencang melintasi daerah itu.
long_description.en: His typical trick is posing as a horse. When a farmer sets out to fetch the midwife, the Dunnie takes the form of his horse, carries them both safely, then suddenly vanishes in the muddiest part of the road. He also poses as a plough-horse: once harnessed, the harness falls to the ground and the horse races off across the country.

long_description.id: Dunnie juga dikatakan berkeliaran di tebing Cheviots sambil mengulang-ulang sebuah bait dengan suara sedih tentang harta di Cockenheugh dan Collierheugh serta kunci yang hilang. Dari lagu itu muncul anggapan bahwa Dunnie sebenarnya hantu seorang perampok perbatasan (reiver) yang menimbun jarahannya di sana dan terus menjaganya. Seorang kawan Henderson bahkan menunjuk bagian batu paling curam di Haselrigg sebagai tempat Dunnie biasa duduk di malam hari.
long_description.en: The Dunnie was also said to wander the crags of the Cheviots, repeating in a melancholy voice a verse about treasure at Cockenheugh and Collierheugh and a lost key. From this song came the idea that the Dunnie is really the ghost of a reiver who hoarded his loot there and still guards it. A friend of Henderson's even pointed to the steepest rocks at Haselrigg as the place where the Dunnie used to sit at night.

claims.quote: A Dunnie is a small Brownie-like being in the folklore of the Anglo-Scottish borders, specifically Northumberland, the most famous being that of the Hazlerigg Dunnie of Hazlerigg in the parish of Chatton, Northumberland.

statement.id: Dunnie adalah makhluk kecil mirip Brownie dalam cerita rakyat perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish borders), khususnya Northumberland; yang paling terkenal adalah Dunnie dari Hazlerigg di paroki Chatton.
statement.en: A Dunnie is a small Brownie-like being in the folklore of the Anglo-Scottish borders, specifically Northumberland; the most famous is the Hazlerigg Dunnie of Hazlerigg in the parish of Chatton.

claims.quote: The Dunnie has been known to take the form of a horse in order to trick a rider into mounting him before disappearing and leaving them in the muddiest part of the road.

statement.id: Dunnie dikenal mengambil wujud kuda untuk memperdaya penunggang agar menaikinya, lalu menghilang dan meninggalkan mereka di bagian jalan yang paling berlumpur.
statement.en: The Dunnie has been known to take the form of a horse to trick a rider into mounting him, then disappear and leave them in the muddiest part of the road.

claims.quote: He also is said to disguise as plough-horses only to vanish when the ploughman takes him into the stalls.

statement.id: Ia juga dikatakan menyamar sebagai kuda bajak, lalu lenyap ketika pembajak membawanya ke kandang.
statement.en: He is also said to disguise himself as plough-horses, only to vanish when the ploughman takes him into the stalls.

claims.quote: The Dunnie was also said to wander the crags and dales of the Cheviots singing

statement.id: Dunnie juga dikatakan berkeliaran di tebing dan lembah Cheviots sambil bernyanyi.
statement.en: The Dunnie was also said to wander the crags and dales of the Cheviots singing.

claims.quote: Cockenheugh there's gear enough, Collierheugh there's mair, For I've lost the key o' the Bounders

statement.id: Lagunya menyebut harta (gear) di Cockenheugh dan lebih banyak lagi di Collierheugh, sementara ia kehilangan kunci 'the Bounders'.
statement.en: His song says there is gear enough at Cockenheugh and more at Collierheugh, for he has lost the key o' the Bounders.

claims.quote: The Dunnie is thus thought to be a ghost of a reiver who hoarded his loot in the fells and guards his ill-gotten gains to this day.

statement.id: Karena itu Dunnie dianggap hantu seorang perampok perbatasan (reiver) yang menimbun jarahannya di perbukitan dan menjaga harta haramnya sampai sekarang.
statement.en: The Dunnie is thus thought to be the ghost of a reiver who hoarded his loot in the fells and guards his ill-gotten gains to this day.

claims.quote: sprite is called the Dunnie ; he appears to be of the Brownie type, and is located at Haselrigg, in the parish of Chatton, in Northumberland.

statement.id: Henderson menyebut sprite ini Dunnie, tampaknya dari jenis Brownie, dan bertempat di Haselrigg, paroki Chatton, Northumberland.
statement.en: Henderson says this sprite is called the Dunnie, appears to be of the Brownie type, and is located at Haselrigg, in the parish of Chatton, in Northumberland.

claims.quote: Like others of his race, he is much addicted to mischievous, troublesome tricks

statement.id: Seperti makhluk sejenisnya, ia sangat gemar melakukan tipu daya yang jahil dan merepotkan.
statement.en: Like others of his race, he is much addicted to mischievous, troublesome tricks.

claims.quote: When the midwife is wanted in a farmer's family, and the master goes out to saddle his horse that he may fetch her, the Dunnie will take its form.

statement.id: Ketika keluarga petani membutuhkan bidan dan sang tuan keluar untuk memasang pelana kudanya, Dunnie akan mengambil wujud kuda itu.
statement.en: When a farmer's family wants the midwife and the master goes out to saddle his horse to fetch her, the Dunnie will take its form.

claims.quote: he will suddenly vanish, and leave the unhappy pair floundering in the mud.

statement.id: Dalam perjalanan pulang ia tiba-tiba menghilang dan meninggalkan petani serta bidan itu menggelepar di lumpur.
statement.en: On the way back he will suddenly vanish and leave the unhappy pair floundering in the mud.

claims.quote: see the harness come " slap to the ground," while the steed kicks up his heels and starts across the country like the wind.

statement.id: Pembajak yang mengira sudah memasang tali kekang pada kudanya akan melihat tali itu jatuh ke tanah, sementara kuda itu menendang dan berlari melintasi daerah itu secepat angin.
statement.en: A ploughman who thinks he has harnessed his horse will see the harness come 'slap to the ground' while the steed kicks up his heels and starts across the country like the wind.

claims.quote: Some years ago, the Dunnie was often seen wandering among the crags of the Cheviots, and heard repeating the following verse again and again, in a melancholy voice

statement.id: Beberapa tahun sebelumnya, Dunnie sering terlihat berkeliaran di antara tebing Cheviots dan terdengar mengulang-ulang sebuah bait dengan suara sedih.
statement.en: Some years ago the Dunnie was often seen wandering among the crags of the Cheviots and heard repeating a verse again and again in a melancholy voice.

claims.quote: Hence it has been thought that the Dunnie is really the ghost of a " reiver," who had hoarded his ill-gotten pelf in those crags, and therefore haunts them constantly.

statement.id: Karena itu Dunnie diduga sebenarnya hantu seorang 'reiver' yang menimbun harta haramnya di tebing-tebing itu dan karenanya terus menghantuinya.
statement.en: Hence it has been thought that the Dunnie is really the ghost of a 'reiver' who hoarded his ill-gotten pelf in those crags and therefore haunts them constantly.

claims.quote: a friend pointed to the steepest part of the rocks, and said it was there that Dunnie used to hang over his legs when he sat on the crags at night.

statement.id: Seorang kawan menunjuk bagian batu paling curam di sebuah tambang di Haselrigg dan berkata di situlah Dunnie biasa menjuntaikan kakinya saat duduk di tebing pada malam hari.
statement.en: A friend pointed to the steepest part of the rocks and said it was there that Dunnie used to hang his legs over when he sat on the crags at night.

claims.quote: The Dunnie, Brag, and Hedley Kow are probably the same as the Nick or Nippeu.

statement.id: Menurut catatan kaki Henderson, Dunnie, Brag, dan Hedley Kow mungkin sama dengan Nick atau Nippeu.
statement.en: According to Henderson's footnote, the Dunnie, Brag and Hedley Kow are probably the same as the Nick or Nippeu.

short_description.id: Dunnie adalah makhluk kecil sejenis Brownie dari cerita rakyat Northumberland yang gemar menyamar sebagai kuda lalu menghilang, dan sering dianggap hantu seorang perampok perbatasan.
short_description.en: The Dunnie is a small Brownie-type being of Northumberland folklore who likes to pose as a horse and then vanish, and is often thought to be the ghost of a border reiver.

long_description.id: Dunnie adalah makhluk kecil mirip Brownie dalam cerita rakyat perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia, khususnya Northumberland. Yang paling terkenal adalah Dunnie dari Hazlerigg (dalam catatan Henderson ditulis Haselrigg) di paroki Chatton. Henderson menulis bahwa seperti makhluk sejenisnya, Dunnie sangat gemar melakukan tipu daya yang jahil dan merepotkan.
long_description.en: Folklore of the Anglo-Scottish borders, Northumberland in particular, tells of the Dunnie, a little creature much like a Brownie. The best known is the Dunnie of Hazlerigg (spelled Haselrigg by Henderson) in the parish of Chatton. Henderson says that, as with the rest of its kind, the Dunnie loves playing troublesome pranks.

long_description.id: Tipuan khasnya adalah menyamar sebagai kuda. Ketika seorang petani hendak menjemput bidan, Dunnie mengambil wujud kudanya, membawa keduanya dengan selamat, lalu tiba-tiba lenyap di bagian jalan paling berlumpur. Ia juga menyamar sebagai kuda bajak: begitu dipasangi tali kekang, tali itu jatuh ke tanah dan sang kuda berlari kencang melintasi daerah itu.
long_description.en: His typical trick is posing as a horse. When a farmer sets out to fetch the midwife, the Dunnie takes the form of his horse, carries them both safely, then suddenly vanishes in the muddiest part of the road. He also poses as a plough-horse: once harnessed, the harness falls to the ground and the horse races off across the country.

long_description.id: Dunnie juga dikatakan berkeliaran di tebing Cheviots sambil mengulang-ulang sebuah bait dengan suara sedih tentang harta di Cockenheugh dan Collierheugh serta kunci yang hilang. Dari lagu itu muncul anggapan bahwa Dunnie sebenarnya hantu seorang perampok perbatasan (reiver) yang menimbun jarahannya di sana dan terus menjaganya. Seorang kawan Henderson bahkan menunjuk bagian batu paling curam di Haselrigg sebagai tempat Dunnie biasa duduk di malam hari.
long_description.en: The Dunnie was also said to wander the crags of the Cheviots, repeating in a melancholy voice a verse about treasure at Cockenheugh and Collierheugh and a lost key. From this song came the idea that the Dunnie is really the ghost of a reiver who hoarded his loot there and still guards it. A friend of Henderson's even pointed to the steepest rocks at Haselrigg as the place where the Dunnie used to sit at night.

short_description.id: Fuath ("kebencian") adalah golongan roh jahat dalam cerita rakyat Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia dan Irlandia, terutama roh air.
short_description.en: Fuath ('hatred') is a class of malevolent spirits in Scottish Highland and Irish folklore, especially water spirits.

long_description.id: Fuath (Gaelik Skotlandia/Scottish Gaelic, harfiah "kebencian"; jamak fuathan) adalah golongan roh jahat dalam cerita rakyat Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highland) dan Irlandia (Irish), terutama roh air. Istilah ini dijelaskan sebagai golongan umum roh yang menghuni laut, sungai, air tawar, atau loch laut, dengan beberapa "subspesies"; kata itu berasal dari Irlandia Kuno (Old Irish) fúath, "benci, rupa", dan juga diartikan "hantu". Nama lain golongan ini adalah arrachd atau fuath-arrachd.
long_description.en: Fuath (Scottish Gaelic, literally 'hatred'; plural fuathan) is a class of malevolent spirits in Scottish Highland and Irish folklore, especially water spirits. The term has been explained as a general class of spirits haunting the sea, rivers, fresh water or sea lochs, with several 'subspecies'; it comes from Old Irish fúath, 'hate, likeness', and is also glossed 'ghost' or 'spectre'. Another name for the class is arrachd or fuath-arrachd.

long_description.id: Di Sutherland ada Moulin na Vaugha, "Penggilingan Fuath", yang dihantui fuath dan putranya, brollachan yang tak berbentuk; fuath yang pernah terlihat di sana adalah banshee tanpa hidung berambut kuning bergaun sutra hijau, yang ditundukkan dengan baja (penusuk dan jarum jahit) tetapi berubah menjadi gumpalan seperti ubur-ubur saat disinari cahaya. Mereka kadang kawin dengan manusia, dan keturunannya tumbuh surai dan ekor. Menurut artikel de, fuath digambarkan berbulu kuning lebat atau hanya bersurai panjang di punggung, berselaput di jari kaki, berekor berduri, tak berhidung, dan biasanya berpakaian hijau, warna peri.
long_description.en: In Sutherland stood Moulin na Vaugha, 'Mill of the Fuath', haunted by a fuath and her son, the formless brollachan; one fuath seen there was a noseless banshee with yellow hair in a green silk dress, subdued with steel (an awl and a sewing needle) but turning into a jellyfish-like mass when light was shone on it. They sometimes marry humans, whose offspring grow a mane and tail. According to the de article fuathan are covered in shaggy yellow fur or have just a long mane down the back, webbed toes, a spiked tail and no nose, and usually wear green, the fairies' colour.

short_description.id: Girt Dog of Ennerdale adalah anjing misterius yang diyakini membantai ratusan domba di perbukitan Cumberland, Inggris, pada 1810 dan kini menjadi sosok legendaris setempat.
short_description.en: The Girt Dog of Ennerdale was a mysterious dog believed to have slaughtered hundreds of sheep in the fells of Cumberland, England, in 1810, and is now a local legendary figure.

long_description.id: Girt Dog of Ennerdale, juga disebut Vampire Dog atau Demon Dog of Ennerdale, diyakini membunuh antara 300 dan 400 domba di perbukitan Cumberland antara Mei dan September 1810. Kata "girt" dalam dialek Cumbria berarti besar. Anjing ini masih dikenang sebagai sosok legendaris di daerah Ennerdale.
long_description.en: The Girt Dog of Ennerdale, also called the Vampire Dog or Demon Dog of Ennerdale, reportedly slaughtered somewhere from 300 to 400 sheep on the Cumberland fells from May to September 1810. "Girt" is Cumbrian for great. The dog is still remembered as a legendary figure in the Ennerdale district.

long_description.id: Ia pertama kali terlihat oleh Mr Mossop dari Thornholme pada 10 Mei 1810. Anjing berbulu licin ini berwarna cokelat tikus dengan belang gelap seperti harimau dan beratnya delapan stone. Asalnya tidak jelas; ada yang mengira ia kabur dari rombongan gipsi, ada pula yang menduga ia persilangan mastiff dan greyhound.
long_description.en: It was first seen by Mr Mossop of Thornholme on 10 May 1810. The smooth-haired dog was tawny mouse-coloured with dark tiger-like streaks and weighed eight stones. Its origin was unclear; some thought it had escaped from a gipsy troop, others that it was a mastiff and greyhound cross.

long_description.id: Anjing itu biasanya berburu pada malam hari dan sering membunuh tujuh atau delapan domba dalam semalam; menurut satu cerita ia meminum darah langsung dari leher korbannya. Ia tidak pernah terdengar menggonggong atau melolong, mengabaikan umpan beracun, dan membawa para pengejarnya berlari puluhan mil tanpa hasil.
long_description.en: The dog usually hunted at night and often killed seven or eight sheep in one night; by one account it drank blood straight from its victims' necks. It was never heard to bark or howl, ignored poisoned bait, and led its pursuers on fruitless chases of many miles.

long_description.id: John Russell menawarkan hadiah £10 untuk anjing itu, hidup atau mati. Pada 12 September 1810 John Steel menembaknya di Eskett Woods dekat Rowrah dan menerima hadiah tersebut. Kulit awetannya kemudian dipamerkan di museum di Keswick sebelum dibuang karena rusak.
long_description.en: John Russell offered a £10 reward for the dog, dead or alive. On 12 September 1810 John Steel shot it in Eskett Woods near Rowrah and received the reward. Its stuffed skin was later displayed in a museum at Keswick before being discarded as it decayed.

short_description.id: Hiisi adalah istilah mitologi Finnik yang semula menunjuk tempat-tempat keramat, lalu berbagai makhluk mitos yang kemudian dipandang sebagai roh jahat.
short_description.en: Hiisi is a Finnic mythological term that first referred to sacred places and later to various mythical beings, eventually seen as evil spirits.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi bangsa-bangsa Finnik, hiisi mula-mula berarti tempat keramat, lalu dipakai untuk bermacam makhluk mitos. Folklor yang lebih kemudian, yang dipengaruhi agama Kristen, menggambarkan mereka sebagai makhluk bersifat iblis atau penipu, sering dianggap penghuni asli tanah itu yang masih kafir, mirip raksasa dalam mitologi. Mereka dikaitkan dengan tanjung yang menonjol, celah yang menyeramkan, batu besar, lubang batu, hutan, bukit, dan medan kasar lainnya.
long_description.en: In the mythologies of the Finnic peoples, hiisi first meant a sacred place and was later used for many kinds of mythical beings. Later, Christian-influenced folklore pictures them as demonic or trickster-like beings, often seen as the original pagan dwellers of the land, much like the giants of myth. They are linked with jutting promontories, forbidding crevasses, big boulders, potholes, woods, hills and other rough ground.

long_description.id: Asal-usul istilah ini ditafsirkan berbeda. Satu pandangan menyebut Hiisi semula roh hutan di perbukitan, dan dalam bahasa Estonia hiis berarti hutan kecil keramat di tanah tinggi; Mauno Koski dan peneliti lain mengaitkannya terutama dengan tempat pemakaman. Dalam mantra orang Finlandia, Hiisi sering dihubungkan dengan bukit atau gunung, sebagai pemilik atau penguasanya. Daftar dewa pagan Finlandia susunan Uskup Mikael Agricola menyebut Hiisi dewa hewan buruan hutan atau bulu, serupa dengan Tapio.
long_description.en: The origin of the term is read in different ways. One view holds that Hiisi was first a spirit of hill forests, and in Estonian hiis means a sacred grove on high ground; Mauno Koski and others link it mainly with burial sites. In Finnish spells Hiisi is often tied to a hill or mountain, as its owner or ruler. Bishop Mikael Agricola's list of Finnish pagan gods calls Hiisi a god of forest game or fur, like Tapio.

long_description.id: Sifat jahat Hiisi diduga makin diperbesar sejak Kristenisasi Finlandia pada abad ke-12 dan ke-13, sampai akhirnya hampir sama dengan iblis Kristen. Cerita rakyat lisan terutama mengisahkan makhluk penghuni situs hiisi, biasanya troll atau raksasa, yang membentuk batu-batu aneh dan bentang alam; dalam satu kisah, para raksasa melempar batu ke laut agar orang tidak bisa berperahu ke gereja. Ada hiidet yang kecil dan ada pula yang raksasa.
long_description.en: Hiisi's evil nature is thought to have grown from the Christianization of Finland in the 12th and 13th centuries until it came close to the Christian devil. Oral folklore mainly tells of beings living at hiisi sites, usually trolls or giants, who shaped odd rocks and landscape features; in one tale the giants throw rocks into the sea to stop people rowing to church. Some hiidet were small, others gigantic.

long_description.id: Hiidet dapat bepergian dalam arak-arakan yang riuh dan menyerang orang yang tidak memberi jalan, dan hiisi bisa masuk mencuri jika pintu dibiarkan terbuka. Orang yang dikejar hiisi dianjurkan berlindung di lahan garapan, yang dalam folklor Finlandia dianggap tanah yang diberkati. Satu sumber menyebut Hiisi putra raksasa Kaleva, penjinak binatang liar, dan perwujudan Lempo; folklor Finlandia juga membedakan hiisi hutan, air, dan gunung.
long_description.en: Hiidet were said to roam in loud processions, assaulting anyone who failed to make way, and a hiisi might slip indoors to steal through an open door. A person pursued by one was told to flee to farmland, which Finnish folklore regarded as blessed ground. One source calls Hiisi a son of the giant Kaleva, a tamer of wild beasts and a form of Lempo; Finnish folk myth also told apart forest, water and mountain hiisis.

long_description.id: Karzełek, juga Skarbnik ("bendahara"), adalah roh dalam mitologi Polandia dan kepercayaan Slavia yang tinggal di tambang dan lorong bawah tanah, penjaga permata, kristal, logam mulia, dan harta yang terkubur. Ia juga dianggap penguasa alam bawah tanah tempat ia membawa jiwa penambang yang tewas saat bekerja. Ia sering tampil sebagai penambang tua berjanggut membawa pelita, dan dapat menjelma kambing, kuda, anjing, tikus, katak, laba-laba, atau lalat, atau tetap tak terlihat sehingga hanya terdengar ketukannya.
long_description.en: Karzełek, also Skarbnik ("treasurer"), is a spirit of Polish mythology and Slavic belief living in mines and underground workings, guardian of gems, crystals, precious metals and buried treasure. He was also held to rule an underground realm to which he took the souls of miners killed at work. He often appeared as an old bearded miner with a lamp, and could become a goat, horse, dog, mouse, frog, spider or fly, or stay invisible so only his knocking was heard.

long_description.id: Ia melindungi penambang dari bahaya, memperingatkan mereka akan runtuhan, banjir, dan kebakaran, menuntun yang tersesat, dan menunjukkan urat bijih. Terhadap orang jahat atau yang menghinanya ia mematikan, mendorong mereka ke jurang gelap atau meruntuhkan terowongan. Melempar batu, bersiul, atau menutup kepala dianggap menyinggungnya; ia akan memperingatkan pelaku dengan segenggam tanah sebelum bertindak lebih keras.
long_description.en: He protects miners from danger, warns them of rockbursts, floods and fires, leads the lost back and shows them veins of ore. Wicked people and those who offend him he kills, shoving them into black chasms or collapsing tunnels on top of them. Throwing rocks, whistling or covering one's head offend him; he warns the offender with handfuls of soil before acting seriously.

short_description.id: Kikimora adalah roh rumah perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia yang bisa bersikap baik atau jahat tergantung perilaku pemilik rumah; belakangan ia juga dibayangkan sebagai roh rawa.
short_description.en: The kikimora is a female house spirit of Slavic mythology who may be good or bad depending on the homeowner's behaviour; later she was also imagined as a swamp spirit.

long_description.id: Kikimora adalah roh rumah perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia, yang perannya biasanya disandingkan dengan domovoi. Ia bisa menjadi roh "baik" atau "jahat", bergantung pada perilaku penghuni rumah, dan biasanya tinggal di balik tungku atau di ruang bawah tanah. Kepercayaan ini bermula pada masa ketika paganisme Slavia perlahan tergantikan oleh agama Kristen antara abad ke-8 dan ke-13, dan tetap kuat sesudahnya.
long_description.en: The kikimora is a female house spirit of Slavic mythology whose role is usually set beside that of the domovoy. She can be a "good" or a "bad" spirit depending on how the household behaves, and usually lives behind the stove or in the cellar. The belief arose as Slavic paganism slowly gave way to Christianity between the 8th and 13th centuries, and stayed strong afterwards.

long_description.id: Wujudnya beragam: ia bisa bermoncong anjing, berparuh ayam, atau menyerupai kambing bermata menyala dan bertanduk, tetapi selalu perempuan, entah nenek tua atau gadis cantik. Ada dua jenis kikimora: yang dari hutan bersuami domovoi, sedangkan yang dari rawa bersuami leshy. Kikimora rawa digambarkan sebagai nenek kecil, buruk rupa, bungkuk, kurus, dan kusut, berhidung runcing dan berambut acak-acakan; ia menakuti orang, menjatuhkan pelancong dari jalan atau bahkan menenggelamkan mereka, dan menculik anak-anak.
long_description.en: Her looks vary: she may have a dog's snout, a chicken's beak or resemble a goat with glowing eyes and horns, but she is always female, either an old woman or a lovely girl. There are two kinds: the forest kikimora is married to the domovoi, while the swamp kikimora is married to the leshy. The swamp kikimora is pictured as a small, ugly, hunchbacked, thin, scruffy old woman with a pointed nose and tangled hair; she frightens people, knocks travellers off the road or even drowns them, and steals children.

long_description.id: Bila rumah terurus, kikimora membantu menjaga ayam dan pekerjaan rumah; bila tidak, ia bersiul, memecahkan piring, dan membuat keributan pada malam hari, dan ia juga keluar malam-malam untuk memintal. Ia menghantui rumah tangga yang kotor, suami yang malas atau kasar, atau anak yang tidak disiplin, dan kepergiannya dipercaya bisa diupayakan dengan memperbaiki perilaku. Tukang bangunan yang tidak senang pada pemilik rumah bisa mengundangnya dengan menaruh boneka mirip kikimora di balok utama, dan sekali masuk ia sulit diusir.
long_description.en: In a tidy home the kikimora tends the hens and helps with chores; in a messy one she whistles, smashes crockery and stirs up a racket after dark, and she also comes out at night to spin. She haunts households that are kept dirty, with a lazy or abusive husband or undisciplined children, and mending one's ways is believed to drive her out. Builders displeased with a homeowner could summon her by placing a kikimora-like doll in the main beam, and once inside she is hard to remove.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan, siapa pun yang melihat kikimora sedang menenun akan segera mati. Untuk menenangkannya, semua panci dan wajan dicuci dengan teh pakis, sedangkan batu ular atau ranting juniper digantung di atas kandang ayam untuk melindungi ayam darinya.
long_description.en: It is believed that anyone who sees the kikimora weaving will soon die. To calm her, all pots and pans are washed with fern tea, while a snake stone or juniper twigs are hung over the henhouse to protect the chickens from her.
