short_description.id: Madam Pigott adalah hantu White Lady dari Chetwynd dan Newport di Shropshire, arwah seorang ibu yang meninggal saat melahirkan dan konon melompat ke kuda para penunggang di malam hari.
short_description.en: Madam Pigott is a White Lady ghost of Chetwynd and Newport in Shropshire, the spirit of a mother who died in childbirth and is said to leap onto riders' horses at night.

long_description.id: Madam Pigott, juga dieja Madam Piggott, adalah hantu yang konon menghantui Chetwynd Park dan kota pasar Newport di Shropshire, dan mirip dengan White Lady lain dalam cerita rakyat Britania. Charlotte Burne menyebutnya teror lama bagi Chetwynd dan Edgmond. Menurut kisahnya, ketika ia melahirkan, suaminya hanya berkata 'one should lop the root to save the branch'; ibu dan bayi sama-sama meninggal, dan arwahnya tidak dapat beristirahat.
long_description.en: Madam Pigott, also spelt Madam Piggott, is a ghost said to haunt Chetwynd Park and the market town of Newport in Shropshire, resembling other White Ladies of British folklore. Charlotte Burne's collection calls her the ancient terror of Chetwynd and Edgmond. In the tale, when she gave birth her husband only said 'one should lop the root to save the branch'; mother and child both died, and her spirit could find no rest.

long_description.id: Setiap malam tepat pukul dua belas ia keluar dari pintu kolong di atap Chetwynd (old) Rectory. Tempat kesukaannya adalah jalan curam bernama Cheney Hill, dan ia biasa duduk di akar pohon yang disebut Madam Pigott's Armchair sambil menyisir rambut bayinya pada malam terang bulan. Bila penunggang kuda lewat, ia bersama kucing hitamnya melompat ke belakangnya dan berpegangan sampai tiba di air mengalir, karena ia tidak bisa menyeberanginya.
long_description.en: Every night at exactly twelve o'clock she came out of a trap-door in the roof of Chetwynd (old) Rectory. Her favourite haunt was the steep lane called Cheney Hill, and she would sit on a tree-root called Madam Pigott's Armchair combing her baby's hair on moonlit nights. Whenever a horseman came by, she leapt up with her black cat onto the horse behind him and held tight until they came to running water, which she could not pass.

long_description.id: Dua belas rohaniwan dipanggil untuk menenangkan arwahnya dengan terus membaca Mazmur, dan seorang di antaranya berhasil karena tetap membaca setelah yang lain kelelahan. Dalam versi yang dituturkan Dimiti kepada Groome (yang menegaskan legenda ini tidak berasal dari kaum Gipsy), ia adalah Miss Pigott yang tewas terlempar dari kuda di Chetwynd End; arwahnya dikurung dalam botol di Chetwynd Pool, tetapi kembali setelah botol itu pecah. Kisah ini dikenal luas di sekitar Chetwynd, dan penampakannya masih dilaporkan hingga 2014 di sekitar jalan A41 antara Newport dan Market Drayton.
long_description.en: Twelve clergy were summoned to lay her by reading Psalms without pause, and one succeeded by reading on after the rest were exhausted. In the version Dimiti told Groome (who stresses that the legend has no claim to Gipsy origin) she is Miss Pigott, killed when thrown from her horse at Chetwynd End; her spirit was bottled in Chetwynd Pool but returned when the bottle broke. The tale was widely known around Chetwynd, and sightings were reported as recently as 2014 around the A41 road between Newport and Market Drayton.

short_description.id: Munaciello atau Monaciello, "biarawan kecil", adalah peri usil berjubah biarawan dari cerita rakyat Napoli yang menyusup ke rumah lewat sumur, mencuri, tetapi juga memberi harta.
short_description.en: The Munaciello or Monaciello, 'little monk', is a mischievous robed sprite of Neapolitan folklore who slips into houses through wells, steals, but also gives treasure.

long_description.id: Munaciello, "biarawan kecil", adalah peri dari cerita rakyat lisan Napoli, lelaki pendek dan kekar berjubah panjang bertudung. Menurut banyak kisah ia penjaga saluran air dan sumur bawah tanah kota, sehingga dapat menyusup diam-diam ke rumah-rumah. Ia usil, mencuri barang berharga dan mengganggu ibu rumah tangga, tetapi juga muncul pada malam hari kepada orang yang sangat membutuhkan dan menuntun mereka ke harta. Kunjungannya tidak boleh diceritakan, agar musibah tidak datang.
long_description.en: The Munaciello, 'little monk', is a sprite of the oral folklore of Naples, a short, stocky man in a long hooded robe. Many tales make him keeper of the city's underground aqueducts and wells, so he can slip secretly into houses. He is mischievous, stealing valuables and pestering housewives, but also appears at night to people in dire need and leads them to treasure. His visits must not be told, or misfortune follows.

long_description.id: Ada beberapa hipotesis asal-usul. Matilde Serao mencatat kisah anak cacat dari tahun 1445 yang didandani ibunya dengan jubah biarawan; tudung merah menjadi pertanda baik dan hitam pertanda buruk. Legenda lain menjadikannya pengelola sumur (pozzaro), dan kebiasaannya memang mirip pengangkut air Napoli kuno; hipotesis ketiga menganggapnya iblis kecil.
long_description.en: There are several theories of origin. Matilde Serao recorded the story of a deformed child of 1445 whom his mother dressed in a monk's habit; a red hood was a good omen and a black one a bad omen. Another legend makes him a well keeper (pozzaro), and his habits do resemble those of old Naples' water carriers; a third theory sees him as a little demon.

long_description.id: Ungkapan "Forse avrà il Monaciello in casa" dipakai untuk rezeki tak terduga. Ia muncul dalam drama Questi fantasmi! karya Eduardo De Filippo dan film The Hand of God (2021).
long_description.en: The saying 'Forse avrà il Monaciello in casa' is used for sudden fortune. He appears in Eduardo De Filippo's play Questi fantasmi! and the film The Hand of God (2021).

who.en: A little monk sprite.

role.id: Mengusili rumah dan memberi harta kepada yang membutuhkan.
role.en: Pesters households and gives treasure to the needy.

famous_for.en: The saying 'Forse avrà il Monaciello in casa'.

claims.quote: Monacello (Italian: [monaˈtʃɛlːo]), or Munaciello (Neapolitan: [munaˈtʃjelːə]), is a sprite from the traditional oral folklore of Naples, Italy.

statement.id: Monacello atau Munaciello (bahasa Neapolitan) adalah peri dari cerita rakyat lisan Napoli, Italia.
statement.en: Monacello, or Munaciello in Neapolitan, is a sprite of the oral folklore of Naples, Italy.

claims.quote: Its name means "little monk" in the Neapolitan language. It gets often described as a "benevolent man, short, stocky, very spiteful" and enjoys visiting houses in the Historic center of Naples. It is thought to wear a long robe with a broad hood on top of it.

statement.id: Namanya berarti "biarawan kecil" dalam bahasa Neapolitan; ia sering digambarkan sebagai "lelaki baik hati, pendek, kekar, sangat usil" yang suka mengunjungi rumah di pusat bersejarah Napoli, mengenakan jubah panjang bertudung lebar.
statement.en: Its name means 'little monk' in Neapolitan; it is often described as a 'benevolent man, short, stocky, very spiteful' who likes visiting houses in Naples' historic centre, wearing a long robe with a broad hood.

claims.quote: According to many tales, he was the caretaker (or "pozzari") of the city's underground aqueducts, canals, and water wells. Monaciello knew every twist and turn in these underground passages and could use the wells to secretly enter the piazzas and homes of Naples.

statement.id: Menurut banyak kisah, ia penjaga (pozzari) saluran air bawah tanah, kanal, dan sumur kota, yang mengenal setiap lorongnya dan memakai sumur untuk diam-diam masuk ke alun-alun dan rumah warga Napoli.
statement.en: According to many tales he was the keeper (pozzari) of the city's underground aqueducts, canals and wells, who knew every passage and used the wells to slip secretly into the squares and homes of Naples.

claims.quote: Despite his mischievous nature—like stealing valuables and bothering housewives—Monaciello is mostly benevolent. He's known to appear at night to those in desperate need, leading them to hidden treasures or giving them his own valuables, sometimes the same ones he had stolen, without asking for anything in return.

statement.id: Meski usil, misalnya mencuri barang berharga dan mengganggu ibu rumah tangga, Monaciello umumnya baik hati: ia muncul pada malam hari kepada orang yang sangat membutuhkan dan menuntun mereka ke harta tersembunyi atau memberi barang berharganya sendiri tanpa meminta balasan.
statement.en: For all his mischief, such as stealing valuables and bothering housewives, Monaciello is mostly benevolent: he appears at night to people in desperate need and leads them to hidden treasure or gives them his own valuables, asking nothing in return.

claims.quote: There's even a saying about unexpected fortune: "Forse avrà il Monaciello in casa" (perhaps he has had the little Monk in his house).

statement.id: Ada ungkapan untuk rezeki tak terduga: "Forse avrà il Monaciello in casa" (mungkin ada Monaciello di rumahnya).
statement.en: There is a saying for unexpected fortune: 'Forse avrà il Monaciello in casa' (perhaps he has had the little monk in his house).

claims.quote: The habits of Monaciello resemble those of the water carriers of ancient Naples who worked in the numerous tunnels connecting the city's underground wells.

statement.id: Kebiasaan Monaciello mirip para pengangkut air Napoli kuno yang bekerja di terowongan penghubung sumur bawah tanah kota.
statement.en: Monaciello's habits resemble those of the water carriers of old Naples who worked in the tunnels linking the city's underground wells.

claims.quote: Monaciello (O'Munaciello en napolitain), « le petit moine », est un nain du folklore napolitain.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Prancis menyebut Monaciello (O'Munaciello dalam bahasa Neapolitan), "biarawan kecil", sebagai kurcaci dari cerita rakyat Napoli.
statement.en: The French article calls Monaciello (O'Munaciello in Neapolitan), 'the little monk', a dwarf of Neapolitan folklore.

claims.quote: Secondo la prima, riportata tra gli altri da Matilde Serao nel suo Leggende napoletane (1881), il munaciello sarebbe un personaggio realmente esistito. L'origine andrebbe fatta risalire al 1445, durante il regno di Alfonso V d'Aragona

statement.id: Menurut hipotesis pertama, yang antara lain dicatat Matilde Serao dalam Leggende napoletane (1881), munaciello adalah tokoh yang benar-benar ada, yang asal-usulnya berawal pada 1445 di masa pemerintahan Alfonso V dari Aragon.
statement.en: According to the first hypothesis, reported among others by Matilde Serao in her Leggende napoletane (1881), the munaciello was a real person whose story goes back to 1445, in the reign of Alfonso V of Aragon.

claims.quote: La madre prese a vestirlo con un abito bianco e nero da monaco, sempre speranzosa in un miracolo, e questo fatto fu all'origine del nomignolo munaciello attribuitogli dal popolo.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, sang ibu mendandani anaknya yang kecil dan cacat dengan jubah biarawan hitam-putih sambil berharap mukjizat, dan inilah asal julukan munaciello dari warga.
statement.en: In that story the mother dressed her small, deformed child in a black-and-white monk's habit, hoping for a miracle, which gave rise to the people's nickname munaciello.

claims.quote: In particolare, se il cappuccio dell'abito era di colore rosso, se ne traevano auspici di buon augurio, mentre la malasorte veniva associata al cappuccio nero.

statement.id: Tudung merah pada jubahnya dianggap pertanda baik, sedangkan tudung hitam dikaitkan dengan nasib buruk.
statement.en: A red hood on his habit was taken as a good omen, while a black hood was linked to bad luck.

claims.quote: Altra leggenda invece vuole che il munaciello fosse l'antico gestore dei pozzi d'acqua (il "pozzaro"), il quale riusciva (per la sua statura piccola) ad entrare nelle case passando attraverso i canali che servivano a calare il secchio.

statement.id: Legenda lain menyebut munaciello dahulu pengelola sumur air (pozzaro) yang karena tubuhnya kecil dapat masuk ke rumah lewat saluran untuk menurunkan ember.
statement.en: Another legend makes the munaciello the old keeper of the water wells (pozzaro), who, being small, could enter houses through the shafts used to lower the bucket.

claims.quote: Vi è anche una terza ipotesi, che descrive il munaciello come un piccolo demone, dispettoso perché cattivo, anche quando lascia monete

statement.id: Ada pula hipotesis ketiga yang menggambarkan munaciello sebagai iblis kecil yang usil karena jahat, bahkan ketika ia meninggalkan uang logam.
statement.en: A third hypothesis describes the munaciello as a little demon, spiteful because wicked, even when he leaves coins.

claims.quote: In nessuno dei tre casi suddetti bisogna però rivelarne la presenza: secondo il folclore napoletano, possono capitare disgrazie e sfortuna a chi rivela una visita del munaciello.

statement.id: Kehadirannya tidak boleh diungkapkan: menurut cerita rakyat Napoli, orang yang membocorkan kunjungan munaciello bisa ditimpa musibah dan kemalangan.
statement.en: His presence must never be revealed: in Neapolitan folklore, misfortune can befall whoever tells of a visit from the munaciello.

claims.quote: Tra le più importanti si ricordano quella di Eduardo De Filippo nella sua opera Questi fantasmi!, in cui la commistione tra la leggenda del visitatore soprannaturale ed il grottesco della vita quotidiana viene espressa attraverso il personaggio dell'amante della moglie, che Eduardo scambia per un munaciello.

statement.id: Salah satu rujukan sastra terpenting adalah drama Eduardo De Filippo, Questi fantasmi!, yang tokoh kekasih sang istri disangka seorang munaciello.
statement.en: Among the most important literary references is Eduardo De Filippo's play Questi fantasmi!, in which the wife's lover is mistaken for a munaciello.

claims.quote: In the 2021 film The Hand of God, the Little Monk appears as a young boy as opposed to a short, older man.

statement.id: Dalam film The Hand of God (2021), Si Biarawan Kecil muncul sebagai anak laki-laki, bukan lelaki tua bertubuh pendek.
statement.en: In the 2021 film The Hand of God, the Little Monk appears as a young boy rather than a short older man.

short_description.id: Zână adalah peri dalam mitologi Rumania, padanan peri ibu baptis, yang tinggal di hutan dan membantu orang baik.
short_description.en: The zână is a fairy of Romanian mythology, akin to the fairy godmother, who lives in the woods and helps good people.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Rumania, zână (jamak zâne) setara dengan Charites Yunani atau peri ibu baptis, dan merupakan kebalikan dari monster seperti Muma Pădurii. Mereka tampil sebagai tokoh baik dalam dongeng dan kebanyakan tinggal di hutan. Ukuran dan rupanya beragam, dan mereka dapat berubah wujud agar menyatu dengan lingkungan untuk berlindung.
long_description.en: In Romanian tradition the zână (plural zâne) corresponds to the Greek Charites or the fairy godmother and is the opposite of monsters such as Muma Pădurii. They appear as good figures in fairy tales and mostly live in the woods. They vary in size and look and can change form to blend into their surroundings for protection.

long_description.id: Zâne memberi kehidupan kepada janin dalam kandungan dan menganugerahkan bakat seperti menari, kecantikan, kebaikan hati, dan keberuntungan. Namun kebaikan mereka ada batasnya: orang yang melanggar pantangan, misalnya masuk ke wilayah zâne tanpa izin, bisa dihukum dengan kebutaan.
long_description.en: Zâne give life to babies still in the womb and grant them talents such as dancing, beauty, kindness and luck. Their goodwill has limits, though: anyone who breaks a taboo, for instance by entering zâne land uninvited, may be punished with blindness.

long_description.id: Zâne terbagi menjadi baik dan jahat; zâne yang baik adalah gadis muda yang cantik dan selalu punya jalan keluar bagi sang pahlawan, biasanya Făt-Frumos. Zâne yang baik dipercaya lahir dari bunga.
long_description.en: Zâne are divided into good and evil ones; the good zâne are beautiful young maidens who always hold the solution for the hero, usually Făt-Frumos. Good zâne are believed to be born from flowers.

literal_meaning.en: from the name of the Roman goddess Diana

claims.quote: În mitologia românească, acestea sunt de 2 categorii morale: bune și rele. Zânele bune sunt preponderente numeric și categorial, sunt fecioare frumoase, zvelte, foarte tinere, năzdrăvane, prielnice omului cinstit și având totdeauna soluțiile esențiale pentru dificultățile ori impasurile inevitabile de care este asaltat eroul arhetipal (de obicei Făt-Frumos).

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Rumania, zâne terbagi menjadi baik dan jahat; zâne yang baik lebih banyak, berupa gadis cantik yang sangat muda dan sakti, berpihak pada orang jujur, dan selalu punya jalan keluar bagi pahlawan, biasanya Făt-Frumos.
statement.en: In Romanian mythology zâne are of two moral kinds, good and evil; the good ones predominate, being beautiful, very young, magical maidens who favour honest people and always hold the solution for the hero, usually Făt-Frumos.

short_description.id: Ojáncanu adalah raksasa bermata satu dalam mitologi Cantabria, perwujudan kekejaman, yang hanya dapat dibunuh dengan mencabut rambut putih di janggutnya.
short_description.en: The Ojáncanu is a one-eyed giant of Cantabrian mythology, an embodiment of cruelty, killed only by pulling the white hair from its beard.

long_description.id: Ojáncanu adalah raksasa mirip kiklops dalam mitologi Cantabria dan perwujudan kekejaman. Ia bermata satu, setinggi 10 sampai 20 kaki, sangat kuat, berjari sepuluh di tiap tangan dan kaki, dan bergigi dua baris. Ia tinggal di gua-gua suram di daerah terpencil La Montaña. Pasangannya disebut ojáncana.
long_description.en: The Ojáncanu is a cyclops-like giant of Cantabrian mythology and the embodiment of cruelty. It is one-eyed, 10 to 20 ft tall, immensely strong, with ten digits on each hand and foot and two rows of teeth. It lives in gloomy caves in remote parts of La Montaña. Its female is called the ojáncana.

long_description.id: Ia terus berbuat jahat: mencabut batu, merusak gubuk, dan menyumbat mata air, dan selalu menang melawan beruang dan banteng. Ia hanya takut pada Anjana, juga pada katak terbang dan burung hantu. Cara termudah membunuhnya adalah mencabut satu-satunya rambut putih di janggutnya. Ojáncanu tidak kawin; jasad yang tua dikubur di bawah pohon ek atau yew.
long_description.en: It constantly does evil, pulling up rocks, wrecking huts and blocking springs, and always beats bears and bulls. It fears only the Anjanas, as well as flying toads and barn owls. short_description.id: Patagon adalah ras raksasa mitos yang menurut catatan Eropa awal tinggal di Patagonia, pertama kali dilaporkan oleh pelayaran Magellan pada tahun 1520-an.
short_description.en: The Patagons were a mythical race of giants that early European accounts placed in Patagonia, first reported by Magellan's voyage in the 1520s.

long_description.id: Patagon atau raksasa Patagonia adalah ras manusia raksasa yang menurut catatan Eropa awal tinggal di Patagonia. Mereka disebut setidaknya dua kali tinggi manusia biasa, bahkan 13 hingga 15 kaki menurut beberapa catatan. Nama Patagonia sendiri berasal dari arti "tanah tempat tinggal Patagon".
long_description.en: The Patagons or Patagonian giants were a race of giant humans that early European accounts placed in Patagonia. They were said to be at least twice normal height, some accounts saying 13 to 15 feet. The name Patagonia itself comes from "land where the Patagons live".

long_description.id: Penyebutan pertama berasal dari pelayaran keliling dunia Ferdinand Magellan pada tahun 1520-an. Penulis catatannya, Pigafetta, menggambarkan lelaki raksasa yang menari dan bernyanyi di pantai, begitu tinggi sehingga para pelaut hanya setinggi pinggangnya, dan mencatat bahwa Magellan menamai mereka Patagão. Kisah ini memengaruhi gambaran Eropa tentang wilayah itu selama berabad-abad hingga dibantah pada akhir abad ke-18.
long_description.en: The first mention came from Ferdinand Magellan's circumnavigation in the 1520s. Its chronicler Pigafetta described a giant dancing and singing on the shore, so tall the sailors reached only his waist, and recorded that Magellan named them Patagão. The story shaped European ideas of the region for centuries until it was disproved in the late 18th century.

short_description.id: Saci adalah tokoh populer mitologi Brasil: makhluk berkaki satu yang mengisap pipa dan memakai topi merah ajaib untuk muncul dan menghilang.
short_description.en: Saci is a popular figure of Brazilian mythology: a one-legged being who smokes a pipe and wears a magic red cap to appear and vanish.

long_description.id: Saci atau Saci-pererê adalah tokoh populer dalam mitologi Brasil: makhluk mirip kobold berkulit hitam dan berkaki satu yang mengisap pipa, meminta tembakau kepada orang, dan memakai topi merah ajaib untuk muncul dan menghilang, biasanya dalam pusaran debu. Tergantung daerahnya, ia bisa baik atau jahat; dalam versi jahatnya ia dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak di kalangan budak dan buruh tani.
long_description.en: The Saci or Saci-pererê is a popular figure of Brazilian mythology: a goblin-like, black-skinned, one-legged being who smokes a pipe, begs for tobacco and wears a magic red cap that lets him appear and vanish, usually in a dust devil. Depending on the region he may be good or bad; in his malicious version he served as a bogeyman for children among slaves and farm workers.

long_description.id: Saci yang tertangkap dapat dikurung dalam botol dan dipaksa mengabulkan permintaan sebagai tebusan kebebasannya. Namanya berasal dari bahasa Tupinambá: saci dari çua ci, "mata jahat", dan akhiran -pererê dari perérég, "melompat-lompat"; nama Saci-pererê awalnya merujuk pada burung kukuk bergaris.
long_description.en: A captured Saci can be shut in a bottle and forced to grant wishes in exchange for freedom. His name is Tupinambá: saci from çua ci, "evil eye", and the suffix -pererê from perérég, "bouncy, jumpy"; the name Saci-pererê originally referred to the striped cuckoo.

short_description.id: Shug Monkey adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Cambridgeshire yang menggabungkan ciri anjing dan monyet, dan dikatakan menghantui jalan kecil Slough Hill Lane.
short_description.en: The Shug Monkey is a creature of Cambridgeshire folklore combining the features of a dog and a monkey, said to haunt the narrow Slough Hill Lane.

long_description.id: Menurut cerita rakyat Cambridgeshire, Shug Monkey menghantui Slough Hill Lane, jalan dari desa West Wratting menuju Balsham. Makhluk ini digambarkan bertubuh seperti anjing gembala yang hitam pekat dan berbulu lebat, tetapi berwajah monyet dengan mata yang menatap tajam. Orang menganggapnya hantu atau iblis. Sebuah halaman sejarah lokal menyebutnya anjing hantu raksasa yang dikaitkan dengan mitos Viking.
long_description.en: In Cambridgeshire folklore the Shug Monkey haunted Slough Hill Lane, the road from the village of West Wratting to Balsham. It was pictured with the body of a jet-black, shaggy sheepdog but the face of a monkey with staring eyes. People took it to be a ghost or a demon. A local history page calls it a giant spectral dog linked to Viking myth.

long_description.id: James Wentworth Day, penulis dan penyiar setempat, adalah orang pertama yang menuliskan kisahnya dalam Here Are Ghosts and Witches (1954). Ia mengutip seorang polisi, A. Taylor, yang semasa kecil mengenal makhluk itu sebagai perpaduan anjing besar berbulu kasar dan monyet bermata besar bersinar; kadang ia berjalan terseret dengan kaki belakang, kadang melesat dengan keempat kakinya. Anak-anak, katanya, menjauhi jalan itu setelah gelap.
long_description.en: Local writer and broadcaster James Wentworth Day was the first to relate its stories, in Here Are Ghosts and Witches (1954). He quoted a police constable, A. Taylor, who as a boy knew the creature as half large rough-haired dog, half monkey, with large gleaming eyes; sometimes it shuffled on its hind legs, at other times it whizzed past on all fours. The children, he said, kept away from the lane after dark.

long_description.id: Wentworth Day menganggapnya variasi aneh dari Black Shuck, sedangkan ahli cerita rakyat setempat Polly Howat menduga keduanya berakar pada mitologi Nordik. Menurut Howat, penampakan Shug Monkey tidak pernah dilaporkan lagi sejak sebelum Perang Dunia II.
long_description.en: Wentworth Day saw it as an odd offshoot of Black Shuck; the local folklorist Polly Howat, for her part, proposes that the two spring from Norse mythology. According to Howat, no sightings of the Shug Monkey have been reported since before World War II.

claims.quote: In the folklore of Cambridgeshire, the Shug Monkey is a creature that shares features of a dog and monkey, which reportedly haunted Slough Hill Lane (a street that leads from the village of West Wratting to nearby Balsham).

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Cambridgeshire, Shug Monkey adalah makhluk berciri anjing dan monyet yang dikabarkan menghantui Slough Hill Lane, jalan dari desa West Wratting ke Balsham.
statement.en: In Cambridgeshire folklore the Shug Monkey is a creature sharing features of a dog and monkey, reportedly haunting Slough Hill Lane, a street from the village of West Wratting to Balsham.

statement.en: The creature was believed to have the body of a jet-black shaggy sheepdog and the face of a monkey with staring eyes, and was believed to be a supernatural ghost or demon.

claims.quote: Local writer and broadcaster James Wentworth Day, who first related stories of the Shug Monkey in Here Are Ghosts and Witches (1954), described it as a curious variation of Black Shuck

claims.quote: while local folklorist Polly Howat suggests that both share common origins in Norse mythology.

short_description.id: Stoor worm adalah ular laut raksasa yang jahat dalam folklor Orkney, yang napas busuknya meracuni tumbuhan dan membunuh hewan serta manusia.
short_description.en: The stoor worm is a gigantic evil sea serpent of Orcadian folklore whose putrid breath blights plants and kills animals and people.

long_description.id: Stoor worm atau Mester Stoor Worm adalah ular laut raksasa yang jahat dalam folklor Orkney, yang mampu meracuni tumbuhan dan membinasakan hewan serta manusia dengan napas busuknya. Ia kemungkinan varian Orkney dari Jörmungandr Norse, Ular Midgard, dan digambarkan sebagai naga laut. Namanya mungkin berasal dari Norse Kuno Storðar-gandr, nama lain Jörmungandr; "Mester" berarti tuan, karena ia "tuan dan bapak semua stoorworm".
long_description.en: The stoor worm, or Mester Stoor Worm, is a gigantic wicked sea serpent of Orkney folklore that could blight plants and kill animals and people with its rotten breath. It is probably an Orkney form of the Norse Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent, and has been called a sea dragon. The name may derive from Old Norse Storðar-gandr, another name for Jörmungandr, and 'Mester' means master, as it was the 'master and father of all stoorworms'.

long_description.id: Seorang raja yang negerinya terancam dinasihati mempersembahkan tujuh perawan setiap minggu; akhirnya ia menawarkan kerajaan, tangan putrinya dan pedang ajaib kepada siapa pun yang dapat membinasakan monster itu. Assipattle, putra bungsu seorang petani, mengalahkannya; saat ia mati, giginya rontok menjadi Kepulauan Orkney, Shetland dan Faroe, dan tubuhnya menjadi Islandia.
long_description.en: A king whose land it threatened was advised to feed it seven virgins every week; in the end he offered his kingdom, his daughter's hand and a magic sword to whoever could destroy it. Assipattle, a farmer's youngest son, overcame it; as it died its teeth dropped out to form Orkney, Shetland and the Faroes, and its body became Iceland.

role.en: Defeated by Assipattle.

famous_for.en: Its body became Iceland.

short_description.id: Sugaar atau Maju adalah dewa ular atau naga dalam mitologi Basque, pasangan dewi Mari, yang bersatu dengannya setiap Jumat untuk menimbulkan badai.
short_description.en: Sugaar or Maju is a serpent or dragon god of Basque mythology, consort of the goddess Mari, who joins her every Friday to raise storms.

long_description.id: Sugaar, juga Sugar, Sugoi, atau Maju, "ular jantan", adalah separuh laki-laki dari dewa Basque pra-Kristen yang berkaitan dengan badai dan guntur. Wujud aslinya ular atau naga, kadang api atau petir. Ia pasangan Mari dan mengunjunginya di Anboto setiap Jumat; pertemuan mereka melahirkan badai dan hujan es dan melambangkan hujan yang menyuburkan bumi. Ia tinggal di gua dan gunung seperti Aralar dan ayah Mikelatz dan Atarrabi.
long_description.en: Sugaar, also Sugar, Sugoi or Maju, 'male serpent', is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity of storms and thunder. His true form is a serpent or dragon, sometimes fire or lightning. He is Mari's consort and visits her at Anboto every Friday; their union brings storms and hail and figures the rain that fertilises the earth. He lives in caves and mountains such as Aralar and fathered Mikelatz and Atarrabi.

long_description.id: Di Betelu ia dianggap roh jahat dan di Ataun momok. Legenda dari Dima menceritakan dua bersaudara yang menemukannya di gua Baltzola; si adik memotong ekornya, dan bertahun-tahun kemudian sabuk merah pemberian Sugaar membakar pohon kastanye. Mitos lain menjadikannya ayah Jaun Zuria, penguasa pertama Biscaya, dari seorang putri Skotlandia.
long_description.en: In Betelu he is an evil spirit and in Ataun a bogeyman. A legend from Dima tells of two brothers who found him in the Baltzola cave; the younger cut his tail, and years later a red belt from Sugaar set a chestnut tree ablaze. Another myth makes him father, by a Scottish princess, of Jaun Zuria, first lord of Biscay.

claims.quote: In Basque mythology, Sugaar (also Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity associated with storms and thunder. He shows may similarities to Herensuge, with Sugaar being much older.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Basque, Sugaar (juga Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) adalah separuh laki-laki dari dewa Basque pra-Kristen yang berkaitan dengan badai dan guntur, dan ia banyak mirip Herensuge meski jauh lebih tua.
statement.en: In Basque mythology Sugaar (also Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity of storms and thunder, much like Herensuge but far older.

claims.quote: Sugaar is sometimes said to take the form of pure fire or lightning, but his true form is usually represented as a serpent or dragon. He is Mari's consort, and is said to visit her at Anboto every Friday.

statement.id: Sugaar kadang berwujud api murni atau petir, tetapi wujud aslinya biasanya ular atau naga; ia pasangan Mari dan konon mengunjunginya di Anboto setiap Jumat.
statement.en: Sugaar sometimes takes the form of pure fire or lightning, but his true form is usually a serpent or dragon; he is Mari's consort and visits her at Anboto every Friday.

claims.quote: The visits are also considered sexual in nature, a reference to how the rain (Sugaar) fertilizes the earth and soil (Mari).

statement.id: Kunjungan itu juga dianggap bersifat seksual, melambangkan hujan (Sugaar) yang menyuburkan bumi dan tanah (Mari).
statement.en: The visits are also seen as sexual, a figure of the rain (Sugaar) fertilising the earth (Mari).

claims.quote: Like Mari, Sugar is said to live in various caves and mountains. One of his homes is said to be the Aralar Mountain Range.

statement.id: Seperti Mari, Sugaar tinggal di berbagai gua dan gunung, salah satunya Pegunungan Aralar.
statement.en: Like Mari he lives in various caves and mountains, one of them the Aralar range.

claims.quote: In Betelu, Sugaar is said to be an evil spirit, and in Ataun, he is used as a bogyman figure.

statement.id: Di Betelu Sugaar dianggap roh jahat, dan di Ataun ia dipakai sebagai momok untuk menakuti anak.
statement.en: In Betelu Sugaar is an evil spirit, and in Ataun a bogeyman.

claims.quote: The pair found Sugaar in a cave in Baltzola, and the younger of the two cut his tail with a stone.

statement.id: Dalam sebuah legenda, dua bersaudara dari Dima menemukan Sugaar di gua Baltzola, dan si adik memotong ekornya dengan batu.
statement.en: In one legend two brothers from Dima found Sugaar in the Baltzola cave, and the younger cut his tail with a stone.

claims.quote: When the brothers met again, the younger brother refused to put the belt on and tied it to a chestnut tree. The tree burst into flames, and they realized that the man must have been Sugaar.

statement.id: Bertahun-tahun kemudian si adik menolak memakai sabuk merah pemberian seorang lelaki misterius dan mengikatkannya ke pohon kastanye, yang langsung terbakar, sehingga mereka sadar lelaki itu Sugaar.
statement.en: Years later the younger brother refused a red belt from a mysterious man and tied it to a chestnut tree, which burst into flames, and they realised the man was Sugaar.

claims.quote: The name Suga(a)r is derived from suge (serpent) and -ar (male), thus "male serpent". The suggestions of a formation based on su (fire) and gar (flame), thus yielding "flame of fire" are considered folk etymology.

statement.id: Nama Sugaar berasal dari suge (ular) dan -ar (jantan), jadi "ular jantan"; tafsiran su (api) + gar (nyala), "nyala api", dianggap etimologi rakyat.
statement.en: Sugaar comes from suge (serpent) and -ar (male), 'male serpent'; the reading su (fire) + gar (flame), 'flame of fire', is considered folk etymology.

claims.quote: L'essentiel de son existence est de se joindre périodiquement (le vendredi, à deux heures de l'après-midi) à Mari dans les montagnes pour y engendrer des orages.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, tugas utamanya adalah bersatu secara berkala dengan Mari di gunung (hari Jumat pukul dua siang) untuk melahirkan badai.
statement.en: According to the French article, his main role is to join Mari periodically in the mountains (on Friday at two in the afternoon) to engender storms.

claims.quote: Additionnellement, il existe un mythe dans lequel il séduit une princesse écossaise dans le village de Mundaka, pour concevoir le mythique premier seigneur de Biscaye, Jaun Zuria.

statement.id: Ada pula mitos bahwa ia menggoda seorang putri Skotlandia di desa Mundaka dan menjadi ayah Jaun Zuria, penguasa pertama Biscaya yang mitis.
statement.en: There is also a myth that he seduced a Scottish princess at Mundaka and fathered Jaun Zuria, the mythical first lord of Biscay.

claims.quote: Maju est considéré comme un génie souterrain qui, en sortant de son antre, s’unit à Mari, provoquant alors une tempête accompagnée de grêle et de grêlons.

statement.id: Maju dianggap roh bawah tanah yang, ketika keluar dari sarangnya dan bersatu dengan Mari, menimbulkan badai disertai hujan es.
statement.en: Maju is considered an underground spirit who, leaving his lair to unite with Mari, brings a storm with hail.

claims.quote: Es una divinidad de carácter masculino, consorte de la diosa Mari (tiene, sin embargo, un papel mucho más oscuro que esta), y padre de Mikelatz (hijo perverso) y Atarrabi (hijo bondadoso).

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ia dewa laki-laki, pasangan dewi Mari dengan peran yang lebih samar, dan ayah Mikelatz (anak jahat) serta Atarrabi (anak baik).
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, he is a male deity, consort of the goddess Mari though with a much dimmer role, and father of Mikelatz (the wicked son) and Atarrabi (the good son).

short_description.id: Laidly Worm dari Spindleston Heugh adalah balada Northumbria tentang seorang putri yang diubah menjadi naga oleh ibu tirinya yang penyihir.
short_description.en: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh is a Northumbrian ballad about a princess turned into a dragon by her witch stepmother.

long_description.id: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh, juga The Laidly Worm of Bamborough, adalah balada Northumbria tentang seorang putri yang diubah menjadi naga, "laidly worm" (naga buruk rupa). Di Kerajaan Northumbria, seorang raja baik di Kastel Bamburgh menikahi penyihir cantik tetapi kejam setelah istrinya wafat. Saat putranya Childe Wynd berada di seberang laut, penyihir itu, iri pada kecantikan Putri Margaret, mengubahnya menjadi naga.
long_description.en: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh, also The Laidly Worm of Bamborough, is a Northumbrian ballad of a princess changed into a dragon, the 'laidly worm' (loathsome serpent) of the title. In the Kingdom of Northumbria a good king at Bamburgh Castle weds a lovely but cruel witch after his wife dies. While his son Childe Wynd is overseas, the witch, envious of Princess Margaret's beauty, turns her into a dragon.

long_description.id: Sang pangeran pulang dan, alih-alih melawan naga itu, menciumnya tiga kali, sehingga sang putri kembali ke wujud aslinya; ia lalu mengubah ratu penyihir menjadi katak dan menjadi raja. Balada ini pertama diterbitkan pada 1778, konon disalin Pendeta Robert Lambe dari naskah Latin tahun 1270, tetapi kini dianggap pemalsuan Lambe yang memakai kisah setempat. Dalam versi Joseph Jacobs, naga itu ditenangkan dengan tujuh sapi per hari.
long_description.en: The prince returns and, rather than fighting the dragon, kisses it three times, and the princess regains her own shape; afterwards he changes the witch-queen into a toad and takes the throne. The ballad was first printed in 1778, supposedly copied by the Reverend Robert Lambe from a Latin manuscript of 1270, but is now thought to be Lambe's forgery drawing on local tales. In Joseph Jacobs's version the dragon is pacified with seven cows a day.

who.en: Princess turned dragon.

role.en: Restored by a kiss.

famous_for.id: Ibu tiri menjadi katak.
famous_for.en: Stepmother turned toad.

did_you_know.id: Dalam balada ini, sang pangeran memulihkan saudarinya bukan dengan bertarung, melainkan dengan mencium naga itu tiga kali.
did_you_know.en: In this ballad the prince restores his sister not by fighting but by kissing the dragon three times.

long_description.id: Uraeus adalah gambaran kobra tegak dalam tradisi Mesir yang melambangkan kekuasaan kerajaan dan otoritas ilahi. Uraeus merupakan lambang dewi Wadjet.
long_description.en: The uraeus is an upright cobra representation in Egyptian tradition symbolizing royal power and divine authority. The uraeus represents the goddess Wadjet.

long_description.id: Pemakaiannya pada mahkota menandakan perlindungan Wadjet terhadap firaun. Nekhbet dan Wadjet menjadi Dua Nyonya yang menjaga Mesir bersatu. Wadjet, yang dilambangkan uraeus, disebut putri Ra dan tokoh kisah Mata Ra. Ensiklopedia pendamping menyebut uraeus sebagai insignia raja berupa kobra Wadjet yang terangkat.
long_description.en: Its use on the crown signifies Wadjet’s protection of the pharaoh. Nekhbet and Wadjet become the Two Ladies protecting unified Egypt. Wadjet, represented by the uraeus, is described as Ra’s daughter and a figure in Eye of Ra stories. The accompanying encyclopedia calls the uraeus the king’s insignia in the form of Wadjet’s rearing cobra.

short_description.id: Xeglun adalah rusa besar langit dalam mitologi Tungusic yang perburuannya oleh Mangi dipercaya menciptakan galaksi Bima Sakti.

long_description.id: Dalam kosmologi Tungusic, Xeglun diyakini sebagai rusa besar surgawi yang melintasi kubah angkasa. Legenda menuturkan bahwa pengejaran terhadap makhluk langit ini oleh sosok Mangi atau Xargi meninggalkan jejak kosmis yang kemudian membentuk formasi galaksi Bima Sakti atau Milky Way.
long_description.en: In Tungusic cosmology, Xeglun is held to be a celestial elk traversing the heavens. Lore recounts that the pursuit of this creature across the sky by Mangi or Xargi left a cosmic trail forming the Milky Way.

short_description.id: Yelbeghen adalah monster pemakan manusia berkepala banyak dalam mitologi bangsa Turkik Siberia, awalnya naga lalu raksasa, yang dalam legenda Altai memangsa Matahari dan Bulan.
short_description.en: Yelbeghen is a many-headed man-eating monster in the mythology of the Turkic peoples of Siberia, first a dragon and later an ogre, that in an Altai legend devours the Sun and Moon.

long_description.id: Yelbeghen adalah monster pemakan manusia berkepala banyak dalam mitologi bangsa Turkik Siberia. Dalam mitos aslinya ia naga atau makhluk mirip ular, tetapi lama-kelamaan menjadi raksasa berkepala banyak; sebagian mitos menggambarkannya sebagai naga bersayap atau raksasa yang menunggang lembu bertanduk 99.
long_description.en: Yelbeghen is a many-headed man-eating monster of the mythology of the Turkic peoples of Siberia. In the original myths it was a dragon or serpent-like creature, but over time it became a many-headed ogre; some myths describe a winged dragon or an ogre riding an ox with 99 horns.

long_description.id: Beberapa epos menampilkan banyak Yelbegen, keturunan Altan Sibaldai, "penyihir emas" pengikut penguasa dunia bawah, termasuk seorang raja bernama Yelmogus. Dalam legenda Altai, Yelbeghen berkepala tujuh membalas dendam kepada Matahari dan Bulan dengan memangsa keduanya, dan Ülgen memanahnya.
long_description.en: Some epics feature many Yelbegen, children of Altan Sibaldai, "the golden witch", a follower of the underworld's lord, including a king named Yelmogus. In an Altai legend the seven-headed Yelbeghen took revenge on the Sun and Moon by eating them, and Ülgen shot arrows at it.

short_description.id: Zitiron atau sea knight adalah makhluk mitologi laut abad pertengahan berwujud kesatria bersenjata dengan ekor ikan.
short_description.en: A zitiron or sea knight is a medieval marine creature with the upper body of an armed knight and the tail of a fish.

long_description.id: Zitiron atau zytiron, juga dikenal sebagai sea knight, merupakan makhluk hibrida lautan pada era Moyen Âge dengan tubuh bagian atas berupa kesatria lengkap berbaju zirah dan bagian bawah berekor ikan. Makhluk ini tercatat dalam karya De natura rerum gubahan Thomas de Cantimpré sekitar tahun 1240, serta diadaptasi oleh Jacob van Maerlant dalam Der Naturen Bloeme pada tahun 1350.
long_description.en: A zitiron or zytiron, known as a sea knight, is a marine hybrid of the Moyen Âge having the upper body of an armed knight and a fish tail. It appears in Thomas de Cantimpré's De natura rerum circa 1240 and Jacob van Maerlant's Der Naturen Bloeme in 1350.

long_description.id: Makhluk ini juga dibahas dalam risalah Hortus sanitatis tahun 1491. Tubuhnya memiliki kulit tebal dan kasar, membawa perisai, serta memiliki lengan kokoh dengan dua jari. Konon zitiron kebal terhadap anak panah dan hanya dapat ditaklukkan menggunakan palu.
long_description.en: The creature is featured in the 1491 text Hortus sanitatis. It possesses rough, hard skin, bears a shield, and has thick arms with only two fingers. Lore states it cannot be slain by arrows, only by hammers.

long_description.id: Antero Vipunen adalah raksasa dalam mitologi dan lagu rune Finlandia. Ia terkubur di bawah tanah dan menyimpan mantra serta pengetahuan yang sangat berharga. Dalam puisi rakyat Balto-Finnik ia orang mati atau raksasa yang berbaring di bawah tanah, seorang tietäjä (dukun bijak) pemilik mantra-mantra purba.
long_description.en: Finnish myth and runic song tell of Antero Vipunen, a giant lying buried beneath the earth who keeps priceless spells and lore. Balto-Finnic folk poetry makes him a dead man or giant asleep underground, a tietäjä (wise sorcerer) holding ancient incantations.

long_description.id: Ketika Väinämöinen membutuhkan tiga kata ajaib (luotteet) untuk menyelesaikan perahunya, ia mendatangi Vipunen dan masuk ke dalam tubuhnya. Di dalam perut Vipunen ia membuat tempat tempa dan memukul-mukul sehingga Vipunen kesakitan, lalu memuntahkannya sambil memberikan kata-kata yang dibutuhkan. Menurut Matti Kuusi, tokoh utama aslinya mungkin Lemminkäinen.
long_description.en: When Väinämöinen needs three magic words (luotteet) to finish his boat, he seeks out Vipunen and ends up inside his body. Inside the giant he builds a forge and hammers away until Vipunen, in pain, spits him out and hands over the words. Matti Kuusi thought the original hero was probably Lemminkäinen.

long_description.id: Dalam bahasa Estonia vibu berarti busur, sehingga di Estonia Vipunen dipahami sebagai pemanah ulung. Dalam banyak versi ia juga disebut pemasang jerat, sesuai namanya: vipu adalah sejenis alat jerat.
long_description.en: In Estonian vibu means a bow, so in Estonia Vipunen was taken to be a skilled archer. Many versions also call him a trapper, as his name suggests: a vipu is a kind of snare.

short_description.id: Archura adalah roh hutan pengubah wujud dalam mitologi Turkik dan Chuvash yang melindungi satwa liar dan bisa menyesatkan pengembara.
short_description.en: Archura is a shapeshifting forest spirit of Turkic and Chuvash mythology who protects wildlife and can lead wanderers astray.

long_description.id: Archura adalah roh hutan dalam mitologi Turkik, dan dalam mitologi Chuvash dikenal sebagai roh penguasa hutan; namanya dalam bahasa Chuvash berarti "setengah manusia". Ia biasanya tampil sebagai lelaki berambut dan berjanggut rumput hidup, kadang berekor, berkuku, dan bertanduk, dan dapat berubah ukuran dari sehelai rumput hingga pohon tinggi. Ia dekat dengan serigala abu-abu dan memberi tahu hewan serta burung kapan harus bermigrasi.
long_description.en: Archura is a forest spirit of Turkic mythology, known in Chuvash mythology as the spirit and master of the forest; its Chuvash name means "half human". He usually appears as a man with hair and beard of living grass, sometimes with tail, hooves and horns, and can change size from a blade of grass to a tall tree. He is close to the grey wolf and tells animals and birds when to migrate.

long_description.id: Archura suka iseng: ia meniru suara orang yang dikenal pengembara, memikat mereka ke gua, dan menggelitiki mereka sampai mati. Namun ia tidak sepenuhnya jahat, karena juga menjaga ternak agar tidak tersesat ke dalam hutan.
long_description.en: Archura is mischievous: he mimics voices wanderers know, lures them to caves and tickles them to death. Yet he is not wholly evil, since he also keeps cattle from straying into the forest.

short_description.id: Asrai adalah sejenis peri air dalam folklor dan sastra Inggris, biasanya perempuan yang tinggal di danau; mungkin ciptaan penyair Robert Williams Buchanan.
short_description.en: The asrai is a kind of water fairy in English folklore and literature, usually female and lake-dwelling; it may be an invention of the poet Robert Williams Buchanan.

long_description.id: Asrai adalah sejenis peri air dalam folklor dan sastra Inggris, biasanya digambarkan perempuan, tinggal di danau, dan mirip putri duyung serta nixie. Etimologinya tidak diketahui; ejaan Asrey atau ashray kadang muncul. Kemunculan cetak tertuanya adalah puisi "The Asrai" karya penyair Skotlandia Robert Williams Buchanan, terbit April 1872, sehingga asrai mungkin ciptaannya sendiri. Dalam puisi Buchanan, asrai adalah makhluk pucat dan lembut, lebih tua dari manusia, yang takut cahaya dan hidup di bawah danau.
long_description.en: The asrai is a type of water fairy in English folklore and literature, generally female, living in lakes and resembling the mermaid and the nixie. Nobody knows where the word comes from; it is sometimes spelled Asrey or ashray. Its earliest known printed appearance is 'The Asrai', a poem by the Scottish poet Robert Williams Buchanan first published in April 1872, so the being may be his own creation. Buchanan's asrai are pale, gentle creatures older than mankind who shun light and live under a lake.

long_description.id: Asrai kembali dikenal lewat karya pencerita Inggris Ruth Tongue, yang keandalannya sebagai folkloris diragukan. Tongue mengaitkan kisahnya dengan Cheshire, Shropshire dan perbatasan Wales: asrai pemalu, sangat cantik, berkaki selaput dan berambut hijau, hidup ratusan tahun dan muncul ke permukaan sekali seabad untuk mandi cahaya bulan. Seorang nelayan yang menangkap asrai terbakar kulitnya oleh sentuhan tangannya yang dingin, dan asrai itu mencair menjadi genangan air karena terlalu lama terkena matahari.
long_description.en: Renewed interest came through the British storyteller Ruth Tongue, whose reliability as a folklorist has been doubted. She located asrai tales in Cheshire, Shropshire and the Welsh Border: shy, very beautiful beings with webbed feet and green hair, living for centuries and rising to the surface once every hundred years to bathe in moonlight. A fisherman who caught one was burned by the touch of its cold hands, and the asrai melted into a puddle because it had been in the sun too long.

short_description.id: Baloz atau bajloz adalah tokoh legenda dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, lawan para pahlawan Albania, yang kadang digambarkan sebagai monster laut.
short_description.en: Baloz or bajloz is a legendary figure of Albanian mythology and folklore, an antagonist of the Albanian heroes, sometimes described as a sea monster.

long_description.id: Baloz atau bajloz muncul dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania sebagai lawan para pahlawan legendaris Albania, dan kadang digambarkan sebagai monster laut. Dalam rapsodi rakyat Albania ia dipandang sebagai bahaya yang datang dari laut; menurut Arshi Pipa, ia digambarkan sebagai raksasa jahat dan kadang monster.
long_description.en: Baloz or bajloz appears in Albanian mythology and folklore as an antagonist of the legendary Albanian heroes, and is sometimes described as a sea monster. In Albanian folk rhapsodies he is seen as a danger coming from the sea; according to Arshi Pipa he is described as an evil giant and at times a monster.

long_description.id: Tokoh ini ditemukan dalam banyak mitos dan legenda Albania tentang pertarungan ketika para bangsawan seperti Constantin, Muji, Halili, dan Gjergj Elez Alia melawannya; ia juga muncul dalam Lagu-Lagu Pejuang Perbatasan Albania. Dalam legenda terkenal, Gjergj Elez Alia melawan bajloz yang datang dari laut dan mengalahkannya, padahal ia baru pulih dari sakit panjang akibat sembilan luka perang.
long_description.en: The figure turns up in many Albanian myths and legends in which nobles like Constantin, Muji, Halili and Gjergj Elez Alia fight him; he also appears in the Albanian Songs of the Frontier Warriors. In a famous legend, Gjergj Elez Alia fought the bajloz who came from the sea and defeated him, although he had just risen from a long illness caused by nine war wounds.

long_description.id: Kata baloz atau bajloz tampaknya berasal dari kata Latin baiulus. Maximilian Lambertz mengusulkan bahwa namanya berasal dari kata Italia bailo, gelar duta besar Venesia untuk Utsmaniyah. Secara historis, tokoh ini berkaitan dengan demonisasi Republik Santo Markus (Venesia).
long_description.en: The word baloz or bajloz seems to derive from the Latin baiulus. Maximilian Lambertz suggested that the name comes from the Italian bailo, the title of the Venetian ambassador to the Ottomans. Historically, the figure relates to the demonisation of the Republic of Saint Mark (Venice).

literal_meaning.id: dari kata Latin baiulus; dalam bahasa Latin berarti pengawas atau pemelihara
literal_meaning.en: from the Latin baiulus, meaning overseer or keeper

short_description.id: Bardha ("yang putih") adalah tokoh mitologi Albania yang tampil sebagai zana (nimfa) atau ora (dewi takdir) pembawa keberuntungan; ia digambarkan sebagai sosok pucat berkabut.
short_description.en: The bardha ("the white one") is an Albanian mythological figure appearing as a zana (nymph) or an ora (Fate goddess) of good luck; she is described as a pale, misty figure.

long_description.id: Bardha, bentuk jamaknya bardhat, adalah tokoh mitologi Albania yang tampil sebagai zana (nimfa) atau sebagai ora (dewi takdir) yang terkait dengan keberuntungan. Namanya berarti "yang putih". Bardhat digambarkan sebagai sosok pucat berkabut atau penampakan perempuan berbaju putih yang tinggal di gunung berkabut dan di dunia bawah, dan kadang dianggap roh gunung atau roh alam.
long_description.en: In Albanian myth the bardha (plural bardhat) takes the shape either of a nymph, a zana, or of a Fate goddess, an ora, and is linked with good fortune. The name means "the white one". Bardhat are described as pale, nebulous figures or apparitions of women in white living on misty mountains and in the underworld, and are sometimes seen as mountain or nature spirits.

long_description.id: Bardhat umumnya tidak peduli pada manusia, tetapi mencelakai orang yang menyinggung mereka; orang yang tak sengaja menginjaknya bisa lumpuh atau bisu, dan penunggang kuda bisa terjatuh bila kudanya menginjak mereka. Untuk menenangkan mereka, terutama setelah kecelakaan, orang meninggalkan gula, kue, atau madu di tanah tempat kejadian dan memuji bardha.
long_description.en: Bardhat are generally indifferent to humans but harm those who offend them; someone who steps on one by accident may be paralysed or struck mute, and a rider may fall if the horse treads on them. To appease them, especially after an accident, people leave sugar, cakes or honey on the ground at the spot and speak well of the bardha.

long_description.id: Penduduk Pegunungan Dukagjini percaya ada tiga jenis ora: e Bardha (Yang Putih) membagikan keberuntungan, e Verdha (Yang Kuning) membawa nasib buruk dan mantra jahat, dan e Zeza (Yang Hitam) menentukan kematian. Dalam cerita rakyat lama yang menganggapnya mirip nimfa, bardha serupa dengan zana e malit.
long_description.en: The people of the Dukagjini Mountains believed in three kinds of ora: e Bardha (The White One) gives good luck, e Verdha (The Yellow One) brings bad luck and evil spells, and e Zeza (The Black One) decides death. In old folklore that sees them as nymph-like, a bardha resembles the zana e malit.

short_description.id: Grant adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Inggris yang digambarkan seperti anak kuda yang berdiri di atas kaki belakang dan berlari di jalan-jalan sebagai peringatan bahaya api.
short_description.en: The Grant is a creature of English folklore described as a foal standing on its hind legs that runs through the streets as a warning of fire.

long_description.id: Grant, atau Gyant, adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Inggris yang dijelaskan dalam karya Latin abad pertengahan Otia Imperialia oleh Gervase dari Tilbury. Menurut kutipan dari Gervase, ia sejenis iblis yang berwujud seperti anak kuda berumur setahun, berdiri tegak pada kaki belakang, dengan mata berkilau.
long_description.en: The Grant (also spelled Gyant) is an English folklore creature known from the medieval Latin Otia Imperialia of Gervase of Tilbury. According to the passage quoted from Gervase, it is a kind of demon that looks like a yearling foal, upright on its hind legs, with sparkling eyes.

long_description.id: Bila bahaya mengancam pada hari atau malam berikutnya, Grant berlari di jalan-jalan dan memancing anjing menggonggong. Peristiwa ini memperingatkan penduduk agar waspada terhadap api, sehingga Gervase menyebutnya iblis yang bersahabat sekalipun ia menakuti orang yang melihatnya.
long_description.en: When danger is impending the following day or night, the Grant runs about the streets and provokes the dogs to bark. This warns the inhabitants to beware of fire, so Gervase calls it a friendly demon even though it frightens those who see it.

long_description.id: Catatan Gervase adalah satu-satunya sumber abad pertengahan yang diketahui yang menyebut nama makhluk ini. Francis Young mengaitkannya dengan motif momok mirip kuda di jalan terpencil di Britania dan Irlandia, sedangkan Joseph Pentangelo berpendapat bahwa ia mungkin seekor kelinci liar dan gambaran Gervase dipoles oleh Gervase atau narasumbernya.
long_description.en: No other medieval source is known to name the creature besides Gervase. Francis Young links it to the motif of horse-like bogies on isolated roads in Britain and Ireland, while Joseph Pentangelo argues that it was probably a hare and that Gervase's description was embellished by Gervase or his informant.

claims.quote: Grant, or Gyant, is a creature of English folklore described in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury.

statement.id: Grant, atau Gyant, adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Inggris yang dijelaskan dalam karya Latin abad pertengahan Otia Imperialia oleh Gervase dari Tilbury.
statement.en: Grant, or Gyant, is a creature of English folklore described in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury.

claims.quote: Gervase's account is the only known medieval source to name the creature.

statement.id: Catatan Gervase adalah satu-satunya sumber abad pertengahan yang diketahui yang menyebut nama makhluk ini.
statement.en: Gervase's account is the only known medieval source to name the creature.

claims.quote: Francis Young links the Grant to a wider motif in Britain and Ireland of horse-like bogies encountered on isolated roads by travellers, such as the púca, kelpie, or shagfoal

statement.id: Francis Young mengaitkan Grant dengan motif yang lebih luas di Britania dan Irlandia tentang momok mirip kuda yang ditemui pelancong di jalan terpencil, seperti púca, kelpie, atau shagfoal.
statement.en: Francis Young links the Grant to a wider motif in Britain and Ireland of horse-like bogies met by travellers on isolated roads, such as the púca, kelpie or shagfoal.

claims.quote: Joseph Pentangelo instead argues that it was probably a hare, and that the description in the Otia Imperialia may reflect embellishment by Gervase or his informant.

statement.id: Joseph Pentangelo sebaliknya berpendapat bahwa makhluk itu mungkin seekor kelinci liar (hare), dan bahwa gambaran dalam Otia Imperialia mungkin hasil pemolesan oleh Gervase atau narasumbernya.
statement.en: Joseph Pentangelo instead argues that it was probably a hare, and that the description in the Otia Imperialia may reflect embellishment by Gervase or his informant.

claims.quote: in England a certain kind of demon whom in their language they call Grant

statement.id: Gervase (dikutip Keightley) menulis bahwa di Inggris ada sejenis iblis (demon) yang dalam bahasa mereka disebut Grant.
statement.en: Gervase (as quoted by Keightley) writes that in England there is a certain kind of demon whom they call Grant in their language.

claims.quote: like a yearling foal, erect on its hind legs, with sparkling eyes.

statement.id: Ia berwujud seperti anak kuda berumur setahun, berdiri tegak dengan kaki belakang, bermata berkilau.
statement.en: It looks like a yearling foal, erect on its hind legs, with sparkling eyes.

claims.quote: If there is any danger impending on the following day or night, it runs about the streets provoking the dogs to bark

statement.id: Bila ada bahaya yang mengancam pada hari atau malam berikutnya, ia berlari di jalan-jalan memancing anjing menggonggong.
statement.en: If danger is impending the following day or night, it runs about the streets provoking the dogs to bark.

claims.quote: This illusion warns the inhabitants to beware of fire, and the friendly demon, while he terrifies those who see him, puts by his coming the ignorant on their guard.

statement.id: Tipuan ini memperingatkan penduduk agar waspada terhadap api; iblis yang bersahabat itu menakuti orang yang melihatnya tetapi dengan kedatangannya membuat orang yang tidak tahu menjadi siaga.
statement.en: This illusion warns the inhabitants to beware of fire; the friendly demon terrifies those who see him but by his coming puts the ignorant on their guard.

summary.id: Gervase menyebutnya sejenis iblis (demon) yang bersahabat.
summary.en: Gervase calls it a kind of friendly demon.

summary.id: Francis Young mengaitkannya dengan momok mirip kuda di jalan terpencil.
summary.en: Francis Young links it to horse-like bogies of isolated roads.

summary.id: Joseph Pentangelo berpendapat bahwa ia mungkin seekor kelinci liar.
summary.en: Joseph Pentangelo argues it was probably a hare.

short_description.id: Penyihir Anaga, menurut kepercayaan populer Kepulauan Canaria, adalah perempuan yang mengadakan pertemuan sihir di pegunungan Anaga, Tenerife, dan kemudian dianggap penyihir-vampir pengisap darah bayi.
short_description.en: The Witches of Anaga, by Canarian popular belief, were women holding covens in the Anaga mountains of Tenerife, later held to be witch-vampires who sucked infants' blood.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan populer, Penyihir Anaga adalah perempuan yang mengabdi pada perkumpulan sihir di pegunungan Anaga di timur laut Pulau Tenerife, Kepulauan Canaria, Spanyol. Ritual mereka diadakan di punggung pegunungan antara San Andrés dan Taganana, di tempat bernama El Bailadero, yang merujuk pada tarian para penyihir mengelilingi api unggun. Setelah pertemuan itu mereka konon turun ke pantai untuk mandi telanjang.
long_description.en: Popular belief held the Witches of Anaga to be women bound to covens in the Anaga mountains of north-eastern Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. Their rites took place on the ridge between San Andrés and Taganana, at a spot called El Bailadero after the witches' dances around a bonfire. After the gatherings they supposedly went down to the coast to bathe naked.

long_description.id: Lama-kelamaan, karena pengaruh kisah vampir dari Eropa Timur, mitos itu menambahkan unsur mengisap darah sehingga mereka menjadi penyihir-vampir yang mengisap darah bayi yang tidur di buaian. Ada pula teori bahwa legenda ini berasal dari ritual pagan bangsa Guanche untuk memanggil hujan, yang oleh Gereja Katolik dianggap sihir. Unsur serupa ada di tempat lain di Spanyol, seperti guaxa di Asturias dan guajona di Cantabria.
long_description.en: Over time, under the influence of Eastern European vampire stories, the myth gained a blood-drinking element, turning them into witch-vampires who sucked the blood of babies asleep in their cradles. Another theory traces the legend to Guanche pagan rain rituals that the Catholic Church deemed witchcraft. The same motif appears elsewhere in Spain, as with the guaxa of Asturias and the guajona of Cantabria.

short_description.id: Zburător ("yang terbang") adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, roh pengembara yang mendatangi gadis-gadis pada malam hari dalam rupa pemuda tampan.
short_description.en: The zburător ("flyer") is a supernatural being of Romanian folklore, a roving spirit who visits maidens by night in the guise of a handsome youth.

long_description.id: Zburător atau sburător, yang berarti "yang terbang", adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, digambarkan sebagai roh pengembara yang bercinta dengan gadis-gadis pada malam hari. Ia disamakan dengan inkubus: iblis jahat yang mendatangi perempuan dalam mimpi dengan menyamar sebagai pemuda tampan. Di beberapa daerah ia disebut zmeu, atau dianggap salah satu wujud zmeu.
long_description.en: Known as zburător or sburător, "the flyer", this Romanian folk being is pictured as a wandering spirit who makes love to girls at night. He is compared to an incubus, a malicious demon that comes to women in dreams disguised as a handsome young man. In some regions he is called a zmeu, or seen as one of the shapes a zmeu can take.

long_description.id: Dimitrie Cantemir menulis tentangnya dalam Descriptio Moldaviae (1714–1716): menurut kepercayaan orang Moldavia, ia hantu berupa pemuda tampan yang datang tengah malam kepada perempuan, terutama pengantin baru, dan tidak dapat dilihat orang lain. Penyair Ion Heliade Rădulescu mengolah mitos ini dalam puisi Zburătorul (1843), dan George Călinescu menggolongkannya sebagai salah satu dari empat mitos dasar puisi rakyat Rumania.
long_description.en: Dimitrie Cantemir wrote of him in Descriptio Moldaviae (1714–1716): Moldavians believed he was a ghost in the form of a handsome youth who came at midnight to women, especially newlyweds, unseen by anyone else. The poet Ion Heliade Rădulescu reworked the myth in the poem Zburătorul (1843), and George Călinescu counted it among the four fundamental myths of Romanian folk poetry.

short_description.id: Kurupi adalah tokoh mitologi Guaraní, salah satu dari tujuh anak mengerikan Tau dan Kerana, yang ditakuti sebagai penculik perempuan dan dikenal karena alat kelaminnya yang sangat panjang.
short_description.en: Kurupi is a figure of Guaraní mythology, one of the seven monstrous children of Tau and Kerana, feared as an abductor of women and known for an extremely long penis.

long_description.id: Kurupi atau Curupi adalah tokoh mitologi Guaraní dan salah satu dari tujuh anak mengerikan Tau dan Kerana. Ia termasuk sedikit tokoh legenda yang masih menonjol dalam budaya masa kini di wilayah berbahasa Guaraní. Ia paling dikenal karena alat kelaminnya yang sangat panjang hingga melilit pinggang, dan ditakuti sebagai penculik serta pemerkosa perempuan.
long_description.en: Kurupi or Curupi is a figure of Guaraní mythology and one of the seven monstrous children of Tau and Kerana. He is one of the few legendary figures still prominent in present-day Guaraní-speaking cultures. He is best known for an extremely long penis that winds around his waist, and is feared as an abductor and rapist of women.

long_description.id: Versi Paraguay modern menggambarkannya pendek, buruk rupa, dan berbulu, dengan kaki menghadap ke belakang yang menyesatkan pelacak ke semak belukar. Sebagian narasumber menyebut ia bisa menjadi tak terlihat, dan ia juga dianggap pelindung alam. Penampilannya sering disamakan dengan Pombero.
long_description.en: The modern Paraguayan version makes him short, ugly and hairy, with backward feet that lead trackers into the thicket. Some informants say he can turn invisible, and he is also seen as a protector of nature. His appearance is often compared to Pombero's.

short_description.id: Lauma (dalam bahasa Lituania Laumė) adalah roh hutan mirip peri dan roh pelindung anak yatim dalam mitologi Baltik Timur, yang semula roh langit.
short_description.en: Lauma (Lithuanian Laumė) is a forest spirit resembling a fairy in Eastern Baltic mythology, a protector of orphans who began as a spirit of the sky.

long_description.id: Lauma dari Latvia atau Laumė dari Lituania adalah roh hutan mirip peri dan roh pelindung anak yatim dalam mitologi Baltik Timur. Semula ia roh langit, tetapi belas kasihnya pada penderitaan manusia membawanya turun ke bumi untuk berbagi nasib manusia. Satu sumber menyebut para Laumė sebagai dewi tertua dalam mitologi Lituania.
long_description.en: In Eastern Baltic mythology, the Latvian Lauma or Lithuanian Laumė is a forest spirit resembling a fairy and a protector of orphans. Originally a sky spirit, her compassion for human suffering brought her down to earth to share the human lot. One source calls the Laumės the oldest goddesses of Lithuanian mythology.

long_description.id: Laumė dapat muncul dalam wujud hewan, seperti kuda betina, kambing betina, beruang, dan anjing. Kemudian mereka berwujud lebih mirip manusia: biasanya berkaki cakar burung dan tampak sebagai perempuan berkepala atau bertubuh bawah kambing betina. Mereka tinggal di dekat danau, di pemandian yang ditinggalkan, di pulau danau, atau di hutan lebat, dan takut pada perkakas dari besi.
long_description.en: Laumės could appear as animals such as mares, female goats, bears and dogs. Later they took a more human form: usually with birds' claws for feet, looking like women whose head or lower half was that of a she-goat. They lived near lakes, in abandoned bath-houses, on lake islands or in dense forests, and feared iron tools.

long_description.id: Sifat mereka mendua. Satu sumber menyebut mereka berbahaya bagi laki-laki maupun perempuan, sementara sumber lain menggambarkan mereka sebagai peri yang disukai dalam cerita rakyat, mengikuti dewi takdir Laima, memintal, menenun, dan mencuci, menolong orang baik, tetapi menghukum perempuan jahat dan malas. Dalam bahasa Lituania, pelangi disebut laumės juosta, "selempang Laumė".
long_description.en: Their nature is two-sided. One source calls them dangerous to both men and women, while another describes them as popular fairies of folklore who follow the fate goddess Laima, spin, weave and wash, help good people, but punish wicked and lazy women. In Lithuanian the rainbow is called laumės juosta, "Laumė's sash".

short_description.id: Lugat adalah makhluk mirip vampir dalam mitologi Albania, mayat hidup yang berdiam di kegelapan, bisa terbang, dan menyerang korbannya saat tidur.
short_description.en: The lugat is a vampire-like being of Albanian mythology, an undead that dwells in darkness, can fly and attacks its victims in their sleep.

long_description.id: Lugat atau liogat adalah makhluk mirip vampir dalam mitologi Albania. Arshi Pipa menggambarkannya sebagai jiwa tersiksa yang dimuntahkan bumi karena suatu kejahatan berat. Lugat berdiam di bayang-bayang dan tempat yang tak pernah terkena sinar matahari, seperti sumur, reruntuhan tua, dan gua; rupanya menakutkan dan ia sangat ganas.
long_description.en: The lugat or liogat is a vampire-like being of Albanian mythology. Arshi Pipa described it as a tormented soul cast out by the earth for some grave wrongdoing. Lugats dwell in shadows and places never touched by sunlight, such as wells, old ruins and caves; they look frightening and are extremely violent.

long_description.id: Lugat bisa terbang dan menunggang angin, menyerang korban saat tidur, dan memikat orang, terutama anak-anak, dari kegelapan. Mereka sering dipercaya mengenakan kulit orang mati dan berkuku panjang. Sebagai mayat hidup mereka tak bisa dibunuh pada malam hari, tetapi bisa dibakar bila tertangkap di makamnya.
long_description.en: A lugat can fly and ride the winds, attacks victims in their sleep and lures people, especially children, out of the dark. They are often believed to wear a dead person's skin and have long fingernails. As undead they cannot be killed at night, but can be burnt if caught in their graves.

long_description.id: Di Kosovo dipercaya bahwa orang mati bisa bangkit sebagai lugat bila tidak diletakkan besi di dekatnya, karena besi menjauhkan roh. Menurut Hahn, orang utara percaya orang Kristen tak pernah menjadi lugat, sedangkan di selatan tidak ada pembedaan agama. Nama lugat mungkin berasal dari Latin Vulgar *lupus peccatus, dan kata llugat juga dipakai untuk orang jahat.
long_description.en: In Kosovo it was believed that the dead could rise as lugats if no iron was placed beside them, since iron keeps spirits away. According to Hahn, northerners held that Christians never became lugats, whereas in the south there was no religious distinction. The name may come from Vulgar Latin *lupus peccatus, and the word llugat is also used for a wicked person.

short_description.id: Marțolea adalah entitas demonik dalam mitologi Rumania yang berwujud kambing berkepala manusia dan menghukum perempuan yang bekerja pada malam Selasa.
short_description.en: Marțolea is a demonic entity of Romanian mythology, shaped like a goat with a human head, that punishes women who work on Tuesday evenings.

long_description.id: Marțolea adalah entitas demonik dalam mitologi Rumania, terutama di Bucovina dan Maramureș, walau menurut Simeon Florea Marian ia dikenal di seluruh wilayah Rumania. Namanya juga Marț-sara atau Marți Seara, "Selasa Malam". Ia tinggal di pegunungan dan turun pada malam Selasa untuk memikat dengan nyanyiannya dan menghukum perempuan yang memintal wol, menjahit, merebus cucian, atau memanggang roti pada hari itu.
long_description.en: Marțolea is a demonic entity of Romanian mythology, especially in Bucovina and Maramureș, though according to Simeon Florea Marian it is known across all Romanian territory. It is also called Marț-sara or Marți Seara, "Tuesday Evening". It lives in the mountains and comes down on Tuesday nights to lure with its singing and punish women who spin wool, sow, boil laundry or bake bread that day.

long_description.id: Biasanya ia berwujud kambing berkepala mirip manusia dengan tanduk dan kuku, tetapi bisa menjadi perempuan tua berpakaian putih, prajurit, atau lelaki tampan sesuai siapa yang ditemuinya. Hukumannya kejam: ia melempar banyak gelendong lewat cerobong yang harus diisi benang, ditenun, dan dijahit menjadi pakaian sebelum fajar, dan yang gagal akan mati.
long_description.en: Usually it has the form of a goat with a human-like head, horns and hooves, but it can become an old woman in white, a soldier or a handsome man depending on whom it meets. Its punishment is cruel: it throws many spindles down the chimney that must be filled with thread, woven and sewn into a garment by dawn, and whoever fails dies.

long_description.id: Marțolea juga membalas kebaikan: perempuan yang menghormati hari Selasa mendapat telur atau bunga gunung di ambang pintu, dan sebagai pelindung 1 Maret ia memberi gadis pemakai mărțișor sekeping koin perak yang dikalungkan sepanjang tahun. Doina Ruști juga menggambarkannya sebagai kekasih jahat yang memakan jantung gadis, dan menyamakan wujud hewannya dengan Silenus, Pan, dan Mars.
long_description.en: Marțolea also rewards: women who honour Tuesday find eggs or mountain flowers at their door, and as patron of 1 March it gives girls who wear the mărțișor a silver coin worn at the neck all year. Doina Ruști also describes it as a malefic lover who eats girls' hearts, and likens its animal forms to Silenus, Pan and Mars.

claims.quote: Marțolea is a demonic entity in Romanian mythology (especially in the regions of Bucovina and Maramureș). The entity's gender is unclear, as it can shapeshift at will. It lives up in the mountains and descends on Tuesday nights to lure with its singing and punish the women caught working.

statement.id: Marțolea adalah entitas demonik dalam mitologi Rumania, terutama di Bucovina dan Maramureș; jenis kelaminnya tidak jelas karena ia bisa berubah wujud sesuka hati, ia tinggal di pegunungan dan turun pada malam Selasa untuk memikat dengan nyanyiannya dan menghukum perempuan yang kedapatan bekerja.
statement.en: Marțolea is a demonic entity of Romanian mythology, especially in Bucovina and Maramureș; its gender is unclear since it can shapeshift at will, and it lives in the mountains and comes down on Tuesday nights to lure with its singing and punish women caught working.

claims.quote: Also known as Marț-sara or Marți Seara (the old Romanian words for "Tuesday Evening"), it is a malefic entity who demands the semi-holy day of Tuesday to be respected and who forbids four women's chores: spinning of the wool, sowing, boiling laundry and baking bread.

statement.id: Dikenal juga sebagai Marț-sara atau Marți Seara ("Selasa Malam" dalam bahasa Rumania lama), ia entitas jahat yang menuntut hari Selasa yang setengah suci dihormati dan melarang empat pekerjaan perempuan: memintal wol, menjahit, merebus cucian, dan memanggang roti.
statement.en: Also called Marț-sara or Marți Seara (old Romanian for "Tuesday Evening"), it is a malefic entity that demands the semi-holy day of Tuesday be respected and forbids four women's chores: spinning wool, sowing, boiling laundry and baking bread.

claims.quote: Usually its form is of a goat with a human-like head, horns and hooves. It can shapeshift into an ugly, old woman dressed all in white, a soldier or as a handsome man. To married women, it shows as an old woman; to married men as a virgin, and to unmarried women as a young charming man.

statement.id: Biasanya ia berwujud kambing berkepala mirip manusia, bertanduk dan berkuku belah; ia bisa menjadi perempuan tua buruk rupa berpakaian serba putih, prajurit, atau lelaki tampan; kepada perempuan bersuami ia tampil sebagai perempuan tua, kepada lelaki beristri sebagai perawan, dan kepada perempuan lajang sebagai pemuda memikat.
statement.en: Usually it has the form of a goat with a human-like head, horns and hooves; it can become an ugly old woman all in white, a soldier or a handsome man; to married women it appears as an old woman, to married men as a virgin, and to unmarried women as a charming young man.

claims.quote: Marțolea este un personaj mitologic, răspândit pe întreg teritoriul românesc, după cum precizează Simeon Florea Marian (1847-1907), în Mitologie românească

statement.id: Menurut Simeon Florea Marian (1847–1907) dalam Mitologie românească, Marțolea adalah tokoh mitologi yang tersebar di seluruh wilayah Rumania.
statement.en: According to Simeon Florea Marian (1847–1907) in Mitologie românească, Marțolea is a mythological figure spread across the whole Romanian territory.

claims.quote: Marțolea patronează serile de marți, din care cauză se mai numește și Marțsara, dar este și patronul zilei de 1 Martie, respectiv al Mărțișorului. ... Fericit că fetele îl poartă, el dăruiește un mart sau un mărțișor, adică un ban de argint curat, care se poartă la gât tot anul.

statement.id: Marțolea menaungi malam-malam Selasa (marți), sehingga disebut juga Marțsara, dan juga pelindung tanggal 1 Maret (Martie), yakni Mărțișor; senang melihat gadis-gadis memakainya, ia menghadiahkan mart atau mărțișor, yaitu koin perak murni yang dikalungkan sepanjang tahun.
statement.en: Marțolea patronises Tuesday (marți) evenings, hence also the name Marțsara, and is also patron of 1 March (Martie), that is of the Mărțișor; glad to see girls wearing it, it gives a mart or mărțișor, a coin of pure silver worn at the neck all year.

claims.quote: Pedeapsa administrată de Marțolea era de-a dreptul sadică: le arunca împricinatelor pe horn o puzderie de fuse, pe care bietele femei trebuiau să le umple cu lână toarsă. Din firul care rezulta trebuiau să îi țeasă o pânză și să-i facă din ea o haină până în zori. Cine nu reușea, murea.

statement.id: Hukuman dari Marțolea sungguh kejam: ia melemparkan banyak sekali gelendong lewat cerobong kepada perempuan yang bersalah, yang harus mereka isi dengan benang wol; dari benang itu mereka harus menenun kain dan menjahit pakaian untuknya sebelum fajar, dan yang gagal akan mati.
statement.en: Marțolea's punishment was downright sadistic: it threw a host of spindles down the chimney to the guilty women, who had to fill them with spun wool, weave cloth from the thread and make it a garment by dawn; whoever failed died.

claims.quote: În Dicționar de teme și simboluri de Doina Ruști, Marțolea apare și ca îndrăgostit malefic, care mănâncă inima fetelor de care se îndrăgostește. Zoomorfismele sale îl apropie de Silen, de Pan și de Marte.

statement.id: Dalam Dicționar de teme și simboluri karya Doina Ruști, Marțolea juga tampil sebagai kekasih jahat yang memakan jantung gadis yang ia cintai, dan wujud hewannya mendekatkannya pada Silenus, Pan, dan Mars (Silen, Pan, Marte).
statement.en: In Doina Ruști's Dicționar de teme și simboluri, Marțolea also appears as a malefic lover who eats the hearts of the girls it falls for, and its animal forms bring it close to Silenus, Pan and Mars (Silen, Pan, Marte).

claims.quote: Marțolea repays the women who keep the Tuesday day sacred by leaving them eggs on their doorstep or flowers from the highest mountains in Bukovina.

statement.id: Marțolea membalas perempuan yang menyucikan hari Selasa dengan meninggalkan telur di ambang pintu atau bunga dari pegunungan tertinggi di Bukovina.
statement.en: Marțolea repays women who keep Tuesday holy by leaving eggs on their doorstep or flowers from the highest mountains of Bukovina.
