short_description.id: Moryana adalah roh laut perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Slavia, mungkin seorang dewi, putri Tsar Laut yang menguasai angin dari laut.
short_description.en: Moryana is a female sea spirit of Slavic folklore, possibly a goddess, the Sea Tsar's daughter who rules the winds from the sea.

long_description.id: Moryana adalah roh laut perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Slavia, mungkin seorang dewi; A. M. Remizov menyebutnya dewi laut dan penguasa angin. Ia vodyanitsa laut dan putri Tsar Laut. Kadang moryany disebut sebagai banyak roh laut, semacam rusalka laut yang mengancam kapal, tetapi biasanya Moryana digambarkan sebagai satu sosok.
long_description.en: Slavic folklore tells of Moryana, a spirit of the sea who may once have been a goddess. Writer A. M. Remizov calls her goddess of the sea and mistress of the winds. She was a sea vodyanitsa and the Sea Tsar's daughter. At times the moryany were said to be many sea spirits, a marine kind of rusalka threatening ships, but Moryana was usually a single figure.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari kata more, "laut", dengan akhiran perempuan -yana, kira-kira "dia yang dari laut". Di beberapa daerah Rusia namanya dipakai untuk angin dingin dan keras yang bertiup dari laut ke darat. Karena namanya mirip Morana, ia kadang disamakan dengan dewi itu dan disebut dewi kematian.
long_description.en: Her name comes from more, "sea", with the feminine ending -yana, roughly "she of the sea". In some Russian regions the name is used for the cold, harsh winds blowing from sea to land. Because her name sounds like Morana, she was sometimes identified with that goddess and called the goddess of death.

long_description.id: Ia dipercaya sering berenang jauh di laut dalam wujud ikan besar sambil bermain dengan lumba-lumba, dan hanya naik ke darat pada senja yang tenang. Bila Tsar Laut marah dan badai muncul, Moryana menenangkannya sehingga badai reda. Menurut kepercayaan lain, ia raksasa perempuan berwajah keras dengan rambut kusut dan berbaju putih yang menguasai angin tenggara di muara Volga, berbahaya bagi pelaut di Laut Kaspia; musuh utamanya Ded Shapka Dranaya, penguasa angin barat laut.
long_description.en: She was believed to swim deep in the sea as a big fish, playing with dolphins, and to come ashore only on quiet evenings. When the Sea Tsar grew angry and a storm rose, Moryana calmed him and the storm died down. In another belief she is a stern giantess with uncombed hair and white clothes who rules the southeast winds at the mouth of the Volga, a danger to sailors on the Caspian Sea; her chief enemy is Ded Shapka Dranaya, lord of the northwest wind.

short_description.id: Muroni adalah vampir dalam mitologi Wallachia yang bisa berubah menjadi berbagai hewan; namanya ubahan Inggris lama dari moroi Rumania.
short_description.en: The Muroni is a vampire of Wallachian mythology able to turn into various animals; its name is an old English corruption of the Romanian moroi.

long_description.id: Muroni atau Murony adalah vampir dalam mitologi Wallachia. Ia mampu berubah menjadi berbagai hewan, sehingga serangannya sering dikira serangan hewan, dan satu-satunya tanda kehadirannya adalah kehilangan darah yang luar biasa. Muroni dipercaya sebenarnya hantu pengisap darah yang mengambil wujud makhluk lain agar mudah memangsa.
long_description.en: The Muroni or Murony is a vampire of Wallachian mythology. It could turn into various animals, so its attacks were often taken for animal attacks, the only sign of its presence being exceptional blood loss. It was believed to be really a blood-sucking ghost that took other forms to feed more easily.

long_description.id: Nama murony dan muroni adalah bentuk ubahan Inggris lama dari istilah Rumania moroi, yang terutama dipakai dalam dialek selatan seperti di Wallachia. Moroi berbeda dari strigoi karena fana, tetapi bila dibunuh strigoi ia menjadi strigoi yang abadi. Ia bisa berubah menjadi anjing, kucing, kodok, atau serangga, dan hanya bisa dimusnahkan dengan menggali jasadnya, menusuk dahi dengan jarum, menancapkan pasak kayu ke jantung, lalu membakarnya.
long_description.en: The names murony and muroni are old English corruptions of the Romanian term moroi, used mostly in southern dialects such as in Wallachia. The moroi differs from the strigoi in being mortal, but if killed by a strigoi it becomes an immortal strigoi. It can turn into a dog, cat, toad or insects, and could be destroyed only by digging up the body, driving a needle into the forehead, staking the heart and burning it.

long_description.id: Muroni atau Murony adalah vampir dalam mitologi Wallachia. Ia mampu berubah menjadi berbagai hewan, sehingga serangannya sering dikira serangan hewan, dan satu-satunya tanda kehadirannya adalah kehilangan darah yang luar biasa. Muroni dipercaya sebenarnya hantu pengisap darah yang mengambil wujud makhluk lain agar mudah memangsa.
long_description.en: The Muroni or Murony is a vampire of Wallachian mythology. It could turn into various animals, so its attacks were often taken for animal attacks, the only sign of its presence being exceptional blood loss. It was believed to be really a blood-sucking ghost that took other forms to feed more easily.

long_description.id: Nama murony dan muroni adalah bentuk ubahan Inggris lama dari istilah Rumania moroi, yang terutama dipakai dalam dialek selatan seperti di Wallachia. Moroi berbeda dari strigoi karena fana, tetapi bila dibunuh strigoi ia menjadi strigoi yang abadi. Ia bisa berubah menjadi anjing, kucing, kodok, atau serangga, dan hanya bisa dimusnahkan dengan menggali jasadnya, menusuk dahi dengan jarum, menancapkan pasak kayu ke jantung, lalu membakarnya.
long_description.en: The names murony and muroni are old English corruptions of the Romanian term moroi, used mostly in southern dialects such as in Wallachia. The moroi differs from the strigoi in being mortal, but if killed by a strigoi it becomes an immortal strigoi. It can turn into a dog, cat, toad or insects, and could be destroyed only by digging up the body, driving a needle into the forehead, staking the heart and burning it.

short_description.id: Ora adalah roh pelindung dalam mitologi Albania yang dimiliki setiap manusia sejak lahir dan terkait nasib serta takdirnya.
short_description.en: The Ora is a protective spirit of Albanian mythology that every human has from birth, tied to their fate and destiny.

long_description.id: Ora adalah tokoh mitologi Albania yang dimiliki setiap manusia sejak lahir, terkait nasib dan takdir, dan bertugas menjaga tatanan alam semesta. Rupanya berubah menurut watak pemiliknya: Ora putih bagi yang berani dan rajin, Ora hitam bagi yang malas atau pengecut. Di Albania Utara, Ora juga digambarkan sebagai tiga dewi yang berkumpul pada malam hari untuk menentukan nasib bayi yang baru lahir.
long_description.en: The Ora is an Albanian mythological figure that every human has from birth, tied to fate and destiny and charged with maintaining the order of the universe. Its appearance changes with its owner's character: a white Ora for the brave and industrious, a black Ora for the lazy or cowardly. In Northern Albania the Oras are also depicted as three goddesses who gather at night to determine a newborn's fate.

long_description.id: Ora berdiam di utara Sungai Drin, di hutan, gunung, sungai kecil, danau, dan gua, dan di Albania Tengah dipercaya hadir di mana-mana untuk mewujudkan berkat dan kutuk orang. Mereka bisa menjadi burung, binatang buas, perempuan, atau ular, dan di Albania Utara sering tampil sebagai ular bertanduk emas yang membawa emas. Dalam sebuah kisah, seorang ora memulihkan penglihatan Zuku yang dibutakan.
long_description.en: The Ora dwell north of the Drin River, in forests, mountains, streams, lakes and caves, and in Central Albania were believed to be everywhere, fulfilling people's blessings and curses. They can become birds, beasts, women or serpents, and in Northern Albania often appear as golden-horned serpents that bring gold. In one tale, an ora restores the sight of the blinded Zuku.

statement.en: The Ora (Albanian orë, definite form ora) is an Albanian mythological figure that every human has from birth, tied to destiny and fate; its essential function is to maintain the order of the universe and enforce its laws.

claims.quote: Within Albanian folklore and poetry, the Ora is a protective spirit that every human possesses from birth. The Ora's appearance alters according to the personality and attributes of the human – “a white Ora for the brave and industrious, or a black Ora for the lazy or cowardly.”

statement.id: Dalam folklor dan puisi Albania, Ora adalah roh pelindung yang dimiliki setiap manusia sejak lahir, dan rupanya berubah menurut watak orangnya: Ora putih bagi yang berani dan rajin, Ora hitam bagi yang malas atau pengecut.
statement.en: In Albanian folklore and poetry the Ora is a protective spirit everyone has from birth, and its appearance changes with the person's character: a white Ora for the brave and industrious, a black Ora for the lazy or cowardly.

claims.quote: The Ora reside towards the north of the Drin River in Northern Albania. statement.id: Ora berdiam di utara Sungai Drin di Albania Utara; di Albania Tengah mereka dipercaya hadir di mana-mana, mendengarkan berkat dan kutuk orang lalu berusaha cepat mewujudkannya, sedangkan di luar Albania Tengah mereka tinggal di hutan dan gunung, di sungai kecil, danau, dan gua.
statement.en: The Ora dwell north of the Drin River in Northern Albania; in Central Albania they were believed to be everywhere, listening to people's blessings and curses and trying to fulfil them quickly, while outside Central Albania they live in forests and mountains, in streams, lakes and caves.

claims.quote: Within Albanian folklore and poetry, Ora had the ability to take any form they pleased, including “birds, beasts, women, or serpents.” ... statement.en: The Ora could take any form, including birds, beasts, women or serpents; in Northern Albania they often appear as serpents, like the Southern Albanian deity Vitore, and both are depicted as a golden-horned serpent that brings gold.

short_description.en: Rokita is a devil of Polish folklore dwelling in bogs, forests and old willow trees, very strong but not very cunning.

long_description.id: Rokita adalah iblis dalam cerita rakyat Polandia yang konon mendiami gerbang ke dunia bawah: lahan basah, hutan, dan bagian dalam pohon dedalu tua. Ia sangat kuat tetapi tidak terlalu cerdik. Di Łęczyca ia sering disamakan dengan Boruta dan digambarkan sebagai jenderal bermantel emas, serta bisa muncul sebagai babi, burung, ikan, kuda, anjing, tikus, atau kucing, selalu dengan niat jahat terhadap manusia.
long_description.en: Rokita is a devil of Polish folklore said to inhabit gateways to the underworld: wetlands, forests and the insides of old willow trees. He is enormously strong but not very cunning. In Łęczyca he is often equated with Boruta and shown as a general in a golden cloak, and he can appear as a pig, bird, fish, horse, dog, mouse or cat, always hostile to people.

long_description.id: Dalam satu versi ia disebut Rokietnik, jiwa jahat penghuni rawa yang menenggelamkan penyusup. Legenda lain mengisahkannya minum bir bersama Boruta di sebuah kedai di Łódź, atau meminjamkan uang tanpa bunga kepada petani miskin dengan jiwa sebagai jaminan. Para penyihir juga memohon kepadanya agar sapi memberi lebih banyak susu.
long_description.en: In one version he is called Rokietnik, an evil bog-dwelling soul who drowns intruders. Other legends have him drinking beer with Boruta at an inn in Łódź, or lending a poor peasant money without interest against his soul. Witches also prayed to him for cows that gave more milk.

short_description.id: Rokita adalah iblis dalam cerita rakyat Polandia yang mendiami rawa, hutan, dan pohon dedalu tua, sangat kuat tetapi tidak terlalu cerdik.
short_description.en: Rokita is a devil of Polish folklore dwelling in bogs, forests and old willow trees, very strong but not very cunning.

long_description.id: Rokita adalah iblis dalam cerita rakyat Polandia yang konon mendiami gerbang ke dunia bawah: lahan basah, hutan, dan bagian dalam pohon dedalu tua. Ia sangat kuat tetapi tidak terlalu cerdik. Di Łęczyca ia sering disamakan dengan Boruta dan digambarkan sebagai jenderal bermantel emas, serta bisa muncul sebagai babi, burung, ikan, kuda, anjing, tikus, atau kucing, selalu dengan niat jahat terhadap manusia.
long_description.en: Rokita is a devil of Polish folklore said to inhabit gateways to the underworld: wetlands, forests and the insides of old willow trees. He is enormously strong but not very cunning. In Łęczyca he is often equated with Boruta and shown as a general in a golden cloak, and he can appear as a pig, bird, fish, horse, dog, mouse or cat, always hostile to people.

long_description.id: Dalam satu versi ia disebut Rokietnik, jiwa jahat penghuni rawa yang menenggelamkan penyusup. Legenda lain mengisahkannya minum bir bersama Boruta di sebuah kedai di Łódź, atau meminjamkan uang tanpa bunga kepada petani miskin dengan jiwa sebagai jaminan. Para penyihir juga memohon kepadanya agar sapi memberi lebih banyak susu.
long_description.en: In one version he is called Rokietnik, an evil bog-dwelling soul who drowns intruders. Other legends have him drinking beer with Boruta at an inn in Łódź, or lending a poor peasant money without interest against his soul. Witches also prayed to him for cows that gave more milk.

short_description.id: Sigmund adalah pahlawan saga Völsunga, satu-satunya yang dapat mencabut pedang Gram dari pohon Barnstokk, yang sempat hidup sebagai manusia serigala dan menjadi ayah Sigurð.
short_description.en: Sigmund is the hero of the Völsunga saga, the only one able to pull the sword Gram from the tree Barnstokk, who lived for a time as a werewolf and fathered Sigurð.

long_description.id: Sigmund adalah pahlawan mitologi Jermanik dalam saga Völsunga, putra Völsung dan ayah Sigurð si pembunuh naga. Ia satu-satunya yang mampu mencabut pedang Gram yang ditancapkan Odin ke pohon Barnstokk. Setelah ayahnya dibunuh Siggeir dan saudara-saudaranya dimangsa serigala betina, ia selamat dengan menggigit lidah serigala itu.
long_description.en: Sigmund is a hero of Germanic myth in the Völsunga saga, son of Völsung and father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer. He alone could pull the sword Gram that Odin had thrust into the tree Barnstokk. After Siggeir killed his father and a she-wolf devoured his brothers, he survived by biting off the wolf's tongue.

long_description.id: Bersama putranya Sinfjötli, yang lahir dari saudarinya Signý, ia hidup sebagai buronan, sempat menjadi manusia serigala, lalu membunuh Siggeir. Ia juga disebut dalam Beowulf dan kisahnya diadaptasi dalam opera Die Walküre karya Richard Wagner.
long_description.en: With his son Sinfjötli, born of his sister Signý, he lived as an outlaw, for a time as a werewolf, and then killed Siggeir. He is also mentioned in Beowulf and his story is adapted in Richard Wagner's opera Die Walküre.

claims.quote: In Germanic mythology, Sigmund (Old Norse: Sigmundr [ˈsiɣˌmundz̠], Old English: Sigemund) is a hero whose story is told in the Völsunga saga.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Jermanik, Sigmund (Norse Kuno: Sigmundr; Inggris Kuno: Sigemund) adalah pahlawan yang kisahnya diceritakan dalam saga Völsunga.
statement.en: In Germanic mythology Sigmund (Old Norse Sigmundr, Old English Sigemund) is a hero whose story is told in the Völsunga saga.

claims.quote: He and his sister, Signý, are the children of Völsung and his wife Hljod. Sigmund is best known as the father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer

statement.id: Ia dan saudarinya Signý adalah anak Völsung dan istrinya Hljod, dan Sigmund paling dikenal sebagai ayah Sigurð si pembunuh naga.
statement.en: He and his sister Signý are the children of Völsung and his wife Hljod, and Sigmund is best known as the father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer.

claims.quote: when Odin, disguised as a beggar, plunges a sword (Gram) into the living tree Barnstokk ("offspring-trunk") around which Völsung's hall is built. The disguised Odin announces that the man who can remove the sword will have it as a gift. Only Sigmund is able to free the sword from the tree.

statement.id: Odin yang menyamar sebagai pengemis menancapkan pedang Gram ke pohon Barnstokk di tengah balairung Völsung dan menyatakan siapa pun yang mencabutnya boleh memilikinya; hanya Sigmund yang berhasil.
statement.en: Odin, disguised as a beggar, thrusts the sword Gram into the tree Barnstokk in Völsung's hall, saying whoever pulls it out may keep it; only Sigmund succeeds.

claims.quote: When the Völsung clan arrive, they are attacked by the Gauts; King Völsung is killed and his sons captured.

statement.id: Ketika klan Völsung datang ke Gautland, mereka diserang orang Gaut; Raja Völsung tewas dan putra-putranya ditawan.
statement.en: When the Völsungs arrive in Gautland they are attacked by the Gauts; King Völsung is killed and his sons captured.

claims.quote: On the ninth night, she has a servant smear honey on Sigmund's face and when the she-wolf arrives, she starts licking the honey off and sticks her tongue into Sigmund's mouth, whereupon Sigmund bites her tongue off, killing her.

statement.id: Setelah serigala betina jelmaan ibu Siggeir memangsa saudara-saudaranya satu per satu, pada malam kesembilan Signý menyuruh pelayan mengoleskan madu ke wajah Sigmund; ketika serigala itu menjilat dan memasukkan lidahnya ke mulut Sigmund, ia menggigit putus lidahnya.
statement.en: After the she-wolf, Siggeir's shapeshifting mother, devours his brothers one by one, on the ninth night Signý has honey smeared on Sigmund's face; when the wolf licks it and puts her tongue in his mouth, he bites it off and kills her.

claims.quote: Mit seiner Zwillingsschwester Signy zeugte er einen Sohn Sinfiötli, mit dem zusammen er den Mord an seinem Vater Wölsung rächte.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, bersama saudari kembarnya Signy ia memperoleh putra Sinfjötli, yang bersamanya membalas pembunuhan Völsung.
statement.en: According to the German article, with his twin sister Signy he fathered Sinfjötli, with whom he avenged Völsung's murder.

claims.quote: Die beiden lebten als Geächtete, erlebten einige Abenteuer, zwischenzeitlich auch als Werwölfe, bis es ihnen gelang ihren Vater/Großvater Wölsung zu rächen, indem sie Siggeir töteten.

statement.id: Keduanya hidup sebagai buronan, sempat menjadi manusia serigala, sampai berhasil membalas dendam dengan membunuh Siggeir.
statement.en: The two lived as outlaws, for a time as werewolves, until they avenged Völsung by killing Siggeir.

claims.quote: Il apparaît notamment dans la Völsunga saga, la Þiðrekssaga, et est également mentionné dans le poème anglo-saxon Beowulf sous le nom de Sigemund. Une adaptation de son histoire apparaît dans l'opéra La Walkyrie (Die Walküre) du cycle de L'Anneau du Nibelung (Der Ring des Nibelungen), de Richard Wagner.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, ia muncul dalam saga Völsunga dan Þiðrekssaga, disebut sebagai Sigemund dalam Beowulf, dan kisahnya diadaptasi dalam opera Die Walküre dari siklus Der Ring des Nibelungen karya Richard Wagner.
statement.en: According to the French article, he appears in the Völsunga saga and Þiðrekssaga, is named Sigemund in Beowulf, and his story is adapted in the opera Die Walküre of Richard Wagner's Ring cycle.

long_description.id: Bersama putranya Sinfjötli, yang lahir dari saudarinya Signý, ia hidup sebagai buronan, sempat menjadi manusia serigala, lalu membunuh Siggeir. Ia juga disebut dalam Beowulf dan kisahnya diadaptasi dalam opera Die Walküre karya Richard Wagner.
long_description.en: With his son Sinfjötli, born of his sister Signý, he lived as an outlaw, for a time as a werewolf, and then killed Siggeir. He is also mentioned in Beowulf and his story is adapted in Richard Wagner's opera Die Walküre.

role.en: Avenges his father.

famous_for.en: Drawing the sword Gram.

note.id: Saudarinya.

claims.quote: In Germanic mythology, Sigmund (Old Norse: Sigmundr [ˈsiɣˌmundz̠], Old English: Sigemund) is a hero whose story is told in the Völsunga saga.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Jermanik, Sigmund (Norse Kuno: Sigmundr; Inggris Kuno: Sigemund) adalah pahlawan yang kisahnya diceritakan dalam saga Völsunga.
statement.en: In Germanic mythology Sigmund (Old Norse Sigmundr, Old English Sigemund) is a hero whose story is told in the Völsunga saga.

claims.quote: He and his sister, Signý, are the children of Völsung and his wife Hljod. Sigmund is best known as the father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer

statement.id: Ia dan saudarinya Signý adalah anak Völsung dan istrinya Hljod, dan Sigmund paling dikenal sebagai ayah Sigurð si pembunuh naga.
statement.en: He and his sister Signý are the children of Völsung and his wife Hljod, and Sigmund is best known as the father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer.

claims.quote: when Odin, disguised as a beggar, plunges a sword (Gram) into the living tree Barnstokk ("offspring-trunk") around which Völsung's hall is built. The disguised Odin announces that the man who can remove the sword will have it as a gift. Only Sigmund is able to free the sword from the tree.

statement.id: Odin yang menyamar sebagai pengemis menancapkan pedang Gram ke pohon Barnstokk di tengah balairung Völsung dan menyatakan siapa pun yang mencabutnya boleh memilikinya; hanya Sigmund yang berhasil.
statement.en: Odin, disguised as a beggar, thrusts the sword Gram into the tree Barnstokk in Völsung's hall, saying whoever pulls it out may keep it; only Sigmund succeeds.

claims.quote: When the Völsung clan arrive, they are attacked by the Gauts; King Völsung is killed and his sons captured.

statement.id: Ketika klan Völsung datang ke Gautland, mereka diserang orang Gaut; Raja Völsung tewas dan putra-putranya ditawan.
statement.en: When the Völsungs arrive in Gautland they are attacked by the Gauts; King Völsung is killed and his sons captured.

claims.quote: On the ninth night, she has a servant smear honey on Sigmund's face and when the she-wolf arrives, she starts licking the honey off and sticks her tongue into Sigmund's mouth, whereupon Sigmund bites her tongue off, killing her.

statement.id: Setelah serigala betina jelmaan ibu Siggeir memangsa saudara-saudaranya satu per satu, pada malam kesembilan Signý menyuruh pelayan mengoleskan madu ke wajah Sigmund; ketika serigala itu menjilat dan memasukkan lidahnya ke mulut Sigmund, ia menggigit putus lidahnya.
statement.en: After the she-wolf, Siggeir's shapeshifting mother, devours his brothers one by one, on the ninth night Signý has honey smeared on Sigmund's face; when the wolf licks it and puts her tongue in his mouth, he bites it off and kills her.

claims.quote: Mit seiner Zwillingsschwester Signy zeugte er einen Sohn Sinfiötli, mit dem zusammen er den Mord an seinem Vater Wölsung rächte.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, bersama saudari kembarnya Signy ia memperoleh putra Sinfjötli, yang bersamanya membalas pembunuhan Völsung.
statement.en: According to the German article, with his twin sister Signy he fathered Sinfjötli, with whom he avenged Völsung's murder.

claims.quote: Die beiden lebten als Geächtete, erlebten einige Abenteuer, zwischenzeitlich auch als Werwölfe, bis es ihnen gelang ihren Vater/Großvater Wölsung zu rächen, indem sie Siggeir töteten.

statement.id: Keduanya hidup sebagai buronan, sempat menjadi manusia serigala, sampai berhasil membalas dendam dengan membunuh Siggeir.
statement.en: The two lived as outlaws, for a time as werewolves, until they avenged Völsung by killing Siggeir.

claims.quote: Il apparaît notamment dans la Völsunga saga, la Þiðrekssaga, et est également mentionné dans le poème anglo-saxon Beowulf sous le nom de Sigemund. Une adaptation de son histoire apparaît dans l'opéra La Walkyrie (Die Walküre) du cycle de L'Anneau du Nibelung (Der Ring des Nibelungen), de Richard Wagner.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, ia muncul dalam saga Völsunga dan Þiðrekssaga, disebut sebagai Sigemund dalam Beowulf, dan kisahnya diadaptasi dalam opera Die Walküre dari siklus Der Ring des Nibelungen karya Richard Wagner.
statement.en: According to the French article, he appears in the Völsunga saga and Þiðrekssaga, is named Sigemund in Beowulf, and his story is adapted in the opera Die Walküre of Richard Wagner's Ring cycle.

short_description.id: Sihuanaba adalah roh pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Tengah yang tampil sebagai perempuan cantik berambut panjang, lalu menampakkan wajah tengkorak atau kepala kuda.
short_description.en: The Sihuanaba is a shapeshifting spirit of Central American folklore that appears as a beautiful long-haired woman, then reveals a skull or horse face.

long_description.id: Sihuanaba, juga disebut Siguanaba, Cigua, atau Cegua, adalah roh pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Tengah, dengan varian di sebagian Meksiko. Ia tampil sebagai perempuan menarik berambut panjang yang sering terlihat mencuci atau mandi di sungai. Ia memikat pria yang sendirian ke tempat terpencil, lalu menampakkan wajah aslinya, tengkorak tanpa daging atau kepala kuda, yang membuat korban mati ketakutan atau menjadi gila.
long_description.en: The Sihuanaba, also called Siguanaba, Cigua or Cegua, is a shapeshifting spirit of Central American folklore with variants in parts of Mexico. She appears as an attractive long-haired woman, often seen washing or bathing in rivers. She lures lone men to remote places, then reveals her true face, a fleshless skull or a horse's head, which makes victims die of fright or go mad.

long_description.id: Para ahli menduga legenda ini berasal dari Spanyol dan dibawa ke Amerika Latin pada masa kolonial, ketika penjajah memakainya sebagai alat kendali sosial atas penduduk pribumi dan mestizo.
long_description.en: Scholars suggest the legend came from Spain in the colonial period, when colonists used it as a tool of social control over Indigenous and mestizo people.

short_description.id: Kurcaci Simonside, juga disebut Brownmen, Bogles dan Duergar, adalah ras kurcaci dalam folklor Inggris dari Simonside Hills, Northumberland.
short_description.en: The Simonside Dwarfs, also called Brownmen, Bogles and Duergar, are a race of dwarfs in English folklore from the Simonside Hills of Northumberland.

long_description.id: Kurcaci Simonside, juga dikenal sebagai Brownmen, Bogles dan Duergar, adalah ras kurcaci dalam folklor Inggris yang terutama dikaitkan dengan Simonside Hills di Northumberland, Inggris utara; pemimpin mereka konon bernama Heslop. Dalam kisah tradisional The Duergar yang dituturkan Frederick Grice (1944), salah satunya digambarkan pendek, bermantel kulit domba, bercelana kulit tikus mondok, dan bertopi lumut yang dihiasi bulu.
long_description.en: The Simonside Dwarfs, also known as Brownmen, Bogles and Duergar, are a race of dwarfs in English folklore tied especially to Northumberland's Simonside Hills in the north of England, and said to be led by one Heslop. In Frederick Grice's 1944 retelling of the traditional tale The Duergar, one is short, wearing a lambskin coat, moleskin trousers and a moss hat stuck with a feather.

long_description.id: Mereka senang menyesatkan para pengembara, terutama setelah gelap, sering membawa obor menyala untuk menuntun mereka ke rawa, mirip Will-o'-the-wisp, dan menghilang saat fajar. Kata duergar kemungkinan berasal dari kata dialek perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia untuk "kurcaci" ditambah akhiran jamak Norse -ar, atau dari kata Norse Kuno dvergar. Artikel it menyebut mereka ras kurcaci yang jelek dan jahat.
long_description.en: They loved to lead travellers astray, above all after dark, often carrying lit torches to draw them into bogs like a Will-o'-the-wisp, and would vanish at dawn. The word duergar probably comes from Border dialect words for 'dwarf' with a mistakenly added Norse plural -ar, or from Old Norse dvergar. The it article calls them an ugly, particularly wicked race of dwarfs.

short_description.id: Tartalo atau Tartaro adalah raksasa bermata satu pemakan manusia dari mitologi Basque yang tinggal di gua pegunungan, mirip Kiklops Polifemos, dan memiliki cincin ajaib yang dapat berbicara.
short_description.en: Tartalo or Tartaro is a one-eyed man-eating giant of Basque mythology who lives in mountain caves, much like the Cyclops Polyphemus, and owns a talking magic ring.

long_description.id: Tartalo, Tartaro, atau Torto adalah raksasa bermata satu yang sangat kuat dari mitologi Basque, mirip Kiklops Polifemos, yang tinggal di gua pegunungan, beternak domba, dan menangkap orang muda untuk dimakan. Ukurannya dan nafsu makannya sangat besar, dan ia gemar melempar batu antargunung. Cerquand menduga namanya dari bangsa Tatar, dan tokoh bernama Tartari juga dikenal di Agenais.
long_description.en: Tartalo, Tartaro or Torto is an enormously strong one-eyed giant of Basque mythology, much like the Cyclops Polyphemus, who lives in mountain caves, keeps sheep and catches young people to eat. His size and appetite are huge, and he loves hurling stones between mountains. Cerquand derived his name from the Tartar people, and a figure called Tartari is known in the Agenais.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah terkenal, dua bersaudara dari Antimuño berlindung di gua Tartalo; ia memakan si kakak, lalu si adik mencuri cincinnya, membutakan matanya dengan tusuk panggangan, dan lolos berbalut kulit domba. Cincin ajaib itu berteriak memberi tahu tempatnya, maka si anak memotong jarinya dan melemparkannya ke jurang, dan Tartalo yang mengikuti suara cincin jatuh dari tebing.
long_description.en: In a well-known tale two brothers from Antimuño shelter in Tartalo's cave; he eats the elder, then the younger steals his ring, blinds him with a roasting spit and escapes in a sheepskin. The magic ring shouts out where he is, so the boy cuts off his finger and throws it into the ravine, and Tartalo, following the ring's voice, falls off the cliff.

role.en: Preys on young people.

famous_for.en: The shouting ring.

description.id: Satu-satunya matanya dapat dibutakan dengan tusuk panggangan.
description.en: His single eye can be blinded with a roasting spit.

role.en: Man-eating giant

summary.id: Tartalo memakan si kakak, dibutakan si adik, lalu jatuh dari tebing mengikuti teriakan cincinnya.
summary.en: Tartalo eats the elder brother, is blinded by the younger, then falls off a cliff following his ring's shouts.

note.en: The name Anxo is sometimes used for both.

claims.quote: One day, while two brothers of the Antimuño baserri were hunting, a storm broke, so they decided to take refuge from the rain in a cave, which was Tartalo's cave.

statement.id: Suatu hari dua bersaudara dari pertanian Antimuño yang sedang berburu berlindung dari badai di sebuah gua, yang ternyata gua Tartalo.
statement.en: One day two brothers from the Antimuño farm, out hunting, sheltered from a storm in a cave that turned out to be Tartalo's.

claims.quote: While he was sleeping, the youngest brother stole Tartalo's ring and then he stuck the roasting spit in his only eye.

statement.id: Setelah Tartalo memakan si kakak dan tertidur, si adik mencuri cincinnya dan menusukkan tusuk panggangan ke satu-satunya matanya.
statement.en: After Tartalo ate the elder brother and fell asleep, the younger stole his ring and drove the roasting spit into his only eye.

claims.quote: He started to look for the boy among his sheep, but he put on a sheep's skin and escaped from Tartalo.

statement.id: Tartalo mencari si anak di antara dombanya, tetapi anak itu memakai kulit domba dan lolos.
statement.en: Tartalo searched for the boy among his sheep, but the boy put on a sheepskin and escaped.

claims.quote: The young one wasn't able to take off the ring, so, when he arrived to the edge of a cliff, he cut off his finger, and since Tartalo was near, he decided to throw it down the cliff. Tartalo, following the ring's shouting, fell off the cliff.

statement.id: Cincin itu berteriak memberi tahu tempatnya dan tidak dapat dilepas, maka di tepi tebing si anak memotong jarinya dan melemparkannya ke bawah; Tartalo mengikuti teriakan cincin itu dan jatuh dari tebing.
statement.en: The ring shouted out his whereabouts and would not come off, so at a cliff edge the boy cut off his finger and threw it down; Tartalo followed the ring's shouts and fell off the cliff.

claims.quote: Un personnage appelé Tartari était attesté au-delà de la Gascogne, rive droite de la Garonne, dans l'Agenais

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, tokoh bernama Tartari juga dikenal di luar Gascogne, di Agenais di tepi kanan Garonne.
statement.en: According to the French article, a figure called Tartari was known beyond Gascony, in the Agenais on the right bank of the Garonne.

claims.quote: Les caractéristiques et les aventures qu'on lui prête correspondent d'assez près à celles du cyclope Polyphème. Comme lui il vit dans une caverne, il élève des moutons

statement.id: Ciri dan petualangannya cukup dekat dengan Kiklops Polifemos: seperti dia, Tartalo tinggal di gua dan beternak domba.
statement.en: His traits and adventures closely match those of the Cyclops Polyphemus: like him he lives in a cave and keeps sheep.

claims.quote: Anxo or Ancho is however explained as an alternate name for Basajaun by some sources.

statement.id: Sebagian sumber menyebut Anxo atau Ancho sebagai nama lain Basajaun.
statement.en: Some sources explain Anxo or Ancho as another name for Basajaun.

claims.quote: Su tamaño es descomunal, al igual que su apetito, y su entretenimiento favorito era tirar piedras de un monte a otro. Cuenta la leyenda que debido a este entretenimiento se crearon varias construcciones existentes hoy en día.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ukuran dan nafsu makannya sangat besar, dan kegemarannya melempar batu dari satu gunung ke gunung lain konon menghasilkan beberapa bangunan yang masih ada.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, his size and appetite are enormous, and his favourite pastime of hurling stones from mountain to mountain is said to have created several structures still standing.

text.en: First documented in June 1891; the curse story is linked to the draining of the Fens in the seventeenth century

short_description.id: Tiddy Mun adalah roh rawa legendaris di Inggris yang dipercaya mengendalikan air dan kabut di rawa Lincolnshire dan Isle of Ely, digambarkan seperti lelaki tua kecil berjanggut putih.
short_description.en: Tiddy Mun was a legendary bog spirit in England believed to control the waters and mists of the Lincolnshire and Isle of Ely fens, described as a small old man with a white beard.

long_description.id: Tiddy Mun adalah roh rawa legendaris di Inggris yang dipercaya mampu mengendalikan air dan kabut di rawa-rawa South Lincolnshire, The Carrs di North Lincolnshire, dan rawa Isle of Ely. Kepercayaan ini pertama kali didokumentasikan pada Juni 1891 dalam artikel M. C. Balfour di jurnal Folk-Lore.
long_description.en: Tiddy Mun was a legendary bog spirit of England, thought to hold sway over the water and fog of the South Lincolnshire Fens, the North Lincolnshire Carrs and the Isle of Ely fens. M. C. Balfour put the belief on record for the first time in an article in the journal Folk-Lore, published in June 1891.

long_description.id: Balfour menggambarkannya tidak lebih besar daripada anak tiga tahun, tetapi berpenampilan seperti lelaki tua berambut putih kusut dan berjanggut putih kusut. Ia dikatakan memakai jubah abu-abu sehingga sulit terlihat saat senja, dan tawanya menyerupai panggilan burung peewit. Dalam teks dialek yang dicatat Balfour, ia tinggal di lubang-lubang air rawa, dan penutur lamanya mengaku pernah melihatnya berjalan pincang di kabut, abu-abu dan putih, menjerit seperti peewit.
long_description.en: Balfour describes him as small, no larger than a toddler of three, yet resembling an old man whose long white hair was tangled and whose white beard was matted. A grey gown reportedly made him hard to see at dusk, and his laughter resembled the call of the peewit. In the dialect text Balfour recorded, he dwells in the water-holes of the fen, and the old teller claims to have seen him limping through the fog, grey and white, screeching like a peewit.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah cerita dari Lembah Ancholme, Tiddy Mun menjatuhkan kutukan wabah pada sebuah desa karena marah atas pengeringan Fens oleh orang Belanda di bawah Cornelius Vermuyden pada abad ke-17. Ia akhirnya reda setelah penduduk berkumpul senja saat bulan baru, menuang ember air ke parit, dan meminta maaf atas kerusakan itu.
long_description.en: In a story from the Ancholme Valley, Tiddy Mun laid a plague-curse on a village, furious that the Dutch under Cornelius Vermuyden were draining the Fens in the seventeenth century. He calmed down in the end once the villagers met at dusk at the new moon, emptied buckets of water into the dyke and said sorry for the harm done.

long_description.id: Ia tidak sepenuhnya jahat: bila rawa banjir dan air mencapai desa, orang keluar malam hari dan memanggilnya sampai terdengar teriakan peewit, dan keesokan paginya air surut. Darwin Horn menafsirkan kutukan-kutukannya sebagai kemalangan dan penyakit akibat pengeringan lahan rawa. Penutur dialek menduga Tiddy Mun telah ketakutan dan pergi oleh cara-cara baru sehingga orang tak lagi mengenalnya.
long_description.en: He was not exclusively malevolent: when the fen flooded and the waters reached the villages, people went out at night and called him until they heard the cry of a peewit, and by morning the waters had receded. Darwin Horn reads his curses as the misfortune and disease brought by draining the fenland. The dialect teller guesses he has been frightened away by new ways, so that people no longer know him.

short_description.id: Trauco adalah makhluk kecil mirip kurcaci dalam mitologi Chilote di Chiloé, Chili, yang memikat perempuan dan dijadikan penjelasan atas kehamilan tanpa ayah.
short_description.en: The Trauco is a small dwarf-like being of Chilote mythology in Chiloé, Chile, who seduces women and is blamed for pregnancies without a known father.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Chilote di Chiloé, Chili, Trauco adalah makhluk kecil mirip kurcaci yang tinggal jauh di dalam hutan. Wajahnya buruk, tingginya tidak lebih dari 80 cm, dan kakinya berupa tunggul tanpa telapak. Ia anak dewa ular Coi Coi-Vilu, istrinya adalah Fiura, dan ia membawa tongkat bengkok pahueldún serta kapak batu kecil untuk memukul pohon.
long_description.en: In the Chilote mythology of Chiloé, Chile, the Trauco is a small dwarf-like being living deep in the forest. He has an ugly face, stands no more than 80 cm tall and has stumps instead of feet. He is a child of the snake god Coi Coi-Vilu, his wife is the Fiura, and he carries a twisted pahueldún staff and a small stone hatchet for striking trees.

long_description.id: Trauco punya daya pikat kuat terhadap perempuan, dan sebagian lelaki Chiloé percaya tatapannya dapat mematikan. Bila perempuan lajang hamil tanpa ayah yang jelas, orang menganggap Trauco ayahnya dan tidak menyalahkan perempuan itu.
long_description.en: The Trauco has a strong pull on women, and some men of Chiloé believe his gaze can kill. When an unmarried woman becomes pregnant without a known father, people name Trauco as the father and do not blame her.

short_description.id: Tugarin adalah makhluk mitis dalam bylina dan dongeng Rusia yang melambangkan kejahatan dan kekejaman, berwujud mirip naga, dan menjadi lawan Alyosha Popovich.
short_description.en: Tugarin is a mythical being of Russian byliny and fairy tales who embodies evil and cruelty, takes a dragon-like form and opposes Alyosha Popovich.

long_description.id: Dalam bylina dan dongeng Rusia, Tugarin adalah sosok kejam dan jahat yang tampil menyerupai naga. Ia digambarkan sebagai raksasa dan musuh Alyosha Popovich, juga lawan Dobrynya Nikitich. Namanya beragam, antara lain Zmey Tugarin, Zmey Tugaretin, dan Zmeishche Tugarishche.
long_description.en: In Russian byliny and tales Tugarin is a cruel, wicked figure who appears in the likeness of a dragon. He is pictured as a giant and as the foe of Alyosha Popovich, and also of Dobrynya Nikitich. He goes by many names, among them Zmey Tugarin, Zmey Tugaretin and Zmeishche Tugarishche.

long_description.id: Walau disebut naga, ia sebagian besar tetap berwujud manusia dan menunggang kuda. Ia tampak bersayap dan terbang ke udara saat bertarung dengan Alyosha, meski beberapa versi menjelaskan sayap itu sebagai alat dari kertas yang dipasang pada kudanya. Ia juga sangat rakus: mampu menjejalkan satu roti bundar di tiap pipinya lalu menelan seekor angsa utuh.
long_description.en: Though called a dragon, he mostly keeps a human shape and rides a horse. He seems to have wings and rises into the air while fighting Alyosha, though some versions explain the wings away as a paper device fixed to his horse. He is also a huge glutton, able to cram a whole round loaf into each cheek and then swallow a swan whole.

long_description.id: Sebagian pengulas menganggap Tugarin melambangkan unsur api, karena dalam beberapa versi tubuhnya diselimuti ular berapi yang ia pakai sebagai senjata, dan ia mencoba mencekik Alyosha dengan asap. Namanya dikaitkan dengan khan Polovtsia Tugorkan, walau ada etimologi lain dari akar kata tug, "duka".
long_description.en: Some commentators see Tugarin as the element of fire, since in some versions his body is covered with fiery snakes used as weapons and he tries to choke Alyosha with smoke. His name has been tied to the Polovtsian khan Tugorkan, though another etymology derives it from the root tug, "grief".

short_description.id: Vedmak adalah dukun atau penyihir laki-laki dalam mitologi Slavia, pasangan laki-laki dari vedma (penyihir perempuan), yang bisa menyembuhkan maupun mencelakai.
short_description.en: A vedmak is a warlock or male witch of Slavic mythology, the male counterpart of the vedma, who can both heal and harm.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, vedmak adalah dukun atau penyihir laki-laki; padanan perempuannya adalah vedma. Peran ini sangat menekankan sisi syamanistik paganisme Slavia: mereka mengobati manusia dan hewan, tetapi juga dianggap terhubung dengan iblis dan mampu mencelakai dengan mengirim penyakit, membunuh ternak, atau merusak panen. Dalam demonologi Slavia ia juga pemimpin para penyihir di suatu daerah, yang bisa bekerja sama dengan mereka atau justru melindungi orang dari ulah mereka.
long_description.en: Slavic myth calls a warlock or male witch a vedmak; the woman's counterpart is the vedma. The role leans heavily on the shamanic side of Slavic paganism: such men heal people and animals, yet are also thought to be in league with the devil and able to do harm by sending sickness, killing livestock or ruining harvests. In Slavic demonology he is also the head of the witches of a district, either working with them or shielding people from their mischief.

long_description.id: Vedmak dapat berubah menjadi binatang atau benda apa pun, misalnya ngengat, kuda, atau serigala. Menurut kepercayaan ia bisa "terlahir" atau "terlatih"; vedmak yang terlahir mungkin tak berjanggut tetapi berekor kecil. Kata vedmak berasal dari bahasa Proto-Slavia *vědět, "mengetahui". Karena saga fantasi The Witcher karya Andrzej Sapkowski, istilah ini kadang diterjemahkan sebagai "witcher" dalam bahasa Inggris.
long_description.en: A vedmak can turn into any animal or object, such as a moth, a horse or a wolf. Belief holds that he may be "born" or "taught"; a born vedmak may lack a beard but have a small tail. The word comes from Proto-Slavic *vědět, "to know". Because of Andrzej Sapkowski's fantasy saga The Witcher, the term is sometimes rendered in English as "witcher".

short_description.id: Vishap adalah naga dalam mitologi Armenia yang erat kaitannya dengan air, biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular bersayap, dan musuh dewa Vahagn.
short_description.en: The vishap is a dragon of Armenian mythology closely tied to water, usually shown as a winged serpent, and the foe of the god Vahagn.

long_description.id: Vishap adalah naga dalam mitologi Armenia yang erat kaitannya dengan air, mirip Leviatan. Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular bersayap atau gabungan bagian berbagai hewan. Namanya mungkin berasal dari istilah Iran kuno vi-šāpa, "yang bergetah beracun", yang dipakai untuk ular.
long_description.en: In Armenian myth the vishap is a water-linked dragon comparable to the Leviathan. Artists usually show it as a winged snake or as a blend of parts from several animals. Its name may go back to an old Iranian term, vi-šāpa, "having poisonous juices", applied to snakes.

long_description.id: Gunung Ararat adalah kediaman utama vishap; sifat vulkanik puncaknya dan gempa-gempanya mungkin mengilhami kaitan itu. Kadang bersama anak-anaknya, vishap mencuri bayi dan menggantinya dengan roh jahat kecil dari keturunannya sendiri. Menurut kepercayaan kuno, ia naik ke langit atau turun ke bumi sambil menimbulkan badai petir, angin puting, dan menelan matahari sehingga terjadi gerhana.
long_description.en: Mount Ararat was the vishap's chief home, perhaps because of the peak's volcanic nature and earthquakes. Sometimes with its young, the vishap stole infants and left a small evil spirit of its own brood in their place. Ancient belief had it rise to the sky or come down to earth, raising thunderstorms and whirlwinds and swallowing the sun to cause an eclipse.

long_description.id: Di sejumlah negeri Timur naga ini dipuja sebagai lambang air, kesuburan, dan kekayaan, lalu menjadi lambang kekuasaan yang menakutkan. Menurut legenda kuno, ia bertarung dengan Vahagn Pembunuh Naga, dan di Yerevan berdiri patung Vahagn karya Karlen Nurijanyan dan Nerses Charkhchyan.
long_description.en: In several Eastern lands the dragon was worshipped as a symbol of water, fertility and wealth, and it later became a fearsome symbol of power. Ancient legend has it fight Vahagn the Dragon Slayer, and a statue of Vahagn by Karlen Nurijanyan and Nerses Charkhchyan stands in Yerevan.

claims.quote: The name might derive from an ancient Iranian term vi-šāpa, 'having poisonous juices', used in reference to snakes

statement.id: Namanya mungkin berasal dari istilah Iran kuno vi-šāpa, "yang bergetah beracun", yang dipakai untuk ular.
statement.en: The name might derive from the old Iranian vi-šāpa, "having poisonous juices", used of snakes.

claims.quote: Mount Ararat was the main home of the Vishap. The volcanic character of the Araratian peak and its earthquakes may have suggested its association with the Vishap.

statement.id: Gunung Ararat adalah kediaman utama vishap; sifat vulkanik puncaknya dan gempanya mungkin mengilhami kaitan itu.
statement.en: Mount Ararat was the vishap's main home; the peak's volcanic nature and earthquakes may have suggested the link.

claims.quote: Sometimes with its children, the Vishap used to steal children or toddlers and put a small evil spirit of their own brood in their stead. According to ancient beliefs, the Vishap ascended to the sky or descended therefrom to earth, causing thunderous storms, whirlwinds, and absorption of the sun (causing an eclipse).

statement.id: Kadang bersama anaknya, vishap mencuri anak kecil dan menggantinya dengan roh jahat kecil dari keturunannya; menurut kepercayaan kuno ia naik ke langit atau turun ke bumi, menimbulkan badai petir, angin puting, dan menelan matahari (gerhana).
statement.en: Sometimes with its children the vishap stole toddlers and left a small evil spirit of its brood instead; by ancient belief it rose to the sky or came down, causing thunderstorms, whirlwinds and swallowing the sun (an eclipse).

claims.quote: The dragon was worshipped in a number of Eastern countries, symbolising the element of water, fertility and wealth, and later became a frightful symbol of power. According to ancient legends, the dragon fought Vahagn the Dragon Slayer.

statement.id: Naga ini dipuja di sejumlah negeri Timur sebagai lambang air, kesuburan, dan kekayaan, kemudian menjadi lambang kekuasaan yang menakutkan; menurut legenda kuno ia bertarung dengan Vahagn Pembunuh Naga.
statement.en: The dragon was worshipped in several Eastern countries as a symbol of water, fertility and wealth, later a frightful symbol of power; ancient legend has it fight Vahagn the Dragon Slayer.

claims.quote: There is a statue to Vahagn, who slew the Vishap, in Yerevan by Karlen Nurijanyan and Nerses Charkhchyan.

short_description.id: Zana adalah sosok mirip nimfa dalam mitologi Albania, terkait gunung, mata air, hutan, dan hewan, yang terkenal sangat berani dan melindungi para pejuang.
short_description.en: The zana is a nymph-like figure of Albanian mythology, linked to mountains, springs, forests and animals, famed for great courage and for protecting warriors.

long_description.id: Zana (zanë dalam dialek Gheg, zërë dalam dialek Tosk) adalah sosok mirip nimfa dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, biasanya terkait gunung, mata air dan sungai, hutan, tumbuhan, hewan, energi hidup manusia, dan kadang takdir. Zana e Madhe, "Zana Agung", diduga dewi Iliria yang setara dengan Artemis Yunani dan Diana Romawi.
long_description.en: Albanian myth and folklore know the zana (Gheg zanë, Tosk zërë) as a nymph-like being bound up with mountains, springs and streams, woods, plants, animals, human life-force and at times fate. The "Great Zana", Zana e Madhe, is thought to have been an Illyrian goddess matching the Greek Artemis and the Roman Diana.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, zana luar biasa berani, sehingga ada ungkapan Albania trim si zana, "berani seperti zana", dan mereka melindungi para pejuang seperti Pallas Athena. Di Albania utara dan Kosovo setiap gunung dikatakan punya zana-nya sendiri, yang tampak sebagai gadis cantik mandi di sungai gunung. Zana asli dikawal tiga kambing liar bertanduk emas, dan zana dipercaya dapat membuat manusia membatu dengan tatapannya.
long_description.en: Folk belief holds the zana to be fearless, hence the Albanian saying trim si zana, "brave as a zana", and she shields warriors much as Pallas Athena did. Across northern Albania and Kosovo, each peak is thought to have a zana of its own, seen as a lovely girl bathing in a mountain brook. Three wild, golden-horned goats escort the first zana, and a zana's look alone is believed to turn people to stone.

long_description.id: Thana dari Iliria, nama nimfa atau dewi dalam prasasti nazar zaman Romawi, secara tradisional dianggap cikal bakal Zana Albania, dan dipandang seasal dengan Diāna dalam bahasa Latin. Kepercayaan rakyat bahkan menyebut para zana menyaksikan pidato-pidato di Liga Prizren tahun 1878.
long_description.en: The Illyrian Thana, a nymph or goddess named in Roman-era votive inscriptions, is traditionally held to be the forerunner of the Albanian zana and is seen as cognate with Latin Diāna. Folk belief even has the zanas watching the speeches at the League of Prizren in 1878.

short_description.id: Bodach ("lelaki tua") adalah tokoh penipu atau momok dalam folklor dan mitologi Gaelik, pasangan cailleach dalam legenda Irlandia.
short_description.en: A bodach ('old man') is a trickster or bogeyman figure of Gaelic folklore and myth, paired with the cailleach in Irish legend.

long_description.id: Bodach (jamak bodaich, "lelaki tua; orang desa, kasar"; Irlandia Kuno botach) adalah tokoh penipu atau momok dalam folklor dan mitologi Gaelik. Dalam legenda Irlandia ia dipasangkan dengan cailleach, "nenek tua". Bodach adalah kata Irlandia untuk penyewa tanah, budak tani atau petani, dari bod ("ekor, penis") ditambah akhiran -ach; dalam bahasa Gaelik modern bodach hanya berarti "lelaki tua", sering dengan rasa sayang.
long_description.en: In Gaelic folklore and myth the bodach (plural bodaich; Old Irish botach), whose name means an old man or a coarse rustic, is a trickster or bogeyman figure, set alongside the cailleach, 'hag', in Irish legend. Bodach is the Irish for a tenant, serf or peasant, built from bod, 'tail, penis', and the suffix -ach; in modern Gaelic it just means 'old man', often fondly.

long_description.id: Dalam folklor Gaelik modern, bodach menjadi semacam momok hingga disamakan dengan iblis. Dalam kisah Eachtra Bhodaigh an Chóta Lachtna (abad ke-16 atau ke-17), ia disamakan dengan Manannán mac Lir. Dalam folklor Skotlandia ia turun lewat cerobong untuk menculik anak nakal, sebagai cerita peringatan. Makhluk terkait, Bodach Glas ("Lelaki Tua Kelabu"), dianggap pertanda kematian; dalam novel Waverley karya Walter Scott, Fergus Mac-Ivor melihatnya sebelum ajalnya.
long_description.en: In modern Gaelic lore the bodach becomes a kind of bugbear, even identified with the devil. The 16th- or 17th-century tale Eachtra Bhodaigh an Chóta Lachtna equates him with Manannán mac Lir. Scottish folklore has him come down the chimney to carry off naughty children, a warning tale. A related being, the Bodach Glas ('Old Grey Man'), is a death omen; in Walter Scott's Waverley Fergus Mac-Ivor sees one before his death.

short_description.id: Caipora adalah roh hutan dalam cerita rakyat Brasil yang menjaga satwa liar dari pemburu dan sering digambarkan menunggang peccary.
short_description.en: Caipora is a forest spirit of Brazilian folklore who guards wildlife from hunters and is often shown riding a peccary.

long_description.id: Caipora adalah roh hutan atau makhluk mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat Brasil yang menjaga satwa liar dan hewan buruan. Namanya berasal dari bahasa Tupi dan berarti "penghuni hutan". Luís da Câmara Cascudo berpendapat Caapora adalah bentuk maskulin dan Caipora bentuk femininnya.
long_description.en: Caipora is a forest spirit or humanoid of Brazilian folklore that guards wildlife and game. Its name comes from Tupi and means "inhabitant of the forest". Luís da Câmara Cascudo argued that Caapora is the masculine form and Caipora the feminine.

long_description.id: Wujudnya beragam: anak pribumi kecil berkulit gelap, kerdil, atau makhluk berbulu bertubuh besar. Ia sering menunggang peccary dan membawa tongkat atau cambuk dari tumbuhan tertentu. Caipora menerima suap tembakau dan minuman keras; menurut satu sumber, ia meminta tembakau untuk pipanya dan berbuat iseng jahat bila tidak diberi.
long_description.en: Its form varies: a small dark-skinned Native child, a dwarf, or a large hairy humanoid or beast. It often rides a peccary and carries a stick or whip made of certain plants. Caipora accepts bribes of tobacco and alcohol; one source says she asks for tobacco for her pipe and plays malicious pranks if refused.

long_description.id: Caipora kadang dikacaukan dengan Curupira, roh pelindung hutan lainnya. Dalam bahasa sehari-hari, kata Caipora juga dipakai secara kiasan untuk orang yang dianggap membawa pengaruh buruk.
long_description.en: Caipora is sometimes confused with Curupira, another forest protector. In everyday language the word Caipora is also used figuratively for people thought to bring bad influence.

short_description.id: Doñas de fuera, "Nona-nona dari Luar", adalah makhluk peri dalam cerita rakyat Sisilia yang membawa perempuan ke pertemuan malam di Benevento dan muncul dalam pengadilan penyihir abad ke-16 dan ke-17.
short_description.en: The Doñas de fuera, 'Ladies from the Outside', are fairy beings of Sicilian folklore who carried women to night gatherings at Benevento and appear in the 16th- and 17th-century witch trials.

long_description.id: Doñas de fuera adalah makhluk peri dalam cerita rakyat Sisilia, sebanding dengan peri Inggris, yang namanya juga dipakai untuk perempuan yang bergaul dengan mereka. Mereka cantik, berpakaian putih, merah, atau hitam, berkaki cakar kucing atau kuku kuda, datang dalam kelompok lima atau tujuh diiringi kecapi, dan membawa perempuan "berdarah manis" ke Benevento dengan kambing terbang. Setiap Selasa, Kamis, dan Sabtu mereka bertemu anggota kelompoknya di hutan, dan kelompok Tujuh Peri dapat berubah menjadi kucing.
long_description.en: The Doñas de fuera are fairy beings of Sicilian folklore, comparable to English fairies, whose name was also used for the women who kept company with them. Beautiful, dressed in white, red or black, with cat's paws or horse's hooves for feet, they came in groups of five or seven to lute music and carried 'sweet-blooded' women to Benevento on flying goats. Every Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday they met their company in the woods, and the Seven Fairies could turn into cats.

long_description.id: Mereka mudah tersinggung: lelaki yang memukul atau tersandung peri yang tak terlihat menderita kram. Pada malam hari mereka berkeliling rumah, makan, minum, dan memeluk bayi. Antara akhir abad ke-16 dan pertengahan abad ke-17, 65 orang di Sisilia, banyak di antaranya dianggap rekan para peri, diadili Inkuisisi karena sihir.
long_description.en: They were easily offended: a man who struck or tripped over an unseen fairy got a cramp. By night they went from house to house, eating, drinking and embracing infants. Between the late 16th and mid-17th centuries, 65 people in Sicily, many thought to be fairy associates, were tried by the Inquisition for sorcery.

sources.title: Procès des sorcières féeriques de Sicile

claims.quote: Doñas de fuera (Spanish for "Ladies from the Outside"; Sicily was under Spanish rule at the time) were supernatural female beings comparable to the fairies of English folklore. In the 16th to mid-17th centuries, the doñas de fuera also played a role in the witch trials in Sicily.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Sisilia, Doñas de fuera (bahasa Spanyol, "Nona-nona dari Luar", karena Sisilia saat itu di bawah Spanyol) adalah makhluk gaib perempuan yang sebanding dengan peri Inggris, dan pada abad ke-16 sampai pertengahan abad ke-17 berperan dalam pengadilan penyihir di Sisilia.
statement.en: In Sicilian folklore the Doñas de fuera (Spanish, 'Ladies from the Outside', as Sicily was then under Spain) were supernatural female beings like English fairies, and from the 16th to mid-17th centuries they figured in Sicily's witch trials.

claims.quote: would make contact with humans, mostly women deemed to have “sweet blood”, whom they took to Benevento ... by mounting them on magical, flying goats.

statement.id: Mereka menghubungi manusia, kebanyakan perempuan yang dianggap "berdarah manis", dan membawa mereka ke Benevento dengan menunggang kambing terbang ajaib.
statement.en: They contacted humans, mostly women thought to have 'sweet blood', and carried them to Benevento on magical flying goats.

claims.quote: They were described as beauties dressed in white, red or black; they could be male or female, and their feet were the paws of cats, horses or of a peculiar "round" shape. They came in groups of five or seven and a male fairy played the lute or the guitar while dancing.

statement.id: Mereka digambarkan cantik dan berpakaian putih, merah, atau hitam, bisa laki-laki atau perempuan, dengan kaki seperti cakar kucing, kuku kuda, atau berbentuk "bulat", dan datang dalam kelompok lima atau tujuh sementara peri laki-laki bermain kecapi atau gitar sambil menari.
statement.en: They were beauties in white, red or black, male or female, with feet like cat's paws, horse's hooves or a strange 'round' shape, coming in groups of five or seven while a male fairy played lute or guitar and danced.

claims.quote: Every Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, the fairies met the humans belonging to their company in the woods.

statement.id: Setiap Selasa, Kamis, dan Sabtu para peri bertemu manusia anggota kelompok mereka di hutan.
statement.en: Every Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday the fairies met the humans of their company in the woods.

claims.quote: A congregation called The Seven Fairies could transform themselves to cats and something called aydon; ayodons were able to kill.

statement.id: Kelompok bernama Tujuh Peri dapat berubah menjadi kucing dan makhluk bernama aydon yang mampu membunuh.
statement.en: A congregation called the Seven Fairies could turn into cats and into 'aydons', which could kill.

claims.quote: In one story, a man who was not associated with the fairies and was unable to see them developed a painful cramp after hitting one of the fairies who was listening to him play music.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, seorang lelaki yang tidak bisa melihat para peri menderita kram yang menyakitkan setelah memukul peri yang sedang mendengarkan musiknya.
statement.en: In one story a man who could not see the fairies suffered a painful cramp after striking a fairy who was listening to him play.

claims.quote: Another story involves several people who had disturbed the fairies while they nocturnally travelled from house to house, eating and drinking as they routinely embraced the town's infants.

statement.id: Kisah lain menceritakan orang-orang yang mengganggu para peri saat mereka berkeliling dari rumah ke rumah pada malam hari, makan, minum, dan memeluk bayi-bayi kota.
statement.en: Another tells of people who disturbed the fairies as they went from house to house by night, eating, drinking and embracing the town's infants.

claims.quote: The trial summaries, sent to the Spanish Inquisition's Suprema in Madrid by the Sicilian tribunal, reflected a total of 65 people, eight of them male, many of whom were believed to be associates of fairies, who were put on trial for sorcery.

statement.id: Ringkasan pengadilan yang dikirim tribunal Sisilia ke Suprema Inkuisisi Spanyol di Madrid mencatat 65 orang, delapan di antaranya laki-laki, banyak yang dianggap rekan para peri, yang diadili karena sihir.
statement.en: Trial summaries sent by the Sicilian tribunal to the Spanish Inquisition's Suprema in Madrid record 65 people, eight of them men, many believed to be fairy associates, tried for sorcery.

claims.quote: Les procès des sorcières féeriques de Sicile se sont déroulés de la fin du XVIe siècle au milieu du XVIIe siècle. Ils représentent un phénomène unique, car dans cette région, les procès de sorcières impliquèrent le folklore des fées.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, pengadilan "penyihir peri" Sisilia berlangsung dari akhir abad ke-16 sampai pertengahan abad ke-17 dan unik karena melibatkan cerita rakyat tentang peri.
statement.en: According to the French article, the Sicilian 'fairy witch' trials ran from the late 16th to the mid-17th century and were unique in involving fairy folklore.

claims.quote: Dans une histoire, un homme sans rapport avec elles, et ne les voyant donc pas, souffrit d'une crampe douloureuse après avoir trébuché sur une d'elles.

statement.id: Dalam versi artikel bahasa Prancis, lelaki itu kram setelah tersandung salah satu peri.
statement.en: In the French article's version, the man got the cramp after tripping over one of the fairies.

claims.quote: erano esseri femminili soprannaturali paragonabili alle fate del folclore britannico.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, Donas de fuera adalah makhluk gaib perempuan yang sebanding dengan peri dalam cerita rakyat Britania.
statement.en: According to the Italian article, the Donas de fuera were supernatural female beings comparable to the fairies of British folklore.

short_description.id: Duppy adalah sebutan Karibia untuk hantu atau roh, umumnya dianggap roh jahat yang membawa kemalangan dan menghantui orang pada malam hari.
short_description.en: Duppy is the Caribbean word for a ghost or spirit, generally seen as a malevolent spirit that brings misfortune and haunts people at night.

long_description.id: Duppy adalah kata asal Afrika yang dipakai di pulau-pulau Karibia seperti Bahama, Barbados, dan Jamaika untuk hantu atau roh; di banyak pulau Antilles Kecil roh ini disebut jumbie. long_description.en: Duppy is a word of African origin used on Caribbean islands such as the Bahamas, Barbados and Jamaica for a ghost or spirit; on many islands of the Lesser Antilles these spirits are called jumbies. short_description.id: Duppy adalah sebutan Karibia untuk hantu atau roh, umumnya dianggap roh jahat yang membawa kemalangan dan menghantui orang pada malam hari.
short_description.en: Duppy is the Caribbean word for a ghost or spirit, generally seen as a malevolent spirit that brings misfortune and haunts people at night.

long_description.id: Duppy adalah kata asal Afrika yang dipakai di pulau-pulau Karibia seperti Bahama, Barbados, dan Jamaika untuk hantu atau roh; di banyak pulau Antilles Kecil roh ini disebut jumbie. Duppy umumnya dianggap roh jahat yang membawa kemalangan dan menghantui orang pada malam hari. Rolling Calf yang berbelit rantai, kuda berkaki tiga, dan Ol' Hige termasuk roh yang paling jahat.
long_description.en: Duppy is a word of African origin used on Caribbean islands such as the Bahamas, Barbados and Jamaica for a ghost or spirit; on many islands of the Lesser Antilles these spirits are called jumbies. Duppy are generally seen as malevolent spirits that bring misfortune and haunt people at night. The chained Rolling Calf, the three-footed horse and Ol' Hige are among the most malicious.

long_description.id: Asal katanya diperdebatkan: dari bahasa Ga, mengingat banyak tradisi Afrika di Jamaika berasal dari orang Ashanti; dari Dapaa, hari khusus dalam kalender Akan; atau dari kata patois Jamaika yang asal-usulnya tidak pasti.
long_description.en: Its origin is debated: from the Ga language, since much African tradition in Jamaica comes from the Ashanti; from Dapaa, a special day in the Akan calendar; or from a Jamaican patois word of uncertain origin.

short_description.id: Groac'h adalah peri air Breton, sering tua dan mirip penyihir, yang tinggal di gua dan di bawah laut, dapat berubah wujud, dan dikenal jahat lewat cerita Émile Souvestre.
short_description.en: The groac'h is a Breton water fairy, often old and witch-like, living in caves and under the sea, able to change shape, and known as malevolent through Émile Souvestre's story.

long_description.id: Groac'h, kata Breton untuk peri, penyihir, atau nenek tua, adalah peri air Bretagne yang muncul dalam berbagai wujud, sering pada malam hari, kadang bergigi walrus. Ia tinggal di gua, di bawah pantai, dan di bawah laut, berkuasa atas alam dan dapat berubah wujud. Groagez paling sering dijumpai di hutan dan dekat mata air sebagai peri sumur, dan kisah lain menyebut mereka peri tua penyendiri yang murah hadiah.
long_description.en: The groac'h, Breton for fairy, witch or crone, is a water fairy of Brittany appearing in many forms, often at night, sometimes with walrus teeth. It lives in caves, under the beach and under the sea, commands nature and can shift shape. The groagez are met most often in forests and by springs as fairies of wells, and other tales make them lonely old fairies generous with gifts.

long_description.id: Citra jahatnya terutama berasal dari cerita Émile Souvestre tentang groac'h di Kepulauan Glénan yang mengubah lelaki menjadi ikan; menurut Joseph Rio, penyamaannya dengan peri lebih karena cerita itu daripada tradisi rakyat. Nama tempat seperti pulau Groix dan mercusuar La Vieille terkait dengannya, dan asal-usulnya dicari pada dewi kuno yang dijadikan setan. Ia muncul dalam novel La Pâleur et le Sang (1983).
long_description.en: Its wicked image comes mostly from Émile Souvestre's tale of a groac'h on the Glénan Islands who turns men into fish; Joseph Rio holds that its equation with the fairy owes more to that tale than to folk tradition. Place names such as the island of Groix and the La Vieille lighthouse are linked to it, and its origin is sought in demonized ancient goddesses. It appears in the novel La Pâleur et le Sang (1983).

statement.en: A groac'h (Breton for 'fairy', 'witch' or 'crone'; plural groagez) is a kind of Breton water fairy, seen in various forms, often at night, many old, like ogres and witches, sometimes with walrus teeth.

statement.id: Groagez adalah peri yang paling sering dijumpai di Bretagne, biasanya di hutan dan dekat mata air; mereka pada dasarnya peri sumur Breton.
statement.en: The groagez are the fairies most often met in Brittany, generally in forests and near springs; they are essentially the fairies of Breton wells.

claims.quote: It is mainly known as a malevolent figure, largely because of Émile Souvestre's story La Groac'h de l'île du Lok, in which the fairy seduces men, changes them into fish and serves them as meals to her guests, on one of the Glénan Islands.

statement.id: Ia terutama dikenal jahat karena cerita Émile Souvestre, La Groac'h de l'île du Lok, tentang peri di salah satu Kepulauan Glénan yang merayu lelaki, mengubah mereka menjadi ikan, dan menyajikannya kepada tamunya.
statement.en: It is known mainly as malevolent because of Émile Souvestre's story La Groac'h de l'île du Lok, in which the fairy on one of the Glénan Islands seduces men, turns them into fish and serves them to her guests.

claims.quote: Other tales present them as old solitary fairies who can overwhelm with gifts the humans who visit them.

claims.quote: The origin of those fairies that belong to the archetype of "the crone" is to be found in the ancient female divinities demonized by Christianity.

claims.quote: According to Joseph Rio the assimilation of the groac'h with the fairy is more the result of the influence of Émile Souvestre's tale, and commentaries on it, than a belief deriving from the popular traditions of Lower Brittany

statement.id: Menurut Joseph Rio, penyamaan groac'h dengan peri lebih merupakan hasil pengaruh cerita Émile Souvestre dan tafsirannya daripada kepercayaan rakyat Bretagne Bawah.

short_description.id: Gwragedd Annwn adalah peri perempuan cantik dalam folklor Welsh yang tinggal di bawah danau dan sungai, bagian dari Tylwyth Teg.
short_description.en: Gwragedd Annwn are beautiful female fairies of Welsh folklore who live beneath lakes and rivers, counted among the Tylwyth Teg.

long_description.id: Gwragedd Annwn (tunggal gwraig Annwn), juga disebut Dames of Elfin Land atau Wives of the Lower World, adalah peri perempuan cantik dalam folklor Welsh yang tinggal di bawah danau dan sungai. Mereka termasuk Tylwyth Teg, bangsa peri Welsh, dan kisah mereka terjalin dengan asal-usul sapi hitam Welsh. Kadang mereka naik ke dunia atas dan dapat dilihat orang biasa.
long_description.en: Gwragedd Annwn (singular gwraig Annwn), also called Dames of Elfin Land or Wives of the Lower World, are lovely female fairies of Welsh folklore living under lakes and rivers. They belong to the Tylwyth Teg, the Welsh fairy folk, and their story is bound up with the origin of the Welsh black cattle. At times they rise to the upper world and can be seen by ordinary people.

long_description.id: Konon mereka diciptakan St. Patrick saat ia pergi dari Irlandia ke Wales menemui St. David: orang-orang Welsh yang mencacinya diubah menjadi ikan, sedangkan para perempuan menjadi peri danau. Tidak seperti selkie atau merrow, mereka tidak bercirikan makhluk laut, dan hanya tinggal di danau dan sungai seperti Llyn Barfog di Gwynedd dan Danau Crumlyn dekat Briton Ferry; mereka berpakaian hijau.
long_description.en: They were supposedly made by St. Patrick on a journey from Ireland to Wales to see St. David: Welsh folk who abused him were turned into fish, and the women among them into lake fairies. Unlike selkies or merrows they have no sea-creature traits, living only in lakes and rivers such as Llyn Barfog in Gwynedd and Crumlyn Lake near Briton Ferry, and they dress in green.

short_description.id: Jentil adalah bangsa raksasa berbulu dalam mitologi Basque, pembangun dolmen dan pelempar batu antargunung, yang lenyap ke bumi saat cahaya kelahiran Kristus muncul.
short_description.en: The jentil are a race of hairy giants in Basque mythology, dolmen builders and mountain-to-mountain stone throwers, who vanished into the earth when the light of Christ's birth appeared.

long_description.id: Jentil atau jentilak, dari bahasa Latin gentilis, "orang kafir", adalah bangsa raksasa Basque yang dianggap pembangun dolmen dan monumen megalitik lain. Mereka berbulu, begitu tinggi hingga dapat berjalan di laut, dan melempar batu dari gunung ke gunung, yang menjelaskan bongkah batu terpencil dan bahkan permainan pilota; sebagian orang mengaitkan kekalahan Roland di Roncevaux dengan mereka. Mereka menemukan pengolahan logam dan gergaji serta mengajari manusia bertani.
long_description.en: The jentil or jentilak, from Latin gentilis, 'gentile', are a Basque race of giants credited with building dolmens and other megaliths. They were hairy, tall enough to wade in the sea, and threw rocks from mountain to mountain, explaining lone boulders and even the game of pilota; some tied Roland's defeat at Roncevaux to them. They invented metalworking and the saw and taught humans to farm.

long_description.id: Ketika awan bercahaya pertanda kelahiran Kristus (Kixmi) muncul, mereka bersembunyi di bawah dolmen di lembah Arratzaren atau menjatuhkan diri dari gunung; hanya Olentzero yang tersisa dan kini muncul saat Natal. Sekitar selusin legenda "Akhir Kaum Jentil" dikenal sampai Bigorre dan Couserans, dan nama tempat seperti jentilarri dan jentilzulo mengenang mereka. Mereka tampaknya mewakili bangsa Basque pra-Kristen sendiri.
long_description.en: When a bright cloud heralding Christ's birth (Kixmi) appeared, they hid under a dolmen in the Arratzaren valley or leapt from a mountain; only Olentzero remained and now appears at Christmas. About a dozen 'End of the Gentiles' legends are known as far as Bigorre and Couserans, and place names such as jentilarri and jentilzulo recall them. They seem to stand for the pre-Christian Basques themselves.

claims.quote: The jentil (or jentilak with the Basque plural), are a race of giants in Basque mythology. This word meaning gentile, from Latin gentilis, was used to refer to pre-Christian civilizations and in particular to the builders of megalithic monuments, to which the other Basque mythical legend the Mairuak are involved too.

statement.id: Jentil (jamak Basque: jentilak) adalah bangsa raksasa dalam mitologi Basque; kata ini berarti "orang kafir", dari bahasa Latin gentilis, dan dipakai untuk peradaban pra-Kristen, khususnya pembangun monumen megalitik, yang juga dikaitkan dengan Mairu (mairuak).
statement.en: The jentil (Basque plural jentilak) are a race of giants in Basque mythology; the word means 'gentile', from Latin gentilis, and was used for pre-Christian civilisations, especially the builders of megalithic monuments, with which the Mairu (mairuak) are also linked.

claims.quote: The jentil were believed to have lived alongside the Basque people. They were hairy and so tall that they could walk in the sea and throw rocks from one mountain to another.

statement.id: Jentil dipercaya hidup berdampingan dengan orang Basque; mereka berbulu dan begitu tinggi sehingga dapat berjalan di laut dan melempar batu dari satu gunung ke gunung lain.
statement.en: The jentil were believed to have lived alongside the Basques; they were hairy and so tall they could walk in the sea and throw rocks from one mountain to another.

claims.quote: This stone throwing has led to several tales and explanations for ancient stone buildings and large isolated rocks. Even the Basque ball game, pilota, is ascribed to these stone-throwers.

statement.id: Lemparan batu ini menjelaskan bangunan batu kuno dan bongkah batu besar yang terpencil, bahkan permainan bola Basque pilota dikaitkan dengan mereka.
statement.en: This stone-throwing explains ancient stone buildings and big isolated rocks, and even the Basque ball game pilota is ascribed to them.

claims.quote: Some attributed to the jentil the defeat of Roland in the Battle of Roncevaux, where the Basques defeated the Frankish army by throwing rocks on them.

statement.id: Sebagian orang mengaitkan kekalahan Roland dalam Pertempuran Roncevaux, ketika orang Basque mengalahkan pasukan Frank dengan melempar batu, dengan para jentil.
statement.en: Some credited the jentil with Roland's defeat at Roncevaux, where the Basques beat the Frankish army by hurling rocks.

claims.quote: They also were said to have invented metallurgy and the saw and first grew wheat, teaching humans to farm.

statement.id: Mereka juga dikatakan menemukan pengolahan logam dan gergaji, pertama kali menanam gandum, dan mengajari manusia bertani.
statement.en: They were also said to have invented metalworking and the saw, first grown wheat and taught humans to farm.

claims.quote: They disappeared into the earth under a dolmen in the Arratzaren valley in Navarra when a portentous luminous cloud – perhaps a star – appeared, said to have heralded the birth of Christ (Kixmi) and the end of the jentil age. Other stories say jentil threw themselves from a mountain.

statement.id: Mereka lenyap ke dalam bumi di bawah sebuah dolmen di lembah Arratzaren, Navarra, ketika muncul awan bercahaya, mungkin bintang, pertanda kelahiran Kristus (Kixmi) dan akhir zaman jentil; kisah lain menyebut mereka menjatuhkan diri dari gunung.
statement.en: They vanished into the earth under a dolmen in the Arratzaren valley in Navarre when a portentous bright cloud, perhaps a star, appeared, heralding the birth of Christ (Kixmi) and the end of the jentil age; other stories say they threw themselves off a mountain.

claims.quote: Only Olentzero remained, a giant who appears at Christmas and is reproduced as straw dolls.

statement.id: Hanya Olentzero yang tersisa, raksasa yang muncul saat Natal dan dibuat sebagai boneka jerami.
statement.en: Only Olentzero remained, a giant who appears at Christmas and is made as straw dolls.

claims.quote: Dolmens are   jentilarri or jentiletxe, harrespil are jentilbaratz, caves can be jentilzulo or jentilkoba.

statement.id: Dolmen disebut jentilarri atau jentiletxe, lingkaran batu harrespil disebut jentilbaratz, dan gua disebut jentilzulo atau jentilkoba.
statement.en: Dolmens are called jentilarri or jentiletxe, harrespil stone circles jentilbaratz, and caves jentilzulo or jentilkoba.

claims.quote: Au Pays basque, mais aussi en Bigorre et en Couserans, on connait une douzaine de légendes avec le titre « La fin des Gentils » qui racontent les circonstances de la disparition d'une « race » qui précéda les humains actuels, à l'âge d'or des Pyrénées.

statement.id: Di negeri Basque, Bigorre, dan Couserans dikenal sekitar selusin legenda berjudul "Akhir Kaum Jentil" tentang lenyapnya bangsa yang mendahului manusia sekarang pada zaman keemasan Pyrenees.
statement.en: In the Basque Country, Bigorre and Couserans about a dozen legends titled 'The End of the Gentiles' tell how a race that preceded present humans vanished in the Pyrenees' golden age.

claims.quote: Los gentiles parecen representar al propio pueblo vasco precristiano, montañés por excelencia.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, para jentil tampaknya mewakili bangsa Basque pra-Kristen sendiri, penghuni gunung sejati.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, the jentilak seem to represent the pre-Christian Basque people themselves, mountain-dwellers par excellence.
