short_description.id: Maggy Moulach (Meg Mullach) adalah brownie Dataran Tinggi dalam folklor Skotlandia, ibu dari dobie Brownie-Clod, juga dijuluki Hairy Meg.
short_description.en: Maggy Moulach (Meg Mullach) is a Highland brownie of Scottish folklore, mother of the dobie Brownie-Clod, also called Hairy Meg.

long_description.id: Maggy Moulach (juga Meg Mullach, Maggie Moloch, Maug Moulach dan Hairy Meg) adalah tokoh folklor Skotlandia yang dikatakan brownie Dataran Tinggi. Ia punya putra bernama Brownie-Clod, seorang dobie, yaitu brownie yang agak lamban tetapi bermaksud baik. Ia digambarkan setinggi dua kaki dengan rambut lebat atau tangan berbulu, sehingga dijuluki Hairy Meg; dalam versi kemudian ia menjulurkan tangan lewat cerobong untuk mencuri anak, dan dapat berubah menjadi belalang.
long_description.en: Maggy Moulach (also Meg Mullach, Maggie Moloch, Maug Moulach and Hairy Meg) is a figure of Scottish folklore said to be a Highland brownie. Her son Brownie-Clod was a dobie, a rather slow but well-meaning kind of brownie. She stood two feet high with a great mass of hair or hairy hands, hence Hairy Meg; later versions have her reaching down chimneys to steal children, and she could turn into a grasshopper.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda awal, Meg dan putranya tinggal di kastel Tullochgorm milik keluarga Grant; ia mengerjakan tugas brownie, membantu kepala klan menang catur, dan bertindak sebagai banshee yang mengabarkan kematian keluarga itu. Dalam kisah lain, Brownie-Clod yang menjaga sebuah penggilingan disiram air mendidih oleh seorang gadis yang mengaku bernama "Mi fein" (diriku sendiri); ia mati, dan Maggy kemudian membalas dendam dengan melempar bangku hingga gadis itu tewas.
long_description.en: In early legends Meg and her son lived in Tullochgorm castle, owned by the Grant family; she did brownie work, helped the clan chief beat rivals at chess, and served as a banshee announcing deaths in the family. In another tale Brownie-Clod, guarding a mill, was scalded by a girl who gave her name as 'Mi fein', 'me myself'; he died, and Maggy later took revenge by hurling a stool that killed the girl.

short_description.id: Nicnevin adalah penyihir atau ratu peri dalam folklor Skotlandia, sering disamakan dengan Gyre-Carling atau Hecate.
short_description.en: Nicnevin is a witch or fairy queen of Scottish folklore, often equated with the Gyre-Carling or Hecate.

long_description.id: Nicneven, Nicnevin atau Nicnevan adalah penyihir atau ratu peri dalam folklor Skotlandia. Ia sering dianggap sama dengan Gyre-Carling atau Hecate, meski sebagian sarjana tidak setuju, dan masih diperdebatkan apakah nama itu awalnya merujuk pada perempuan nyata atau dewi. Namanya mungkin dari nama keluarga Gaelik Skotlandia Neachneohain ("putri yang ilahi") atau NicNaoimhein ("putri santo kecil"), atau dari dewi perang Irlandia Neamhain.
long_description.en: Nicneven, Nicnevin or Nicnevan is a witch or queen of the fairies in Scottish folklore. She is frequently identified with the Gyre-Carling or Hecate, though some scholars dispute this, and it is unclear whether the name first belonged to a real woman or a goddess. It may come from the Scottish Gaelic surname Neachneohain, 'daughter(s) of the divine', or NicNaoimhein, 'daughter of the little saint', or from the Irish war goddess Neamhain.

long_description.id: Penyebutan pertamanya oleh penyair istana Alexander Montgomerie sekitar 1580, dalam flyting melawan Patrick Hume dari Polwarth di bawah Raja James VI: bayi Polwart diserahkan kepada Nicneven dan para penyihirnya, yang mempersembahkannya kepada Hecate dan Pluto. Pada 1801 John Leyden menyebut Nicneven salah satu nama untuk gyre-carlin, Ratu Peri. Robert Cromek menggambarkannya bermantel kelabu panjang dan membawa tongkat yang dapat mengubah air menjadi batu; para ibu menakuti anak-anak dengan ancaman akan menyerahkan mereka kepada McNeven.
long_description.en: She is first named by the court poet Alexander Montgomerie around 1580 in a flyting against Patrick Hume of Polwarth under King James VI, where the infant Polwart is handed to Nicneven and her witches, who devote him to Hecate and Pluto. In 1801 John Leyden listed Nicneven among the names of the gyre-carlin, Queen of Fairies. Robert Cromek described her in a long grey cloak, bearing a wand able to turn water to rock, and said mothers scared children by threatening to give them to McNeven.

short_description.id: Portunes adalah makhluk kecil bermuka tua dalam cerita rakyat Inggris yang menurut Gervase dari Tilbury masuk ke rumah petani pada malam hari, membantu pekerjaan berat, dan sesekali mengerjai penunggang kuda.
short_description.en: The Portunes are small, old-faced creatures of English folklore who, according to Gervase of Tilbury, enter farmers' houses at night, help with heavy work, and sometimes prank lone riders.

long_description.id: Portunes, atau Neptunes, adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Inggris yang oleh Gervase dari Tilbury hanya dijelaskan dalam karyanya Otia Imperialia dari abad pertengahan. Gervase menyebutnya iblis tetapi ragu apakah mereka lebih tepat disebut sosok yang asal-usulnya tak diketahui; orang Prancis menyebutnya Neptunes dan orang Inggris Portunes.
long_description.en: The Portunes, also called Neptunes, are English folklore creatures that Gervase of Tilbury describes solely in his medieval Latin Otia Imperialia. Gervase calls them demons but doubts whether they are better described as figures of unknown origin; the French call them Neptunes and the English Portunes.

long_description.id: Mereka memasuki rumah petani pada malam hari, menghangatkan diri di dekat api, dan memanggang katak kecil yang mereka bawa. Wajah mereka seperti lelaki tua dengan pipi berkerut, dan tubuh mereka sangat kecil. Mereka membantu pekerjaan berat dan menyelesaikannya lebih cepat daripada manusia, dan sifat mereka melayani, bukan mencelakai.
long_description.en: By night they come into farmers' houses, warm up at the hearth, and grill little frogs that they bring along. Their faces are like old men's with wrinkled cheeks, and their bodies are very small. They help with heavy work and finish it faster than any man, and their nature is to serve, not to harm.

long_description.id: Satu kebiasaan mengganggu mereka: bergabung tanpa terlihat dengan penunggang kuda yang sendirian pada malam hari, mengambil kendali, menuntun kuda ke lumpur, lalu pergi dengan tawa keras.
long_description.en: They have one annoying habit: invisibly joining a lone rider at night, taking the reins, leading the horse into a slough, and going off with a loud laugh.

long_description.id: Para ahli berbeda pendapat. K. M. Briggs menggolongkan mereka sebagai peri, C. C. Oman menilai keterangan ukurannya keliru, dan Banks serta Binns membantahnya. Young menilai kaitan langsung antara nama Inggris itu dan dewa Romawi Portunus tidak mungkin.
long_description.en: Scholars differ. K. M. Briggs classes them as fairies, C. C. Oman thinks the description of their size is corrupted, and Banks and Binns dispute that. Young judges a direct link between the English name and the Roman god Portunus unlikely.

claims.quote: Portunes, or Neptunes, are creatures of English folklore described only in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury.

statement.id: Portunes, atau Neptunes, adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Inggris yang hanya dijelaskan dalam karya Latin abad pertengahan Otia Imperialia oleh Gervase dari Tilbury.
statement.en: Portunes, or Neptunes, are creatures of English folklore described only in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury.

claims.quote: Portunes enter peasant houses at night, warm themselves by the fire, and roast small frogs which they carry in their pockets.

statement.id: Dalam catatan Gervase, Portunes memasuki rumah petani pada malam hari, menghangatkan diri di dekat api, dan memanggang katak kecil yang mereka bawa di saku.
statement.en: In Gervase's account Portunes enter peasant houses at night, warm themselves by the fire, and roast small frogs which they carry in their pockets.

claims.quote: K. M. Briggs classes them as a type of fairy, arguing that Gervase's account was the first description of small English fairies.

statement.id: K. M. Briggs menggolongkan mereka sebagai sejenis peri dan berpendapat catatan Gervase adalah gambaran pertama tentang peri-peri kecil Inggris.
statement.en: K. M. Briggs classes them as a type of fairy, arguing that Gervase's account was the first description of small English fairies.

claims.quote: C. C. Oman argues that the description of the size of the Portunes is corrupted because the size of the creatures is incompatible with the housework they do

statement.id: C. C. Oman berpendapat bahwa keterangan ukuran Portunes keliru karena ukuran itu tidak sesuai dengan pekerjaan rumah yang mereka lakukan.
statement.en: C. C. Oman argues that the description of the size of the Portunes is corrupted because their size is incompatible with the housework they do.

claims.quote: S. E. Banks and J. W. Binns dispute this, arguing that the manuscripts are in agreement and Gervase clearly intended to describe them as very small.

statement.id: S. E. Banks dan J. W. Binns membantahnya, dengan alasan naskah-naskah sepakat dan Gervase jelas bermaksud menggambarkan mereka sangat kecil.
statement.en: S. E. Banks and J. W. Binns dispute this, arguing that the manuscripts agree and Gervase clearly meant to describe them as very small.

claims.quote: Young also considers a link between the English name and the Roman god Portunus, but argues that a direct relationship is unlikely because there is no evidence for a cult of Portunus in Roman Britain

statement.id: Young mempertimbangkan kaitan antara nama Inggris itu dan dewa Romawi Portunus, tetapi menilai hubungan langsung tidak mungkin karena tidak ada bukti pemujaan Portunus di Britania Romawi.
statement.en: Young considers a link between the English name and the Roman god Portunus but argues a direct relationship is unlikely because there is no evidence for a cult of Portunus in Roman Britain.

claims.quote: They have in England certain demons, though I know not whether I should call them demons or figures of a secret and unknown generation, which the French call Neptunes, the English Portunes.

statement.id: Gervase (dikutip Keightley) menulis bahwa di Inggris ada semacam iblis (demons), meski ia ragu apakah harus menyebutnya iblis atau sosok yang asal-usulnya rahasia dan tak diketahui; orang Prancis menyebutnya Neptunes, orang Inggris Portunes.
statement.en: Gervase (as quoted by Keightley) writes that in England there are certain demons, though he doubts whether to call them demons or figures of a secret and unknown generation, which the French call Neptunes and the English Portunes.

claims.quote: It is their nature to embrace the simple life of comfortable farmers

statement.id: Sudah menjadi sifat mereka untuk menjalani hidup sederhana para petani yang berkecukupan.
statement.en: It is their nature to embrace the simple life of comfortable farmers.

claims.quote: They have the countenance of old men, with wrinkled cheeks, and they are of a very small stature, not being quite half-an-inch high.

statement.id: Mereka berwajah lelaki tua dengan pipi berkerut dan bertubuh sangat kecil, tingginya tidak sampai setengah inci.
statement.en: They have the countenance of old men with wrinkled cheeks and are of very small stature, not quite half-an-inch high.

claims.quote: if anything is to be carried into the house, or any laborious work to be done, they lend a hand, and finish it sooner than any man could. It is their nature to have the power to serve, but not to injure.

statement.id: Bila ada barang yang harus dibawa ke rumah atau pekerjaan berat yang harus dilakukan, mereka membantu dan menyelesaikannya lebih cepat daripada manusia mana pun; sifat mereka berkuasa melayani tetapi tidak mencelakai.
statement.en: If anything is to be carried into the house or any laborious work done, they lend a hand and finish it sooner than any man could; their nature is to have the power to serve but not to injure.

short_description.id: Shtriga adalah penyihir vampir dalam mitologi Albania yang mengisap darah bayi saat malam lalu berubah menjadi serangga terbang.
short_description.en: The shtriga is a vampiric witch of Albanian mythology who sucks the blood of infants at night and then turns into a flying insect.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Albania, shtriga adalah penyihir vampir yang malam-malam mengisap darah bayi yang sedang tidur, lalu menjelma serangga terbang, biasanya ngengat, lalat, atau lebah. Hanya shtriga itu sendiri yang dapat menyembuhkan korbannya, sering dengan meludah ke mulut mereka; yang tidak disembuhkan akan sakit lalu mati.
long_description.en: In Albanian folklore the shtriga is a vampire witch who drinks the blood of sleeping babies by night and then becomes a flying insect, usually a moth, fly or bee. Only the shtriga herself can heal her victims, often by spitting into their mouths; those left uncured fall ill and die.

long_description.id: Ia sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan bertatapan penuh benci, kadang berjubah, dengan wajah rusak mengerikan, tinggal di tempat tersembunyi di hutan dan punya kekuatan gaib. Kata shtriga juga berarti "penyihir" secara umum; bentuk laki-lakinya shtrigu atau shtrigan. Menurut cerita rakyat Albania utara, perempuan tidak lahir sebagai penyihir, melainkan menjadi penyihir, sering karena tidak punya anak atau karena iri hati.
long_description.en: She is often pictured as a woman with a hate-filled gaze, sometimes caped, with a dreadfully disfigured face, hiding in the forest and wielding supernatural powers. The word also means "witch" in general; the male form is shtrigu or shtrigan. Northern Albanian folklore holds that a woman is not born a witch but becomes one, often through childlessness or envy.

long_description.id: Kata shtrigë berasal dari bahasa Latin strīga, "roh jahat, penyihir", yang berkerabat dengan strega dalam bahasa Italia dan strzyga dalam bahasa Polandia.
long_description.en: The word shtrigë comes from Latin strīga, "evil spirit, witch", akin to Italian strega and Polish strzyga.

short_description.id: Solomonar adalah penyihir dalam cerita rakyat Rumania yang dipercaya menunggang naga dan mengendalikan cuaca, mendatangkan hujan, guntur, atau badai es.
short_description.en: The solomonar is a wizard of Romanian folklore believed to ride a dragon and control the weather, bringing rain, thunder or hail.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, solomonar (jamak solomonari) adalah penyihir yang menunggang naga, zmeu atau balaur, dan mengatur cuaca, mendatangkan hujan, guntur, atau badai es. Solomonari bukan makhluk gaib, melainkan manusia yang mempelajari sihir; mereka direkrut dari rakyat biasa dan belajar di sekolah sihir Solomonărie atau Şolomanţă.
long_description.en: In Romanian folklore the solomonar (plural solomonari) is a wizard who rides a dragon, a zmeu or balaur, and governs the weather, bringing rain, thunder or hailstorms. They are not supernatural beings but people who have learned sorcery; they are drawn from ordinary folk and trained at the magic school called Solomonărie or Şolomanţă.

long_description.id: Mereka digambarkan bertubuh tinggi, berambut merah, berjubah putih panjang seperti petani atau berpakaian compang-camping. Saat tidak melayani Iblis, mereka sering terlihat meminta-minta, dan uang yang terkumpul dilempar ke sungai sebagai persembahan bagi roh air. Tas sihir mereka berisi kapak besi, tali kekang dari kulit kayu birch atau kekang emas, dan sebuah kitab kebijaksanaan yang menjadi sumber kekuatan mereka.
long_description.en: They are pictured as tall and red-haired, in long white peasant robes or in rags. When not serving the Devil they are often seen begging, and the coins they collect are thrown into rivers as offerings to the water spirits. Their magic bag holds an iron axe, birch-bark reins or a golden bridle, and a book of wisdom that is the source of their power.

long_description.id: Pada masa awal solomonari dianggap penyihir baik, tetapi setelah datangnya Kekristenan mereka berubah menjadi jahat. Nama mereka umumnya dikaitkan dengan Raja Salomo melalui akhiran pekerjaan -ar, walau itu mungkin etimologi rakyat.
long_description.en: Early on the solomonari were thought of as good magicians, but after Christianity arrived they turned evil. Their name is usually linked to King Solomon through the occupational suffix -ar, though this may be folk etymology.

short_description.id: Soucouyant adalah nenek sihir pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Karibia yang pada malam hari melepas kulitnya, terbang sebagai bola api, dan mengisap darah orang yang tidur.
short_description.en: The soucouyant is a shape-shifting hag of Caribbean folklore who sheds her skin at night, flies as a fireball and sucks the blood of sleepers.

long_description.id: Soucouyant adalah nenek sihir pengubah wujud dan pengisap darah dalam cerita rakyat Karibia; di Guyana, Belize, dan Jamaika ia disebut Ol' Higue. Pada siang hari ia tampak sebagai orang tua penyendiri. Pada malam hari ia melepas kulit keriputnya, menaruhnya di lesung, lalu terbang sebagai bola api untuk mengisap darah orang yang tidur, meninggalkan memar biru kehitaman. Darah itu ditukarnya dengan kekuatan jahat dari Bazil, iblis penghuni pohon kapuk.
long_description.en: The soucouyant is a shape-shifting, blood-sucking hag of Caribbean folklore, called Ol' Higue in Guyana, Belize and Jamaica. By day she looks like a reclusive old person. At night she sheds her wrinkled skin into a mortar and flies as a fireball to suck the blood of sleepers, leaving black and blue marks. She trades the blood for evil powers with Bazil, the demon of the silk cotton tree.

long_description.id: Untuk membongkarnya, orang menaburkan beras di sekitar rumah atau persimpangan desa, karena soucouyant terpaksa memungutinya butir demi butir. Di Trinidad dan Tobago, salib di jendela dipercaya melindungi rumah darinya.
long_description.en: To expose her, people heap rice around the house or the village crossroads, since the soucouyant must gather it grain by grain. In Trinidad and Tobago a cross in the window is believed to protect a house from her.

short_description.id: Tangie adalah roh laut pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Orkney dan Shetland, berwujud kuda atau lelaki tua berselimut rumput laut.
short_description.en: The tangie is a shape-shifting sea spirit of Orkney and Shetland folklore, appearing as a horse or an old man covered in seaweed.

long_description.id: Tangie (atau tongie) adalah roh laut pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Kepulauan Orkney dan Shetland di Skotlandia (Scotland). Sebagai kuda laut atau duyung lelaki, ia berwujud kuda atau lelaki tua. Biasanya ia digambarkan berselimut rumput laut, dan namanya berasal dari "tang", rumput laut genus Fucus. Ia terkenal meneror pelancong yang sendirian, terutama perempuan muda di jalan dekat danau (loch) pada malam hari, yang diculiknya dan dimakannya di bawah air.
long_description.en: Island lore from Orkney and Shetland in Scotland tells of the tangie (or tongie), a sea spirit that changes shape; as a sea horse or merman it appears as either a horse or an old man. It is usually said to be draped in seaweed, and its name comes from 'tang', seaweed of the genus Fucus. It is known for frightening lone travellers, above all young women on roads near the lochs at night, whom it carries off and devours underwater.

long_description.id: Mirip tetapi berbeda dari nuggle yang lebih kecil dan kurang berbahaya, tangie dapat membuat manusia dan hewan gila. Tangie berperan besar dalam legenda Shetland tentang Black Eric, pencuri domba: tangie yang ditungganginya memberinya bantuan gaib saat ia menyerbu pertanian sekitar. Dalam pertarungan terakhirnya dengan petani Sandy Breamer, Black Eric jatuh ke laut dan tewas, tetapi tangie terus meneror daerah itu. Menurut artikel ru, Танги juga disebut pengubah wujud laut yang dapat membuat orang atau hewan gila.
long_description.en: Similar to yet distinct from the smaller, milder nuggle, the tangie can drive people and animals mad. It plays a big part in Shetland's tale of Black Eric the sheep thief, whose tangie steed gave him supernatural help as he raided nearby crofts. In his last fight with the crofter Sandy Breamer, Black Eric fell into the sea and died, but the tangie went on terrorising the area. According to the ru article the Танги is likewise a sea shapeshifter able to drive a person or animal mad.

short_description.id: Ratman dari Southend adalah legenda urban Inggris dari Southend-on-Sea, Essex, tentang hantu lelaki tunawisma yang wajahnya dimakan tikus.
short_description.en: The Ratman of Southend is an English urban legend from Southend-on-Sea, Essex, about the ghost of a homeless man whose face was eaten by rats.

long_description.id: Ratman dari Southend adalah legenda urban Inggris yang berasal dari Southend-on-Sea, Essex. Kisahnya tentang seorang lelaki tua tunawisma yang, saat berlindung dari dingin di sebuah terowongan bawah jalan, diserang sekelompok pemuda dan dipukuli hingga hampir mati; dingin dan kehilangan darah mengakhiri hidupnya. Saat ia mati, binatang pengerat yang menghuni tempat itu berkumpul dan ternyata memakan wajahnya.
long_description.en: The Ratman of Southend is an English urban legend from Southend-on-Sea in Essex. It tells of an old homeless man who, sheltering from the cold in an underpass, was attacked by a gang of youths and beaten nearly to death; cold and blood loss did the rest. As he died the vermin of the place gathered and were found to have eaten his face.

long_description.id: Setelah itu sesosok bayangan hantu terlihat di terowongan itu, dan orang mendengar cicitan seperti tikus serta bunyi garukan seolah cakar besar bergerak di dinding. Sebuah film pendek tentang Ratman karya Michael Holiday diikutkan dalam festival Horror-on-Sea pada 2019, dan Ratman muncul sebagai musuh dalam mod Fallout: London (2024).
long_description.en: Afterwards a ghostly figure was seen in the underpass, with rat-like squeals and scraping as of large claws on the walls. A short film about the Ratman by Michael Holiday was entered in the 2019 Horror-on-Sea festival, and the Ratman appears as an enemy in the 2024 mod Fallout: London.

short_description.id: Vântoase adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, sejenis iele, yang menimbulkan badai debu dan angin kencang.
short_description.en: The vântoase are female spirits of Romanian folklore, a kind of iele, who raise dust storms and strong winds.

long_description.id: Vântoase adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, sejenis roh perempuan (iele). Kepercayaan rakyat menggambarkan mereka mampu menimbulkan badai debu dan angin kencang, mirip harpy. Nama mereka berasal dari kata Rumania vânt, "angin".
long_description.en: In Romanian folklore the vântoase are a kind of female spirit, counted among the iele. Popular belief credits them with whipping up dust storms and fierce winds, rather like harpies. Their name comes from the Romanian vânt, "wind".

long_description.id: Mereka tinggal di hutan, di udara, dan di danau yang dalam, dan bepergian dengan kereta khusus atau dengan angin. Kadang dikatakan mereka menimbulkan angin saat menari hora. Mereka dipercaya dapat menyerang anak-anak, dan satu-satunya perlindungan adalah "rumput angin" yang misterius. Dalam beberapa legenda mereka justru digambarkan sebagai pelayan Tuhan.
long_description.en: They live in forests, in the air and in deep lakes, and travel in a special wagon or on the winds. They are sometimes said to raise winds while dancing the hora. They are believed able to attack children, the only protection being the mysterious "grass of the winds". In some legends they are instead servants of God.

short_description.id: Yekyua atau "hewan induk" adalah roh pendamping berwujud hewan yang melindungi dukun Yakut, dan nasib dukun terikat pada hewannya.
short_description.en: A yekyua or "mother animal" is an animal-shaped familiar spirit protecting Yakut shamans, whose fate is bound to their animal.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan Yakut, yekyua atau "hewan induk" adalah golongan roh yang bersembunyi sampai salju mencair pada musim semi. Setiap yekyua terkait dengan seekor hewan dan menjadi roh pendamping yang melindungi dukun; yang paling berbahaya melekat pada dukun perempuan. Hanya dukun yang dapat melihatnya.
long_description.en: In Yakut belief a yekyua or "mother animal" is a class of spirit that hides until the snow melts in spring. Each yekyua is tied to an animal and acts as a familiar that protects a shaman; the most dangerous belong to female shamans. Only shamans can see them.

long_description.id: Jenis hewan menentukan kekuatannya: yekyua anjing lemah, yekyua rusa elk kuat, dan yang terkuat adalah mamut. Nasib dukun terikat pada hewannya: saat para yekyua bertarung pada musim semi dukunnya jatuh sakit, dan bila hewannya dibunuh dukun lain, ia pun meninggal.
long_description.en: The animal decides its strength: dog yekyua are weak, elk yekyua strong, and the mammoth strongest. A shaman's fate is bound to the animal: when yekyua fight in spring their shamans fall ill, and if the animal is killed by another shaman, its shaman dies.

short_description.id: Yuxa adalah ular tua dalam mitologi Turkik yang berubah menjadi makhluk berkepala naga dan dapat menjelma gadis cantik untuk menikahi lelaki.
short_description.en: Yuxa is an aged snake of Turkic mythology that becomes a dragon-headed creature and can take the form of a beautiful maiden to marry men.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Yuxa adalah makhluk berkepala naga, bertubuh reptil, dan berekor berduri, yang konon menyemburkan api atau bergigitan berbisa. Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, ular berusia 100 tahun berubah menjadi Yuxa; versi Bashkir dan Tatar menyebut ajdaha yang hidup 500 hingga 1000 tahun. Dalam dongeng ia menjelma gadis cantik yang menikahi lelaki, dan ia juga bisa menjadi pemuda tampan untuk menggoda atau menakuti orang.
long_description.en: In Turkic mythology Yuxa is a dragon-headed, reptile-bodied creature with a barbed tail, said to breathe fire or bite venomously. Popular belief holds that a 100-year-old snake becomes a Yuxa; Bashkir and Tatar versions speak of an ajdaha that lives 500 to 1000 years. In fairy tales it becomes a beautiful maiden who marries men, and it can also become a handsome youth to seduce or frighten people.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Bashkir dan Tatar, Yuxa adalah iblis jahat yang terkait dengan air dan muncul dalam dongeng serta epos Ural-batyr. Bahasa Bashkir masih menyimpan ungkapan seperti yukha yylan untuk orang licik.
long_description.en: In Bashkir and Tatar mythology Yuxa is an evil demon linked with water, appearing in fairy tales and the epic Ural-batyr. Bashkir still uses phrases like yukha yylan for a treacherous person.

short_description.id: Dökkálfar ("Elf Gelap") dan Ljósálfar ("Elf Terang") adalah dua jenis elf yang berlawanan dalam mitologi Nordik, yang satu tinggal di dalam bumi dan yang lain di Álfheimr.
short_description.en: The Dökkálfar ('Dark Elves') and Ljósálfar ('Light Elves') are two contrasting kinds of elves in Norse myth, one dwelling in the earth and the other in Álfheimr.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik (Norse mythology), Dökkálfar ("Dark Elves") dan Ljósálfar ("Light Elves") adalah dua jenis elf yang berlawanan: elf gelap tinggal di dalam bumi dan berkulit gelap, sedangkan elf terang tinggal di Álfheimr dan "lebih elok dari matahari untuk dipandang". Keduanya tercatat dalam Prose Edda karya Snorri Sturluson abad ke-13 dan dalam puisi Norse Kuno akhir Hrafnagaldr Óðins. Dalam bab 17 Gylfaginning, High menyebut Ljósálfar tinggal di Álfheimr, sedangkan Dökkálfar tinggal di bawah tanah dan tampak, terlebih berperilaku, sangat berbeda; elf terang "lebih elok dari matahari", elf gelap "lebih hitam dari ter".
long_description.en: In Norse myth the Dökkálfar ('Dark Elves') and Ljósálfar ('Light Elves') are two opposed kinds of elves: the dark ones live inside the earth and are dark-skinned, while the light ones dwell in Álfheimr and outshine the sun in beauty. Both appear in the Prose Edda, written by Snorri Sturluson in the 13th century, and in the late Old Norse poem Hrafnagaldr Óðins. In chapter 17 of Gylfaginning, High says the Ljósálfar dwell in Álfheimr while the Dökkálfar live underground and differ greatly in looks and still more in conduct; the light are 'fairer than the sun', the dark 'blacker than pitch'.

long_description.id: High juga menyebut bahwa langit-langit lain di atas, Andlàngr dan Víðbláinn tempat Gimlé berada, untuk sementara hanya dihuni elf terang. Karena konsep ini hanya tercatat dalam Gylfaginning dan Hrafnagaldr Óðins, tidak jelas apakah pembedaan dua jenis elf berasal dari Snorri sendiri; sebagian sarjana, seperti Anne Holtsmark dengan ragu, menduganya hasil pengaruh Kristen tentang malaikat terang dan gelap. Terjemahan Anderson atas Younger Edda (Gutenberg) berbunyi: elf terang tinggal di Alfheim, elf gelap di dalam bumi, berbeda rupa dan lebih berbeda lagi dalam perbuatan.
long_description.en: High also says the further heavens above, Andlàngr and Víðbláinn where Gimlé stands, are for now inhabited only by light elves. Since the idea is found only in Gylfaginning and Hrafnagaldr Óðins, it is unclear whether Snorri devised the split himself; some scholars, Anne Holtsmark among them with reservations, think it reflects Christian ideas of angels of light and darkness. Anderson's translation of the Younger Edda (Gutenberg) reads that the light-elves live in Alfheim and the dark-elves down in the earth, unlike in looks and more so in deeds.

statement.en: Attested in Snorri Sturluson's 13th-century Prose Edda and the Old Norse poem Hrafnagaldr Óðins.

claims.quote: High says that the Ljósálfar live in Álfheimr, while the Dökkálfar dwell underground and look—and particularly behave—quite unlike the Ljósálfar. High describes the Ljósálfar as "fairer than the sun to look at", while the Dökkálfar are "blacker than pitch".

statement.id: Dalam bab 17 Gylfaginning, High: Ljósálfar di Álfheimr, Dökkálfar di bawah tanah; terang lebih elok dari matahari, gelap lebih hitam dari ter.
statement.en: In Gylfaginning ch. 17 High says the Ljósálfar live in Álfheimr, the Dökkálfar underground; light fairer than the sun, dark blacker than pitch.

claims.quote: High adds that "we believe it is only light-elves who inhabit these places for the time being".

statement.id: High: langit lain (Andlàngr, Víðbláinn, Gimlé) untuk sementara hanya dihuni elf terang.
statement.en: High: the other heavens (Andlàngr, Víðbláinn, Gimlé) are for now inhabited only by light elves.

claims.quote: There dwell the folk that are called light-elves; but the dark-elves dwell down in the earth, and they are unlike the light-elves in appearance, but much more so in deeds.

statement.id: Terjemahan Anderson (Younger Edda, Gutenberg): elf terang di Alfheim, elf gelap di dalam bumi, berbeda rupa dan perbuatan.
statement.en: Anderson's translation (Younger Edda, Gutenberg): light-elves in Alfheim, dark-elves in the earth, unlike in appearance and deeds.

claims.quote: As the concept is only recorded in Gylfaginning and the late poem Hrafnagaldr Óðins, it is unclear whether the distinction between the two types of elves originated with Snorri, or if he was merely recounting a concept already developed.

statement.id: Tak jelas apakah pembedaan ini berasal dari Snorri.
statement.en: It is unclear whether the distinction originated with Snorri.

claims.quote: The sub-classification perhaps resulted from Christian influence, by way of importation of the concept of good and evil and angels of light and darkness. Anne Holtsmark aired this view, though with some reservation

statement.id: Mungkin pengaruh Kristen (Christian), malaikat terang dan gelap; pendapat Anne Holtsmark.
statement.en: Perhaps Christian influence, angels of light and darkness; Anne Holtsmark's view.

short_description.id: Mazapégul adalah peri malam usil dari Romagna, Italia, bertopi merah dan berbulu kelabu, yang menimbulkan mimpi buruk, mengepang surai kuda, dan menyukai gadis cantik.
short_description.en: The mazapégul are mischievous night elves of Romagna, Italy, red-capped and grey-furred, who cause nightmares, braid horses' manes and dote on pretty girls.

long_description.id: Mazapégul adalah peri malam usil dari cerita rakyat Romagna, terutama di Apennine Forlì. Mereka campuran kera dan manusia kecil berbulu kelabu yang memakai topi merah, sumber kekuatan usil mereka. Mereka menimbulkan mimpi buruk dan rasa tercekik, menghilangkan benda, membuat piring beterbangan, dan mengepang surai kuda; mereka juga tidur di atas perut gadis cantik sambil memujinya.
long_description.en: The mazapégul are mischievous night elves of the folklore of Romagna, above all the Forlì Apennines. They are grey-furred crosses of ape and homunculus wearing a red cap, the source of their mischief. They cause nightmares and choking, make things vanish, send dishes flying and braid horses' manes; they also sleep on pretty girls' stomachs and flatter them.

long_description.id: Mencuri topinya atau menaburkan beras di jendela dapat menangkal mereka. Mereka diturunkan dari inkubus dan mirip Laurieddhu dari Italia selatan. Cerita tentang mereka dicatat Giuliano Fantaguzzi di Cesena awal abad ke-15, namanya muncul dalam kontrak tahun 1487 di Forlì, dan topi merahnya kini menjadi kostum karnaval Romagna.
long_description.en: Stealing its cap or scattering rice on the sill wards them off. They derive from the incubus and resemble the Laurieddhu of southern Italy. Giuliano Fantaguzzi recorded their lore in early 15th-century Cesena, the name appears in a 1487 contract at Forlì, and the red cap is now a Romagnol carnival costume.

who.en: A red-capped night elf.

role.en: Disturbs sleep.

famous_for.id: Topi merah.
famous_for.en: The red cap.

description.id: Topinya diperlukan untuk berbuat usil; bila dicuri, kekuatannya hilang.
description.en: It needs its cap for mischief; if stolen, its power goes.

description.id: Ia sibuk menghitung beras di ambang jendela sampai fajar.
description.en: It is kept busy counting rice on the sill until dawn.

description.id: Nama keluarga peri ini pertama kali tercatat.
description.en: The elves' family name is first recorded.

note.id: Peri Italia selatan yang mirip.
note.en: A similar southern Italian elf.

note.id: Iblis asal-usulnya.
note.en: The demon it descends from.

claims.quote: The mazapégul, also known by several other names in Romagnol, are mischievous nocturnal elves in the folklore of Romagna, especially around the Apennines of Forlì, in northern Italy.

statement.id: Mazapégul, yang punya banyak nama lain dalam bahasa Romagnol, adalah peri malam yang usil dalam cerita rakyat Romagna, terutama di Pegunungan Apennine sekitar Forlì, Italia utara.
statement.en: The mazapégul, known by several other Romagnol names, are mischievous night elves of the folklore of Romagna, especially around the Apennines of Forlì in northern Italy.

claims.quote: The elves are portrayed as a cross between apes and homunculi, with grey fur, also resembling cats or monkeys. They wear a distinctive red cap, which they require to perform their mischief.

statement.id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai campuran kera dan manusia kecil berbulu kelabu, mirip kucing atau monyet, dan memakai topi merah khas yang mereka perlukan untuk berbuat usil.
statement.en: They are shown as a cross between apes and homunculi with grey fur, also like cats or monkeys, wearing a distinctive red cap they need for their mischief.

claims.quote: The mazapégul are credited for causing nightmares, including sleep paralysis or sensations of suffocation, ruffling women's hair in their sleep, causing stomach pains, making objects disappear, playing the cymbals, causing dishes to fly, and making victims gain weight.

statement.id: Mazapégul dianggap menyebabkan mimpi buruk, termasuk kelumpuhan tidur dan rasa tercekik, mengacak rambut perempuan yang tidur, sakit perut, menghilangkan benda, memainkan simbal, dan membuat piring beterbangan.
statement.en: The mazapégul are blamed for nightmares, including sleep paralysis and choking sensations, tousling sleeping women's hair, stomach aches, vanishing objects, clashing cymbals and flying dishes.

claims.quote: In the countryside, they disturb animals, especially horses, who wake in the mornings covered in sweat and with braided tails and manes.

statement.id: Di pedesaan mereka mengganggu hewan, terutama kuda, yang bangun pagi dengan tubuh berkeringat serta ekor dan surai terkepang.
statement.en: In the countryside they bother animals, especially horses, which wake sweating with braided tails and manes.

claims.quote: Attracted by beautiful young girls, the elves enter their rooms at night and fall asleep on their stomachs. They compliment them, saying: "What beautiful eyes! What beautiful hair!"

statement.id: Tertarik pada gadis cantik, mereka masuk ke kamar gadis pada malam hari, tidur di atas perutnya, dan memujinya: "Betapa indah matamu! Betapa indah rambutmu!"
statement.en: Drawn to pretty girls, they enter their rooms at night, fall asleep on their stomachs and praise them: 'What beautiful eyes! What beautiful hair!'

claims.quote: If its cap is stolen or thrown into the well, either its vanquisher is tormented at night with the demand of "give me back my cap!"

statement.id: Bila topinya dicuri atau dilempar ke sumur, si pencuri bisa diganggu setiap malam dengan tuntutan "kembalikan topiku!".
statement.en: If its cap is stolen or thrown down the well, the thief may be pestered at night with the cry 'give me back my cap!'

claims.quote: sprinkling grains of rice on a windowsill so that the mazapégul is distracted by counting them until daybreak.

statement.id: Menaburkan butir beras di ambang jendela membuat mazapégul sibuk menghitungnya sampai fajar.
statement.en: Grains of rice scattered on a windowsill keep the mazapégul busy counting them until daybreak.

claims.quote: The mazapégul  descend from the mythological incubus, a demon that would disturb sleeping humans and take advantage of women. They share characteristics with elves from other regions of Italy, such as the Laurieddhu ... of southern Italy, as well as from the French Vosges.

statement.id: Mazapégul diturunkan dari inkubus, iblis yang mengganggu orang tidur dan memperdaya perempuan, dan memiliki kemiripan dengan peri daerah lain seperti Laurieddhu dari Italia selatan dan peri Vosges di Prancis.
statement.en: The mazapégul descend from the incubus, a demon that troubled sleepers and preyed on women, and share traits with elves elsewhere, such as the Laurieddhu of southern Italy and those of the French Vosges.

claims.quote: Folklore surrounding the mazapégul is recorded in a survey of early 15th-century Cesena by Giuliano Fantaguzzi.

statement.id: Cerita rakyat tentang mazapégul tercatat dalam tinjauan Giuliano Fantaguzzi tentang Cesena awal abad ke-15.
statement.en: Mazapégul lore is recorded in Giuliano Fantaguzzi's survey of early 15th-century Cesena.

claims.quote: El nombre de la familia que se menciona está documentado por primera vez en un extracto de un contrato de venta del 9 de mayo de 1487 en el Archivo general de Forlì

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, nama keluarga peri ini pertama kali tercatat dalam kutipan kontrak jual beli tertanggal 9 Mei 1487 di Arsip Umum Forlì.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, the family name is first recorded in an extract of a sales contract of 9 May 1487 in the General Archive of Forlì.

claims.quote: Il Mazapégul è un folletto della mitologia italiana, appartenente alla tradizione folclorica della Romagna, in particolare dell'Appennino forlivese.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Italia juga menyebut Mazapégul peri usil (folletto) dari tradisi rakyat Romagna, terutama Apennine Forlì.
statement.en: The Italian article also calls the Mazapégul a sprite (folletto) of the folk tradition of Romagna, especially the Forlì Apennines.

claims.quote: The mazapégul, particularly its red cap, features in Romagnol carnival costumes.

statement.id: Mazapégul, terutama topi merahnya, muncul dalam kostum karnaval Romagna.
statement.en: The mazapégul, especially its red cap, appears in Romagnol carnival costumes.

short_description.id: Will-o'-the-wisp adalah fenomena cahaya hantu di malam hari yang dalam cerita rakyat dikaitkan dengan arwah atau peri penyesat musafir di rawa-rawa.
short_description.en: The will-o'-the-wisp is an atmospheric ghost light in folklore attributed to spirits or fairies that mislead travelers in marshes.

long_description.id: Will-o'-the-wisp, yang juga dikenal sebagai ignis fatuus, adalah penampakan cahaya hantu di malam hari, terutama di atas rawa atau lahan basah. Cerita rakyat sering mengaitkannya dengan hantu, peri, atau roh alam yang menampakkan atau menyembunyikan arah jalan. Sosok ini digambarkan menari atau melayang hingga kemudian memudar saat didekati.
long_description.en: The will-o'-the-wisp, also called ignis fatuus, is an atmospheric ghost light seen at night, particularly over bogs or marshes. Folklore associates it with ghosts, fairies, or elemental spirits that reveal or conceal paths. It is depicted as dancing or flowing until fading when approached.

long_description.id: Secara etimologi, istilah ini merujuk pada lentera jerami yang dibawa oleh sosok bernama Will, serupa dengan sebutan jack-o'-lantern. Cerita rakyat mencatat nama-nama padanan seperti feu follet, Irrlicht, sebutan hinkypunk, serta Ellylldan.
long_description.en: Etymologically, the term stems from a straw torch associated with Will, akin to jack-o'-lantern. Folklore records corresponding names such as feu follet, Irrlicht, hinkypunk, and Ellylldan.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Skotlandia, fenomena ini sering digambarkan sebagai roh jahil atau hantu yang memikat musafir ke tempat berbahaya hingga menemui ajal, meski beberapa kisah mengaitkannya dengan petunjuk menuju harta terpendam. Beberapa keyakinan menyebut roh-roh ini adalah jiwa yang tidak diterima di Surga maupun Neraka sehingga terpaksa mengembara selamanya.
long_description.en: In Scottish traditions, these lights are often depicted as mischievous spirits or ghosts luring travelers off safe paths to their doom, though rare tales associate them with guiding to vast treasure. Some believe they represent souls rejected by both Heaven and Hell, doomed to wander.

literal_meaning.id: ikatan jerami yang dipakai sebagai obor
literal_meaning.en: a twist of straw used as a torch

learning_questions.id: Mengapa cahaya rawa di berbagai belahan dunia hampir selalu dihubungkan dengan makhluk gaib penyesat jalan?
learning_questions.en: Why are marsh lights across different world cultures almost consistently linked to deceptive supernatural beings?

claims.quote: In folklore, a will-o'-the-wisp, or will-o'-wisp (Latin: ignis fatuus, "foolish flame"), is an atmospheric ghost light seen by travellers at night, especially over bogs, swamps, or marshes.

statement.id: Will-o'-the-wisp atau ignis fatuus adalah cahaya hantu atmosfer yang dilihat musafir di malam hari di atas rawa atau lahan basah.
statement.en: A will-o'-the-wisp or ignis fatuus is an atmospheric ghost light seen by travellers at night, especially over bogs, swamps, or marshes.

claims.quote: In folklore, will-o'-the-wisps are typically attributed as ghosts, fairies or elemental spirits meant to reveal (or conceal) a path or direction.

statement.id: Will-o'-the-wisp biasanya dianggap sebagai hantu, peri, atau roh alam penunjuk atau penyembunyi jalan.
statement.en: Will-o'-the-wisps are typically attributed as ghosts, fairies or elemental spirits meant to reveal or conceal a path or direction.

claims.quote: These wisps are portrayed as dancing or flowing in a static form, until noticed or followed, in which case they visually fade or disappear.

statement.id: Cahaya ini digambarkan menari atau melayang statis hingga memudar atau lenyap saat diikuti.
statement.en: These wisps are portrayed as dancing or flowing in a static form, until noticed or followed, in which case they visually fade or disappear.

claims.quote: The term will-o'-the-wisp comes from wisp, a bundle of sticks or paper sometimes used as a torch and the name 'Will', thus meaning 'Will of the torch'.

statement.id: Istilah will-o'-the-wisp berasal dari kata wisp yang berarti ikatan kayu atau kertas untuk obor, dan nama Will.
statement.en: The term will-o'-the-wisp comes from wisp, a bundle of sticks or paper used as a torch, and the name Will.

claims.quote: The term jack-o'-lantern ('Jack of the lantern') originally referred to a will-o'-the-wisp.

statement.id: Istilah jack-o'-lantern awalnya merujuk pada will-o'-the-wisp.
statement.en: The term jack-o'-lantern originally referred to a will-o'-the-wisp.

claims.quote: Equivalents of the will-o'-the-wisps appear in European folklore by various names, e.g., ignis fatuus in Latin, feu follet in French, Irrlicht or Irrwisch in Germany, dwaallicht in The Netherlands and fuoco fatuo in Italy.

statement.id: Padanan will-o'-the-wisp muncul dalam cerita rakyat Eropa dengan berbagai nama, seperti ignis fatuus, feu follet, Irrlicht, dwaallicht, dan fuoco fatuo.
statement.en: Equivalents of will-o'-the-wisps appear in European folklore under names such as ignis fatuus, feu follet, Irrlicht, dwaallicht, and fuoco fatuo.

claims.quote: The phenomenon is known in the United Kingdom by a variety of names, including jack-o'-lantern, friar's lantern, and hinkypunk, and is said to mislead and/or guide travellers by resembling a flickering lamp or lantern.

statement.id: Di Britania Raya fenomena ini dikenal dengan berbagai nama termasuk jack-o'-lantern, friar's lantern, dan hinkypunk.
statement.en: The phenomenon is known in the United Kingdom by various names including jack-o'-lantern, friar's lantern, and hinkypunk.

claims.quote: In Scottish folklore, will-o’-the-wisps are variously depicted either as mischievous spirits (typically fairies), or even the ghosts of the dead, eager to lead travellers off their path and into their death.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, will-o'-the-wisp digambarkan sebagai roh jahil atau hantu orang mati yang memikat pengelana keluar dari jalur menuju kematian.
statement.en: In Scottish folklore, will-o'-the-wisps are depicted as mischievous spirits or ghosts of the dead eager to lead travellers off path and to death.

claims.quote: The lights typically appear close to a bog, marsh, or swamp, places where straying off the beaten path can become dangerous – or even deadly.

statement.id: Cahaya tersebut biasanya muncul dekat rawa atau paya di mana tersesat dari jalan setapak bisa berbahaya atau mematikan.
statement.en: The lights typically appear close to a bog, marsh, or swamp where straying off path can become dangerous or deadly.

claims.quote: Few myths, however, show the will-o’-the-wisps leading those brave enough to follow the light in the middle of the dark night to a vast treasure, and riches beyond comprehension.

statement.id: Beberapa mitos menggambarkan will-o'-the-wisp memandu orang yang berani mengikuti cahaya menuju harta karun besar.
statement.en: Few myths show the will-o'-the-wisps leading those brave enough to follow the light in the dark night to vast treasure.

claims.quote: Some believe that the spirits behind the will-o’-the-wisps were souls who could enter neither Heaven nor Hell, and were thus forced to wander the earth forever.

statement.id: Sebagian percaya roh will-o'-the-wisp adalah jiwa yang tidak dapat masuk Surga maupun Neraka dan terpaksa mengembara selamanya.
statement.en: Some believe the spirits behind will-o'-the-wisps were souls unable to enter Heaven or Hell, forced to wander the earth forever.

claims.quote: Uniquely, in Sweden, the will-o’-the-wisp is a manifestation of an unbaptised soul, who tries to lead travellers into bodies of water, in hopes of being baptised.

statement.id: Di Swedia will-o'-the-wisp dipandang sebagai perwujudan jiwa yang belum dibaptis yang menuntun musafir ke perairan demi dibaptis.
statement.en: In Sweden, the will-o'-the-wisp is a manifestation of an unbaptised soul trying to lead travellers into water in hopes of baptism.

claims.quote: Will-o'-the-Wisp is the most common English designation for a family of fairy-beings characterized by their fiery appearance and their tendency to lead nighttime wayfarers astray.

statement.id: Will-o'-the-Wisp adalah sebutan bahasa Inggris paling umum bagi keluarga makhluk peri berpenampilan api yang suka menyesatkan pejalan malam.
statement.en: Will-o'-the-Wisp is the most common English designation for fairy-beings characterized by fiery appearance and misleading wayfarers.

claims.quote: The term wisp refers to a twist of straw, used as a torch.

statement.id: Istilah wisp merujuk pada pilinan jerami yang digunakan sebagai obor.
statement.en: The term wisp refers to a twist of straw, used as a torch.

claims.quote: Other names for these apparitions include Hobby-Lantern, Jack-o'-Lantern, Jenny-Burnt-Tale, Kitty-Candlestick, Peg-a-Lantern, and many more.

statement.id: Nama lain untuk penampakan ini mencakup Hobby-Lantern, Jack-o'-Lantern, Jenny-Burnt-Tale, Kitty-Candlestick, dan Peg-a-Lantern.
statement.en: Other names for these apparitions include Hobby-Lantern, Jack-o'-Lantern, Jenny-Burnt-Tale, Kitty-Candlestick, and Peg-a-Lantern.

claims.quote: The Ellylldan is a species of elf exactly corresponding to the English will-o'-wisp.

statement.id: Ellylldan adalah jenis peri Wales yang berpadanan persis dengan will-o'-wisp Inggris.
statement.en: The Ellylldan is a species of elf exactly corresponding to the English will-o'-wisp.

short_description.id: Chai nenesi adalah roh air perempuan dalam mitologi Turkik yang menyeret orang ke rawa dan danau, dan pada malam hari duduk menyisir rambutnya di tepi air.
short_description.en: Chai nenesi is a female water spirit of Turkic mythology who drags people into swamps and lakes and at night sits combing her hair by the water.

long_description.id: Chai nenesi adalah sebutan bagi roh air dalam mitologi Turkik dan Azerbaijan, biasanya penghuni sungai kecil. Ia menyeret orang ke rawa dan danau, membunuh hewan yang berdiri dekat air tenang, mengganggu orang, dan membawa sial bagi pemabuk. Dalam kebanyakan versi ia makhluk gelisah yang dikaitkan dengan "kekuatan najis" dan keluar dari air pada malam hari untuk bernyanyi di pohon atau menyisir rambut di dermaga.
long_description.en: Chai nenesi is a name for water spirits in Turkic and Azerbaijani mythology, usually dwelling in creeks. She drags people into swamps and lakes, kills animals standing by still water, harasses people and brings bad luck to drunkards. In most versions she is a restless being tied to the "unclean force" who leaves the water at night to sing in a tree or comb her hair on a dock.

short_description.id: Hantu Hampton Court adalah sosok berjubah panjang yang terekam kamera CCTV di Istana Hampton Court pada Oktober 2003 ketika sebuah pintu darurat berulang kali terbuka sendiri.
short_description.en: The Hampton Court ghost is a figure in a long robe captured by CCTV at Hampton Court Palace in October 2003, when a fire door repeatedly opened by itself.

long_description.id: Sebutan hantu Hampton Court merujuk pada sosok yang tampak dalam rekaman CCTV di dekat Istana Hampton Court pada Oktober 2003. Sosok itu mengenakan kain panjang mirip jubah dan diduga menghantui tempat itu selama beberapa hari atau bulan. Istana abad ke-16 di Surrey itu memang sudah lama punya reputasi berhantu.
long_description.en: The name Hampton Court ghost refers to a figure seen on CCTV footage near Hampton Court Palace in October 2003. The figure wore a long robe-like cloth and was said to haunt the place for some days or months. The 16th-century palace in Surrey already had a long reputation for being haunted.

long_description.id: Petugas keamanan berulang kali mendapati pintu darurat di sebuah area pameran terbuka. Pada kesempatan pertama rekaman hanya menunjukkan pintu terbanting terbuka tanpa sebab yang terlihat; pada kesempatan kedua muncul sosok berpakaian zaman dahulu yang lalu menutup pintu itu; pada hari ketiga pintu kembali terbuka tetapi tidak ada sosok yang tampak. Bahkan sebelumnya seorang pengunjung menulis di buku tamu istana bahwa ia merasa melihat hantu di area yang sama.
long_description.en: Security staff repeatedly found a fire door standing open in an exhibition area. The first time, the footage showed only the doors flying open with no visible cause; the second time, a figure in period dress appeared and closed them; on a third day the same happened but no figure was seen. Earlier still, a visitor had noted in the palace's visitor book a belief of having encountered a ghost in that same area.

long_description.id: Dalam foto diam yang dirilis istana, sosok pria berpakaian mirip jubah melangkah keluar dari ambang pintu yang gelap sambil menjulurkan satu lengan ke gagang pintu. Wajahnya tampak putih tidak wajar dibandingkan tangannya, dan seorang penjaga, James Faukes, berkata wajah itu tidak tampak seperti wajah manusia. Penjaga lain, Ian Franklin, menggambarkan sosok bermantel penuh yang menarik kedua daun pintu lalu menutupnya di belakangnya.
long_description.en: In the still photograph released by the palace, a man in a robe-like garment steps out of the shadowy doorway, one arm reaching for the door handle. His face looks unnaturally white beside his hand, and a warder, James Faukes, said the face did not look human. Another warder, Ian Franklin, described a figure in a full cloak pulling in both doors and closing them behind it.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel pertama, sosok itu pertama kali dilaporkan pada awal 2001, dan kejadian serupa pada 2015 kemudian terbukti bukan penampakan. Kejadian 2015 itu berupa foto seorang anak perempuan berumur 12 tahun yang dikaitkan dengan Grey Lady; Mick West menilai distorsinya mirip efek yang muncul saat seseorang lewat di depan kamera ketika mengambil foto panorama iPhone.
long_description.en: According to the first article, the figure was first reported in early 2001, and a similar incident in 2015 was later debunked. The 2015 case was a photo taken by a 12-year-old girl and linked to the Grey Lady; Mick West judged its distortion to resemble the effect of someone walking through the frame of an iPhone panorama.

short_description.en: The Irshi is a fairy of Turkic and Altai folklore who takes the form of a beautiful girl, dances superbly, cannot lie and sometimes kidnaps humans.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Turkik dan Altai, Irshi atau İrşi adalah peri, makhluk perempuan tanpa tubuh yang berwujud roh. Ia biasanya menjelma gadis cantik bersihir yang baik hati, lembut, pandai menari, dan tidak bisa berbohong, padahal sebenarnya tidak bermata, bertelinga, berhidung, atau berambut. Dalam dongeng, peri-peri ini menikahi para pahlawan.
long_description.en: In Turkic and Altai folklore the Irshi or İrşi is a fairy, a bodiless female being in spirit form. It usually takes the guise of a beautiful, magical girl who is kind, gentle, a superb dancer and unable to lie, though in truth it has no eyes, ears, nose or hair. In tales these fairies marry the heroes.

short_description.en: Joan the Wad is the Queen of the Pixies in Cornish folklore, a torch-bearing figure who may lead travellers astray or instead light their way to safety and good luck.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Cornwall, Joan the Wad dikenal sebagai Ratu para Pixie, makhluk mungil yang biasanya dihubungkan dengan Cornwall dan Devon di Inggris. Sebuah glosarium dialek menyebut namanya sebagai nama seorang elf atau pisky. Kata wad dalam bahasa sehari-hari Cornwall Timur berarti obor atau seikat jerami.
long_description.en: In Cornish folklore Joan the Wad is known as the Queen of the Pixies, tiny beings usually linked with Cornwall and Devon in England. A dialect glossary records her name as that of an elf or pisky. In Eastern Cornwall speech the word wad means a torch or a bundle of straw.

long_description.id: Ia dipasangkan dengan Jack o' the Lantern, Raja para Pixie, dan keduanya dapat dipandang sebagai tokoh sejenis will-o'-the-wisp yang membuat pelancong tersesat di padang sunyi. Namun, Joan juga dipercaya memakai obornya untuk menuntun orang menuju keselamatan dan keberuntungan. Ia sering digambarkan tanpa busana serta dihubungkan dengan unsur api dan air.
long_description.en: She is paired with Jack o' the Lantern, King of the Pixies, and both can be seen as will-o'-the-wisp type figures who lead travellers astray on lonely moors. Yet Joan is also believed to use her torch to guide people to safety and good luck. She is often shown naked and linked with the elements of fire and water.

long_description.id: Pada abad lalu, jimat keberuntungan berbentuk Joan the Wad dibuat secara luas sebagai industri rumahan, dan orang membawa figur kecilnya untuk peruntungan; gambarnya juga dipasang pada pengetuk pintu sebagai roh pelindung. Museum of Witchcraft di Boscastle menyimpan beberapa figur antik ini, termasuk jimat kuningan yang menampilkannya duduk dengan satu lengan melengkung di atas kepala. Catatan museum menyebut jimat ini tampaknya dirancang oleh F.T. Nettleinghame, yang mendaftarkannya pada 1932.
long_description.en: In the last century Joan the Wad lucky charms were widely made as a cottage industry, and people carried small figures of her for luck; her image also appeared on door knockers as a protective spirit. The Museum of Witchcraft in Boscastle holds some of these antique figures, including a brass charm showing her seated with one arm curved over her head. According to the museum record, F.T. Nettleinghame was apparently the designer of the charms and registered them in 1932.

short_description.id: Lavellan adalah makhluk air dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, mirip hewan pengerat atau kadal, yang dipercaya berbisa dan membahayakan ternak, bahkan dari kejauhan.
short_description.en: The lavellan is a water creature of Scottish folklore, rodent- or lizard-like, believed to be venomous and harmful to cattle, even from a distance.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, lavellan atau làbh-allan digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip hewan pengerat atau kadal dengan gigitan berbisa. Ia dikabarkan tinggal di perairan dan muncul dalam kisah-kisah dari Sutherland dan Caithness. Robert Sibbald dalam Scotia Illustrata menyebutnya hewan yang umum di Caithness, hidup di air, dengan kepala dan warna seperti musang, serta napas yang mencelakakan.
long_description.en: Scottish folklore pictures the lavellan (làbh-allan) as a beast resembling a rodent or a lizard, whose bite carries venom. It reportedly lives in water and features in tales from Sutherland and Caithness. Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata called it an animal common in Caithness, living in water, with a weasel-like head and colouring and a harmful breath.

long_description.id: Penduduk setempat percaya lavellan sangat berbahaya bagi ternak, dan Campbell mencatat bahwa ia konon dapat mencelakai sapi dari jarak empat puluh yard. Sebagai obat, ternak yang sakit diberi minum air tempat kulit lavellan dicelupkan; teks Latin Sibbald menyebut air rebusan kepalanya. Penyair Sutherland, Rob Donn, juga menyebut lavellan dalam lagu satirnya sebagai bahaya bagi orang yang pergi ke rawa atau hutan.
long_description.en: Local people believed the lavellan was especially harmful to cattle, and Campbell recorded that it was said to hurt cattle from forty yards away. As a cure, sick beasts were given water in which a lavellan's skin had been dipped; Sibbald's Latin text speaks of water in which its head was boiled. The Sutherland bard Rob Donn also named the lavellan in a satirical song as a danger to anyone who went to moss or wood.

long_description.id: Thomas Pennant, yang menanyakan makhluk ini di Ausdale, menduga lavellan sebenarnya cerurut air dan menyamakannya dengan hewan yang di Sutherland disebut water mole. Menurut peneliti Lee Raye, pandangan Pennant ini kini umumnya diterima sebagai tepat.
long_description.en: Thomas Pennant, who asked about the creature at Ausdale, suspected that the lavellan was really the water shrew and equated it with the animal called the water mole in Sutherland. The researcher Lee Raye notes that most now accept Pennant's identification as correct.

claims.quote: In Scottish folklore, the lavellan, làbh-allan, la-mhalan, or la-bhallan is a rodent- or lizard-like creature with a venomous bite.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, lavellan (làbh-allan, la-mhalan, la-bhallan) adalah makhluk mirip hewan pengerat atau kadal dengan gigitan berbisa.
statement.en: In Scottish folklore the lavellan (làbh-allan, la-mhalan, la-bhallan) is a rodent- or lizard-like creature with a venomous bite.

claims.quote: It reportedly lives in bodies of water. ... It features in tales from both Sutherland and Caithness.

statement.id: Makhluk ini dikabarkan hidup di perairan dan muncul dalam kisah-kisah dari Sutherland maupun Caithness.
statement.en: It reportedly lives in bodies of water and features in tales from both Sutherland and Caithness.

claims.quote: The lavellan was described in Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata as "an animal common in Caithness, it stays in water, it has a head similar to the weasel, and is a beast of the same colouring. The breath from these beasts does harm."

statement.id: Robert Sibbald dalam Scotia Illustrata menggambarkan lavellan sebagai hewan yang umum di Caithness, tinggal di air, berkepala dan berwarna seperti musang (weasel), dan napasnya mencelakakan.
statement.en: Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata described the lavellan as an animal common in Caithness that stays in water, with a head and colouring like a weasel, whose breath does harm.

claims.quote: In the settlement of Ausdale, Thomas Pennant asked the local people about the lavellan. They reportedly believed that the lavellan was particularly harmful to cattle

statement.id: Di permukiman Ausdale, Thomas Pennant menanyai penduduk tentang lavellan; mereka percaya lavellan sangat berbahaya bagi ternak sapi (cattle).
statement.en: At the settlement of Ausdale Thomas Pennant asked local people about the lavellan; they believed it was particularly harmful to cattle.

claims.quote: Pennant posited that the mythical lavellan was, in actuality, a water shrew (Neomys fodiens). According to researcher Lee Raye, Pennant's view is now generally accepted as accurate.

statement.id: Pennant menduga lavellan sebenarnya adalah cerurut air (water shrew, Neomys fodiens); menurut peneliti Lee Raye, pandangan Pennant kini umumnya diterima.
statement.en: Pennant posited that the lavellan was actually a water shrew (Neomys fodiens); according to researcher Lee Raye, this view is now generally accepted.

claims.quote: Lavellan.—This animal is peculiar to the north, where it is said to be able to hurt cattle from a distance of forty yards

statement.id: Campbell menulis bahwa lavellan khas wilayah utara dan dikatakan mampu mencelakai ternak dari jarak empat puluh yard.
statement.en: Campbell writes that the lavellan is peculiar to the north, where it is said to hurt cattle from forty yards away.

claims.quote: Lavellan, animal in Cathanesia frequens, in aquis degit, capite mustelae sylvestri simile, ejusdemque coloris, bestia est. Halitu Bestiis nocet.

statement.id: Teks Latin Sibbald yang dikutip Campbell: lavellan (Lavellan) adalah hewan yang umum di Caithness (Cathanesia), hidup di air (in aquis), berkepala seperti musang (mustelae), dan napasnya (halitu) mencelakai hewan ternak.
statement.en: Sibbald's Latin, quoted by Campbell: the Lavellan is an animal common in Caithness (Cathanesia), living in water (in aquis), with a head like a weasel (mustelae), harming beasts with its breath (halitu).

claims.quote: Remedium autem est, si de aqua bibant in quâ ejus caput coctum est.

statement.id: Menurut teks Latin itu, obatnya (remedium) adalah bila ternak minum air (aqua) tempat kepala (caput) hewan itu direbus.
statement.en: According to the Latin text, the remedy (remedium) is for the beasts to drink water (aqua) in which its head (caput) has been boiled.

claims.quote: I inquired here after the Lavellan, which, from description, I suspect to be the water shrew mouse.

statement.id: Pennant menulis bahwa ia menanyakan Lavellan dan dari deskripsinya menduga hewan itu cerurut air (water shrew mouse).
statement.en: Pennant wrote that he inquired after the Lavellan and from the description suspected it to be the water shrew mouse.

claims.quote: The country people have a notion that it is noxious to cattle; they preserve the skin, and, as a cure for their sick beasts, give them the water in which it has been dipt.

statement.id: Penduduk desa beranggapan lavellan berbahaya bagi ternak; mereka menyimpan kulitnya dan, sebagai obat ternak yang sakit, memberi mereka air tempat kulit itu dicelupkan.
statement.en: Country people thought it noxious to cattle; they kept its skin and, as a cure for sick beasts, gave them water in which it had been dipped.

claims.quote: I believe it to be the same animal which, in Sutherland, is called the water mole.

statement.id: Pennant meyakini hewan ini sama dengan yang di Sutherland disebut tikus mondok air (water mole).
statement.en: Pennant believed it to be the same animal called the water mole in Sutherland.

claims.quote: It is also mentioned by Rob Donn, the Sutherland bard, in his satirical song on “Mac Rorie’s Breeches”: “Let him not go away from the houses, to moss or wood, lest the Lavellan come and smite him.”

statement.id: Lavellan juga disebut oleh Rob Donn, penyair Sutherland, dalam lagu satirnya tentang "Mac Rorie's Breeches": jangan biarkan ia pergi dari rumah ke rawa atau hutan, agar Lavellan tidak datang dan memukulnya.
statement.en: It is also mentioned by Rob Donn, the Sutherland bard, in his satirical song on "Mac Rorie's Breeches": let him not leave the houses for moss or wood, lest the Lavellan come and smite him.

summary.id: Menurut Pennant, ternak diberi air tempat kulit lavellan dicelupkan.
summary.en: According to Pennant, cattle were given water in which the lavellan's skin had been dipped.

summary.id: Menurut teks Latin Sibbald, ternak minum air tempat kepalanya direbus.
summary.en: According to Sibbald's Latin, beasts drank water in which its head had been boiled.

did_you_know.id: Ternak yang sakit diobati dengan air tempat kulit lavellan dicelupkan.

description.id: Lavellan digambarkan memiliki gigitan berbisa.

description.id: Ia konon dapat mencelakai ternak dari jarak empat puluh yard, dan napasnya disebut mencelakakan.
description.en: It was said to hurt cattle from forty yards, and its breath was said to do harm.

learning_questions.id: Bagaimana pengamatan terhadap hewan nyata dapat melahirkan makhluk legenda?
learning_questions.en: How can observations of real animals give rise to legendary creatures?

sources.title: Superstitions of the Highlands and Islands of Scotland
sources.author: John Gregorson Campbell

claims.quote: In Scottish folklore, the lavellan, làbh-allan, la-mhalan, or la-bhallan is a rodent- or lizard-like creature with a venomous bite.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, lavellan (làbh-allan, la-mhalan, la-bhallan) adalah makhluk mirip hewan pengerat atau kadal dengan gigitan berbisa.
statement.en: In Scottish folklore the lavellan (làbh-allan, la-mhalan, la-bhallan) is a rodent- or lizard-like creature with a venomous bite.

claims.quote: It reportedly lives in bodies of water. ... It features in tales from both Sutherland and Caithness.

statement.id: Makhluk ini dikabarkan hidup di perairan dan muncul dalam kisah-kisah dari Sutherland maupun Caithness.
statement.en: It reportedly lives in bodies of water and features in tales from both Sutherland and Caithness.

claims.quote: The lavellan was described in Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata as "an animal common in Caithness, it stays in water, it has a head similar to the weasel, and is a beast of the same colouring. The breath from these beasts does harm."

statement.id: Robert Sibbald dalam Scotia Illustrata menggambarkan lavellan sebagai hewan yang umum di Caithness, tinggal di air, berkepala dan berwarna seperti musang (weasel), dan napasnya mencelakakan.
statement.en: Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata described the lavellan as an animal common in Caithness that stays in water, with a head and colouring like a weasel, whose breath does harm.

claims.quote: In the settlement of Ausdale, Thomas Pennant asked the local people about the lavellan. They reportedly believed that the lavellan was particularly harmful to cattle

statement.id: Di permukiman Ausdale, Thomas Pennant menanyai penduduk tentang lavellan; mereka percaya lavellan sangat berbahaya bagi ternak sapi (cattle).
statement.en: At the settlement of Ausdale Thomas Pennant asked local people about the lavellan; they believed it was particularly harmful to cattle.

claims.quote: Pennant posited that the mythical lavellan was, in actuality, a water shrew (Neomys fodiens). According to researcher Lee Raye, Pennant's view is now generally accepted as accurate.

statement.id: Pennant menduga lavellan sebenarnya adalah cerurut air (water shrew, Neomys fodiens); menurut peneliti Lee Raye, pandangan Pennant kini umumnya diterima.
statement.en: Pennant posited that the lavellan was actually a water shrew (Neomys fodiens); according to researcher Lee Raye, this view is now generally accepted.

claims.quote: Lavellan.—This animal is peculiar to the north, where it is said to be able to hurt cattle from a distance of forty yards

statement.id: Campbell menulis bahwa lavellan khas wilayah utara dan dikatakan mampu mencelakai ternak dari jarak empat puluh yard.
statement.en: Campbell writes that the lavellan is peculiar to the north, where it is said to hurt cattle from forty yards away.

claims.quote: Lavellan, animal in Cathanesia frequens, in aquis degit, capite mustelae sylvestri simile, ejusdemque coloris, bestia est. Halitu Bestiis nocet.

statement.id: Teks Latin Sibbald yang dikutip Campbell: lavellan (Lavellan) adalah hewan yang umum di Caithness (Cathanesia), hidup di air (in aquis), berkepala seperti musang (mustelae), dan napasnya (halitu) mencelakai hewan ternak.
statement.en: Sibbald's Latin, quoted by Campbell: the Lavellan is an animal common in Caithness (Cathanesia), living in water (in aquis), with a head like a weasel (mustelae), harming beasts with its breath (halitu).

claims.quote: Remedium autem est, si de aqua bibant in quâ ejus caput coctum est.

statement.id: Menurut teks Latin itu, obatnya (remedium) adalah bila ternak minum air (aqua) tempat kepala (caput) hewan itu direbus.
statement.en: According to the Latin text, the remedy (remedium) is for the beasts to drink water (aqua) in which its head (caput) has been boiled.

claims.quote: I inquired here after the Lavellan, which, from description, I suspect to be the water shrew mouse.

statement.id: Pennant menulis bahwa ia menanyakan Lavellan dan dari deskripsinya menduga hewan itu cerurut air (water shrew mouse).
statement.en: Pennant wrote that he inquired after the Lavellan and from the description suspected it to be the water shrew mouse.

claims.quote: The country people have a notion that it is noxious to cattle; they preserve the skin, and, as a cure for their sick beasts, give them the water in which it has been dipt.

statement.id: Penduduk desa beranggapan lavellan berbahaya bagi ternak; mereka menyimpan kulitnya dan, sebagai obat ternak yang sakit, memberi mereka air tempat kulit itu dicelupkan.
statement.en: Country people thought it noxious to cattle; they kept its skin and, as a cure for sick beasts, gave them water in which it had been dipped.

claims.quote: I believe it to be the same animal which, in Sutherland, is called the water mole.

statement.id: Pennant meyakini hewan ini sama dengan yang di Sutherland disebut tikus mondok air (water mole).
statement.en: Pennant believed it to be the same animal called the water mole in Sutherland.

claims.quote: It is also mentioned by Rob Donn, the Sutherland bard, in his satirical song on “Mac Rorie’s Breeches”: “Let him not go away from the houses, to moss or wood, lest the Lavellan come and smite him.”

statement.id: Lavellan juga disebut oleh Rob Donn, penyair Sutherland, dalam lagu satirnya tentang "Mac Rorie's Breeches": jangan biarkan ia pergi dari rumah ke rawa atau hutan, agar Lavellan tidak datang dan memukulnya.
statement.en: It is also mentioned by Rob Donn, the Sutherland bard, in his satirical song on "Mac Rorie's Breeches": let him not leave the houses for moss or wood, lest the Lavellan come and smite him.

summary.id: Menurut Pennant, ternak diberi air tempat kulit lavellan dicelupkan.
summary.en: According to Pennant, cattle were given water in which the lavellan's skin had been dipped.

summary.id: Menurut teks Latin Sibbald, ternak minum air tempat kepalanya direbus.
summary.en: According to Sibbald's Latin, beasts drank water in which its head had been boiled.
