short_description.id: La Encantada adalah perempuan tersihir dalam banyak legenda Spanyol yang muncul pada malam Santo Yohanes sambil menyisir rambut panjangnya dengan sisir emas, menunggu dibebaskan.
short_description.en: La Encantada is the enchanted woman of many Spanish legends who appears on St John's Eve combing her long hair with a golden comb, waiting to be freed.

long_description.id: La Encantada, "yang tersihir", adalah nama umum untuk legenda di banyak tempat di Spanyol tentang perempuan muda berambut panjang yang muncul pada malam Santo Yohanes sambil menyisir rambut dengan sisir emas, dengan cermin dan janji pernikahan. Di Las Camarillas ia bertanya kepada yang lewat apakah mereka memilih sisir atau dirinya, dan gembala yang memilih sisir membuatnya tetap tersihir; di Rojales ia meminta digendong ke Sungai Segura untuk mematahkan kutukannya.
long_description.en: La Encantada, 'the enchanted one', is the generic name for legends in many Spanish places about a long-haired young woman who appears on St John's Eve combing her hair with a golden comb, with a mirror and a promise of marriage. At Las Camarillas she asked passers-by whether they preferred the comb or her, and a shepherd who chose the comb left her enchanted; at Rojales she asks to be carried to the Segura River to break her curse.

long_description.id: Ia dianggap berkerabat dengan Lamia, Moura, Mari, Mairu, Anjana, Xana, dan bahkan Xtabay Meksiko. Nama encantada umum dalam toponimi Spanyol dan sering menandai situs arkeologi; bentuk mora encantada tidak berarti situs itu dari masa Muslim.
long_description.en: She is thought akin to the Lamias, Mouras, Mari, Mairu, Anjanas, Xanas and even the Mexican Xtabay. The name encantada is common in Spanish place names and often marks archaeological sites; the form mora encantada does not mean the site is from the Muslim period.

who.en: An enchanted woman.

role.id: Menunggu dibebaskan pada malam Santo Yohanes.
role.en: Waits to be freed on St John's Eve.

famous_for.id: Sisir emas.
famous_for.en: The golden comb.

role.en: The enchanted woman left unfreed.

summary.id: Di kaki gua Camareta, perempuan putih bertanya kepada gembala apakah ia memilih sisir emas atau dirinya; gembala memilih sisir dan ia tetap tersihir.
summary.en: At the foot of the Camareta cave the white lady asks a shepherd whether he prefers the golden comb or her; he chooses the comb and she remains enchanted.

note.id: Padanan dari Galisia.
note.en: The counterpart from Galicia.

note.id: Tokoh Meksiko yang mirip.
note.en: A similar Mexican figure.

claims.quote: The Spanish legend of la Encantada is a generic name that refers to a set of oral traditions and legends mythological narrated in numerous Spanish localities.

statement.id: Legenda Spanyol la Encantada adalah nama umum untuk sekumpulan tradisi lisan dan legenda mitologis yang diceritakan di banyak tempat di Spanyol.
statement.en: The Spanish legend of la Encantada is a generic name for a set of oral traditions and mythological legends told in many Spanish localities.

claims.quote: Although there are multiple local variants, a series of elements are common: the protagonist (a young woman with long hair), the time (St. John's Eve), the manifestation (combing her hair) and other elements (mirror, wedding, comb—generally gold).

statement.id: Meski banyak varian, unsurnya sama: tokoh utama perempuan muda berambut panjang, waktu malam Santo Yohanes, penampakan sambil menyisir rambut, serta cermin, pernikahan, dan sisir yang biasanya emas.
statement.en: Despite many local variants, common elements are a young long-haired woman, St John's Eve, her appearing while combing her hair, and a mirror, a wedding and a comb, usually golden.

claims.quote: La Encantada is supposedly closely related to mythological beings such as the Lamias, Mouras (Galician mythology), Mari and Mairu (Basque mythology), the Anjanas (Cantabrian mythology) and the Xanas (Asturian mythology)

statement.id: La Encantada konon berkerabat dekat dengan Lamia, Moura (Galisia), Mari dan Mairu (Basque), Anjana (Cantabria), dan Xana (Asturias).
statement.en: La Encantada is said to be closely related to the Lamias, the Mouras (Galicia), Mari and Mairu (Basque), the Anjanas (Cantabria) and the Xanas (Asturias).

claims.quote: Likewise, its relationship with the Mexican figure Xtabay suggests a very ancient and almost universal presence of the myth

statement.id: Hubungannya dengan tokoh Meksiko Xtabay menunjukkan mitos ini sangat tua dan hampir universal.
statement.en: Its link with the Mexican figure Xtabay suggests a very ancient, almost universal myth.

claims.quote: The term encantada ("enchanted") is quite common in Spanish toponymy and microtoponymy and, normally, designates the apparition.

statement.id: Istilah encantada, "yang tersihir", cukup umum dalam nama tempat di Spanyol dan biasanya menandai tempat penampakan.
statement.en: The term encantada, 'enchanted', is common in Spanish place names and usually marks the apparition.

claims.quote: Gálmez de Fuentes considers said toponym as an explanation or a posteriori adaptation of the Pre-Roman term *kanto ("stone, stony shore").

statement.id: Gálmez de Fuentes menganggap nama tempat itu adaptasi belakangan dari istilah pra-Romawi *kanto, "batu, pantai berbatu".
statement.en: Gálmez de Fuentes sees the place name as a later adaptation of the pre-Roman *kanto, 'stone, stony shore'.

claims.quote: Many times the toponym is presented under the form mora encantada ("enchanted mora"), which may lead to believe that the sites are from the period of the Muslim domination. This is not true, since many of them are earlier

statement.id: Nama tempat sering berbentuk mora encantada, yang bisa membuat orang mengira situs itu dari masa kekuasaan Muslim, padahal banyak yang lebih tua.
statement.en: The place name often appears as mora encantada, suggesting sites from the Muslim period, though many are older.

claims.quote: In the early morning of St. John's Day (June 24), a very white lady with very long blonde hair used to appear at the foot of the Camareta cave

statement.id: Di Las Camarillas (Hellín), pada dini hari Santo Yohanes (24 Juni) seorang perempuan sangat putih berambut pirang sangat panjang biasa muncul di kaki gua Camareta.
statement.en: At Las Camarillas (Hellín), in the early morning of St John's Day (24 June), a very white lady with very long blonde hair used to appear at the foot of the Camareta cave.

claims.quote: They say that on a certain occasion a shepherd passed by and when she asked him the question, he answered that it was the comb, and she exclaimed: "Damn you, because of you I will continue to be enchanted!"

statement.id: Ia bertanya kepada yang lewat mana yang lebih disukai, sisir atau dirinya; ketika seorang gembala memilih sisir, ia berseru, "Terkutuklah kau, karenamu aku tetap tersihir!"
statement.en: She asked passers-by whether they liked the comb or her more; when a shepherd chose the comb she cried, 'Damn you, because of you I will stay enchanted!'

claims.quote: If a brave man meets her, la Encantá will ask him to carry her in his arms to the Segura River to bathe her feet and thus break the curse.

statement.id: Di Rojales, la Encantá meminta pemberani menggendongnya ke Sungai Segura untuk membasuh kakinya agar kutukannya patah.
statement.en: At Rojales, la Encantá asks a brave man to carry her to the Segura River to bathe her feet and so break the curse.

claims.quote: La Leyenda española de la Encantada es un nombre genérico que hace referencia a un conjunto de tradiciones orales y leyendas mitológicas narradas en numerosas localidades españolas.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Spanyol juga menyebut la Encantada nama umum untuk tradisi lisan dan legenda di banyak tempat di Spanyol.
statement.en: The Spanish article likewise calls la Encantada a generic name for oral traditions and legends in many Spanish places.

claims.quote: A Lenda espanhola da Encantada é um nome genérico que faz referência a um conjunto de tradições orais e lendas mitológicas narradas em numerosas localidades espanholas.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Portugis menyebut hal yang sama.
statement.en: The Portuguese article says the same.

short_description.id: Vjesci (wieszczy) adalah vampir dalam cerita rakyat Polandia; orang yang ditakdirkan menjadi vjesci lahir dengan selaput ketuban di kepala.
short_description.en: The vjesci (wieszczy) is a vampire of Polish folklore; those fated to become one are born with a caul on the head.

long_description.id: Vjesci, dalam bahasa Polandia wieszczy, adalah vampir dalam cerita rakyat Polandia. Menurut legenda, sebagian orang lahir dengan takdir menjadi vjesci, yang tampak dari selaput ketuban di kepala bayi. Untuk mencegahnya, selaput itu dilepas, dikeringkan, digiling, lalu diberikan kepada anak itu pada ulang tahunnya yang ketujuh. Dalam demonologi Slavia, wieszczy adalah bentuk keberadaan jiwa manusia setelah mati, mirip upiór atau vampir, tetapi di banyak daerah punya ciri tersendiri.
long_description.en: Called wieszczy in Polish, the vjesci is a vampire of Polish lore. Legend says some people are born destined for it, marked by a caul on the newborn's head. To prevent this, the caul was taken off, dried, ground and given to the child on their seventh birthday. In Slavic demonology the wieszczy is a form of the soul's existence after death, close to the upiór or vampire yet with its own traits in many regions.

long_description.id: Semasa hidup, vjesci biasanya tidak bisa dibedakan dari manusia. Saat meninggal ia menolak sakramen; tubuhnya cepat dingin, anggota badannya tetap lentur, dan bibir serta pipinya tetap merah. Menurut legenda ia bangkit pada tengah malam setelah dikubur, memakan pakaian dan sebagian dagingnya sendiri, lalu pulang untuk memangsa keluarga dan tetangga, kemudian membunyikan lonceng gereja; yang mendengarnya akan menjadi korban berikutnya.
long_description.en: In life a vjesci could rarely be told apart from other people. At death it refuses the sacrament; the body cools fast, the limbs stay supple and the lips and cheeks stay red. Legend has it rise at midnight after burial, eat its clothes and some of its own flesh, go home to prey on family and neighbours, then ring the church bell; whoever hears it will be the next victim.

long_description.id: Untuk mencegah serangan, orang yang sekarat harus menerima Ekaristi, tanah ditaruh di dalam peti, dan salib atau koin diletakkan di bawah lidah jenazah agar diisap sang vampir. Jenazah juga dibaringkan telungkup agar, bila bangkit, ia justru menggali lebih dalam ke tanah.
long_description.en: To prevent attacks, the dying had to receive the Eucharist, soil was put in the coffin, and a crucifix or coin was laid under the corpse's tongue for the vampire to suck on. Bodies were also laid face down so that, if they woke, they would only dig deeper into the earth.

who.en: The vjesci is a Polish vampire.

claims.quote: is a vampire in Polish folklore. According to legend, some people are born with the destiny of becoming vjesci, discernible by a caul located on the newborn's head. In order to prevent these individuals from becoming vjesci, the caul was removed, dried, ground and fed to the person on their seventh birthday.

statement.id: Vjesci adalah vampir dalam cerita rakyat Polandia; sebagian orang lahir ditakdirkan menjadi vjesci, tampak dari selaput ketuban di kepala bayi; untuk mencegahnya selaput itu dilepas, dikeringkan, digiling, dan diberikan pada ulang tahun ketujuh.
statement.en: The vjesci is a vampire of Polish folklore; some are born destined for it, marked by a caul on the head; to prevent it the caul was removed, dried, ground and fed to them on their seventh birthday.

claims.quote: Typically, vjesci were said to be indistinguishable from humans, although in some stories, they had a ruddy complexion and an excitable nature. At the time of their death, a vjesci would refuse to take the sacrament. Their body would cool quickly, and their limbs would remain limber. Their lips and cheeks would remain red

statement.id: Vjesci biasanya tak bisa dibedakan dari manusia; saat mati ia menolak sakramen, tubuhnya cepat dingin, anggota badan tetap lentur, dan bibir serta pipinya tetap merah.
statement.en: Vjesci were usually indistinguishable from humans; at death they refused the sacrament, the body cooled quickly, the limbs stayed limber and lips and cheeks stayed red.

claims.quote: the vjesci did not die, instead returning to life at midnight after its burial and eating its clothes and some of its own flesh. The vampire would leave the grave and return home to eat its family and neighbors. After visiting its relatives, it would go to the local church and ring the church bell. Those who heard the bell were supposedly destined to be the vampire's next victims.

statement.id: Vjesci tidak mati, melainkan bangkit pada tengah malam setelah dikubur, memakan pakaian dan sebagian dagingnya, meninggalkan kubur untuk memangsa keluarga dan tetangga, lalu membunyikan lonceng gereja; yang mendengarnya menjadi korban berikutnya.
statement.en: The vjesci did not die but rose at midnight after burial, ate its clothes and some of its flesh, left the grave to eat family and neighbours, then rang the church bell; those who heard it were its next victims.

claims.quote: All dying persons must receive the Eucharist. ... Soil was placed inside the coffin and underneath the body to prevent it from returning home.

statement.id: Semua orang yang sekarat harus menerima Ekaristi; tanah ditaruh di dalam peti dan di bawah jenazah agar tidak pulang.
statement.en: All dying persons must receive the Eucharist; soil was placed in the coffin and under the body to stop it returning home.

claims.quote: A crucifix or coin was placed under the tongue of the corpse for the vampire to suck on. ... Bodies were laid in the coffin face down in belief that the corpse, if it returned to life, would simply dig further into the earth.

statement.id: Salib atau koin diletakkan di bawah lidah jenazah agar diisap sang vampir; jenazah dibaringkan telungkup agar menggali lebih dalam bila bangkit.
statement.en: A crucifix or coin was put under the corpse's tongue for the vampire to suck on; bodies were laid face down so that, if revived, they would dig deeper.

short_description.id: Bichura adalah roh rumah dalam mitologi Tatar dan Turkik, berpakaian merah, yang bertingkah seperti poltergeist dan memberi pertanda bahaya atau kematian.
short_description.en: Bichura is a house spirit of Tatar and Turkic mythology, dressed in red, that acts like a poltergeist and warns of danger or death.

long_description.id: Bichura adalah roh rumah dalam mitologi Turkik dan dalam dongeng Tatar. Orang Tatar membayangkannya sebagai perempuan kecil berpenutup kepala kuno yang tinggal di bawah lantai atau di pemandian; sumber lain menyebutnya berpakaian merah dan bisa menjelma kucing atau anjing. Namanya mungkin berasal dari kata Turkik Kuno bičin, "kera".
long_description.en: Bichura is a house spirit of Turkic mythology and Tatar tales. Tatars pictured it as a small woman in an old-fashioned headdress living under the floor or in the bathhouse; another source says it wears red and can take the form of a cat or dog. Its name may come from Old Turkic bičin, "monkey".

long_description.id: Tingkahnya mirip poltergeist dan tidak selalu merugikan: ia menarik rambut untuk memperingatkan perempuan akan lelaki kasar, melolong sebagai tanda bahaya, dan bila menampakkan diri atau menangis, itu pertanda kematian. Bila tidak senang, ia mengusili penghuni rumah. Ada yang menyebut setiap rumah punya Bichura, tetapi sumber lain menyatakan tidak semua rumah dihuninya.
long_description.en: Its behaviour resembles a poltergeist's and is not always harmful: it pulls hair to warn a woman of an abusive man, howls to warn of trouble, and when it shows itself or weeps, death is near. When unhappy it plays tricks on the household. Some say every house has a Bichura, but another source says not every house does.

short_description.id: Coco atau Cuco adalah momok mirip hantu dari Portugal dan Spanyol yang datang pada malam hari membawa pergi anak-anak yang tidak patuh.
short_description.en: The Coco or Cuco is a ghost-like bogeyman of Portugal and Spain who comes at night to carry off disobedient children.

long_description.id: Coco, Coca, Cuco, atau Cucuy adalah monster mirip hantu padanan bogeyman yang berasal dari Portugal utara dan Galisia lalu menyebar ke negara-negara berbahasa Spanyol dan Portugis. Ia datang pada malam hari ke rumah anak yang nakal atau tidak mau tidur dan membawa mereka pergi; ia tidak memiliki wujud pasti. Namanya terkait kata coco, "kepala" atau "tengkorak".
long_description.en: The Coco, Coca, Cuco or Cucuy is a ghost-like bogeyman that began in northern Portugal and Galicia and spread through Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries. It comes at night to the homes of children who misbehave or will not sleep and carries them off; it has no fixed form. Its name is tied to coco, 'head' or 'skull'.

long_description.id: Di Amerika Latin ia disebut El Cuco dan di New Mexico "the Coco Man". Di Brasil, Cuca digambarkan sebagai buaya perempuan berambut pirang, wujud yang sebenarnya berasal dari acara televisi tahun 1952, sedangkan Monteiro Lobato dalam O saci (1921) hanya menyebut wajah buaya dan jari bercakar.
long_description.en: Many Latin American countries call it El Cuco and New Mexico 'the Coco Man'. In Brazilian folklore the Cuca is drawn as a blonde female alligator, a form that actually comes from a 1952 TV show, while Monteiro Lobato in O saci (1921) mentions only an alligator face and clawed fingers.

who.en: A bogeyman who takes naughty children.

role.en: Frightens children into obedience.

claims.quote: The Coco or Coca (also known as the Cucuy, Cuco, Cuca, Cucu, Cucuí or El Cucuí) is a mythical ghost-like monster, equivalent to the bogeyman, found in Portugal and Spain. Those beliefs have also spread in many Hispanophone and Lusophone countries.

statement.id: Coco atau Coca (juga Cucuy, Cuco, Cuca, atau El Cucuí) adalah monster mitis mirip hantu, padanan bogeyman, di Portugal dan Spanyol, yang kepercayaannya juga menyebar ke banyak negara berbahasa Spanyol dan Portugis.
statement.en: The Coco or Coca (also Cucuy, Cuco, Cuca or El Cucuí) is a mythical ghost-like monster, the bogeyman's equivalent, found in Portugal and Spain, whose belief has spread to many Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries.

claims.quote: The Cucuy is a male being while Cuca is a female version of the mythical monster. The "monster" will come to the house of disobedient children at night and take them away.

statement.id: Cucuy adalah sosok laki-laki dan Cuca versi perempuannya; monster ini datang pada malam hari ke rumah anak yang tidak patuh dan membawa mereka pergi.
statement.en: The Cucuy is male and the Cuca the female version; the monster comes at night to the homes of disobedient children and takes them away.

claims.quote: The myth of the Coco, or Cucuy, originated in northern Portugal and Galicia. The word coco is used in colloquial speech to refer to the human head in Spanish. Coco also means "skull".

statement.id: Mitos Coco atau Cucuy berasal dari Portugal utara dan Galisia; dalam bahasa Spanyol sehari-hari coco berarti kepala manusia, dan juga "tengkorak".
statement.en: The myth of the Coco or Cucuy began in northern Portugal and Galicia; colloquially in Spanish coco means the human head, and also 'skull'.

claims.quote: In Brazilian folklore, the monster is referred to as Cuca and pictured as a female humanoid alligator with blond hair. Though this reptilian form resembles the Portuguese coca, a dragon, it actually originates from the 1952's TV show Sítio do Pica-pau Amarelo (1952 TV series).

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Brasil ia disebut Cuca, digambarkan sebagai buaya perempuan mirip manusia berambut pirang; wujud reptil ini sebenarnya berasal dari acara televisi Sítio do Pica-pau Amarelo tahun 1952.
statement.en: In Brazilian folklore it is the Cuca, pictured as a blonde female humanoid alligator; this reptile form actually comes from the 1952 TV show Sítio do Pica-pau Amarelo.

claims.quote: In the only book she appears, O saci (1921), Cuca's description is vague, Monteiro Lobato only states that she had an "alligator face" and "clawed fingers".

statement.id: Dalam satu-satunya buku yang memuatnya, O saci (1921), Monteiro Lobato hanya menyebut Cuca berwajah buaya dan berjari bercakar.
statement.en: In the only book she appears in, O saci (1921), Monteiro Lobato says only that Cuca had an 'alligator face' and 'clawed fingers'.

claims.quote: Many Latin American countries refer to the monster as El Cuco. In northern New Mexico and southern Colorado, where there is a large Hispanic population, it is referred to by its anglicized name, "the Coco Man".

statement.id: Banyak negara Amerika Latin menyebutnya El Cuco, dan di New Mexico utara serta Colorado selatan ia disebut "the Coco Man".
statement.en: Many Latin American countries call it El Cuco, and in northern New Mexico and southern Colorado it is 'the Coco Man'.

statement.en: According to the French article, the Coco, also Cuco, Cucuy or Cuculelé, is a kind of bogeyman of Hispanic and Portuguese folklore who comes to punish badly behaved children.

short_description.id: Dhampir adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Balkan yang lahir dari hubungan antara vampir dan manusia, dan dipercaya mampu melihat serta memburu vampir.
short_description.en: The dhampir is a creature of Balkan folklore born of a union between a vampire and a human, believed able to see and hunt vampires.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Balkan, dhampir adalah makhluk hasil hubungan antara vampir dan manusia. Biasanya ayahnya vampir laki-laki dan ibunya perempuan manusia; kisah tentang vampir perempuan yang mendapat anak dari laki-laki manusia jarang ada. Kata dhampir berasal dari bahasa Albania, yang meminjamnya dari kata Slavia Selatan vampir.
long_description.en: In Balkan folklore the dhampir is a creature born of a union between a vampire and a human. Usually the father is a male vampire and the mother a human woman; tales of female vampires bearing children by human men are rare. The word dhampir is Albanian, itself borrowed from South Slavic vampir.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, dhampir umumnya hidup sebagai warga biasa. Namun mereka, terutama anak laki-laki keturunan ayah vampir, dapat melihat vampir yang tak kasatmata dan mempraktikkan sihir, sehingga sering menjadi pemburu vampir secara turun-temurun. Di Kosovo, putra dhampir dipandang sebagai agen magis utama untuk membinasakan vampir, bahkan kadang satu-satunya yang mampu melihatnya.
long_description.en: Legends say dhampirs mostly lived as ordinary members of the community. Yet they, especially sons with a vampire father, could see invisible vampires and work sorcery, and often became vampire hunters, a calling passed down the generations. In Kosovo a dhampir son was seen as the main magical agent for destroying vampires, sometimes the only one able to see them.

long_description.id: Beberapa tradisi menyebut tanda-tanda anak vampir. Dalam cerita rakyat Bulgaria, tandanya antara lain tubuh lunak tanpa kuku atau tulang; tanda lain adalah hidung yang menonjol atau telinga, gigi, dan mata yang lebih besar dari biasa. Di beberapa daerah, dhampir sejati dikatakan bertubuh licin seperti jeli dan berumur pendek.
long_description.en: Some traditions list signs of a vampire's child. In Bulgarian folklore these include a soft body without nails or bones; other signs were a prominent nose or unusually large ears, teeth or eyes. In some areas a true dhampir was said to have a slippery, jelly-like body and a short life.

long_description.id: Satu sumber menggambarkan dhampir sebagai makhluk dari legenda Eropa Timur dan Rusia yang tampak seperti manusia biasa, tetapi mampu mendeteksi dan membunuh vampir. Kebanyakan meninggal tak lama setelah lahir, tetapi yang tumbuh dewasa kadang menjadi pemburu vampir. Perburuan vampir oleh dhampir berbentuk seperti ritual: ia meniup seruling, berlari ke sana kemari, dan bertarung dengan musuh yang tak terlihat sebelum menyatakan kemenangan. Menurut sumber yang sama, vampir yang kembali kepada keluarganya kadang meminta hubungan badan, bukan darah.
long_description.en: One source describes the dhampir as a being from Eastern European and Russian legend who looks like an ordinary human yet can detect and kill vampires. Most die soon after birth, but those who grow up sometimes become vampire hunters. A dhampir's vampire hunt takes a ritual form: blowing a flute, running about and fighting an unseen foe before declaring victory. The same source says a vampire returning to its family sometimes demands intercourse rather than blood.

short_description.id: E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit ("Putri Bulan dan Matahari") adalah tokoh mitologi Albania, petir dari langit yang menghantam kesombongan dan kejahatan.
short_description.en: In Albanian myth, the Daughter of the Moon and the Sun (E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit) is lightning falling from the sky that strikes down pride and evil.

long_description.id: E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit adalah tokoh mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, putri Hëna (Bulan) dan Dielli (Matahari). Ia digambarkan sebagai pika e qiellit, "tetes langit" atau "petir", yang jatuh dari langit ke mana-mana di gunung dan lembah untuk menghantam kesombongan dan kejahatan.
long_description.en: Albanian myth and folklore know her as the child of two personified heavenly bodies: her mother is Hëna, the Moon, and her father Dielli, the Sun. She is called pika e qiellit, meaning a drop of the sky or lightning, and comes down from heaven onto mountains and valleys alike, smiting pride and evil.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Albania, matahari dan bulan adalah dewa yang dipersonifikasikan: matahari sebagai sosok laki-laki dan bulan sebagai perempuan. Ada tradisi yang menganggap keduanya suami-istri dan ada yang menganggapnya kakak-adik; dalam kisah putri ini, matahari adalah ayahnya dan bulan ibunya.
long_description.en: In Albanian folk belief the sun and moon are personified deities, the sun a male figure and the moon a female one. Some traditions see them as husband and wife, others as brother and sister; in this daughter's story the sun is her father and the moon her mother.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda ia membantu seorang pahlawan mengalahkan kulshedra, dewa atau iblis bumi yang berasal dari kegelapan. Kemenangannya melambangkan keunggulan dewa langit atas dewa dunia bawah dalam pertarungan dualistis antara terang dan gelap. Legendanya juga dituturkan Mitrush Kuteli dalam kumpulan Tregime të moçme shqiptare yang terbit tahun 1965.
long_description.en: In the legends she helps a hero defeat a kulshedra, an earthly or chthonic deity or demon arising from darkness. Her victory symbolises the supremacy of the sky deity over that of the underworld in the dualistic struggle of light and darkness. Her legend was also retold by Mitrush Kuteli in the collection Tregime të moçme shqiptare, published in 1965.

short_description.id: Jiangshi adalah mayat hidup dalam legenda dan cerita rakyat Tiongkok, dikenal pula sebagai vampir melompat; dalam budaya populer ia digambarkan sebagai mayat kaku berbusana pejabat dinasti Qing.
short_description.en: The jiangshi is a reanimated corpse of Chinese legend and folklore, also called the hopping vampire; popular culture shows it as a stiff corpse in Qing dynasty official robes.

long_description.id: Jiangshi adalah jenis mayat hidup atau mayat yang bangkit kembali dalam legenda dan cerita rakyat Tiongkok, yang juga dijuluki vampir melompat. Kata jiang dalam namanya secara harfiah berarti keras atau kaku, dan memang jiangshi selalu tidak lentur seperti orang hidup. Ia digambarkan berkulit putih kehijauan, mungkin dari jamur yang tumbuh pada mayat, berambut panjang, buas, rakus, dan sangat kuat.
long_description.en: The jiangshi is a type of undead being or reanimated corpse in Chinese legend and folklore, also nicknamed the hopping vampire. The syllable jiang in its name literally means hard or stiff, and the jiangshi indeed never has a living person's suppleness. It is said to have greenish-white skin, perhaps from fungus growing on corpses, long hair, and a fierce, ravenous nature with enormous strength.

long_description.id: Menurut sarjana dinasti Qing Ji Xiaolan, mayat bangkit karena dua sebab: orang yang baru meninggal hidup kembali, atau mayat yang lama dikubur tetapi tidak membusuk. Sebab lain yang disebut antara lain roh hun yang meninggalkan tubuh sementara roh po tetap tinggal dan mengendalikannya, atau mayat yang belum dikubur tersambar petir atau dilompati kucing hamil. Jiangshi biasanya membunuh makhluk hidup untuk menyerap qi mereka pada malam hari, dan siang harinya bersembunyi di peti mati atau tempat gelap seperti gua.
long_description.en: According to the Qing dynasty scholar Ji Xiaolan, a corpse is reanimated for one of two reasons: a recently dead person returns to life, or a long-buried body fails to decay. Other causes include the hun soul leaving the body while the po soul stays and takes control, or an unburied corpse being struck by lightning or leapt over by a pregnant cat. The jiangshi usually kills the living to absorb their qi at night, and by day hides in a coffin or a dark place such as a cave.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya populer, jiangshi umumnya bergerak dengan melompat, sedangkan dalam cerita rakyat ia lebih menakutkan: bisa mengejar dengan berlari, dan bila sudah sangat tua atau cukup menyerap energi yang, ia bahkan bisa terbang. Cerita rakyat menyebut jiangshi datang dari perbukitan, melayang di udara, untuk memangsa bayi. Gambaran mayat kaku berbusana resmi dinasti Qing berasal dari pengaruh sinema Hong Kong, dan film seperti Mr. Vampire beserta sekuelnya menjadi film kultus komedi-horor.
long_description.en: In popular culture the jiangshi usually moves by hopping, but folklore makes it more fearsome: it can give chase by running and, if old enough or full of enough yang energy, can even fly. Folk tales describe one flying down from the hills to prey on babies. The image of a stiff corpse in Qing dynasty official dress comes from the influence of Hong Kong cinema, and films such as Mr. Vampire and its sequels became comedy-horror cult classics.

long_description.id: Sejarawan J. J. M. de Groot berpendapat kepercayaan ini lahir dari rasa ngeri alami terhadap mayat, diperkuat oleh banyaknya jenazah yang tak dikuburkan di Tiongkok masa kekaisaran. Kepercayaan ini juga sebagian bersumber dari tradisi "mengantar mayat", yaitu memulangkan jenazah para buruh di provinsi Xiang (kini Hunan) ke kampung halaman: mayat diikat pada batang bambu dan dipikul sehingga tampak seperti melompat.
long_description.en: Historian J. J. M. de Groot suggested the belief grew from a natural horror of dead bodies, fed by the many unburied corpses of imperial China. It also drew partly on "corpse-driving", the return of dead labourers' bodies across Xiang province (now Hunan) to their home villages: the corpses were tied to bamboo poles and carried, which made them seem to hop.

statement.id: Jenazah diikat pada batang bambu dan dipikul oleh para pengantar mayat profesional sejauh ribuan mil ke desa leluhurnya, sehingga tampak seperti mayat yang melompat.
statement.en: The corpses were tied to bamboo sticks and carried by professional corpse-drivers for thousands of miles to their ancestral villages, giving the impression of a hopping corpse.

claims.quote: The Qing dynasty scholar Ji Xiaolan mentioned in his book Yuewei Caotang Biji ... that the causes for a corpse to be reanimated can be classified in either of two categories: a recently deceased person returning to life, or a corpse that has been buried for a long time but does not decompose.

statement.id: Sarjana dinasti Qing Ji Xiaolan dalam bukunya Yuewei Caotang Biji menggolongkan sebab mayat bangkit menjadi dua: orang yang baru meninggal hidup kembali, atau mayat yang lama dikubur tetapi tidak membusuk.
statement.en: Qing dynasty scholar Ji Xiaolan, in his Yuewei Caotang Biji, classified reanimation into two kinds: a recently dead person returning to life, or a long-buried corpse that does not decompose.

claims.quote: When the hun leaves the body after death but the po remains and takes control of the body, the dead person becomes a jiangshi.

statement.id: Bila roh hun meninggalkan tubuh setelah mati tetapi roh po tetap tinggal dan mengendalikan tubuh, orang itu menjadi jiangshi.
statement.en: When the hun leaves the body after death but the po remains and takes control, the dead person becomes a jiangshi.

claims.quote: The corpse comes to life after it is struck by a bolt of lightning, or when a pregnant cat (or a black cat in some tales) leaps across the coffin.

statement.id: Mayat yang belum dikubur bisa hidup kembali setelah tersambar petir, atau bila kucing hamil (atau kucing hitam dalam sebagian kisah) melompati peti matinya.
statement.en: An unburied corpse comes to life when struck by lightning, or when a pregnant cat (or a black cat in some tales) leaps across the coffin.

claims.quote: in "jiangshi" literally means "hard" or "stiff".

statement.id: Aksara jiang dalam "jiangshi" secara harfiah berarti "keras" atau "kaku".
statement.en: The character jiang in "jiangshi" literally means "hard" or "stiff".

claims.quote: Jiangshi are described as having greenish-white skin, possibly deriving from fungus or mould growing on corpses. They have long hair and may behave like animals. They are ferocious, ravenous beings possessing extreme strength

statement.id: Jiangshi digambarkan berkulit putih kehijauan, mungkin dari jamur yang tumbuh pada mayat, berambut panjang, bisa berperilaku seperti hewan, buas, rakus, dan sangat kuat.
statement.en: Jiangshi are described with greenish-white skin, perhaps from fungus or mould on corpses, long hair and animal-like behaviour; they are ferocious, ravenous and extremely strong.

claims.quote: Jiangshi are also said to be terrified of their own reflections.
claims.locator: Methods and items used to counter jiangshi

statement.id: Jiangshi juga dikatakan takut pada bayangannya sendiri.
statement.en: Jiangshi are also said to be terrified of their own reflections.

claims.quote: Fulu (Taoist talisman), stuck on the forehead to immobilise them.
claims.locator: Methods and items used to counter jiangshi

statement.id: Fulu, jimat Tao, ditempel di dahi untuk melumpuhkan jiangshi.
statement.en: Fulu, a Taoist talisman, is stuck on the forehead to immobilise jiangshi.

claims.quote: According to Yuan Mei's book Zi Bu Yu, "Evil spirits withdraw when they hear a rooster's call"
claims.locator: Methods and items used to counter jiangshi

statement.id: Menurut buku Zi Bu Yu karya Yuan Mei, roh jahat mundur ketika mendengar kokok ayam jantan.
statement.en: According to Yuan Mei's Zi Bu Yu, evil spirits withdraw when they hear a rooster's call.

claims.quote: "Peach is the essence of the Five Elements. It can subjugate evil auras and deter evil spirits."
claims.locator: Methods and items used to counter jiangshi

statement.id: Persik adalah inti Lima Unsur, mampu menundukkan aura jahat dan menangkal roh jahat.
statement.en: Peach is the essence of the Five Elements and can subdue evil auras and deter evil spirits.

claims.quote: Movies such as Mr. Vampire and its various sequels (Mr. Vampire II, Mr. Vampire III, and Mr. Vampire IV) became cult classics in comedy-horror and inspired a vampire craze in East Asia, including Taiwan and Japan.

statement.id: Film seperti Mr. Vampire dan sekuelnya (Mr. Vampire II, III, dan IV) menjadi film kultus komedi-horor dan memicu demam vampir di Asia Timur, termasuk Taiwan dan Jepang.
statement.en: Films such as Mr. Vampire and its sequels (Mr. Vampire II, III and IV) became comedy-horror cult classics and sparked a vampire craze in East Asia, including Taiwan and Japan.

claims.quote: Mereka biasanya digambarkan sebagai mayat kaku mengenakan pakaian resmi dari Dinasti Qing, dan bergerak dengan melompat-lompat, dengan lengan terentang. Membunuh makhluk hidup untuk menyerap qi, atau "kekuatan hidup" mereka, biasanya pada malam hari, sedangkan di siang hari, mereka ada di dalam peti mati atau bersembunyi di tempat gelap seperti gua.

statement.id: Jiangshi biasanya digambarkan sebagai mayat kaku berpakaian resmi Dinasti Qing yang melompat dengan lengan terentang; mereka membunuh makhluk hidup untuk menyerap qi pada malam hari, dan siang harinya berada di peti mati atau bersembunyi di tempat gelap seperti gua.
statement.en: Jiangshi are usually depicted as stiff corpses in Qing dynasty official dress, hopping with arms outstretched; they kill the living to absorb their qi, usually at night, and by day stay in coffins or hide in dark places like caves.

claims.quote: Holding one's breath, which makes the jiangshi unable to find you as they are blind, though this contradicts the earlier statement that they are afraid of their own reflection.
claims.locator: Methods and items used to counter jiangshi

statement.id: Menahan napas membuat jiangshi tidak bisa menemukan orang karena mereka buta, meski hal ini bertentangan dengan pernyataan bahwa mereka takut pada bayangannya sendiri.
statement.en: Holding one's breath keeps jiangshi from finding you since they are blind, though this contradicts the claim that they fear their own reflection.

claims.quote: "Jiangshi" dibaca goeng-si dalam bahasa Kanton.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Kanton, "jiangshi" dibaca goeng-si.
statement.en: In Cantonese, "jiangshi" is pronounced goeng-si.

summary.id: Budaya populer dan satu sumber: melompat-lompat dengan lengan terentang.
summary.en: Popular culture and one source: hopping with arms outstretched.

summary.id: Catatan cerita rakyat: berlari mengejar dan bisa terbang.
summary.en: Folkloric accounts: running in pursuit and able to fly.

summary.id: Ia takut pada bayangannya sendiri di cermin.
summary.en: It fears its own reflection in a mirror.

summary.id: Ia buta sehingga orang yang menahan napas tak bisa ditemukannya.
summary.en: It is blind, so it cannot find someone holding their breath.

short_description.id: Little People of the Pryor Mountains (Nirumbee atau Awwakkulé) adalah ras kurcaci gaib dalam cerita rakyat Suku Crow yang tinggal di Pryor Mountains, Montana, kuat, ditakuti, sekaligus pemandu spiritual.
short_description.en: The Little People of the Pryor Mountains (Nirumbee or Awwakkulé) are a race of supernatural dwarfs in the folklore of the Crow Tribe who live in the Pryor Mountains of Montana, strong and feared yet also spiritual guides.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Suku Crow, Little People of the Pryor Mountains, disebut Nirumbee atau Awwakkulé dalam bahasa Crow, adalah ras kurcaci yang ganas. Mereka tinggal di Pryor Mountains di Montana dan karena itu pegunungan tersebut suci bagi Crow. Sumber akademik menggambarkan mereka sebagai kurcaci yang sekaligus manusia dan makhluk gaib serta dapat menjadi pemandu spiritual.
long_description.en: Crow Tribe folklore tells of the Little People of the Pryor Mountains, whom the Crow language calls Nirumbee or Awwakkulé, a fierce race of dwarfs. They live in the Pryor Mountains of Montana, which is why the mountains are sacred to the Crow. An academic source describes them as dwarves that are both human and supernatural and can act as spiritual guides.

long_description.id: Menurut sumber pertama mereka tidak lebih tinggi dari 18 inci, sangat kuat, berlengan dan berkaki pendek, dan nyaris tanpa leher. Tesis menggambarkan mereka setinggi antara dua puluh inci dan 4 kaki, tampak seperti orang dewasa mini. Mereka dikenal mencuri anak, makanan, obat, dan tembakau, dan dipercaya membuat mata panah batu.
long_description.en: The first source says they are no more than 18 inches tall, very strong, with short arms and legs and little or no neck. The thesis describes them as between twenty inches and 4 feet tall, looking like miniature adults. They were known for stealing children, food, medicine and tobacco, and were believed to have made stone arrowheads.

long_description.id: Orang Crow pada umumnya enggan memasuki pegunungan itu. Bagi banyak orang Little People adalah pemandu dan penolong spiritual, bagi yang lain mereka jahil dan harus dihindari, tetapi semuanya diajarkan menghormati mereka sebagai tetua. Persembahan seperti manik, kain, tembakau, daging, dan tumpukan batu, serta menembakkan panah ke tebing, dilakukan agar mendapat jalan aman.
long_description.en: The Crow would generally avoid entering the mountains. To many the Little People are spiritual guides and helpers, to others mischievous and to be avoided, but all are taught to respect them as Elders. Offerings such as beads, cloth, tobacco, meat and piles of rocks, and shooting arrows at the cliff, were made to win safe passage.

long_description.id: Little People juga terkait praktik Sun Dance, dan dalam penglihatan kepala Little People menubuatkan bahwa Plenty Coups akan menjadi kepala suku. Dalam satu kisah, mereka mengadopsi seorang anak Crow yang tersesat di pegunungan; menurut sejarah lisan, tempat bernama Arrow Shot Into Rock adalah tempat Crow pertama kali bertemu mereka.
long_description.en: The Little People are also tied to the Sun Dance, and in a vision their chief prophesied that Plenty Coups would become a chief. In one story they adopted a Crow child lost in the mountains; according to oral history the place called Arrow Shot Into Rock is where the Crow first met them.

short_description.id: Mavka adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Ukraina, "jiwa hutan" berambut panjang yang memikat laki-laki muda ke dalam hutan hingga menemui ajal.
short_description.en: The mavka is a female spirit of Ukrainian folklore, a long-haired "soul of the forest" who lures young men into the woods to their death.

long_description.id: Mavka adalah sejenis roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Ukraina. Ia dikenal sebagai "jiwa hutan" berambut panjang dan biasanya digambarkan sebagai penggoda yang menuntun laki-laki menuju kematian. Namanya berasal dari kata yang berarti "orang mati", istilah untuk arwah mereka yang meninggal secara tragis dan terlalu cepat.
long_description.en: The mavka is a kind of female spirit in Ukrainian folklore and mythology. Known as a long-haired "soul of the forest", she is usually pictured as a temptress who leads men to their deaths. Her name derives from a word meaning "the dead", a term for the spirits of those who died tragically and too early.

long_description.id: Roh ini dianggap sebagai jiwa gadis yang mati secara tidak wajar, tragis, atau terlalu dini, terutama bayi yang belum dibaptis. Bila jiwa bayi itu tidak masuk surga dalam tujuh tahun, ia berubah menjadi mavka dan bergentayangan. Untuk menyelamatkannya, orang harus melempar kain kepala ke atas saat hari raya Pentakosta, menyebut namanya, dan mengucapkan kata pembaptisan.
long_description.en: These spirits were held to be the souls of girls who died unnatural, tragic or early deaths, especially unbaptized babies. If such a baby's soul did not reach heaven within seven years, it became a mavka and haunted the earth. To save it, one had to toss a kerchief up during the Pentecost holidays, say its name and speak words of baptism.

long_description.id: Mavka sering tampil sebagai gadis muda yang cantik, tinggi, berwajah bulat, berambut panjang, dan kadang telanjang. Ia memikat pemuda ke hutan lalu "menggelitik" mereka sampai mati. Mavka tidak memantulkan bayangan di air dan tidak berbayang. Subjenisnya, nyavka, berperilaku sama tetapi "tidak berpunggung", sehingga tulang belakang dan organ dalamnya terlihat.
long_description.en: The mavka often appears as a beautiful young girl, tall, round-faced, long-haired and sometimes naked. She lures young men into the woods and "tickles" them to death. She has no reflection in water and casts no shadow. A subtype, the nyavka, behaves the same but has "no back", so her spine and inner organs can be seen.

long_description.id: Mavka dipercaya hidup berkelompok di hutan, gua gunung, atau gudang yang mereka hiasi permadani. Pada musim semi mereka menanam bunga di pegunungan untuk memikat pemuda. Saat Pentakosta mereka mengadakan permainan, tarian, dan pesta pora dengan iringan seruling setan. Namun menurut beberapa kisah, mereka juga membantu petani dengan menjaga ternak dan mengusir binatang liar. Dalam sastra, mavka antara lain muncul dalam The Forest Song karya Lesia Ukrainka.
long_description.en: Mavkas were thought to dwell together in woods, in mountain caves or in sheds adorned with rugs. In spring they planted flowers in the mountains to lure young men. At Pentecost they held games, dances and orgies to the flute of a demon. Yet some accounts say they also helped farmers by tending cattle and chasing off wild animals. In literature, mavkas appear notably in Lesia Ukrainka's The Forest Song.

short_description.id: Mullo adalah mayat hidup atau vampir dalam cerita rakyat Roma, arwah orang yang mati tidak wajar yang kembali untuk mencekik dan mengisap darah kerabatnya.
short_description.en: The mullo is an undead or vampire of Roma folklore, the ghost of someone who died unnaturally and returns to strangle relatives and suck their blood.

long_description.id: Mullo, "orang yang sudah mati", adalah mayat hidup atau vampir dalam cerita rakyat Roma. Ia tercipta bila seseorang mati mendadak secara tidak wajar atau tanpa upacara pemakaman yang layak. Ia berpakaian putih, berambut sampai ke kaki, dan punya satu keanehan fisik yang berbeda menurut daerah. Ia kembali untuk mencekik dan mengisap darah, biasanya kerabat yang menyebabkan kematiannya atau melalaikan adat pemakaman.
long_description.en: The mullo, 'one who is dead', is an undead or vampire of Roma folklore. It arises when someone dies suddenly and unnaturally or without proper funeral rites. It wears white, has hair down to its feet and one bodily oddity that differs by region. It returns to strangle and drink the blood of people, usually relatives who caused its death or neglected the burial customs.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Serbia ia bisa tak terlihat atau tampak normal, dan selalu kembali kepada pasangannya. Untuk menyingkirkannya orang menyewa Dhampir; untuk menangkalnya, jarum baja atau besi ditusukkan ke jantung mayat, hawthorn ditaruh di kaus kakinya, atau mayat dipenggal dan dibakar.
long_description.en: According to the Serbian article it can be invisible or look normal, and it always goes back to its partner. To be rid of it people hired a Dhampir; to ward it off, steel or iron needles were driven into the corpse's heart, hawthorn put in its sock, or the body beheaded and burned.

role.en: Takes revenge on relatives.

statement.en: The mullo (Muli for a female, Mulo for a male) is an undead, revenant or vampire of Roma folklore; the name means 'one who is dead'.

claims.quote: A mullo is created when a person dies suddenly of some unnatural cause or the person did not have proper funeral rites.

statement.id: Mullo tercipta bila seseorang mati mendadak karena sebab tidak wajar atau tidak mendapat upacara pemakaman yang layak.
statement.en: A mullo arises when someone dies suddenly of an unnatural cause or does not receive proper funeral rites.

statement.en: A mullo is described with white clothes, hair to its feet and one physical oddity that varies by region; it seeks out and harasses people it disliked in life.

claims.quote: Mullo are believed to return and do malicious things and/or attack by strangling and suck the blood of a person (usually a relative who had caused their death, or hadn't properly observed the burial ceremonies, or who kept the deceased's possessions instead of destroying them as was proper).

statement.id: Mullo dipercaya kembali untuk berbuat jahat atau menyerang dengan mencekik dan mengisap darah, biasanya kerabat yang menyebabkan kematiannya, tidak menjalankan upacara pemakaman dengan benar, atau menyimpan barang milik almarhum yang semestinya dimusnahkan.
statement.en: Mullos are believed to return to do harm or attack by strangling and sucking blood, usually from a relative who caused their death, neglected the burial rites, or kept the dead person's belongings instead of destroying them.

claims.quote: To get rid of a vampire people would hire a Dhampir (the son of a vampire and his widow) to detect the vampire.

statement.en: To get rid of a vampire, people hired a Dhampir, the son of a vampire and his widow, to detect it.

statement.en: To ward off vampires, Romani people drove steel or iron needles into a corpse's heart and put bits of steel in the mouth, over the eyes and ears and between the fingers at burial.

statement.en: They also put hawthorn in the corpse's sock or drove a hawthorn stake through the legs; other measures were staking the grave, pouring boiling water on it, beheading the corpse or burning it.

short_description.id: Sleih beggey, bahasa Manx untuk 'orang kecil', adalah sebutan umum bagi peri-peri Pulau Man, yang dipercaya ada yang baik hati dan ada yang jahat.
short_description.en: Sleih beggey, Manx for 'little people', is the umbrella term for the fairies of Manx belief, some of them kindly and some harmful.

long_description.id: Sleih beggey berarti 'orang kecil' dalam bahasa Manx dan menjadi istilah payung untuk peri Manx; mereka juga disebut ferrishyn, dari kata Inggris fairies. Banyak makhluk mitos yang berbeda tercakup dalam istilah ini, ada yang baik dan ada yang jahat. Menurut A. W. Moore, orang menyebut mereka 'orang kecil' atau 'orang baik' dan tidak pernah menyebut kata fairy, karena mereka dipercaya tidak menyukainya.
long_description.en: Sleih beggey means 'little people' in Manx and serves as the umbrella term for Manx fairies; they are also called ferrishyn, from the English word fairies. Many different mythical beings fall under the term, both benevolent and malevolent. According to A. W. Moore, people called them 'the little people' or 'the good people' and never said the word fairy, which they were thought to dislike.

long_description.id: Mereka biasanya digambarkan bertubuh kekar dan sebagai peri rumah tangga yang gemar berburu, bermusik, dan menculik manusia; pakaian mereka umumnya hijau. Moore menggambarkan mereka mirip manusia tetapi jauh lebih kecil dan halus, berpakaian biru atau hijau dengan topi runcing merah, dan tinggal di lereng bukit hijau, terutama di gundukan makam kuno. Sebagian menyembuhkan penyakit dan menolong orang dari kemalangan, sebagian lain mencuri anak dan mendatangkan kesialan.
long_description.en: They are generally pictured as stocky domestic fairies fond of hunting, music and abducting humans, usually dressed in green. Moore describes them as human in form but much smaller and more delicate, clad in blue or green with red peaked caps, and living in green hillsides, especially the ancient tumuli. Some cure diseases and rescue people from misfortune, while others steal children and bring bad luck.

long_description.id: John Rhys membandingkan peri Manx dengan peri Wales: seperti peri Wales, mereka menculik bayi, menguasai perapian setelah petani dan keluarganya tidur, membawa pergi orang dewasa selama bertahun-tahun, serta memiliki kuda tunggangan dan anjing. Bedanya, peri Manx tidak segan memakai senjata untuk menyerang manusia. Sebagian dari mereka, yang disebut Ferrish, digambarkan setinggi satu sampai tiga kaki, menunggang kuda, memelihara anjing pemburu, dan tidak memiliki raja atau ratu.
long_description.en: John Rhys compared the Manx fairies with the Welsh: like Welsh fairies they kidnap babies, take over the hearth once the farmer and his family are in bed, carry adults away for years, and have horses to ride and dogs. Unlike the Welsh fairies, however, the Manx ones did not hesitate to use weapons against humans. One group, the Ferrish, is described as one to three foot tall, riding horses and keeping hunting dogs, with no named king or queen.

long_description.id: Peri-peri ini tidak menyukai abu, cahaya buatan, garam, dan pembaptisan. Moore mencatat bahwa garam dan besi sangat ampuh untuk melindungi diri dari mereka.
long_description.en: These fairies dislike ashes, artificial light, salt and baptisms. Moore notes that salt and iron are very effective protection against them.

claims.quote: Manx for Little people, also Beggys , Sleigh veggy , Sleigh beggey , and Ferrishyn from the English: faeries ) is the umbrella term for Manx fairies.

statement.id: Sleih beggey (bahasa Manx untuk 'orang kecil', juga Beggys, Sleigh veggy, Sleigh beggey, dan Ferrishyn dari kata Inggris faeries) adalah istilah payung untuk peri Manx.
statement.en: Sleih beggey (Manx for little people, also Beggys, Sleigh veggy, Sleigh beggey and Ferrishyn from English faeries) is the umbrella term for Manx fairies.

claims.quote: A wide variety of individual mythical creatures come under the umbrella of sleih beggey, with both benevolent and malevolent fairies.

statement.id: Beragam makhluk mitos tercakup dalam istilah sleih beggey, termasuk peri yang baik maupun yang jahat.
statement.en: A wide variety of mythical creatures come under the umbrella of sleih beggey, with both benevolent and malevolent fairies.

claims.quote: Generally, the Sleih beggey are seen as stocky in stature, and as domestic fairies, who lived in burghs. They are fond of hunting, music, and abducting humans.

statement.id: Sleih beggey umumnya dianggap bertubuh kekar, sebagai peri rumah tangga yang tinggal di burgh, dan gemar berburu, bermusik, serta menculik manusia.
statement.en: Sleih beggey are generally seen as stocky domestic fairies who lived in burghs, fond of hunting, music and abducting humans.

claims.quote: They dislike ashes, artificial light, salt, and baptisms. They commonly wore green clothes.

statement.id: Mereka tidak menyukai abu, cahaya buatan, garam, dan pembaptisan, dan umumnya berpakaian hijau.
statement.en: They dislike ashes, artificial light, salt and baptisms, and commonly wore green clothes.

claims.quote: John Rhys noted that Manx and Welsh fairies were similar in most aspects, but that Manx fairies had no issue using weapons to attack humans, unlike the Welsh fairies.

statement.id: John Rhys mencatat bahwa peri Manx dan Wales mirip dalam banyak hal, tetapi peri Manx tidak segan memakai senjata untuk menyerang manusia, tidak seperti peri Wales.
statement.en: John Rhys noted that Manx and Welsh fairies were similar in most aspects, but Manx fairies had no issue using weapons to attack humans, unlike the Welsh fairies.

claims.quote: The Ferrish have been described as a particular tribe of fairies, standing between one and three foot tall, who rode horses and kept dogs for hunting, having no named king or queen. They were known to replace human babies with changelings

statement.id: Ferrish digambarkan sebagai suku peri tertentu setinggi satu sampai tiga kaki yang menunggang kuda dan memelihara anjing pemburu, tanpa raja atau ratu, dan dikenal menukar bayi manusia dengan changeling.
statement.en: The Ferrish are described as a particular tribe of fairies one to three foot tall, who rode horses and kept hunting dogs, with no named king or queen, known to replace human babies with changelings.

statement.en: They are supposed to be like human beings in form and feature, though very much smaller and more delicately constructed.

claims.quote: They are usually represented as being clad in blue or green, with red peaked caps. They live in green hill sides, more especially affecting the ancient tumuli.

statement.id: Mereka biasanya digambarkan berpakaian biru atau hijau dengan topi runcing merah, dan tinggal di lereng bukit hijau, terutama di gundukan makam kuno (tumuli).

claims.quote: Some of them are benevolent, curing men of diseases and delivering them from misfortune. Others are malevolent, stealing children, even abducting grown people, and bringing misfortune.

short_description.id: Vadleány, "gadis liar", adalah makhluk hutan dalam cerita rakyat Hungaria yang berambut sangat panjang dan telanjang, yang menggoda pengembara dan mencuri kekuatan mereka.
short_description.en: The vadleány, the "wild girl", is a forest being of Hungarian folklore with very long hair and no clothing, who seduces wanderers and steals their strength.

long_description.id: Vadleány adalah makhluk roh dari cerita rakyat Eropa Tengah, khususnya Hungaria, yang namanya berarti "gadis liar". Ia mirip nimfa atau driad: tinggal di hutan, berambut sangat panjang, berkuku panjang, dan telanjang. Ia menggoda para pengembara dan mencuri kekuatan mereka, dan pepohonan berdesir ketika ia hadir.
long_description.en: The vadleány is a spirit being of Central European, particularly Hungarian, folklore whose name means "wild girl". She resembles nymphs or dryads: she lives in the forest, has very long hair and long nails, and goes naked. She seduces wanderers and steals their strength, and the trees rustle when she is present.

long_description.id: Orang Hungaria di Lápos menggambarkannya berwajah cantik tetapi bertubuh penuh bulu sampai ke tanah. Bila dibuat marah, ia menimbulkan angin yang mematahkan pohon dan memorakporandakan pondok gembala. Di Domokos dipercaya ia bisa ditangkap dengan meletakkan sebelah sepatu bot di jalurnya: karena penasaran ia memasukkan kedua kakinya dan tidak bisa lari. Di Mezőség dan Székelyföld ia disebut gadis hutan, nona penyanyi, atau gadis riang.
long_description.en: The Hungarians of Lápos described her as beautiful of face but covered in hair down to the ground. When angered she raises a wind that breaks trees and scatters the shepherd's hut. In Domokos it was believed she could be caught by setting a single boot on her path: out of curiosity she put both feet in and could not run. In Mezőség and Székelyföld she was called the forest girl, the singing maiden or the merry girl.

short_description.id: Vila adalah peri perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Slavia, roh alam yang bisa bersikap ramah maupun berbahaya terhadap manusia.
short_description.en: The vila is a female fairy of Slavic folklore, a nature spirit who can be either friendly or dangerous towards people.

long_description.id: Vila adalah peri Slavia yang mirip nimfa. Ia terutama dikenal di kalangan Slavia Selatan, tetapi beberapa variannya juga muncul dalam mitologi Slavia Barat. Menurut satu sumber, vila adalah roh alam perempuan yang biasanya digambarkan berkelompok, terutama dikaitkan dengan unsur air, tetapi juga hadir di hutan, ladang, dan pegunungan.
long_description.en: The vila is a Slavic fairy resembling a nymph. She is chiefly known among the South Slavs, though some variants also occur in West Slavic mythology. One source describes vile as female nature spirits usually pictured in groups, mainly tied to the element of water but also found in woods, fields and mountains.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah rakyat, vila adalah gadis cantik bertubuh tembus pandang dan berambut panjang; kehilangan sehelai rambut saja berarti kematian baginya. Ada tiga golongan vila: penghuni darat dan hutan, nimfa air, serta nimfa awan atau udara. Mereka tampil sebagai angsa, elang, kuda, atau serigala, sedangkan vila awan muncul sebagai angin puyuh.
long_description.en: In folk tales the vila is a beautiful girl with a translucent body and long hair; losing even a single hair means her death. There are three kinds of vile: dwellers of land and forest, water nymphs, and cloud or air nymphs. They appear as swans, falcons, horses or wolves, while cloud vile appear as a whirlwind.

long_description.id: Hubungan vila dengan manusia bersifat mendua. Dalam dongeng, mereka bisa membunuh orang, merusak panen, mengacaukan jiwa laki-laki dengan panah, dan menukar anak dengan anak tukaran, tetapi juga bisa menolong pahlawan dengan benda ajaib dan tunggangan. Mereka biasanya ramah, namun membalas dengan kejam bila dihina atau bila tarian lingkaran mereka didekati tanpa undangan. Mereka juga memiliki kekuatan gaib dan pandai menyembuhkan.
long_description.en: The vila's relationship with humans is ambivalent. In fairy tales they may kill people, ruin crops, confuse men's spirits with arrows and swap children for changelings, yet they may also aid a hero with magical objects and mounts. They are usually friendly, but take cruel revenge when insulted or when their circle dances are approached uninvited. They also hold supernatural powers and are skilled in healing.

long_description.id: Dalam puisi epik Kroasia dan Serbia, banyak pahlawan memiliki vila sebagai saudari angkat. Kegemaran vila bertempur dinilai unik dalam mitologi Slavia. Di Slowakia, vila dipercaya sebagai arwah gadis yang meninggal dan memikat pemuda ke dalam tarian lingkaran yang mematikan, sedangkan dalam tradisi Ceko mereka hampir selalu jahat kecuali dihormati dan dihindari.
long_description.en: Many heroes of Croatian and Serbian epic poetry count a vila as a sworn or blood sister. The vilas' love of fighting is considered unique in Slavic mythology. In Slovakia vile are believed to be the restless souls of dead girls who lure young men into a deadly circle dance, while in Czech tradition they are almost always malicious unless respected and avoided.

long_description.id: Pemujaan mereka dalam kultus pra-Kristen sudah dilaporkan pada abad ke-6, walaupun penulisnya tidak memakai nama Slavia dan menyebut mereka nimfa. Asal-usul nama vila tidak jelas; salah satu dugaan menghubungkannya dengan kata kerja Slavia viti, "melilit, memintal, menganyam". Roh yang berkerabat dengannya adalah rusalka, yang umumnya lebih membawa celaka.
long_description.en: Their worship in pre-Christian cult was already reported in the 6th century, though the writer did not use the Slavic name and called them nymphs. The origin of the name vila is unclear; one proposal links it to the Slavic verb viti, "to wind around, twist, weave". A related spirit is the rusalka, which is usually more harmful.

literal_meaning.en: to wind around, twist, weave (one proposal)

short_description.id: Anjana adalah peri baik dari mitologi Cantabria yang melindungi hutan, hewan, dan orang yang menderita, melawan raksasa Ojáncanu, dan membawa hadiah bagi anak miskin pada malam 5 Januari.
short_description.en: The anjana is a good fairy of Cantabrian mythology who protects forests, animals and the suffering, opposes the giant Ojáncanu and brings gifts to poor children on the night of 5 January.

long_description.id: Anjana, dari kata lama jana, "penyihir", adalah salah satu peri paling terkenal dalam mitologi Cantabria, dicatat Manuel Llano pada awal abad ke-20. Mereka berkulit putih, berkepang panjang berhias pita sutra, bermahkota bunga liar, berjubah biru, dan membawa tongkat yang berganti warna setiap hari. Sebagian menyebut mereka utusan Tuhan yang kembali ke surga setelah 400 tahun, yang lain roh pohon penjaga hutan; mereka juga dapat berubah wujud.
long_description.en: The anjana, from the old word jana, 'witch', is one of the best-known fairies of Cantabrian mythology, recorded by Manuel Llano in the early 20th century. They are white-skinned, with long silk-ribboned braids, a crown of wild flowers and a blue cape, and carry a staff that changes colour each day. Some call them God's envoys who return to heaven after 400 years, others tree spirits who tend the forests; they can also change shape.

long_description.id: Anjana berbicara dengan air mata air, menolong hewan, pohon, kekasih, orang tersesat, dan orang miskin, serta menggagalkan Ojáncanu yang kejam. Mereka memiliki istana dan harta di gua bawah tanah, menari pada malam ekuinoks musim semi sambil menaburkan mawar, dan setiap empat tahun membawa hadiah bagi anak miskin pada malam 5 Januari. Ada juga anjana jahat, tetapi kekuatannya dinetralkan anjana baik. Mereka mirip xana Asturias dan lamia Basque.
long_description.en: Anjanas talk with spring water, help animals, trees, lovers, the lost and the poor, and foil the cruel Ojáncanu. They keep palaces and treasure in underground caves, dance on the spring equinox night scattering roses, and every four years bring gifts to poor children on the night of 5 January. There are also wicked anjanas, but the good ones neutralise them. They resemble the xanas of Asturias and the Basque lamias.

who.en: A good fairy.

role.en: Protects people and forests.

famous_for.id: Hadiah pada malam 5 Januari.
famous_for.en: Gifts on the night of 5 January.

description.id: Mereka dapat berubah menjadi manusia, pohon, hewan, atau benda.
description.en: They can turn into people, trees, animals or objects.

description.id: Mereka menolong hewan yang terluka dan pohon yang rusak.
description.en: They help injured animals and damaged trees.

note.id: Raksasa kejam yang rencananya mereka gagalkan.
note.en: The cruel giant whose deeds they foil.

note.id: Peri air Asturias yang serupa.
note.en: The similar water fairy of Asturias.

claims.quote: are one of the best-known fairies of Cantabrian mythology. These female fairy creatures foil the cruel and ruthless Ojáncanu. In most stories, they are the good fairies of Cantabria, generous and protective of all people.

statement.id: Anjana adalah salah satu peri paling terkenal dalam mitologi Cantabria, peri perempuan yang menggagalkan Ojáncanu yang kejam, dan dalam kebanyakan cerita peri baik yang murah hati dan melindungi semua orang.
statement.en: The anjanas are among the best-known fairies of Cantabrian mythology, female fairies who foil the cruel Ojáncanu and in most tales are good, generous fairies protecting everyone.

claims.quote: Some say they are heavenly beings sent by God to do good deeds, and they go back to heaven after 400 years, never to return. Others, however, indicate that they are spirits of trees who take care of the forests.

statement.id: Sebagian orang menyebut mereka makhluk surgawi utusan Tuhan untuk berbuat baik yang kembali ke surga setelah 400 tahun, sementara yang lain menyebut mereka roh pohon penjaga hutan.
statement.en: Some say they are heavenly beings sent by God to do good who return to heaven after 400 years, while others call them tree spirits who tend the forests.

claims.quote: They wear long, jet black or golden braids, adorned with multicolored silk bows and ribbons; a beautiful crown of wild flowers on their head; and a blue cape on a long thin white tunic, and carry in their hands a stick of wicker or hawthorn which shines in a different color every day of the week.

statement.id: Mereka berkepang panjang hitam legam atau keemasan berhias pita sutra warna-warni, bermahkota bunga liar, bertunik putih panjang dan berjubah biru, dan membawa tongkat rotan atau hawthorn yang bersinar dengan warna berbeda setiap hari.
statement.en: They wear long jet-black or golden braids with coloured silk ribbons, a crown of wild flowers, a long white tunic and blue cape, and carry a wicker or hawthorn staff that shines a different colour each day of the week.

claims.quote: They are able to talk with the water that flows from the sources and springs. They help injured animals and trees damaged by storms or Ojáncanu, lovers, people who lose their way in the forest, and the poor and suffering.

statement.id: Mereka dapat berbicara dengan air dari mata air, dan menolong hewan yang terluka, pohon yang dirusak badai atau Ojáncanu, para kekasih, orang yang tersesat di hutan, serta orang miskin dan menderita.
statement.en: They can talk with the water of springs, and help injured animals, trees damaged by storms or the Ojáncanu, lovers, people lost in the forest, and the poor and suffering.

claims.quote: Traditions state that at night during the spring equinox, they gather in the fells and dance until dawn holding hands and scattering roses. Anyone who manages to find a rose with purple, green, blue, or golden petals will be happy until the time of their death.

statement.id: Pada malam ekuinoks musim semi mereka berkumpul di bukit dan menari sampai fajar sambil bergandengan tangan dan menaburkan mawar; siapa pun yang menemukan mawar berkelopak ungu, hijau, biru, atau emas akan bahagia sampai mati.
statement.en: On the night of the spring equinox they gather on the fells and dance till dawn holding hands and scattering roses; whoever finds a rose with purple, green, blue or golden petals will be happy until death.

claims.quote: Anjanas come to villages of the region during the night of January 5, with the intention of bringing children a variety of toys and gifts. This occurs every four years, generally to poor families

statement.id: Anjana datang ke desa-desa pada malam 5 Januari membawa mainan dan hadiah untuk anak-anak, setiap empat tahun sekali, biasanya kepada keluarga miskin.
statement.en: Anjanas come to the villages on the night of 5 January bringing toys and gifts for children, every four years, usually to poor families.

claims.quote: es un personaje fantástico, referido por el costumbrista Manuel Llano en el primer tercio del s. XX como parte de la mitología cántabra.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, anjana adalah tokoh fantastis yang dicatat penulis adat Manuel Llano pada sepertiga awal abad ke-20 sebagai bagian mitologi Cantabria.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, the anjana is a fantastic figure recorded by the folklore writer Manuel Llano in the early 20th century as part of Cantabrian mythology.

claims.quote: Tienen una piel blanquísima y una mirada amorosa y serena, pero pueden convertirse en personas, árboles, animales u objetos inanimados.

statement.id: Mereka berkulit sangat putih dan bertatapan penuh kasih, tetapi dapat berubah menjadi manusia, pohon, hewan, atau benda mati.
statement.en: They have very white skin and a loving, serene gaze, but can turn into people, trees, animals or objects.

claims.quote: y poseen grandes palacios subterráneos, ocultos en torcas y cuevas -frecuentemente en fuentes y ríos-, en donde guardan magníficos tesoros

statement.id: Mereka memiliki istana bawah tanah yang tersembunyi di lubang dan gua, sering di mata air dan sungai, tempat mereka menyimpan harta yang megah.
statement.en: They own great underground palaces hidden in sinkholes and caves, often at springs and rivers, where they keep magnificent treasures.

claims.quote: Pero también hay anjanas malvadas, si bien su poder suele ser neutralizado por las bondadosas.

statement.id: Namun ada juga anjana jahat, meski kekuatannya biasanya dinetralkan oleh anjana yang baik.
statement.en: But there are also wicked anjanas, though their power is usually neutralised by the good ones.

claims.quote: Bu qadın pərilər qəddar və zalım Oxankanunun qarşısında duran xeyirxah varlıqlardır.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Azerbaijan juga menyebut peri-peri perempuan ini makhluk baik yang melawan Ojáncanu yang kejam.
statement.en: The Azerbaijani article also calls these female fairies benevolent beings opposing the cruel Ojáncanu.

claims.quote: from jana, a former word for witches during the Middle Ages

statement.id: Namanya berasal dari jana, kata lama untuk penyihir pada Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: The name comes from jana, an old word for witches in the Middle Ages.

claims.quote: Their depiction in the Cantabrian mythology is reminiscent of the lamias in ancient Greek mythology, as well as the xanas in Asturias, the janas in León, and the lamias in Basque Country, the latter without the zoomorphic appearance.

statement.id: Gambaran mereka mengingatkan pada lamia Yunani kuno, xana di Asturias, jana di León, dan lamia Basque, tetapi tanpa ciri hewan.
statement.en: Their depiction recalls the lamias of ancient Greece, the xanas of Asturias, the janas of León and the Basque lamias, though without animal features.

short_description.id: Cauld Lad of Hylton adalah hantu pemuda kandang Robert Skelton yang dibunuh, konon menghantui reruntuhan Kastel Hylton di Sunderland, Inggris Utara.
short_description.en: The Cauld Lad of Hylton is said to be the spirit of Robert Skelton, a stable lad who was murdered, and to haunt the ruined Hylton Castle in Sunderland, Northern England.

long_description.id: Cauld Lad of Hylton adalah hantu Robert Skelton, pemuda penjaga kandang yang dibunuh, yang konon menghantui reruntuhan Kastel Hylton di Sunderland, Inggris Utara. Peristiwanya dikatakan terjadi pada abad ke-16 atau ke-17. Satu versi menyebut ia ketahuan mendekati putri Baron Hylton; versi lain menyebut sang baron murka karena Skelton kesiangan, lalu membunuhnya dan membuang jasadnya ke kolam atau sumur.
long_description.en: The Cauld Lad of Hylton is the ghost of Robert Skelton, a murdered stable boy, said to haunt the ruins of Hylton Castle in Sunderland in the north of England. The events supposedly took place in the 16th or 17th century. In one version he was caught courting Baron Hylton's daughter; in another the baron, furious that Skelton had overslept, killed him and threw the body into a pond or well.

short_description.id: Sava Savanović adalah salah satu vampir paling terkenal dalam cerita rakyat Balkan dan Serbia, yang konon tinggal di sebuah kincir air tua dan meminum darah para penggiling gandum.
short_description.en: Sava Savanović is one of the most famous vampires of Balkan and Serbian folklore, said to have lived in an old watermill and drunk the blood of millers.

long_description.id: Sava Savanović adalah salah satu vampir paling terkenal dalam cerita rakyat Balkan dan Serbia, dan hingga kini tetap vampir yang paling dikenal di Serbia. Menurut legenda, ia tinggal di sebuah kincir air tua di Sungai Rogačica, di desa Zarožje, wilayah Bajina Bašta, dan membunuh serta meminum darah para penggiling yang datang menggiling biji-bijian mereka.
long_description.en: Sava Savanović is one of the most famous vampires of Balkan and Serbian folklore and remains the best-known vampire in Serbia today. Legend places his home in an old watermill beside the Rogačica river near the village of Zarožje, in Bajina Bašta, where he killed millers who brought their grain and drank their blood.

long_description.id: Kisahnya hanya diwariskan secara lisan dan memiliki banyak versi, tetapi intinya sama: seorang laki-laki dari desa Zarožje yang tewas secara tragis setelah sebuah pembunuhan, lalu dikuburkan di dekat tempat kejadian. Setelah para penggiling di kincir air Sungai Rogačica berulang kali ditemukan tewas dengan bekas gigitan di leher, penduduk yakin Sava telah menjadi vampir. Ketika kuburnya dibuka, jasadnya ditemukan tidak membusuk, dan untuk mematahkan kutukan sebuah pancang runcing ditancapkan ke jantungnya.
long_description.en: His story was passed down only orally and has many versions, but they share a core: a man of Zarožje village who died tragically after a killing and was buried near the scene. After millers at the Rogačica watermills were repeatedly found dead with bite marks on their necks, villagers concluded that Sava had become a vampire. When his grave was opened his body was found undecayed, and to break the curse a sharpened stake was driven through his heart.

long_description.id: Meski ia biasanya disebut vampir Serbia pertama, ada klaim bahwa cerita rakyat Serbia sudah mengenal Petar Blagojević dari Kisiljevo, yang meninggal pada 1725. Sava Savanović juga muncul dalam cerita Posle devedeset godina karya Milovan Glišić dan dalam film horor Leptirica yang terilhami cerita itu.
long_description.en: Although he is usually called the first Serbian vampire, there are claims that Serbian folklore already knew Petar Blagojević of Kisiljevo, who died in 1725. Sava Savanović also appears in Milovan Glišić's story Posle devedeset godina and in the horror film Leptirica inspired by it.

short_description.id: Syöjätär adalah demon perempuan pemakan manusia dalam puisi rakyat dan dongeng Finlandia, yang dianggap asal-usul ular dan berbagai hal buruk di dunia.
short_description.en: Syöjätär is a man-eating female demon of Finnish folk poetry and fairy tales, held to be the origin of snakes and various evils in the world.

long_description.id: Dalam puisi rakyat dan dongeng, Syöjätär adalah makhluk perempuan jahat, roh jahat dalam tradisi rakyat Finlandia. Pada 1789 Christfried Ganander menggambarkannya sebagai demon perempuan, setengah demon atau setengah troll, pemakan daging yang kejam dan kanibal. Dalam kumpulan mantra susunan Elias Lönnrot ia roh jahat atau penyihir yang disebut bersama Hiisi, Perkele, dan Louhi. Sebuah lagu menyebut ia lahir ketika Louhi melahirkan Sembilan Penyakit dan anak kesepuluh, seorang putri.
long_description.en: In folk poetry and fairy tales Syöjätär is an evil female being, an evil spirit of Finnish folk tradition. In 1789 Christfried Ganander described her as a she-demon, part demon or part troll, a savage eater of flesh and of people. In the charm collection compiled by Elias Lönnrot she is an evil spirit or witch named alongside Hiisi, Perkele and Louhi. One song says she was born when Louhi bore the Nine Diseases and a tenth child, a daughter.

long_description.id: Syöjätär dianggap merusak ciptaan yang baik: kadal disebut brosnya, ular lahir dari ludahnya, dan karena keluhannya Tuhan mengurangi puting sapi sehingga susu berkurang. Ia dibandingkan dengan Áhčešeatni Sami, dan dalam dongeng ia sering dibunuh pada akhir cerita, dengan ular dan hewan tak menyenangkan muncul dari jasadnya.
long_description.en: Syöjätär is held to spoil the good creation: the lizard is called her brooch, the snake was born of her spit, and because of her complaint God reduced the cow's teats so there is less milk. She is compared to the Sámi Áhčešeatni, and in fairy tales she is often killed at the end, with snakes and unpleasant animals emerging from her corpse.

long_description.id: Dalam lagu "Putri Raja dan Syöjätär", ia menyihir seorang putri menjadi syöjätär yang buta dan bisu lalu menyamar sebagai sang putri. Sang putri akhirnya kembali ke wujudnya, dan bersama saudaranya memancing Syöjätär ke sauna, tempat ia jatuh ke lubang jebakan dan terbakar.
long_description.en: In the song "King's Princess and Syöjätär" she bewitches a princess into a blind, mute syöjätär and takes on the princess's likeness. The princess finally regains her form and, with her brother, lures Syöjätär into a sauna, where she falls into a trap pit and is burned.

statement.en: Syöjätär may be a memory of the good-and-bad-creator dualism of Finno-Ugric origin myths and has been compared to the Sámi Áhčešeatni, whose corpse turns into frogs, toads and other unpleasant animals; in fairy tales she is often killed at the end and snakes and other unpleasant animals come from her corpse.
