short_description.id: Poludnitsa atau "Nyonya Tengah Hari" adalah iblis siang hari dalam mitologi Slavia yang menghampiri orang yang bekerja di ladang pada tengah hari dan membawa sengatan panas atau penyakit.
short_description.en: Poludnitsa, or "Lady Midday", is a noon demon of Slavic mythology who accosts people working in the fields at midday, bringing heatstroke or illness.

long_description.id: Poludnitsa, yang namanya berarti "tengah hari", adalah tokoh mitos yang dikenal di berbagai negeri Slavia di Eropa Timur. Ia iblis siang hari dalam mitologi Slavia dan dalam bahasa Inggris dijuluki "Lady Midday" atau "Noonwraith". Asal-usul sosoknya dihubungkan dengan personifikasi sengatan matahari, suasana khas siang yang terik, dan sisa kepercayaan pada dewa serta iblis kuno. Di antara bangsa Slavia Timur, hanya orang Rusia di barat laut Rusia yang mempercayainya.
long_description.en: Poludnitsa, whose name means "midday", is a mythical figure known across the Slavic lands of Eastern Europe. She is a noon demon of Slavic mythology, called "Lady Midday" or "Noonwraith" in English. Her figure is traced to a personification of sunstroke, the peculiar air of a scorching noon and remnants of belief in ancient gods and demons. Among the East Slavs, only Russians in north-western Russia believed in her.

long_description.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda berbaju putih yang berkeliaran di pematang ladang, tetapi bisa juga tampil sebagai nenek tua, perempuan cantik, atau gadis berusia 12 tahun. Ia muncul di tengah hari musim panas yang terik dalam bentuk pusaran debu, membawa sabit, arit, atau gunting. Ia menyerang orang yang bekerja di ladang pada tengah hari, menyebabkan sengatan panas, sakit leher, bahkan kegilaan.
long_description.en: She is usually pictured as a young woman in white roaming the edges of fields, though she may equally take the shape of a beautiful woman, a 12-year-old girl or an old crone. She shows herself in the heat of summer noons as a whirling cloud of dust, carrying a scythe, sickle or shears. She attacks those working the fields at midday, bringing heatstroke, neck pain and even madness.

long_description.id: Poludnitsa menghentikan orang di ladang untuk mengajukan pertanyaan sulit; siapa yang gagal menjawab atau mengalihkan pembicaraan akan dipenggal atau dibuat sakit. Menurut satu sumber, orang yang diganggunya hanya selamat bila terus bercerita tentang pekerjaan petani, terutama mengolah rami, sampai pukul satu, karena setelah jam istirahat itu ia kehilangan kekuatan. Ia juga suka menari dan memaksa gadis yang beristirahat di ladang menari sampai senja, tetapi gadis yang mampu mengalahkannya diberi mas kawin yang kaya.
long_description.en: Poludnitsa stops people in the field to put hard questions to them; whoever fails to answer or changes the subject is beheaded or struck with illness. One source says her victims can only save themselves by talking about farm work, especially flax processing, until one o'clock, for after that rest hour she loses her power. She also loves to dance, making a girl resting in the field dance until dusk, yet a girl able to outdance her receives a rich dowry.

long_description.id: Menurut kebanyakan kepercayaan, ia bermusuhan dan sangat berbahaya bagi manusia, terutama bagi perempuan hamil, ibu yang baru melahirkan, dan anak kecil; ia bahkan mencuri dan menukar bayi. Namun ada pula kepercayaan bahwa ia menjaga tanaman biji-bijian dan sayuran dari manusia dan dari terik matahari, dan ia dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak agar menjauhi tanaman berharga. Untuk melawannya, orang membuat tanda salib, berdoa, memercikkan air suci, atau melarikan diri.
long_description.en: Most beliefs hold her hostile and very dangerous to people, especially to pregnant women, new mothers and small children; she even steals and swaps infants. Yet some beliefs say she guards grain and vegetables from people and from the scorching sun, and she served to scare children away from valuable crops. Against her, people crossed themselves, prayed, sprinkled holy water or simply ran away.

short_description.id: Likhoradka adalah roh perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia, perwujudan penyakit demam yang dapat merasuki tubuh manusia.
short_description.en: Likhoradka is a female spirit of Slavic mythology, the embodiment of fever that can possess a person's body.

long_description.id: Likhoradka atau tryasavitsa adalah roh perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia yang dipercaya dapat merasuki tubuh seseorang dan membuatnya sakit, menimbulkan menggigil dan panas bergantian. Dalam beberapa kisah ia ciptaan dewa kegelapan Chernobog. Legenda Rusia yang lebih kemudian menyebut dua belas Likhoradka dengan nama masing-masing yang terkait penyakit tertentu.
long_description.en: Likhoradka, or tryasavitsa, is a female spirit of Slavic myth said to enter a person's body and make them ill, bringing chills and heat in turn. Some tales make her a creation of the dark god Chernobog. Later Russian legends speak of twelve Likhoradkas, each named for a particular illness.

long_description.id: Ia kadang digambarkan sebagai perempuan tinggi berambut kusut, berwajah pucat, dan berbaju putih yang membawa penyakit kepada orang yang disentuh atau diciumnya. Ciri khasnya adalah jumlah yang banyak, tujuh, sembilan, dua belas, atau tujuh puluh tujuh perempuan bersaudara, dan wujud yang berubah-ubah.
long_description.en: She was sometimes shown as a tall woman with tangled hair, a pale face and a white dress who sickened anyone she touched or kissed. Her hallmark is multiplicity, seven, nine, twelve or seventy-seven sisters, and a changing form.

long_description.id: Kata likhoradka berasal dari bahasa Rusia kuno likho, "kejahatan, nasib buruk", dan radet, "berusaha". Dalam bahasa Rusia modern kata ini berarti "demam". Sebagai tokoh mitologi ia berkerabat dengan Chuma, sosok wabah.
long_description.en: The word likhoradka comes from Old Russian likho, "harm, bad luck", and radet, "to strive". In modern Russian it means "fever". As a mythological figure she is related to Chuma, the figure of plague.

short_description.id: Mouros adalah bangsa makhluk gaib dalam legenda Portugal, Galisia, dan Asturias yang tinggal di bawah tanah dekat castro dan makam kuno, mengolah emas, dan menyimpan harta yang dijaga cuélebre.
short_description.en: The Mouros are a supernatural race of Portuguese, Galician and Asturian legend who live underground near castros and ancient barrows, work gold and keep treasure guarded by cuélebres.

long_description.id: Mouros atau Moiros adalah bangsa makhluk gaib yang mendiami Galisia, Asturias, dan Portugal sejak awal zaman lalu berlindung di bawah tanah, sehingga kini terlihat di sekitar castro dan makam gundukan panjang. Mereka mengolah emas, perak, dan permata menjadi harta yang dijaga cuélebre, dan jarang keluar kecuali untuk mencari makan atau pada pertengahan musim panas. Mouros laki-laki pandai emas berkulit gelap, sedangkan mouras dikenal sebagai penyihir berambut merah.
long_description.en: The Mouros or Moiros are a supernatural race who have lived in Galicia, Asturias and Portugal since the beginning of time and then took refuge underground, so they are now seen around castros and long barrows. They work gold, silver and gems into treasures guarded by cuélebres and rarely come out except for food or at Midsummer. The male mouros are dark-skinned goldsmiths, while the mouras are reputed red-haired sorceresses.

long_description.id: Mereka berdagang dengan manusia dan membayar dengan emas yang berubah menjadi batu atau arang bila asal-usulnya diceritakan. Mouros encantados kadang muncul sebagai raksasa atau prajurit, dan termasuk mourinhos yang kecil seperti peri. Namanya dikaitkan dengan Latin mortuus, "mati", atau dengan ouro, "emas"; antropolog Galisia menganggap mereka kebalikan petani Galisia.
long_description.en: They trade with humans and pay in gold that turns to stone or coal if its origin is told. The Mouros encantados sometimes appear as giants or warriors and include the small, elf-like mourinhos. The name is linked to Latin mortuus, 'dead', or to ouro, 'gold'; Galician anthropologists see them as the opposite of the Galician peasant.

short_description.id: Muma Pădurii ("ibu hutan") adalah roh hutan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania berwujud perempuan tua buruk rupa, pelindung hewan dan tumbuhan yang juga menculik anak-anak.
short_description.en: Muma Pădurii ("mother of the forest") is a forest spirit of Romanian folklore in the form of an ugly old woman, protector of animals and plants who also kidnaps children.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, Muma Pădurii adalah perempuan tua buruk rupa yang nakal atau gila, tinggal di jantung hutan perawan dalam pondok atau pohon tua. Ia lawan peri seperti Zână, tetapi juga pelindung hewan dan tumbuhan: meracik ramuan, menolong hewan terluka, menyembuhkan hutan yang sekarat, dan mengusir penyusup dengan membuat mereka gila dan ketakutan. Ia makhluk netral yang hanya mencelakai orang yang merusak hutan.
long_description.en: Romanian folklore pictures Muma Pădurii as a hideous old woman, mischievous or mad, who dwells deep in untouched woodland in a hut or an ancient tree. Fairies like the Zână are her opposites, yet she also protects animals and plants: brewing potions, helping injured animals, healing a dying forest and driving off trespassers by maddening and frightening them. She is a neutral being, harming only those who harm the forest.

long_description.id: Ia roh hutan dalam tubuh perempuan tua yang sangat buruk rupa, kadang dapat berubah wujud, dan tinggal di rumah kecil yang gelap dan tersembunyi. Ia dipercaya menyerang anak-anak sehingga banyak mantra (descântece) dipakai melawannya; dalam satu kisah populer ia hendak merebus seorang gadis kecil hidup-hidup, tetapi kakak gadis itu mengakalinya dan mendorongnya ke dalam tungku, mirip kisah Hansel dan Gretel. Orang Rumania kadang berkata "ia mirip Muma Pădurii" untuk menyebut seseorang jelek.
long_description.en: She is a forest spirit in the body of a very ugly old woman, sometimes able to change shape, living in a dark, hidden little house. She is thought to attack children, so many spells (descântece) are used against her; in one popular tale she tries to boil a little girl alive, but the girl's brother outwits her and pushes her into the oven, like Hansel and Gretel. Romanians sometimes say "she looks like Muma Pădurii" to call someone ugly.

short_description.id: Odei atau Hodei adalah roh guntur dan awan badai mitologi Basque yang merusak panen dengan petir dan kadang disebut putra jahat Mari.
short_description.en: Odei or Hodei is the Basque spirit of thunder and storm clouds who ruins crops with lightning and is sometimes called Mari's wicked son.

long_description.id: Odei, Hodei, atau Odai adalah roh guntur dan personifikasi awan badai dalam mitologi Basque, "dia yang bergemuruh". Ia menakuti petani dengan merusak panen lewat petir, tampak sebagai awan badai, dan dianggap pengganti dewa langit lama Ortzi; kadang ia putra jahat Mari. Saat guntur terdengar orang berkata "Odeiak jo", dan di Arrasate angin tenggara pembawa badai disebut angin Odei.
long_description.en: Odei, Hodei or Odai is the Basque spirit of thunder and personified storm cloud, 'the one who thunders'. He frightens farmers by ruining crops with lightning, appears as a storm cloud, and is seen as successor to the old sky god Ortzi; sometimes he is Mari's wicked son. At thunder people say 'Odeiak jo', and at Arrasate the stormy south-east wind is Odei's wind.

long_description.id: Untuk meredakan amarahnya, di Lapurdi orang menyalakan lilin yang diberkati, membakar laurel, atau menaruh kapak bermata ke atas di ambang pintu.

short_description.id: Revenant adalah roh atau mayat hidup dalam cerita rakyat Eropa yang bangkit dari kubur untuk menghantui orang hidup, kepercayaan yang jejaknya terlihat dalam kuburan sejak Zaman Perunggu.
short_description.en: A revenant is a spirit or animated corpse of European folklore that rises from the grave to haunt the living, a belief traced in graves back to the Bronze Age.

long_description.id: Revenant, "yang kembali", adalah roh atau mayat hidup yang dipercaya bangkit untuk menghantui orang hidup, dikenal dalam berbagai budaya termasuk Kelt dan Norse dan dicatat sejarawan Inggris abad pertengahan. Kematian tidak wajar dianggap penyebab arwah mengembara. Banyak folkloris menganggapnya istilah umum untuk mayat hidup, meski sebagian membedakannya dari vampir Eropa Timur.
long_description.en: The revenant, 'one who returns', is a spirit or animated corpse believed to rise to haunt the living, known in many cultures including Celtic and Norse and recorded by medieval English historians. An unusual death was thought to make the dead wander. Many folklorists treat it as a general term for the undead, though some distinguish it from the Eastern European vampire.

long_description.id: Arkeolog menemukan kuburan revenant di seluruh Eropa, dengan batu di atas kaki atau di rahang dan bagian tubuh yang dibuang, yang tertua dari Zaman Perunggu sekitar 4.000 tahun lalu. Kepercayaan ini tercatat dalam sastra Romawi, umum di Abad Pertengahan, kuat di Polandia abad ke-17, dan dikaji Augustin Calmet pada 1751.
long_description.en: Archaeologists have found revenant graves throughout Europe, with stones on the legs or in the jaw and body parts removed, the oldest from the Bronze Age about 4,000 years ago. The belief appears in Roman literature, was common in the Middle Ages, strong in 17th-century Poland, and studied by Augustin Calmet in 1751.

who.en: The returning dead.

role.en: Haunts the living.

famous_for.id: Kuburan revenant Zaman Perunggu.
famous_for.en: Bronze Age revenant graves.

claims.quote: In folklore, a revenant is a spirit or animated corpse that is believed to have been resurrected to haunt the living. The word revenant is derived from the Old French word revenant 'returning' (see also the related French verb revenir 'to come back').

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, revenant adalah roh atau mayat hidup yang dipercaya bangkit untuk menghantui orang hidup; kata revenant berasal dari bahasa Prancis Kuno, "yang kembali".
statement.en: In folklore a revenant is a spirit or animated corpse believed to have risen to haunt the living; the word comes from Old French revenant, 'returning'.

claims.quote: Revenants are part of the legend of various cultures, including Celtic and Norse mythology, and stories of supposed revenant visitations were documented by English historians in the Middle Ages.

statement.id: Revenant ada dalam legenda berbagai budaya, termasuk mitologi Kelt dan Norse, dan kisah kunjungan revenant dicatat sejarawan Inggris pada Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: Revenants feature in the legends of various cultures, including Celtic and Norse mythology, and tales of revenant visits were recorded by English historians in the Middle Ages.

claims.quote: Archaeologists have found revenant graves throughout Europe, characterized by bodies that had precautions taken to prevent them from rising up and causing mischief for the living, such as stones placed over the legs, stones placed in the jaw so it could not speak, bodies lodged with bricks, or body parts removed.

statement.id: Arkeolog menemukan kuburan revenant di seluruh Eropa, berisi jasad yang diberi pencegahan agar tidak bangkit, seperti batu di atas kaki, batu di rahang agar tak bisa bicara, jasad yang diganjal bata, atau bagian tubuh yang dibuang.
statement.en: Archaeologists have found revenant graves across Europe, with bodies given precautions against rising, such as stones on the legs, stones in the jaw so it could not speak, bodies wedged with bricks or body parts removed.

claims.quote: The oldest known graves are as old as 4,000 years BP from the Bronze Age. Roman literature contained writings about revenants. They were common throughout the Middle Ages, and 17th-century Poland was reportedly a hot-bed of revenant superstition.

statement.id: Kuburan tertua berasal dari sekitar 4.000 tahun lalu pada Zaman Perunggu; sastra Romawi menulis tentang revenant, kepercayaan ini umum sepanjang Abad Pertengahan, dan Polandia abad ke-17 konon menjadi pusatnya.
statement.en: The oldest known graves date to about 4,000 years BP in the Bronze Age; Roman literature wrote of revenants, they were common through the Middle Ages, and 17th-century Poland was reportedly a hotbed of the belief.

claims.quote: The term "revenant" has been used interchangeably with "ghost" by folklorists. While some maintain that vampires derive from Eastern European folklore and revenants derive from Western European folklore, many assert that revenant is a generic term for the undead.

statement.id: Folkloris memakai istilah revenant bergantian dengan hantu; sebagian berpendapat vampir berasal dari Eropa Timur dan revenant dari Eropa Barat, tetapi banyak yang menganggap revenant istilah umum untuk mayat hidup.
statement.en: Folklorists have used 'revenant' interchangeably with 'ghost'; some say vampires come from Eastern and revenants from Western European folklore, but many hold revenant is a general term for the undead.

claims.quote: Augustin Calmet conducted extensive research on the topic in his work titled Traité sur les apparitions des esprits et sur les vampires ou les revenans de Hongrie, de Moravie, &c. (1751) in which he describes the related rumors of the time.

statement.id: Augustin Calmet meneliti topik ini secara luas dalam Traité sur les apparitions des esprits et sur les vampires ou les revenans de Hongrie, de Moravie (1751).
statement.en: Augustin Calmet researched the subject at length in his Traité sur les apparitions des esprits et sur les vampires ou les revenans de Hongrie, de Moravie (1751).

claims.quote: No folclore, um revenant ou revenã é um espírito ou cadáver animado, em que se acredita ter sido revivido da morte para assombrar os vivos.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Portugis juga menyebut revenant roh atau mayat hidup yang dipercaya bangkit dari kematian untuk menghantui orang hidup.
statement.en: The Portuguese article also calls the revenant a spirit or animated corpse believed revived from death to haunt the living.

claims.quote: Revenant je v mytologii a folklóru oživené mrtvé tělo, které přichází do kontaktu s živými. Slovo je odvozeno od latinského revenire („navracet se“)

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Ceko, revenant adalah jasad mati yang hidup kembali dan berhubungan dengan orang hidup, dan katanya dari bahasa Latin revenire, "kembali".
statement.en: According to the Czech article, a revenant is a revived dead body that comes into contact with the living, the word from Latin revenire, 'to return'.

claims.quote: Přesvědčení, že neobvyklá smrt je příčinou posmrtného bloudění, je u Indoevropanů obecně rozšířena.

statement.id: Keyakinan bahwa kematian yang tidak wajar menyebabkan arwah mengembara setelah mati tersebar luas di kalangan bangsa Indo-Eropa.

short_description.id: Upiór adalah makhluk iblis dari cerita rakyat Slavia dan Turkik, cikal bakal vampir: arwah najis yang merasuki jasad yang membusuk dan membutuhkan darah orang hidup.
short_description.en: The upiór is a demonic being of Slavic and Turkic folklore, the prototype of the vampire: an unclean spirit possessing a decaying body that needs the blood of the living.

long_description.id: Upiór adalah makhluk iblis dari cerita rakyat Slavia dan Turkik, cikal bakal vampir. Diduga kepercayaan akan ubır (upiór) menyebar melintasi stepa Eurasia lewat migrasi bangsa Kipchak-Kuman, setelah berasal dari wilayah sekitar Sungai Volga dan stepa Pontus. Kata modern "vampir" berasal dari bentuk Slavia Kuno dan Turkik onpyr.
long_description.en: The upiór is a demonic being of Slavic and Turkic lore and the forerunner of the vampire. Belief in the ubır (upiór) is thought to have spread over the Eurasian steppes with the migrations of the Kipchak-Cuman people, having begun around the Volga and the Pontic steppes. The modern word "vampire" goes back to the Old Slavic and Turkic form onpyr.

long_description.id: Bangsa Slavia percaya bahwa saat seseorang mati, jiwanya keluar dari tubuh dan berkeliaran di sekitar rumah dan tempat kerjanya selama 40 hari, dan selama itu dapat masuk kembali ke jasad. Kematian anak yang belum dibaptis, kematian karena kekerasan atau sebelum waktunya, atau kematian pendosa berat seperti penyihir atau pembunuh dapat membuat jiwa menjadi najis. Vampir adalah perwujudan roh najis yang merasuki jasad yang membusuk; makhluk mayat hidup ini membutuhkan darah orang hidup dan pendendam serta iri kepada mereka.
long_description.en: Slavs believed that at death the soul leaves the body and wanders its home and workplace for 40 days, during which it can re-enter the corpse. The death of an unbaptised child, a violent or untimely death, or the death of a grave sinner such as a sorcerer or murderer could make the soul unclean. A vampire is an unclean spirit possessing a rotting body; this undead creature needs the blood of the living and is vengeful and envious toward them.

short_description.id: Uriaș adalah sebutan Rumania untuk raksasa dalam cerita rakyat, makhluk berwajah manusia yang begitu besar hingga bisa mengobrol dari satu gunung ke gunung lain.
short_description.en: Uriaș is the Romanian name for the giants of folklore, human-faced beings so huge they can chat from one mountain to another.

long_description.id: Uriaș adalah sebutan umum dalam bahasa Rumania untuk raksasa, tokoh penting dalam cerita rakyat Rumania. Mereka berwajah manusia, kekar dan perkasa, setinggi beberapa depa, dengan langkah sangat jauh dan kepala sangat besar; mereka bisa mengobrol dari satu gunung ke gunung lain dan berpegangan pada pegangan langit. Kadang mereka digambarkan sebagai kiklops bermata satu pemakan manusia.
long_description.en: Uriaș is the common Romanian word for giants, prominent figures of Romanian folklore. They have human faces, are brawny and mighty, several fathoms tall, with enormous strides and huge heads; they can chat from one mountain to another and grab the handles of the sky. Sometimes they are described as one-eyed, man-eating cyclopes.

long_description.id: Sebuah kisah umum menceritakan anak uriaș yang membawa pulang seorang petani beserta bajak dan lembunya seperti mainan, lalu orang tuanya meramalkan punahnya bangsa raksasa yang akan digantikan makhluk kecil. Di beberapa daerah Oltenia dan Transilvania mereka disebut Jidovi atau Novaci, dan mereka dianggap membangun benteng prasejarah dan gundukan tanah, yang sebenarnya tumulus pemakaman Zaman Perunggu dan Besi.
long_description.en: A common tale tells of an uriaș child who brings home a farmer with his plough and oxen like toys, and the parents foretell the passing of the giants and their replacement by small beings. In parts of Oltenia and Transylvania they are called Jidovi or Novaci, and they are credited with building prehistoric forts and earth mounds, which are in fact burial tumuli of the Bronze and Iron Ages.

claims.quote: Uriașii sunt figuri de mitologie sau basm, cu chip de om, mari, vânjoși, voinici, înalți de mai mulți stânjeni, cu pasul de o de poștă, cu capul cât trei ocale domnești sau mare cât o baniță. Ei pot sta la taifas de la un munte la altul, fiind în stare să se apuce cu mâinile de toartele cerului.

statement.id: Uriaș adalah tokoh mitologi atau dongeng berwajah manusia, besar, kekar, dan perkasa, setinggi beberapa depa, dengan langkah sejauh satu pos perjalanan dan kepala sebesar takaran gandum; mereka bisa mengobrol dari satu gunung ke gunung lain dan mampu berpegangan pada pegangan langit.
statement.en: The uriași are figures of myth or fairy tale with human faces, huge, brawny and strong, several fathoms tall, with a stride as long as a post-stage and heads as big as a grain measure; they can chat from one mountain to another and can grab the handles of the sky.

claims.quote: Uneori sunt descriși ca ciclopi, cu un singur ochi în frunte și hrănindu-se cu carne de om.

statement.id: Kadang mereka digambarkan sebagai kiklops bermata satu di dahi yang memakan daging manusia.
statement.en: Sometimes they are described as cyclopes with a single eye in the forehead, feeding on human flesh.

claims.quote: De asemenea, e frecvent tipul de poveste în care copilul de Uriaș care aduce acasă în palmă (sau poală) un om cu plugul cu boi, ca pe niște jucării, iar părinții îi explică divinatoriu pieirea propriei stirpe și înlocuirea ei cu ființe mărunte. În unele zone din Oltenia și Transilvania Uriașii se mai numesc și Jidovi sau Novaci.

statement.id: Sering ada kisah anak uriaș yang membawa pulang seorang manusia beserta bajak dan lembunya di telapak tangan seperti mainan, lalu orang tuanya meramalkan punahnya bangsa mereka yang akan digantikan makhluk-makhluk kecil; di beberapa daerah Oltenia dan Transilvania, uriaș juga disebut Jidovi atau Novaci.
statement.en: A common tale tells of an uriaș child who brings home a man with his plough and oxen in his palm like toys, and the parents prophetically explain the passing of their own kind and its replacement by tiny beings; in parts of Oltenia and Transylvania the uriași are also called Jidovi or Novaci.

claims.quote: Uriașii sunt cunoscuți și ca giganți care ar fi construit cetățile preistorice și movilele de pământ.

statement.id: Uriaș juga dikenal sebagai raksasa yang konon membangun benteng-benteng prasejarah dan gundukan tanah.
statement.en: The uriași are also known as giants said to have built prehistoric forts and earth mounds.

claims.quote: În ținuturile extracarpatice movilele puse pe seama Uriașilor, care ar fi cărat pământul cu poala, sunt de origine antropomorfă, tumuli funerari din Epocile Bronzului și Fierului.

statement.id: Di daerah di luar Karpatia, gundukan yang dikaitkan dengan uriaș, yang konon mengangkut tanah dengan pangkuannya, sebenarnya buatan manusia, yaitu tumulus pemakaman dari Zaman Perunggu dan Besi.
statement.en: In the lands beyond the Carpathians, the mounds attributed to the uriași, said to have carried earth in their laps, are man-made, burial tumuli of the Bronze and Iron Ages.

short_description.id: Xana adalah peri air yang sangat cantik dari mitologi Asturias yang tinggal di mata air dan gua, menjanjikan harta, bernyanyi pada malam musim panas, dan menukar bayi manusia dengan anaknya.
short_description.en: The xana is a beautiful water fairy of Asturian mythology who lives in springs and caves, promises treasure, sings on summer nights and swaps human babies for her own.

long_description.id: Xana adalah peri perempuan yang luar biasa cantik dari mitologi Asturias, tinggal di mata air, sungai, air terjun, dan gua; namanya mungkin dari nama dewi Diana. Ia pirang dan menyisir rambutnya dengan sisir emas di tepi sungai, mandi di mata air saat pagi, menjanjikan harta, dan memberi "air cinta" atau emas kepada yang layak. Suaranya pada malam musim panas menenangkan orang berjiwa murni tetapi membuat gila yang tidak murni.
long_description.en: The xana is an extraordinarily beautiful female fairy of Asturian mythology who lives in springs, rivers, waterfalls and caves; her name may come from the goddess Diana. Blonde, she combs her hair with a golden comb on riverbanks, bathes in her spring in the morning, promises treasure and gives 'love water' or gold to the worthy. Her voice on summer nights calms the pure of soul but maddens the impure.

long_description.id: Karena tidak dapat menyusui, xana menukar bayi manusia dengan anaknya, xanín, yang ketahuan bila kulit telur ditumpuk di dekat perapian. Sebagian xana juga menyerang orang dan mencuri makanan.
long_description.en: Unable to nurse, xanas swap human babies for their own xaninos, who give themselves away when eggshells are stacked by the hearth. Some xanas also attack people and steal food.

who.en: A beautiful water fairy.

role.en: Promises treasure and swaps babies.

famous_for.id: Anak tukaran dan kulit telur.
famous_for.en: The changeling and the eggshells.

claims.quote: The xana (Asturian: /ˈʃana/or [ˈɕa.na]) is a character found in Asturian mythology. Always female, she is a creature of extraordinary beauty believed to live in fountains, rivers, waterfalls, or forested regions with pure water.

statement.id: Xana adalah tokoh mitologi Asturias, selalu perempuan dan luar biasa cantik, yang dipercaya tinggal di mata air, sungai, air terjun, atau hutan berair jernih.
statement.en: The xana is a figure of Asturian mythology, always female and extraordinarily beautiful, believed to live in springs, rivers, waterfalls or forests with pure water.

claims.quote: The origin of the Asturian word xana is unclear, though some scholars see it as a derivation from the Latin name for the goddess Diana. References to where the mythological xanas lived are still common in Asturian toponyms.

statement.id: Asal kata xana tidak jelas, tetapi sebagian sarjana menganggapnya turunan nama Latin dewi Diana, dan tempat tinggal xana masih banyak terekam dalam nama tempat di Asturias.
statement.en: The origin of xana is unclear, though some scholars derive it from the Latin name of the goddess Diana, and the xanas' homes are still common in Asturian place names.

claims.quote: The xanas promise treasures and can be disenchanted. Some xanas also attack people and steal their food. They live in fountains and caves.

statement.id: Xana menjanjikan harta dan dapat dibebaskan dari sihir, sebagian juga menyerang orang dan mencuri makanan, dan mereka tinggal di mata air dan gua.
statement.en: Xanas promise treasure and can be disenchanted; some also attack people and steal food, and they live in springs and caves.

claims.quote: A xana can be a beneficial spirit, offering "love water" to travellers and rewards of gold or silver to those found worthy through some undefined judgment. Their hypnotic voices can be heard during spring and summer nights.

statement.id: Xana dapat menjadi roh baik yang memberi "air cinta" kepada pelancong dan emas atau perak kepada yang dianggap layak, dan suaranya yang memukau terdengar pada malam musim semi dan musim panas.
statement.en: A xana can be kindly, offering 'love water' to travellers and gold or silver to those judged worthy, and her hypnotic voice is heard on spring and summer nights.

claims.quote: Those who have a pure soul and hear the song will be filled with a sense of peace and love. Those whose souls are not pure will feel they are being suffocated and may be driven insane.

statement.id: Orang berjiwa murni yang mendengar nyanyiannya dipenuhi damai dan cinta, sedangkan yang tidak murni merasa tercekik dan bisa menjadi gila.
statement.en: The pure of soul who hear her song are filled with peace and love, while the impure feel smothered and may go mad.

claims.quote: Xanas have children called xaninos (singular: xanín), but because they cannot take care of them—xanas cannot produce milk to feed their babies—they usually take a human baby from his cradle and put their own fairy child in instead, similar to changelings in other cultures.

statement.id: Xana memiliki anak bernama xaninos, tetapi karena tidak dapat menyusui, mereka biasanya menukar bayi manusia di buaian dengan anak peri mereka, mirip changeling di budaya lain.
statement.en: Xanas have children called xaninos, but since they cannot make milk they usually swap a human baby in its cradle for their own fairy child, like changelings elsewhere.

claims.quote: Die Xana erscheint als schöne junge Frau, die morgens aus einer Gebirgshöhle kommend zu ihrer Quelle wandert, um sich im eiskalten Wasser zu baden. Nach mündlicher Überlieferung aus den Picos de Europa gehen Wünsche, die in diesen Moment an ihr Ohr dringen, in Erfüllung.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, xana tampak sebagai perempuan muda cantik yang pagi-pagi keluar dari gua gunung untuk mandi di mata airnya yang dingin, dan menurut tradisi lisan Picos de Europa keinginan yang ia dengar saat itu akan terkabul.
statement.en: According to the German article, the xana appears as a beautiful young woman who leaves her mountain cave in the morning to bathe in her ice-cold spring, and by oral tradition of the Picos de Europa wishes she hears then come true.

claims.quote: Nur durch das Stapeln von Eierschalen neben dem Herdfeuer verraten sich die ausgetauschten Wechselbälger selbst, weil sie dann überrascht rufen: „Vor hundert Jahren wurde ich geboren, aber so viele Eierschalen beim Feuer habe ich noch nie gesehen!“.

statement.id: Anak tukaran hanya ketahuan bila kulit telur ditumpuk di dekat perapian, karena ia akan berseru heran, "Seratus tahun lalu aku lahir, tetapi belum pernah melihat kulit telur sebanyak ini di dekat api!"
statement.en: A changeling betrays itself only when eggshells are stacked by the hearth, for it cries in surprise, 'I was born a hundred years ago, but I have never seen so many eggshells by the fire!'

claims.quote: Elles se présentent comme des filles jeunes et très belles, de caractère plutôt nordique, c'est-à-dire blondes et aux yeux clairs. Elles se peignent sur les rives des rivières avec des peignes d'or, attendant des voyageurs pour les séduire.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, mereka tampak sebagai gadis muda yang sangat cantik, pirang dan bermata terang, yang menyisir rambut dengan sisir emas di tepi sungai sambil menunggu pelancong untuk dirayu.
statement.en: According to the French article, they appear as very beautiful young girls, blonde and light-eyed, combing their hair with golden combs on riverbanks while waiting to seduce travellers.

short_description.id: Yallery Brown adalah roh alam jahil mirip peri dalam dongeng Lincolnshire, Inggris: makhluk mungil berkulit cokelat yang dibebaskan dari bawah batu oleh seorang pemuda lalu menjadi pembawa sial bagi pemuda itu.
short_description.en: Yallery Brown is a mischievous fairy-like nature spirit in a Lincolnshire folk tale from England: a tiny brown creature freed from under a stone by a young man who then turns his luck sour.

long_description.id: Yallery Brown adalah roh alam jahil mirip peri dalam dongeng lama Lincolnshire di Inggris. Kisahnya pertama kali dikutip M. C. Balfour pada 1891 dari cerita yang dikumpulkan di Lembah Ancholme, North Lincolnshire, lalu juga dimuat Joseph Jacobs dalam More English Fairy Tales.
long_description.en: The tale of Yallery Brown, a mischievous fairy-like nature spirit, is an old Lincolnshire folk story from England. M. C. Balfour first cited the story in 1891 from tales collected in the Ancholme Valley, North Lincolnshire, and Joseph Jacobs later included it in More English Fairy Tales.

long_description.id: Dalam versi Jacobs, pemuda bernama Tom Tiver mengangkat batu pipih dan menemukan makhluk mungil telentang di lubang. Rambut dan janggutnya panjang dan kusut melilit tubuhnya, dan kulitnya cokelat seperti tanah yang baru dibalik. Ia menyebut dirinya Yallery Brown dan menawarkan bantuan, dengan syarat Tom tak boleh berterima kasih.
long_description.en: In Jacobs's version the lad Tom Tiver lifts a flat stone and finds a tiny creature on its back in the hole. Its hair and beard are long and matted around its body, and its skin is brown like freshly turned earth. He calls himself Yallery Brown and offers help, on condition that Tom must never thank him.

long_description.id: Pekerjaan Tom selesai dengan sendirinya, tetapi pekerjaan rekan-rekannya dirusak dan Tom tidak bisa mengerjakan apa pun sendiri. Yallery Brown hanya terlihat dalam gelap. Ketika Tom akhirnya berterima kasih, makhluk itu menyatakan ia tidak akan membantu lagi dan tidak akan pernah meninggalkan Tom; kesialan menimpa Tom seumur hidupnya.
long_description.en: Tom's work gets done by itself, but his fellows' work is undone and Tom can do nothing on his own. Yallery Brown is seen only in the dark. When Tom finally thanks him, the creature declares he will help no more and will never leave Tom alone; misfortune dogs Tom for life.

literal_meaning.id: Nama yang dipilih makhluk itu sendiri, "karena begitulah sifatku"
literal_meaning.en: A name chosen by the creature himself, "'t is my nature"

who.id: Yallery Brown adalah makhluk mungil berkulit cokelat dalam dongeng Lincolnshire.
who.en: Yallery Brown is a tiny brown-skinned creature in a Lincolnshire folk tale.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari dongeng Lincolnshire di Inggris, dikutip pertama pada 1891.
origin.en: He comes from a Lincolnshire folk tale in England, first cited in 1891.

role.id: Ia membantu seorang pemuda bekerja, lalu menimpakan kesialan padanya setelah diberi terima kasih.
role.en: He helps a young man with his work, then brings him misfortune after being thanked.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal karena larangan berterima kasih dan sajak kutukannya.
famous_for.en: He is known for the ban on thanking him and for his curse rhyme.

description.id: Pekerjaan Tom dikerjakan Yallery Brown, bahkan lebih baik daripada jika Tom mengerjakannya sendiri.
description.en: Tom's work is done by Yallery Brown, even better than Tom could do it himself.

description.id: Setelah dibalas dengan terima kasih, ia menimpakan kesialan seumur hidup pada Tom.
description.en: After being thanked, he brings lifelong misfortune on Tom.

description.id: Dalam versi yang dikumpulkan Balfour, penutur bercerita dengan sudut pandang orang pertama.
description.en: In the version Balfour collected, the teller speaks in the first person.

role.id: Makhluk yang dibebaskan, penolong lalu pembawa sial
role.en: The freed creature, helper turned curse-bringer

summary.id: Tom membebaskan makhluk mungil dari bawah batu; makhluk itu menolongnya bekerja tetapi merusak pekerjaan orang lain, dan setelah Tom berterima kasih ia menimpakan kesialan seumur hidup.
summary.en: Tom frees a tiny creature from under a stone; the creature helps him work but ruins others' work, and after Tom thanks him he brings lifelong misfortune.

description.id: Tempat kisah ini dikumpulkan sebelum diterbitkan pada 1891.

description.en: M. C. Balfour cited the story in a set of tales from the Ancholme Valley.

learning_questions.id: Apa pelajaran moral dongeng tentang membalas budi dan berterima kasih kepada makhluk gaib?
learning_questions.en: What moral does the tale draw about repaying favours and thanking uncanny beings?

statement.en: Its skin was the colour of freshly turned earth in spring, brown as brown could be.

claims.quote: Yallery Brown thou mayst call me, Yallery Brown; 't is my nature seest thou, and as for a name 't will do as any other.

statement.id: Makhluk itu sendiri menyuruh Tom menyebutnya Yallery Brown, "karena begitulah sifatku", dan menyebut nama itu cukup sebagai nama seperti yang lain.
statement.en: The creature himself tells Tom to call him Yallery Brown, "'t is my nature", and says it will do as a name like any other.

claims.quote: I'll help thee and welcome, but if ever thou sayest that to me—if ever thou thankest me, see'st thou, thou 'lt never see me more.

statement.id: Yallery Brown bersedia membantu, tetapi bila Tom pernah berterima kasih kepadanya, Tom tidak akan melihatnya lagi.
statement.en: Yallery Brown agrees to help but warns that if Tom ever thanks him, Tom will never see him more.

claims.quote: And so it went on day after day, all the work done by Yallery Brown, and better done, too, than he could have done it himself.

statement.id: Hari demi hari semua pekerjaan Tom dikerjakan Yallery Brown, bahkan lebih baik daripada jika Tom mengerjakannya sendiri.
statement.en: Day after day all Tom's work was done by Yallery Brown, and better than Tom could have done it himself.

statement.id: Bila pekerjaan Tom dikerjakan, pekerjaan rekan-rekannya dirusak: ember Tom terisi, ember mereka ditumpahkan.
statement.en: If Tom's work was done for him, the other lads' work was undone; his buckets were filled while theirs were upset.

claims.quote: For he never saw Yallery Brown in daylight; only in the darklins he saw him hopping about, like a Will-o-th'-wyke without his lanthorn.

statement.id: Tom tidak pernah melihat Yallery Brown pada siang hari; hanya dalam gelap ia melihatnya melompat-lompat seperti Will-o-th'-wyke tanpa lenteranya.
statement.en: Tom never saw Yallery Brown in daylight; only in the dark did he see him hopping about like a Will-o-th'-wyke without his lantern.

claims.quote: I was nice and safe under the stone, Tom, and could do no harm; but thou let me out thyself, and thou can't put me back again!

statement.id: Setelah Tom berterima kasih, makhluk itu berkata ia dulu aman di bawah batu dan tak bisa mencelakai, tetapi Tom sendiri yang melepaskannya dan tak bisa menyimpannya kembali.
statement.en: After Tom thanks him, the creature says he was safe under the stone and could do no harm, but Tom let him out himself and cannot put him back.

claims.quote: And the children died, and the crops rotted—the beasts never fatted, and nothing ever did well with him

statement.id: Kutukan itu terwujud: anak-anak meninggal, tanaman membusuk, ternak tak pernah gemuk, dan tak ada yang berhasil bagi Tom.
statement.en: The curse came true: the children died, the crops rotted, the beasts never fattened, and nothing ever did well with Tom.

short_description.id: Zhytsen adalah roh ladang gandum hitam dalam mitologi Belarus, kakek kecil bermata tiga yang menjaga panen dan memindahkan bulir yang tertinggal ke ladang petani rajin.
short_description.en: Zhytsen is the rye-field spirit of Belarusian mythology, a little three-eyed old man who guards the harvest and moves leftover grain to diligent farmers' fields.

long_description.id: Zhytsen adalah makhluk baik dalam mitologi Belarus yang tinggal di ladang; namanya berarti "makhluk gandum hitam". Ia disebut roh kekayaan dan kesejahteraan yang membantu tanaman matang dan menjaga panen. Ia dibayangkan sebagai kakek kecil berjanggut panjang, "Kakek Gandum Hitam", dengan mata ketiga di tengkuk.
long_description.en: Zhytsen is a benevolent being of Belarusian mythology that lives in the fields; its name means "rye creature". It is called a spirit of wealth and wellbeing that helps crops ripen and cares for the harvest. It was imagined as a little long-bearded old man, the "Rye Grandfather", with a third eye on the back of its head.

long_description.id: Zhytsen berjalan melintasi ladang memastikan panen dituai dengan baik, dan bulir yang ditinggalkan petani ceroboh ia ikat menjadi berkas lalu bawa ke ladang petani yang lebih rajin. Sosoknya masih muncul dalam ungkapan "Zhytsen memberi roti". Namun sebagai dewa kesuburan Belarus kuno, ia digambarkan dan kemungkinan dikarang oleh folkloris Pavel Shpilevsky.
long_description.en: Zhytsen walks the fields making sure crops are well reaped, and the grain left by careless farmers it binds into sheaves and carries to the fields of more diligent ones. The figure still appears in the saying "Zhytsen gave bread". As an ancient Belarusian fertility god, however, it was described and probably invented by the folklorist Pavel Shpilevsky.

short_description.id: Bai Baianai adalah roh hutan dan hewan dalam kepercayaan Yakut, pelindung para pemburu yang diberi persembahan sebelum dan sesudah berburu.
short_description.en: Bai Baianai is the Yakut spirit of forests and animals, patron of hunters, given offerings before and after the hunt.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan Yakut, Bai Baianai adalah roh hutan dan hewan serta pelindung pemburu, yang juga melindungi anak-anak dan garis keturunan. Pada zaman kuno Baianai dipuja di Altai dan Sakha sebagai dewi Turkik untuk satwa liar, kekayaan, dan kesuburan; namanya berarti "kaya, subur, makmur", dan ia disebut putri Kayra. Dikenal tiga Baianai: Bai Baianai dewi perburuan, Tagh Baianai dewi hutan, dan Ughu Baianai dewi perikanan.
long_description.en: In Yakut belief Bai Baianai is the spirit of forests and animals and patron of hunters, who also protects children and the lineage. In ancient times Baianai was worshipped in Altai and Sakha as the Turkic goddess of wildlife, wealth and fertility; her name means "rich, fertile, wealthy", and she is called the daughter of Kayra. There are three Baianai: Bai Baianai of hunting, Tagh Baianai of forests and Ughu Baianai of fishing.

long_description.id: Pemburu menyalakan api dan berdoa kepadanya, dan persembahan diberikan sebelum berburu, setelah tangkapan besar, atau saat lama tidak berhasil. Satu sumber menggambarkannya bukan sebagai dewi, melainkan lelaki tua riang yang tinggal di hutan dan kaya akan bulu binatang.
long_description.en: Hunters light fires and pray to it, and offerings are made before a hunt, after a big catch or after long bad luck. One source pictures it not as a goddess but as a jolly old man living in the forest, rich in furs.

short_description.id: Black Lady of Bradley Woods adalah hantu yang konon menghantui hutan dekat desa Bradley, Lincolnshire, Inggris, perempuan muda berjubah hitam yang tak pernah mencelakai siapa pun.
short_description.en: The Black Lady of Bradley Woods is a ghost said to haunt the woods near the village of Bradley, Lincolnshire, England, a young woman in a black cloak who has never harmed anyone.

long_description.id: Black Lady of Bradley Woods adalah hantu yang konon menghantui hutan dekat desa Bradley, Lincolnshire, Inggris (England). Para saksi menggambarkannya muda dan cantik, tinggi sekitar 168 cm, berjubah hitam panjang dengan tudung hitam yang menutupi rambutnya tetapi memperlihatkan wajahnya yang pucat, sedih, dan basah air mata. Menurut legenda ia tak pernah mencelakai siapa pun dan hanya pemandangan yang memilukan meski meresahkan. Kisah ini telah diceritakan turun-temurun dan dulu dipakai orang tua untuk menakuti anak-anak: "the black lady will get you!"
long_description.en: The Black Lady of Bradley Woods is a ghost said to haunt the woods near the village of Bradley, Lincolnshire, England. Witnesses describe her as young and pretty, about 168 cm tall, in a flowing black cloak and black hood that hides her hair but shows her pale, mournful, tear-stained face. Legend says she has never harmed anyone and is only a pitiful if unsettling sight. The story has been told for generations and was once used by parents to scare children: 'the black lady will get you!'

long_description.id: Menurut mitosnya, pada masa Perang Mawar (Wars of the Roses) atau Perang Para Baron (Barons' Wars), seorang penebang kayu muda tinggal bersama istri dan bayinya di sebuah pondok di Bradley Woods. Ia pergi berperang, dan setiap hari istrinya menunggu di tepi hutan, hingga pasukan musuh menyeberangi Humber; tiga penunggang kuda memperkosanya dan merampas bayinya. Ia mengembara mencari anak dan suaminya dengan sia-sia, dan setelah kematiannya orang mulai melihatnya berkeliaran di hutan. Menurut artikel sv, kisah ini telah diceritakan selama banyak generasi.
long_description.en: By the legend, during the Wars of the Roses or the Barons' Wars a young woodsman lived with his wife and baby son in a cottage in Bradley Woods. He went to war, and every day his wife waited at the wood's edge, until an enemy army crossed the Humber; three horsemen assaulted her and seized her baby. Grief-stricken, she roamed the wood looking for her son and husband but never found them, and after her death people began to see her roaming there. According to the sv article the story has been told for many generations.

short_description.id: Boginka adalah roh atau iblis perempuan alam liar dalam mitologi pagan Polandia, sering perwujudan kekuatan alam, yang terkenal menukar bayi manusia.
short_description.en: The boginka is a female spirit or demon of wild nature in Polish pagan mythology, often personifying natural forces, known for swapping human babies.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi pagan Polandia, boginki (tunggal boginka) adalah roh atau iblis perempuan alam liar, seperti hutan, ladang, gunung, atau perairan, dan sering merupakan perwujudan kekuatan alam. Kata ini secara harfiah berarti "dewi kecil" dan dapat diterjemahkan sebagai peri atau nimfa. Mereka dibayangkan sebagai nenek tua buruk rupa atau gadis muda cantik, biasanya telanjang, dan umumnya jahat.
long_description.en: In Polish pagan myth the boginki (singular boginka) are female spirits or demons of the wild, of forest, field, mountain or water, often embodying natural forces. The name literally means "little goddess" and may be rendered as fairy or nymph. They were pictured as hideous crones or lovely young girls, usually naked, and were mostly malevolent.

long_description.id: Istilah boginka kemudian dipakai untuk rusałka, vila, dziwożona, mamuna, dan lainnya. Boginki dapat mencuri bayi manusia dan menggantinya dengan anak pengganti yang disebut odmieniec atau podrzutek. Fungsi utama mereka adalah mengejar perempuan yang baru melahirkan dan perempuan hamil serta menculik dan menukar bayi. Di wilayah Orava dan Spiš mereka digambarkan buruk rupa dengan kepala besar, perut buncit, kaki bengkok, dan payudara besar yang disampirkan ke belakang bahu, dan dapat tampil sebagai kucing, anjing, atau katak.
long_description.en: The word boginka came to cover the rusałka, vila, dziwożona, mamuna and others. Boginki can steal a human baby and leave a substitute called odmieniec or podrzutek. Their chief role is to hound new mothers and pregnant women and to steal and swap babies. In Orava and Spiš they are described as ugly, with big heads, swollen bellies, crooked legs and large breasts thrown back over the shoulder, and they can appear as cats, dogs or frogs.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Polandia, perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan, bunuh diri, atau membunuh anaknya menjadi boginka. Mereka tinggal di rawa, danau, sungai, hutan, dan gunung, dan dapat dijumpai di tepi air saat mencuci kain dengan pemukul kayu.
long_description.en: Polish folk belief held that women who died in childbirth, took their own lives or killed their children became boginki. They dwelt in marshes, lakes, rivers, forests and mountains and could be met by the water beating cloth with wooden paddles.

short_description.id: Coblyn adalah makhluk mitos mirip gnome yang konon menghuni tambang dan galian batu di Wales serta permukiman Welsh di Amerika.
short_description.en: The coblyn is a mythical gnome-like being said to haunt the mines and quarries of Wales and Welsh settlements in America.

long_description.id: Coblyn (juga koblyn, jamak coblynau atau coblynod) adalah makhluk mitos mirip gnome yang konon menghuni tambang dan galian batu di Wales serta daerah permukiman Welsh di Amerika. Dalam British Goblins, Wirt Sikes menggambarkan coblynau sebagai peri ramah yang pendek, sangat jelek, sering berpakaian penambang dan membawa perkakas untuk meniru kerja para penambang dengan semangat tetapi sia-sia.
long_description.en: The coblyn (also koblyn, plural coblynau or coblynod) is a mythical being rather like a gnome, believed to frequent mines and quarries in Wales and in places in America settled by the Welsh. In British Goblins Wirt Sikes depicts coblynau as friendly fairies, short and very ugly, often in miners' dress and carrying tools with which they copy the miners' labour eagerly but to no effect.

long_description.id: Seperti Knocker dalam folklor Cornwall, mereka menuntun penambang ke urat bijih terkaya dengan bunyi ketukan; bila tidak dihormati mereka melempar batu yang biasanya tidak berbahaya, dan penambang menganggap mereka pembawa untung. Satu kisah menyebut anak-anak melihat lima belas atau enam belas coblynau berpakaian merah menari Morris di sebuah ladang di Bodfari. Kata Coblyn berkerabat dengan goblin dan tercatat dalam kamus bahasa Welsh dan Inggris karya William Salesbury tahun 1547.
long_description.en: Like the Knockers of Cornish lore, they guide miners to the richest veins of ore with their knocking, throw mostly harmless stones when slighted, and are counted good luck by miners. One account has children watching fifteen or sixteen red-clad coblynau Morris dancing in a field at Bodfari. The word Coblyn is akin to goblin and is listed in William Salesbury's 1547 Welsh-English dictionary.

short_description.id: Habernitsa atau Cornflower Wraith adalah iblis tengah hari dalam mitologi Slavia dari daerah Prudnik, perempuan berbaju biru langit yang menghukum orang yang menginjak gandum.
short_description.en: Habernitsa, the Cornflower Wraith, is a noon demon of Slavic mythology from the Prudnik area, a woman in azure who punishes those who trample the grain.

long_description.id: Habernitsa adalah iblis tengah hari dalam mitologi Slavia yang dikatakan tinggal di sekitar Prudnik, di Silesia; dalam bahasa Polandia ia disebut chabernica. Ia mirip dengan Lady Midday (południca). Biasanya ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda ramping berbaju biru langit dengan bunga cornflower di rambutnya, yang berkeliaran di pematang ladang saat tengah hari.
long_description.en: Habernitsa is a noon demon of Slavic mythology said to live around Prudnik in Silesia; in Polish she is the chabernica. She resembles Lady Midday (południca). She was usually pictured as a slim young woman in azure with cornflowers in her hair, roaming the field edges at midday.

long_description.id: Ia marah kepada orang yang menginjak-injak gandum atau memakai alat tajam. Orang yang dianggapnya pantas dihukum ditidurkan dengan bisikannya, lalu ditimpa sakit kepala, kelumpuhan, atau nyeri punggung bawah; kadang ia menyerang dengan mematahkan lengan, kaki, atau leher korbannya. Untuk menghindari amarahnya, pekerja harus beristirahat saat tengah hari ketika doa Angelus.
long_description.en: Trampling the grain or working with sharp tools roused her anger. Those she judged deserving were lulled to sleep by her whisper and then struck with headache, paralysis or low back pain; sometimes she broke her victims' arms, legs or neck. To avoid her wrath a worker had to rest at midday, at the Angelus.

long_description.id: Kamus dialek Polandia menyebut chabernica sebagai momok untuk menakut-nakuti anak-anak agar tidak masuk ke ladang gandum. Ada juga kisah ketika ia membebaskan seorang gadis kecil yang tersangkut di semak berduri lalu mengantarnya pulang.
long_description.en: A dictionary of Polish dialects describes the chabernica as a bogey used to scare children away from the grain fields. There is also a story in which she freed a little girl caught in thorny brambles and led her home.

cultural_context.id: Menurut kamus dialek Polandia, chabernica dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak-anak agar tidak masuk dan merusak ladang gandum.
cultural_context.en: According to a Polish dialect dictionary, the chabernica was used to frighten children so they would not enter and damage the grain fields.

short_description.id: Cyhyraeth adalah roh hantu dalam mitologi Welsh, suara rintihan tanpa wujud yang terdengar sebelum seseorang meninggal.
short_description.en: The cyhyraeth is a ghostly spirit of Welsh myth, a bodiless groaning voice heard ahead of someone's death.

long_description.id: Cyhyraeth adalah roh hantu dalam mitologi Welsh: suara rintihan tanpa tubuh yang terdengar menjelang kematian seseorang. Legenda mengaitkannya dengan daerah sekitar Sungai Tywi di Dyfed timur dan pesisir Glamorganshire. Suaranya mirip erangan orang sakit parah dan terdengar tiga kali, makin lemah setiap kali, sebagai peringatan sebelum orang itu wafat. Di pesisir Glamorganshire ia terdengar sebelum kapal karam, disertai cahaya mayat (corpse-light).
long_description.en: The cyhyraeth is a ghostly spirit of Welsh mythology, a voice without a body that moans as someone nears death. Legend places it around the River Tywi in eastern Dyfed and along the Glamorganshire coast. It sounds like the groans of a gravely ill person and is heard three times, each fainter than the last, as a warning before the death. On the Glamorganshire coast it is heard ahead of a shipwreck, together with a corpse-light.

long_description.id: Seperti banshee Irlandia dan Cailleach Skotlandia, yang berkerabat dekat dengan cyhyraeth dan Gwrach y Rhibyn, cyhyraeth juga meratap bagi orang Wales yang meninggal jauh dari kampung halaman. Kisahnya kadang dicampuradukkan dengan Gwrach y Rhibyn (Hag of the Mist). Asal namanya tidak jelas: unsur pertama mungkin dari kata Welsh cyhyr (otot, urat, daging) atau dari oer (dingin), dan unsur akhir mungkin kata benda aeth (sakit, duka, takut).
long_description.en: Much like the Irish banshee and the Scottish Cailleach, both close kin to the cyhyraeth and the Gwrach y Rhibyn, it also laments Welsh people who die far from home. Its legend is at times blended with that of the Gwrach y Rhibyn (Hag of the Mist). The name's origin is uncertain: the first part may come from Welsh cyhyr, 'muscle, sinew, flesh', or from oer, 'cold', and the ending may be the noun aeth, 'pain, grief, fear'.

short_description.id: E Bukura e Dheut ("Kecantikan Bumi") adalah julukan dalam mitologi Albania bagi peri yang licik atau, dalam tradisi lain, dewi bumi dan dunia bawah.
short_description.en: E Bukura e Dheut ("Beauty of the Earth") is an Albanian mythological epithet for a crafty fairy or, in other traditions, an earth and underworld goddess.

long_description.id: E Bukura e Dheut, "Kecantikan Bumi", adalah julukan dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania. Dalam sebagian tradisi ia peri yang licik, dalam tradisi lain dewi bumi atau dunia bawah, pasangan e Bukura e Detit (Kecantikan Laut) dan i Bukuri i Qiellit (Kecantikan Langit). Dalam cerita rakyat Albania tengah ia saudari e Bukura e Detit dan istri Baba Tomor.
long_description.en: E Bukura e Dheut, "Beauty of the Earth", is an epithet of Albanian myth and folklore. Some traditions make her a cunning fairy, others a goddess of the earth or underworld, matched with e Bukura e Detit (Beauty of the Sea) and i Bukuri i Qiellit (Beauty of the Sky). Central Albanian lore makes her sister of e Bukura e Detit and wife of Baba Tomor.

long_description.id: Ia adalah kecantikan yang menjelma, bercahaya dengan rambut keemasan. Ia bisa roh baik, tetapi lebih sering jahat, dengan kekuatan sihir yang berasal dari pakaiannya. Ia tinggal di dunia bawah, di istana yang dijaga anjing berkepala tiga, kuçedra, dan berbagai makhluk aneh. Mencari atau menyelamatkannya, bahkan sampai ke istananya di dunia bawah, adalah motif yang sangat populer dalam dongeng Albania.
long_description.en: She is beauty in visible form, shining with golden hair. She can be a kindly spirit but is more often wicked, drawing her magic from her dress. She lives in the underworld in a palace guarded by a three-headed dog, a kuçedra and many strange creatures. A prince's quest to find or rescue her, even in her underground palace, is a favourite motif of Albanian tales.

short_description.id: Moura encantada adalah gadis gaib tersihir dari cerita rakyat Portugal dan Galisia yang menjaga harta, gua, dan mata air sambil menyisir rambutnya dengan sisir emas, menunggu dibebaskan.
short_description.en: The moura encantada is an enchanted magical maiden of Portuguese and Galician folklore who guards treasures, caves and springs, combing her hair with a golden comb as she waits to be freed.

long_description.id: Moura encantada adalah gadis gaib yang sangat cantik dari cerita rakyat Portugal dan Galisia, hidup di bawah kutukan seolah tertidur sampai suatu keadaan mematahkannya. Ia sering bernyanyi sambil menyisir rambut emas atau hitamnya dengan sisir emas. Menurut cerita lama, para moura adalah jiwa gadis yang ditinggalkan menjaga harta para mouros encantados, dan mereka menjaga kastel, gua, jembatan, sumur, dan sungai; mereka pengubah wujud dan pembangun batu yang kuat.
long_description.en: The moura encantada is a very beautiful magical maiden of Portuguese and Galician folklore, living under a spell as if asleep until some circumstance breaks it. She often sings while combing her golden or black hair with a golden comb. By old lore the mouras are souls of maidens left guarding the mouros encantados' treasure, and they guard castles, caves, bridges, wells and rivers; they are shapeshifters and mighty stone-builders.

long_description.id: Leite de Vasconcelos menduga mereka menyerap ciri nimfa dan roh alam, Consiglieri Pedroso menyebut mereka jin air perempuan, dan dongengnya dianggap berasal dari tradisi Kelt pra-Romawi. Nama mouro, pasangan laki-lakinya, menurut Isodoro Millán terkait kata Latin mortuus, "orang mati".
long_description.en: Leite de Vasconcelos thought they absorbed traits of nymphs and nature spirits, Consiglieri Pedroso called them female water genies, and their tales are thought pre-Roman Celtic. The name of their male counterpart, mouro, is linked by Isodoro Millán to Latin mortuus, 'dead'.

who.en: An enchanted magical maiden.

role.en: Guards treasures and thresholds.

famous_for.id: Sisir emas.
famous_for.en: The golden comb.

note.id: Pasangan laki-laki yang menyembunyikan harta.
note.en: The male counterparts who hid the treasure.

claims.quote: The Enchanted moura or moura encantada (enchanted female Mouros) is a supernatural being from the fairy tales of Portuguese and Galician folklore. Very beautiful and seductive, she lives under an imposed occult spell. Shapeshifters, the mouras encantadas occupy liminal spaces and are builders with stone of formidable strength.

statement.id: Moura encantada adalah makhluk gaib dari dongeng Portugal dan Galisia, sangat cantik dan menggoda, hidup di bawah kutukan gaib; mereka pengubah wujud yang menghuni ruang ambang dan pembangun batu yang sangat kuat.
statement.en: The moura encantada is a supernatural being of Portuguese and Galician fairy tales, very beautiful and seductive, living under an occult spell; shapeshifters, they haunt liminal places and are stone-builders of great strength.

claims.quote: Aparecem frequentemente cantando e penteando os seus longos cabelos, louros como o ouro ou negros como a noite, com um pente de ouro

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Portugis, mereka sering muncul bernyanyi sambil menyisir rambut panjangnya yang pirang seperti emas atau hitam seperti malam dengan sisir emas.
statement.en: According to the Portuguese article, they often appear singing and combing their long hair, golden or night-black, with a golden comb.

claims.quote: According to José Leite de Vasconcelos, mouras encantadas are “beings compelled by an occult power to live on a certain state of siege as if they were numb or asleep, insofar as a particular circumstance does not break  their spell".

statement.id: Menurut José Leite de Vasconcelos, mereka makhluk yang dipaksa kekuatan gaib hidup seolah terkurung, kebas atau tertidur, selama suatu keadaan tertentu belum mematahkan kutukannya.
statement.en: According to José Leite de Vasconcelos, they are beings forced by an occult power to live as if besieged, numb or asleep, until some circumstance breaks their spell.

claims.quote: According to ancient lore, they are the souls of young maidens who were left guarding the treasures that the males, mouros encantados (enchanted mouros) hid before heading to Mourama.

statement.id: Menurut cerita lama, mereka jiwa gadis-gadis yang ditinggalkan menjaga harta yang disembunyikan para mouros encantados sebelum pergi ke Mourama.
statement.en: By old lore they are the souls of maidens left guarding the treasures the male mouros encantados hid before leaving for Mourama.

claims.quote: Mouras encantadas are magical maidens who guard castles, caves, bridges, wells, fountains, rivers, and treasures.

statement.id: Mouras encantadas adalah gadis gaib penjaga kastel, gua, jembatan, sumur, mata air, sungai, dan harta.
statement.en: Mouras encantadas are magical maidens who guard castles, caves, bridges, wells, fountains, rivers and treasures.

claims.quote: José Leite de Vasconcelos considered as a possibility that the mouras encantadas may have had assimilated the characteristics of local deities, such as nymphs and spirits of nature. Consiglieri Pedroso also referred to the mouras encantadas as "feminine water genies".

statement.id: Leite de Vasconcelos menduga mereka menyerap ciri dewa setempat seperti nimfa dan roh alam, dan Consiglieri Pedroso menyebut mereka "jin air perempuan".
statement.en: Leite de Vasconcelos thought they may have absorbed the traits of local deities such as nymphs and nature spirits, and Consiglieri Pedroso called them 'feminine water genies'.

claims.quote: The fairy tales featuring mouras encantadas are thought to be of pre-Roman, Indo-European Celtic origin.

statement.id: Dongeng tentang mereka dianggap berasal dari tradisi Kelt Indo-Eropa pra-Romawi.
statement.en: Tales of the mouras encantadas are thought to be of pre-Roman, Indo-European Celtic origin.

claims.quote: Las mouras son criaturas fantásticas feéricas del folclore gallego y del folclore portugués de la península iberica. Su par masculino es el mouro.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, moura adalah makhluk peri dari cerita rakyat Galisia dan Portugal, dengan pasangan laki-laki bernama mouro.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, mouras are fairy beings of Galician and Portuguese folklore, whose male counterpart is the mouro.

claims.quote: La voz latina maurus (de donde el gal. mouro) para el filólogo Isodoro Millán procede del celta mrvos afín al término indoeuropeo mr-tuos, que nos conduce al latín mortuus. De ahí que muchos autores sostengan que los mouros eran razas ya desaparecidas, muertos.

statement.id: Menurut filolog Isodoro Millán, kata mouro (dari bahasa Latin maurus) berasal dari bahasa Kelt mrvos yang terkait istilah Indo-Eropa mr-tuos dan bahasa Latin mortuus, sehingga banyak penulis menganggap mouros ras yang telah punah, orang mati.
statement.en: According to the philologist Isodoro Millán, mouro (from Latin maurus) comes from Celtic mrvos, akin to Indo-European mr-tuos and Latin mortuus, so many authors hold the mouros were vanished races, the dead.

short_description.id: Erlik adalah dewa kematian dan penguasa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Turkik dan Mongol, yang mendatangkan penyakit dan menghakimi orang mati.
short_description.en: Erlik is the god of death and lord of the underworld in Turkic and Mongolian mythology, who sends disease and judges the dead.

long_description.id: Erlik adalah dewa kematian dan dunia bawah dalam mitologi Turkik; dalam bahasa Mongol ia disebut Erleg, dan padanannya dalam mitologi Hungaria adalah Ördög. Ia sudah disebut dalam prasasti Orkhon. Dari istananya di titik terdalam dunia bawah, Erlik mendatangkan kematian, wabah, dan roh jahat, membawa jiwa manusia ke wilayahnya, dan menghakimi orang mati.
long_description.en: Erlik is the god of death and the underworld in Turkic mythology; in Mongolian he is Erleg, and his Hungarian counterpart is Ördög. He is already named in the Orkhon inscriptions. From his castle at the deepest point of the underworld, Erlik sends death, plague and evil spirits, takes human souls to his realm and judges the dead.

long_description.id: Erlik saudara Ülgen, dan keduanya diciptakan oleh Kayra. Ia terlibat dalam penciptaan manusia, membunuh dewa utusan Maidere, mengajarkan dosa, dan kadang dilambangkan dengan beruang. Menurut mitos Altai, ia manusia pertama yang mati karena mencoba mengklaim keilahian, lalu menjadi penguasa alam orang mati.
long_description.en: Erlik is the brother of Ülgen, both created by Kayra. He took part in creating humanity, slew the messenger god Maidere, teaches sin and is sometimes represented by a bear. In Altai myth he was the first human to die, for trying to claim divinity, and became ruler of the dead.

who.en: God of death and the underworld.

role.id: Hakim orang mati dan pembawa penyakit.
role.en: Judge of the dead and bringer of disease.

famous_for.id: Disebut dalam prasasti Orkhon.
famous_for.en: Named in the Orkhon inscriptions.

did_you_know.id: Menurut mitos Altai, Erlik adalah manusia pertama yang mati.
did_you_know.en: In Altai myth, Erlik was the first human to die.

note.id: Saudara Erlik.
note.en: Erlik's brother.

note.id: Dewa yang menciptakan Erlik dan Ülgen.
note.en: The god who created Erlik and Ülgen.

note.id: Padanan dalam mitologi Hungaria.
note.en: His Hungarian counterpart.

claims.quote: is the god of death and the underworld, sometimes referred to as Tamag (hell) in Turkic mythology.

statement.id: Erlik adalah dewa kematian dan dunia bawah dalam mitologi Turkik, yang kadang disebut Tamag (neraka).
statement.en: Erlik is the god of death and the underworld in Turkic mythology, the underworld sometimes called Tamag (hell).

claims.quote: From the underworld, Erlik brings forth death, plague and evil spirits to torment humans and take their souls into his realm.

statement.id: Dari dunia bawah, Erlik mendatangkan kematian, wabah, dan roh jahat untuk menyiksa manusia dan membawa jiwa mereka ke wilayahnya.
statement.en: From the underworld Erlik sends death, plague and evil spirits to torment people and take their souls to his realm.

claims.quote: Erlik has already been mentioned in the Orkhon writings and shows a consistent pattern as the lord of the underworld among Turkic belief systems.

statement.id: Erlik sudah disebut dalam prasasti Orkhon dan secara konsisten menjadi penguasa dunia bawah dalam kepercayaan Turkik.
statement.en: Erlik is already named in the Orkhon inscriptions and consistently appears as lord of the underworld in Turkic belief.

claims.quote: In Mongolian, Erlik is referred to as Erleg or Yerleg, and in Hungarian mythology he is equivalent to Ördög.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Mongol ia disebut Erleg atau Yerleg, dan dalam mitologi Hungaria padanannya adalah Ördög.
statement.en: In Mongolian he is called Erleg or Yerleg, and in Hungarian mythology his equivalent is Ördög.

claims.quote: In Turkic mythology, Erlik was involved in the creation of humanity. He slew the messenger-god, Maidere/Maydere, and is a teacher of sin. He is sometimes represented by a totemic bear.

statement.id: Erlik terlibat dalam penciptaan manusia, membunuh dewa utusan Maidere, dan mengajarkan dosa; kadang ia dilambangkan dengan beruang totem.
statement.en: Erlik took part in the creation of humanity, slew the messenger god Maidere and teaches sin; he is sometimes represented by a totemic bear.

claims.quote: Erlik is a brother of Ülgen, they both have been created from Kayra (Tengere Kayra Khan) the god of it.

statement.id: Erlik saudara Ülgen; keduanya diciptakan oleh Kayra (Tengere Kayra Khan).
statement.en: Erlik is a brother of Ülgen; both were created by Kayra (Tengere Kayra Khan).

claims.quote: Erlik gilt als Ursache von Krankheit und Tod, und als Richter über die Verstorbenen in der Unterwelt. Über jene Unterwelt regierte Erlik in deren tiefstem Punkt in einem Schloss.

statement.id: Erlik dianggap penyebab penyakit dan kematian serta hakim bagi orang mati, yang memerintah dari sebuah istana di titik terdalam dunia bawah.
statement.en: Erlik is held to cause sickness and death and to judge the dead, ruling from a castle at the deepest point of the underworld.

claims.quote: Dem altaischen Mythos zur Folge war Erlik der erste Mensch, der starb, eine Konsequenz seines Versuches, Göttlichkeit für sich zu beanspruchen, und somit in das Totenreich hinabstieg, wo er zu dessen Herrscher wurde.

statement.id: Menurut mitos Altai, Erlik adalah manusia pertama yang mati, akibat usahanya mengklaim keilahian, lalu turun ke alam orang mati dan menjadi penguasanya.
statement.en: In Altai myth Erlik was the first human to die, as a result of trying to claim divinity, and descended to the realm of the dead to become its ruler.

summary.id: Diciptakan Kayra bersama Ülgen.
summary.en: Created by Kayra together with Ülgen.

summary.id: Manusia pertama yang mati (mitos Altai).
summary.en: The first human to die (Altai myth).

short_description.id: Farfadet adalah peri kecil keriput dari cerita rakyat Prancis, terutama Vendée dan Poitou, yang membantu di pertanian dengan imbalan susu.
short_description.en: The farfadet is a small, wrinkled sprite of French folklore, especially of the Vendée and Poitou, who helps on farms in return for milk.

long_description.id: Farfadet adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Prancis, mirip brownie atau pixie, yang khas Vendée dan Poitou dan dikenal sebagai fadet di Provence. Mereka kecil, sekitar setengah meter, keriput, berkulit cokelat, dan berpakaian compang-camping atau telanjang. Namanya dari bahasa Provençal farfadet, bentuk penguat dari fadet, "peri".
long_description.en: The farfadet is a creature of French folklore, akin to the brownie or pixie, belonging especially to the Vendée and Poitou and known in Provence as the fadet. Farfadets are small, about half a metre tall, wrinkled, brown-skinned, and wear rags or nothing. The name comes from Provençal farfadet, an intensified form of fadet, 'fairy'.

long_description.id: Mereka lebih suka menolong daripada jahat: merawat kuda, mengepang surai, dan mengerjakan tugas ladang dengan imbalan semangkuk susu atau krim, tetapi pergi bila diberi pakaian baru. A. V. C. Berbiguier yang merasa disiksa mereka menulis otobiografi tentangnya pada 1821.
long_description.en: They are helpful rather than malicious: tending horses, braiding manes and doing field work for a bowl of milk or cream, but leaving if given new clothes. A. V. C. Berbiguier, who felt tormented by them, wrote an autobiography about it in 1821.

who.en: A small farm sprite.

role.en: Helps in the fields.

description.id: Kebaikan berlebihan membuat mereka pergi.
description.en: Too much kindness drives them away.

modern_depictions.title: Les Farfadets ou Tous les démons ne sont pas de l'autre monde

description.id: Otobiografi Berbiguier tentang siksaan farfadet.
description.en: Berbiguier's autobiography about the farfadets' torments.

claims.quote: Farfadets are creatures of French folklore. The word translates variously as "Sprite", "Imp",  "Brownie", or "Leprechaun", though they also resemble the Pixies of Britain's West Country.

statement.id: Farfadet adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Prancis; katanya dapat diterjemahkan sebagai sprite, imp, brownie, atau leprechaun, dan mereka juga mirip pixie dari West Country Britania.
statement.en: Farfadets are creatures of French folklore; the word is rendered as sprite, imp, brownie or leprechaun, and they also resemble the pixies of Britain's West Country.

claims.quote: The term is in general use throughout France, though the creature is local particularly to the Vendée and Poitou regions. Farfadets also  feature in Occitan mythology, particularly in Provence, where they are known as fadets.

statement.id: Istilah ini dipakai di seluruh Prancis, tetapi makhluknya khas Vendée dan Poitou; farfadet juga ada dalam mitologi Occitania, terutama di Provence, dengan nama fadet.
statement.en: The term is used throughout France, though the creature belongs especially to the Vendée and Poitou; farfadets also appear in Occitan mythology, especially in Provence, as fadets.

claims.quote: Farfadets are described as being small (some half-meter tall), wrinkled, and brown-skinned; they generally wear tattered brown clothing, or go naked.

statement.id: Mereka kecil (sekitar setengah meter), keriput, dan berkulit cokelat, biasanya berpakaian cokelat compang-camping atau telanjang.
statement.en: They are small (about half a metre tall), wrinkled and brown-skinned, usually in tattered brown clothes or naked.

claims.quote: They like to tend horses, which they will groom, or weave ringlets into their manes. They live in woodland, but will also attach themselves to a neighbouring farm or homestead, and complete odd tasks in the fields, in return for a bowl of milk or cream left on the doorstep at night.

statement.id: Mereka suka merawat kuda, menyisir atau mengepang surainya; mereka tinggal di hutan tetapi juga menempel pada pertanian terdekat dan mengerjakan tugas di ladang dengan imbalan semangkuk susu atau krim di depan pintu pada malam hari.
statement.en: They like to tend horses, grooming them or braiding their manes; they live in woods but also attach themselves to a nearby farm, doing odd jobs in the fields for a bowl of milk or cream left on the doorstep at night.

claims.quote: However they can be frightened away by too much kindness, such as leaving new clothes out for them.

statement.id: Namun kebaikan yang berlebihan, seperti meninggalkan pakaian baru untuk mereka, dapat membuat mereka pergi.
statement.en: Yet too much kindness, such as leaving new clothes for them, can frighten them away.

claims.quote: In 1821 he was constrained to publish an autobiography, Les Farfadets ou Tous les démons ne sont pas de l'autre monde

statement.id: Penulis Prancis A. V. C. Berbiguier yang merasa disiksa farfadet menerbitkan otobiografi Les Farfadets ou Tous les démons ne sont pas de l'autre monde pada 1821.
statement.en: The French writer A. V. C. Berbiguier, who believed farfadets tormented him, published the autobiography Les Farfadets ou Tous les démons ne sont pas de l'autre monde in 1821.

claims.quote: Farfadet est un mot emprunté au provençal farfadet (« lutin ») du XVIe siècle, probablement forme renforcée de fadet, dérivé lui-même de fada, fado signifiant « fée ».

statement.id: Kata farfadet dipinjam dari bahasa Provençal farfadet ("lutin") abad ke-16, mungkin bentuk penguat dari fadet, yang berasal dari fada atau fado, "peri".
statement.en: Farfadet is borrowed from 16th-century Provençal farfadet ('sprite'), probably an intensified form of fadet, itself from fada or fado, 'fairy'.
