short_description.id: Fat Lips (Fatlips) adalah roh legendaris yang dikaitkan dengan Dryburgh Abbey di Berwickshire, Skotlandia. Ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki kecil bersepatu besi yang disebut-sebut merapikan ruang bawah tanah tempat tinggal seorang perempuan pengembara.
short_description.en: Fat Lips (Fatlips) is a legendary spirit linked with Dryburgh Abbey in Berwickshire, Scotland. He is described as a little man in iron shoes who was said to keep tidy the vault where a female wanderer lived.

long_description.id: Fat Lips adalah nama roh legendaris yang menghuni Dryburgh Abbey di Berwickshire, Skotlandia. Kisahnya terikat pada seorang perempuan tunawisma yang tinggal di ruang bawah tanah di bawah reruntuhan biara itu beberapa waktu setelah pemberontakan Jacobite 1745.
long_description.en: Fat Lips is the name of a legendary spirit said to dwell in Dryburgh Abbey in Berwickshire, Scotland. His story is bound to a homeless woman who lived in a vault beneath the abbey ruins some time after the 1745 Jacobite rising.

long_description.id: Perempuan itu mengaku bahwa Fatlips adalah lelaki kecil yang merapikan ruangan ketika ia pergi dan menjaga sel tempatnya tinggal tetap kering dengan menginjak lembap dari tanah memakai sepatu besi yang berat. Ia keluar hanya pada malam hari dan tidak pernah meninggalkan ruang bawah tanah itu pada siang hari.
long_description.en: In her account, Fatlips was a small man who put the room in order during her absences and kept her cell dry by pounding the damp out of the ground in heavy iron boots. She came out only at night and never left the vault during the day.

long_description.id: Teks kumpulan cerita rakyat kedua mencatat bahwa orang yang berpengetahuan memandang perempuan itu dengan iba sebagai orang yang terganggu akalnya, sedangkan orang awam memandangnya dengan rasa takut. Cara hidupnya diyakini berasal dari sumpah tidak akan memandang matahari selama kekasihnya pergi; kekasih itu gugur dalam perang saudara 1745–46. Ruang bawah tanah itu masih memakai nama Fatlips, dan hanya sedikit petani sekitar yang berani memasukinya pada malam hari.
long_description.en: The second source, a folk-tale collection, records that the well-informed regarded the woman with compassion as deranged in understanding, while the common people regarded her with terror. Her way of life was believed to come from a vow never to look upon the sun while her lover was away; the lover fell in the civil war of 1745-46. The vault still carries the name Fatlips, and few neighbouring peasants dare enter it by night.

short_description.id: Raksasa (Welsh: cewri) sangat menonjol dalam folklor dan mitologi Welsh, seperti Bendigeidfran, Idris Gawr dan Ysbaddaden Bencawr.
short_description.en: Giants (Welsh cewri) are prominent in Welsh folklore and myth, among them Bendigeidfran, Idris Gawr and Ysbaddaden Bencawr.

long_description.id: Raksasa (Welsh: cewri) sangat menonjol dalam folklor dan mitologi Welsh. Yang paling terkenal antara lain Bendigeidfran fab Llyr, raja mitologis Britania dalam Cabang Kedua Mabinogi; Idris Gawr dari Cader Idris; dan Ysbaddaden Bencawr, lawan utama dalam kisah Arthur awal How Culhwch won Olwen. Arthur dan Gwalchmai fab Gwyar menonjol sebagai pembunuh raksasa dalam tradisi Welsh, dan Geoffrey dari Monmouth menggambarkan raksasa sebagai penghuni asli Britania yang dikalahkan pemukim manusia.
long_description.en: Giants (Welsh cewri) loom large in Welsh folklore and mythology. Famous examples include Bendigeidfran fab Llyr, who rules Britain as a mythic king in the Mabinogi's Second Branch; Idris Gawr, linked with Cader Idris; and Ysbaddaden Bencawr, chief villain of the early Arthurian tale How Culhwch won Olwen. Arthur and Gwalchmai fab Gwyar both stand out as giant-killers in Welsh tradition, and Geoffrey of Monmouth calls giants the first inhabitants of Britain, overrun by human settlers.

long_description.id: Dalam Branwen ferch Llyr, Britania diperintah raksasa Bran the Blessed yang tak pernah muat di rumah mana pun, dan Pair Dadeni (kuali kelahiran kembali) dibawa ke Wales dari Irlandia oleh raksasa Llassar Llaes Gyfnewid. Dalam Culhwch and Olwen, Ysbaddaden, ayah Olwen, dibunuh keponakannya Goreu fab Custennin. Kisah terkenal lain menyebut Rhitta Gawr yang memakai jubah dari janggut raja-raja dan menuntut janggut Arthur.
long_description.en: In Branwen ferch Llyr the king of Britain is the giant Bran the Blessed, too large ever to fit inside a house, and the Pair Dadeni (Cauldron of Rebirth) is brought from Ireland to Wales by the giant Llassar Llaes Gyfnewid. In Culhwch and Olwen, Ysbaddaden, Olwen's father, is killed by his nephew Goreu fab Custennin. Another well-known tale tells of Rhitta Gawr, who wore a cloak of kings' beards and demanded Arthur's.

short_description.id: Gwyllion adalah peri perempuan berwujud menakutkan dalam cerita rakyat Wales yang menghantui jalan sepi di pegunungan dan menyesatkan pengelana.
short_description.en: The Gwyllion are female fairies of frightful aspect in Welsh folklore who haunt lonely mountain roads and lead travellers astray.

long_description.id: Menurut Wirt Sikes, gwyllion adalah peri perempuan berwujud menakutkan yang menghantui jalan sepi di pegunungan Wales dan menyesatkan pengelana. Mereka dilukiskan sebagai roh muram yang lebih mirip hag atau penyihir, berbeda dari ellyllon yang lebih baik hati. Siapa pun yang bertemu mereka, pada malam hari atau hari berkabut, pasti tersesat.
long_description.en: Wirt Sikes describes the gwyllion as frightening female fairies that haunt isolated Welsh mountain roads and mislead wayfarers. They are portrayed as gloomy spirits more akin to hags or witches than the more benevolent ellyllon. Anyone who meets them, by night or on a misty day, is sure to lose the way.

long_description.id: Satu gwyll yang paling dikenal ialah Old Woman of the Mountain, yang menghantui Gunung Llanhyddel di Monmouthshire dan dianggap mewakili seluruh jenisnya. Tradisi setempat menyebutnya arwah seorang Juan White yang dianggap penyihir.
long_description.en: The best-known gwyll is the Old Woman of the Mountain, said to have haunted the Llanhyddel Mountain of Monmouthshire and said to typify all her kind. Local tradition held her to be the spirit of a Juan White who was thought to be a witch.

long_description.id: Menurut Jones, di Aberystruth Gwyllion sering masuk ke rumah penduduk saat badai. Mereka disambut dengan air bersih dan penghuni memastikan tidak ada pisau di sudut dekat api, karena orang takut dicelakai bila mereka tersinggung. Di luar rumah, pisau yang dihunus dipercaya dapat mengusir mereka.
long_description.en: According to Jones, at Aberystruth the Gwyllion often entered people's houses in stormy weather. They were welcomed with clean water and no knife was left in the corner near the fire, because people feared harm if the fairies were offended. Outdoors, a drawn knife was believed to drive them off.

short_description.id: Hinzelmann adalah kobold dalam mitologi Jerman utara, roh rumah tangga yang sifatnya mendua, yang menurut legenda menghantui Kastel Hudemühlen di Niedersachsen sejak 1584.
short_description.en: Hinzelmann was a kobold of northern German mythology, an ambivalent household spirit who by legend haunted Hudemühlen Castle in Lower Saxony from 1584.

long_description.id: Hinzelmann (aslinya Hintzelmann, juga Katermann atau Katzen-Veit) adalah kobold dalam mitologi Jerman utara, roh rumah tangga bersifat mendua yang mirip Puck (Robin Goodfellow). Para sarjana modern menganggapnya berbeda dari Heinzelmännchen di Köln yang namanya mirip. Jacob Grimm mengaitkan kelompok nama ini dengan kucing, karena Hinz adalah nama kucing dalam Reineke Fuchs.
long_description.en: Hinzelmann (originally Hintzelmann, also Katermann or Katzen-Veit) was a kobold of northern German mythology, an ambivalent household spirit similar to Puck (Robin Goodfellow). Modern scholars hold him distinct from the similarly named Heinzelmännchen of Cologne. Jacob Grimm linked this group of names to the cat, since Hinz was the cat's name in Reineke Fuchs.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, ia mulai menghantui Kastel Hudemühlen di Niedersachsen pada 1584. Mula-mula hanya terdengar bunyi gedoran, lalu ia mulai berbicara dengan para pelayan dan mengaku bernama Lüring, beristri Hille Bingels, dan dulu tinggal di pegunungan Hutan Bohemia. Ia tampil tanpa wujud dengan suara anak kecil.
long_description.en: According to the legend he began haunting Hudemühlen Castle in Lower Saxony in 1584. At first there were only banging noises; then he began talking with the servants, saying he was called Lüring, had a wife named Hille Bingels and used to live in the Bohemian Forest mountains. He appeared without a body and with a child's voice.

long_description.id: Ia rajin mencuci piring, menggosok perkakas dapur, menemukan barang hilang, dan merawat kuda, tetapi bisa memukul dengan tongkat bila nasihatnya diabaikan; para pelayan wajib menyiapkan semangkuk susu manis berisi remah roti putih untuknya. Ia penipu yang keisengannya umumnya tak berbahaya, dan pernah meramalkan kematian seorang tamu yang mengejeknya. Pada 1588 ia pergi dengan sukarela dan menetap di Eystrup.
long_description.en: He diligently washed dishes, scrubbed cookware, found lost things and groomed horses, yet could strike with a stick when his advice was ignored; the servants had to set out a bowl of sweet milk with crumbled white bread for him. He was a trickster whose pranks were mostly harmless, and once foretold the death of a visitor who mocked him. In 1588 he left of his own accord and settled in Eystrup.

short_description.id: Ileana Cosânzeana adalah tokoh mitologi Rumania, putri jelita dan baik hati atau peri yang sangat sakti.
short_description.en: Ileana Cosânzeana is a figure of Romanian mythology, a beautiful, kind princess or a fairy of immense power.

long_description.id: Ileana Cosânzeana adalah tokoh dalam mitologi Rumania. Ia digambarkan sebagai putri yang cantik dan baik hati, putri seorang kaisar, atau sebagai peri yang sangat sakti. Menurut Nina Cuciuc namanya juga ditulis Cosînzeana, Sânziana, atau Ileana Cosînzeana Sora Soarelui, "Saudari Matahari", dan ia juga disebut "Ratu Bunga".
long_description.en: Ileana Cosânzeana is a character of Romanian myth, shown as a lovely, kind-hearted princess, an emperor's daughter, or as a fairy of great power. Nina Cuciuc lists spellings such as Cosînzeana, Sânziana and Ileana Cosînzeana Sora Soarelui, "Sister of the Sun", and she is also called "Queen of Flowers".

long_description.id: Menurut Adela Ileana Draucean, nama Ileana berasal dari Elena, sedangkan cosânzeana berkaitan dengan sânziană, hari raya Rumania sekaligus sebutan lain bagi peri. Ahli bahasa Sorin Paliga mencatat nama lain seperti Floarea Florilor ("Bunga segala Bunga") dan Frumoasa lumii ("Kecantikan Dunia"), dan Lazar Saineanu menerjemahkan namanya ke bahasa Prancis sebagai Hélène aux cheveux d'or, "Helena Berambut Emas".
long_description.en: Adela Ileana Draucean derives Ileana from Elena and links cosânzeana to sânziană, a Romanian holiday and another word for fairies. The linguist Sorin Paliga lists other names such as Floarea Florilor ("the Flower of Flowers") and Frumoasa lumii ("the Beauty of the World"), and Lazar Saineanu rendered her name in French as Hélène aux cheveux d'or, "Helen with Golden Hair".

short_description.id: Joint-eater atau Alp-luachra adalah peri dalam tradisi Kelt yang tanpa terlihat menghabiskan sari makanan korbannya, sehingga korban tetap kurus walau makan banyak.
short_description.en: The joint-eater or Alp-luachra is a fairy of Celtic tradition that invisibly consumes the goodness of its victim's food, so the victim stays thin however much he eats.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Kelt, joint-eater, just-halver, atau Alp-luachra di Irlandia adalah sejenis peri yang duduk tanpa terlihat dan memakan separuh makanan korbannya. Menurut satu versi, ia muncul dalam wujud kadal air ketika seseorang tertidur di tepi mata air atau sungai kecil, lalu merayap masuk lewat mulut dan hidup dari makanan yang ditelan orang itu. Orang yang dihantuinya tidak pernah gemuk, dan orang yang menelan kadal air dipercaya terkena gangguan ini.
long_description.en: In Celtic mythology the joint-eater, just-halver, or in Ireland the Alp-luachra, is a kind of fairy that sits unseen and eats half of its victim's food. In one version it appears as a newt when someone falls asleep beside a spring or stream, crawls in through the mouth and lives off what the person eats. Its victim never grows fat, and people who swallow newts are thought to suffer this way.

long_description.id: Robert Kirk dalam The Secret Commonwealth menulis bahwa orang yang sangat rakus disertai elf rakus bernama Joint-eater atau Just-halver, yang memakan sari dari makanan orang itu sehingga ia tetap kurus seperti elang atau bangau. Andrew Lang dalam pengantar edisi 1893 menjelaskan bahwa orang Highlanders memakai makhluk semacam ini untuk menerangkan nafsu makan yang tidak wajar.
long_description.en: Robert Kirk in The Secret Commonwealth wrote that a great eater is attended by a voracious elf called a Joint-eater or Just-halver, which feeds on the pith or quintessence of his food so that he stays lean like a hawk or heron. In his introduction to the 1893 edition Andrew Lang explains that the Highlanders used such a being to account for a false or morbid appetite.

long_description.id: Kisah "The Alp-Luachra", yang dicatat Hyde dari tuturan penjaga hewan buruan Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart) di barony Frenchpark, menceritakan seorang petani kaya di Connacht yang makin kurus setelah menelan makhluk ini. Ia akhirnya disembuhkan dengan makan banyak daging sapi asin tanpa minum, lalu berbaring dengan mulut terbuka di atas aliran air, hingga anak-anak makhluk itu dan kemudian induknya melompat keluar ke air karena haus.
long_description.en: The tale "The Alp-Luachra", which Hyde recorded from the telling of the Frenchpark game-keeper Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart), tells of a wealthy farmer in Connacht who wasted away after swallowing the creature. He was finally cured by eating much salted beef without drinking and lying with his mouth open over a stream, until the creature's young and then the mother jumped out into the water from thirst.

cultural_context.id: Menurut Andrew Lang, orang Highlanders memakai makhluk ini untuk menjelaskan nafsu makan yang tidak wajar pada orang sakit.
cultural_context.en: According to Andrew Lang, the Highlanders used this being to explain a false or morbid appetite in a patient.

origin.id: Ia dikenal dalam mitologi Kelt, dengan nama Alp-luachra di Irlandia.
origin.en: It is known in Celtic mythology, called Alp-luachra in Ireland.

role.id: Ia menjelaskan mengapa seseorang tetap kurus walau makan banyak.
role.en: It explains why someone stays thin despite eating a great deal.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal karena dapat diusir dengan daging sapi asin dan aliran air.
famous_for.en: It is known for being driven out with salt beef and a running stream.

did_you_know.id: Dalam kisah Hyde, yang keluar dari mulut si petani adalah selusin anak makhluk itu sebelum induknya akhirnya muncul.
did_you_know.en: In Hyde's tale a dozen young creatures came out of the farmer's mouth before the mother finally appeared.

description.id: Ia duduk tanpa terlihat sambil memakan makanan korban.
description.en: It sits invisibly while consuming the victim's food.

description.id: Alp-luachra muncul dalam wujud kadal air untuk masuk lewat mulut orang yang tidur.
description.en: The Alp-luachra appears as a newt to crawl into a sleeper's mouth.

description.id: Setelah korban makan daging sapi asin tanpa minum, makhluk itu kehausan dan melompat ke aliran air.
description.en: After the victim eats salt beef without drinking, the creature grows thirsty and jumps into the stream.

role.id: Makhluk yang bersarang di perut petani
role.en: The creature lodged in the farmer's stomach

summary.id: Seorang petani kaya di Connacht makin kurus setelah menelan alt-pluachra; ia diobati dengan daging sapi asin lalu berbaring di atas aliran air sampai selusin anak dan induknya keluar.
summary.en: A wealthy farmer in Connacht wastes away after swallowing an alt-pluachra; he is treated with salt beef and lies over a stream until a dozen young and their mother come out.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa masyarakat dulu memakai makhluk gaib untuk menjelaskan penyakit?
learning_questions.en: Why did people once use supernatural beings to explain illness?

claims.quote: In Celtic mythology, a Joint-eater, Just-halver or Alp-luachra (Ireland) is a type of fairy who sits invisibly and consumes half of their victim's food.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Kelt, Joint-eater, Just-halver, atau Alp-luachra (Irlandia/Ireland) adalah sejenis peri yang duduk tanpa terlihat dan memakan separuh makanan korbannya.
statement.en: In Celtic mythology a Joint-eater, Just-halver or Alp-luachra (Ireland) is a type of fairy that sits invisibly and consumes half of its victim's food.

claims.quote: When a person falls asleep by the side of a spring or stream, the Alp-luachra appears in the form of a newt and crawls down the person's mouth, feeding off the food that they had eaten.

statement.id: Ketika seseorang tertidur di tepi mata air atau sungai kecil, Alp-luachra muncul dalam wujud kadal air (newt) dan merayap masuk lewat mulutnya, lalu memakan makanan yang telah dimakan orang itu.
statement.en: When a person falls asleep beside a spring or stream, the Alp-luachra appears as a newt and crawls down the person's mouth, feeding off the food they have eaten.

claims.quote: A man haunted by a joint-eater will never grow fat, because the pith or quintessence of the food is consumed by the fairy. ... People who consume newts are thought to be plagued in this way.

statement.id: Orang yang dihantui joint-eater tidak akan pernah gemuk karena sari makanan (pith or quintessence) dihabiskan peri itu; orang yang menelan kadal air (newt) dipercaya terkena gangguan ini.
statement.en: A man haunted by a joint-eater never grows fat, because the fairy consumes the pith or quintessence of his food; people who consume newts are thought to be plagued this way.

claims.quote: to rid one's self of an Alp-Luachra, one should eat a large quantity of salt beef, without drinking anything, and then lie by a running stream with their mouth wide open

statement.id: Untuk menyingkirkan Alp-luachra, orang harus makan banyak daging sapi asin tanpa minum, lalu berbaring di tepi aliran air dengan mulut terbuka lebar.
statement.en: To rid oneself of an Alp-luachra one should eat a large quantity of salt beef without drinking, then lie by a running stream with the mouth wide open.

claims.quote: after a long wait, the Alp-Luachra will become thirsty, and will jump into the stream to drink.

statement.id: Setelah lama menunggu, Alp-luachra akan kehausan dan melompat ke sungai untuk minum.
statement.en: After a long wait the Alp-luachra becomes thirsty and jumps into the stream to drink.

claims.quote: They avouch that a Heluo, or Great-eater, hath a voracious Elve to be his attender, called a Joint-eater or Just-halver, feeding on the Pith or Quintessence of what the Man eats; and that therefoir he continues Lean like a Hawke or Heron, notwith standing his devouring Appetite
claims.locator: Secret Commonwealth, section on the subterraneans

statement.id: Menurut Kirk, orang yang rakus (Heluo, Great-eater) disertai elf rakus bernama Joint-eater atau Just-halver yang memakan sari (Pith or Quintessence) dari apa yang dimakan orang itu, sehingga ia tetap kurus seperti elang atau bangau meski nafsu makannya besar.
statement.en: Kirk says a Heluo or Great-eater has a voracious elf attending him, called a Joint-eater or Just-halver, feeding on the Pith or Quintessence of what the man eats, so that he stays lean like a hawk or heron despite his devouring appetite.

claims.quote: By an airy being of this kind the Highlanders explained the false or morbid appetite. A “joint-eater” inhabited the patient; “he feeds two when he eats.”

statement.id: Dengan makhluk halus semacam ini orang Highlanders menjelaskan nafsu makan yang tidak wajar: seekor joint-eater mendiami si sakit, sehingga "ia memberi makan dua ketika ia makan".
statement.en: With an airy being of this kind the Highlanders explained false or morbid appetite: a joint-eater inhabited the patient, so that "he feeds two when he eats".

claims.quote: Any place in Ireland that this herb grows, there be’s an alt-pluachra near it, and you have swallowed an alt-pluachra.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Hyde, seorang pengemis berkata bahwa di mana pun di Irlandia (Ireland) ramuan itu tumbuh, ada alt-pluachra di dekatnya, dan si sakit telah menelan seekor alt-pluachra.
statement.en: In Hyde's tale a beggarman says that anywhere in Ireland this herb grows there is an alt-pluachra near it, and that the sick man has swallowed one.

claims.quote: that’s the reason you’re keeping so thin, for every bit you’re eating the alt-pluachra is getting the good out of it

statement.id: Karena itulah si sakit tetap kurus: setiap suap yang dimakannya, sarinya diambil alt-pluachra.
statement.en: That is why the sick man keeps so thin: of every bit he eats, the alt-pluachra gets the good out of it.

claims.quote: There was once a wealthy farmer in Connacht, and he had plenty of substance and a fine family

statement.id: Kisah itu dibuka dengan seorang petani kaya di Connacht yang berharta banyak dan berkeluarga baik.
statement.en: The tale opens with a wealthy farmer in Connacht who had plenty of substance and a fine family.

claims.quote: “Now the thirst’s coming on them; the salt that was in the beef is working them; now they’ll come out.”

statement.id: Sang pangeran berbisik bahwa rasa haus mulai menyerang mereka karena garam dalam daging sapi, sehingga mereka akan keluar.
statement.en: The prince whispers that thirst is coming on them because of the salt in the beef, so they will come out.

claims.quote: “There’s a dozen of them now,” said the prince; “that’s the clutch; the old mother didn’t come yet.”

statement.id: Sang pangeran menghitung selusin anak alt-pluachra keluar, sementara induknya belum muncul.
statement.en: The prince counts a dozen of them, the clutch, while the old mother has not yet come out.

claims.quote: The story of “The Alp-luachra” is written down from notes made at the time I first heard the story. It was told me by Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart), a game-keeper, in the barony of Frenchpark

statement.id: Hyde mencatat kisah "The Alp-luachra" dari catatan saat pertama mendengarnya; kisah itu dituturkan oleh Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart), penjaga hewan buruan di barony Frenchpark.
statement.en: Hyde wrote down "The Alp-luachra" from notes made when he first heard it; it was told by Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart), a game-keeper in the barony of Frenchpark.

claims.quote: This book was published in 1893 and is a careful reproduction of a book printed in 1815 from a manuscript of 1691 by Rev. Robert Kirk. An Introduction and Notes have been added by Andrew Lang for the 1893 publication.

statement.id: Buku ini terbit pada 1893 dan mereproduksi cetakan 1815 dari naskah 1691 karya Pdt. Robert Kirk; pengantar dan catatan (Introduction and Notes) ditambahkan oleh Andrew Lang untuk edisi 1893.
statement.en: The book, published in 1893, reproduces an 1815 printing of Rev. Robert Kirk's 1691 manuscript; an Introduction and Notes were added by Andrew Lang for the 1893 edition.

claims.quote: The Rev. Robert Kirk, the author of The Secret Commonwealth, was a student of theology at St. Andrews

statement.id: Pdt. Robert Kirk, penulis The Secret Commonwealth, pernah belajar teologi di St. Andrews.
statement.en: The Rev. Robert Kirk, author of The Secret Commonwealth, studied theology at St. Andrews.

short_description.id: Joint-eater atau Alp-luachra adalah peri dalam tradisi Kelt yang tanpa terlihat menghabiskan sari makanan korbannya, sehingga korban tetap kurus walau makan banyak.
short_description.en: The joint-eater or Alp-luachra is a fairy of Celtic tradition that invisibly consumes the goodness of its victim's food, so the victim stays thin however much he eats.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Kelt, joint-eater, just-halver, atau Alp-luachra di Irlandia adalah sejenis peri yang duduk tanpa terlihat dan memakan separuh makanan korbannya. Menurut satu versi, ia muncul dalam wujud kadal air ketika seseorang tertidur di tepi mata air atau sungai kecil, lalu merayap masuk lewat mulut dan hidup dari makanan yang ditelan orang itu. Orang yang dihantuinya tidak pernah gemuk, dan orang yang menelan kadal air dipercaya terkena gangguan ini.
long_description.en: In Celtic mythology the joint-eater, just-halver, or in Ireland the Alp-luachra, is a kind of fairy that sits unseen and eats half of its victim's food. In one version it appears as a newt when someone falls asleep beside a spring or stream, crawls in through the mouth and lives off what the person eats. Its victim never grows fat, and people who swallow newts are thought to suffer this way.

long_description.id: Robert Kirk dalam The Secret Commonwealth menulis bahwa orang yang sangat rakus disertai elf rakus bernama Joint-eater atau Just-halver, yang memakan sari dari makanan orang itu sehingga ia tetap kurus seperti elang atau bangau. Andrew Lang dalam pengantar edisi 1893 menjelaskan bahwa orang Highlanders memakai makhluk semacam ini untuk menerangkan nafsu makan yang tidak wajar.
long_description.en: Robert Kirk in The Secret Commonwealth wrote that a great eater is attended by a voracious elf called a Joint-eater or Just-halver, which feeds on the pith or quintessence of his food so that he stays lean like a hawk or heron. In his introduction to the 1893 edition Andrew Lang explains that the Highlanders used such a being to account for a false or morbid appetite.

long_description.id: Kisah "The Alp-Luachra", yang dicatat Hyde dari tuturan penjaga hewan buruan Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart) di barony Frenchpark, menceritakan seorang petani kaya di Connacht yang makin kurus setelah menelan makhluk ini. Ia akhirnya disembuhkan dengan makan banyak daging sapi asin tanpa minum, lalu berbaring dengan mulut terbuka di atas aliran air, hingga anak-anak makhluk itu dan kemudian induknya melompat keluar ke air karena haus.
long_description.en: The tale "The Alp-Luachra", which Hyde recorded from the telling of the Frenchpark game-keeper Seamus o h-Airt (James Hart), tells of a wealthy farmer in Connacht who wasted away after swallowing the creature. He was finally cured by eating much salted beef without drinking and lying with his mouth open over a stream, until the creature's young and then the mother jumped out into the water from thirst.

cultural_context.id: Menurut Andrew Lang, orang Highlanders memakai makhluk ini untuk menjelaskan nafsu makan yang tidak wajar pada orang sakit.
cultural_context.en: According to Andrew Lang, the Highlanders used this being to explain a false or morbid appetite in a patient.

short_description.id: Hantu Lincoln adalah arwah Presiden Abraham Lincoln yang konon menghantui Gedung Putih sejak ia dibunuh pada 1865.
short_description.en: Lincoln's ghost is the spirit of President Abraham Lincoln, said to have haunted the White House since his assassination in 1865.

long_description.id: Hantu Presiden Abraham Lincoln, juga disebut Hantu Gedung Putih, konon menghantui Gedung Putih sejak Lincoln dibunuh pada 1865, dan juga bekas kediamannya di Springfield, Illinois. Di antara yang disebut pernah melihatnya adalah Grace Coolidge, Ratu Wilhelmina, Winston Churchill, dan Theodore Roosevelt.
long_description.en: Abraham Lincoln's ghost, nicknamed the White House Ghost, has reportedly roamed the presidential residence ever since he was assassinated in 1865, and his former homes in Springfield, Illinois, as well. Those said to have seen it include Grace Coolidge, Queen Wilhelmina, Winston Churchill and Theodore Roosevelt.

long_description.id: Grace Coolidge disebut orang pertama yang melihatnya, pada 1927, berdiri di jendela Yellow Oval Room. Pada 1942 Ratu Wilhelmina konon melihat Lincoln di depan pintu kamarnya dan pingsan, meski artikel koran Belanda tahun 1996 menyebut ia tidak pingsan. Pada awal 1870-an janda Lincoln, Mary, berfoto di studio William H. Mumler dengan sosok mirip mendiang suaminya di latar belakang, yang oleh Stephen Wagner dijelaskan sebagai pencahayaan ganda.
long_description.en: Grace Coolidge is said to be the first to see it, in 1927, standing at a window of the Yellow Oval Room. In 1942 Queen Wilhelmina reportedly saw Lincoln at her door and fainted, though a 1996 Dutch newspaper article says she did not faint. In the early 1870s Lincoln's widow Mary was photographed at William H. Mumler's studio with a figure like her late husband behind her, which Stephen Wagner explains as double exposure.

statement.id: Hantu Presiden AS Abraham Lincoln, yang juga disebut Hantu Gedung Putih, konon menghantui Gedung Putih sejak Lincoln dibunuh pada 1865.
statement.en: The ghost of U.S. president Abraham Lincoln, also called the White House Ghost, is said to have haunted the White House since his assassination in 1865.

claims.quote: Lincoln's ghost has also been said to haunt many of his former residences in Springfield, Illinois, including his former law office.

statement.id: Hantunya juga dikatakan menghantui bekas kediamannya di Springfield, Illinois, termasuk bekas kantor hukumnya.
statement.en: His ghost is also said to haunt his former homes in Springfield, Illinois, including his old law office.

claims.quote: First Lady Grace Coolidge, Queen Wilhelmina of the Netherlands, Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and President Theodore Roosevelt are among those claimed to have stated they saw Lincoln's ghost in the White House.

statement.id: Ibu Negara Grace Coolidge, Ratu Wilhelmina dari Belanda, Perdana Menteri Winston Churchill, dan Presiden Theodore Roosevelt disebut pernah mengaku melihat hantu Lincoln di Gedung Putih.
statement.en: First Lady Grace Coolidge, Queen Wilhelmina of the Netherlands, Prime Minister Winston Churchill and President Theodore Roosevelt are said to have claimed seeing Lincoln's ghost in the White House.

claims.quote: The first person reported to have actually seen Lincoln's spirit was First Lady Grace Coolidge, who said she saw the ghost of Lincoln standing at a window in the Yellow Oval Room staring out at the Potomac in 1927.

statement.id: Orang pertama yang dilaporkan melihatnya adalah Grace Coolidge, yang pada 1927 melihat Lincoln berdiri di jendela Yellow Oval Room menatap Sungai Potomac.
statement.en: The first person reported to see it was Grace Coolidge, who in 1927 saw Lincoln standing at a window of the Yellow Oval Room gazing at the Potomac.

claims.quote: Perhaps the most famous incident was in 1942 when Queen Wilhelmina of the Netherlands allegedly heard footsteps outside her White House bedroom and answered a knock on the door, only to see Lincoln in frock coat and top hat standing in front of her (she promptly fainted).

statement.id: Kejadian paling terkenal terjadi pada 1942: Ratu Wilhelmina mendengar langkah kaki, membuka pintu yang diketuk, dan melihat Lincoln bermantel panjang dan bertopi tinggi, lalu pingsan.
statement.en: The most famous incident came in 1942: Queen Wilhelmina heard footsteps, answered a knock and saw Lincoln in frock coat and top hat, then fainted.

claims.quote: According to a Dutch 1996 newspaper article she did not faint, but saw the man, who looked slightly familiar to her, disappear before she could say anything.

statement.id: Menurut artikel koran Belanda tahun 1996, ia tidak pingsan, melainkan melihat lelaki yang agak dikenalnya itu menghilang sebelum ia sempat berbicara.
statement.en: According to a 1996 Dutch newspaper article, she did not faint but saw the faintly familiar man vanish before she could speak.

statement.en: In the early 1870s the widowed Mary was photographed at spirit photographer William H. Mumler's studio; behind her appeared a man she said resembled her late husband.

short_description.id: Mhachkay adalah makhluk mirip vampir dalam mitologi Turkik dan Tatar: orang berjiwa dua yang bangkit setelah mati dan terbang sebagai burung hantu untuk mengisap darah.
short_description.en: Mhachkay is a vampire-like being of Turkic and Tatar mythology: a person with two souls who rises after death and flies as an owl to suck blood.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, terutama Tatar, Mhachkay adalah makhluk yang agak mirip vampir. Orang yang lahir dengan dua jantung dan dua jiwa dipercaya sebagai Mhachkay dan diusir dari permukiman. Bila ia mati muda, hanya satu jiwanya pergi; jiwa lainnya menghidupkan jasadnya, yang lalu terbang pada malam hari sebagai burung hantu, menyerang pejalan malam, mengisap darah, dan memakan isi tubuh korban.
long_description.en: In Turkic, especially Tatar, mythology Mhachkay is a somewhat vampire-like being. A person born with two hearts and two souls was thought to be a Mhachkay and was driven from settlements. If such a person died young, only one soul left; the other revived the corpse, which then flew at night as an owl, attacking night travellers, sucking their blood and eating their insides.

long_description.id: Untuk mencegahnya bangkit, jasad Mhachkay dipenggal dan kepalanya dikubur terpisah. Dalam sumber lain, məçkəy dibayangkan sebagai perempuan tua bungkuk pembawa maut yang menyebarkan wabah, seperti Nosferatu.
long_description.en: To stop it rising, a Mhachkay's corpse was beheaded and the head buried apart. In another source the məçkəy is imagined as a hunched old woman spreading death and plague, like Nosferatu.

short_description.id: Mooinjer veggey adalah istilah Manx untuk "orang kecil", sebutan peri dalam folklor Pulau Man.
short_description.en: Mooinjer veggey is Manx for 'little people', the term for fairies in Isle of Man folklore.

long_description.id: Mooinjer veggey adalah bahasa Manx untuk "orang kecil", istilah untuk peri dalam tradisi Gaelik; padanannya dalam bahasa Irlandia dan Gaelik Skotlandia adalah Muintir Bheaga dan Muinntir Bheaga. Dalam folklor Manx mereka makhluk kecil setinggi 2–3 kaki, selain itu sangat mirip manusia; mereka memakai topi merah dan jaket hijau dan paling sering terlihat menunggang kuda diikuti kawanan anjing kecil beraneka warna pelangi. Mereka cenderung nakal dan pendendam.
long_description.en: Mooinjer veggey is Manx for 'little people', the Gaelic term for fairies, matched by Irish Muintir Bheaga and Scottish Gaelic Muinntir Bheaga. In Manx folklore they are small, 2–3 feet tall, but otherwise much like mortals; they wear red caps and green jackets and are usually seen on horseback with packs of little hounds in every colour of the rainbow. They tend to be mischievous and spiteful.

long_description.id: Mereka tinggal di lereng bukit hijau, terutama gundukan kubur kuno; siapa pun yang mendekat pada malam musim panas mungkin mendengar musik indah tetapi harus waspada agar tidak terjebak. Sebagian baik hati, menyembuhkan penyakit dan menolong dari kemalangan; sebagian lain jahat, mencuri anak dan membawa sial. Dahulu orang menyalakan api semalaman, meninggalkan roti dan mengisi kendi dengan air bersih untuk mereka, dan perempuan Manx tidak memintal pada Sabtu malam. Garam dan besi dianggap ampuh melawan pesona jahat.
long_description.en: They live on green hillsides, especially ancient burial mounds; anyone lingering near one on a summer evening might hear lovely music but must beware of being trapped. Some are kindly, curing illness and rescuing people from misfortune; others are wicked, stealing children and bringing bad luck. People used to keep a fire burning overnight, leave bread and fill water crocks for them, and Manx women would not spin on Saturday evenings. Salt and iron were thought effective against evil charms.

who.en: Manx fairies.

role.en: Live in ancient mounds.

famous_for.id: Takut garam dan besi.
famous_for.en: Repelled by salt and iron.

did_you_know.id: Perempuan Manx dahulu tidak memintal pada Sabtu malam agar tidak membuat mooinjer veggey tidak senang.
did_you_know.en: Manx women once avoided spinning on Saturday evenings so as not to displease the mooinjer veggey.

description.id: Garam dan besi dianggap ampuh melawan pesona jahat.
description.en: Salt and iron were held effective against malevolent charms.

statement.en: Mooinjer veggey, Manx for little people (fairies) in Gaelic lore; Irish Muintir Bheaga, Scottish Gaelic Muinntir Bheaga; Isle of Man.

claims.quote: In Manx folklore, the mooinjer veggey are small creatures ranging 2–3 ft (0.61–0.91 m) in height, otherwise very like mortals. They wear red caps and green jackets and are most often seen on horseback followed by packs of little hounds of all the colours of the rainbow. They are rather inclined to be mischievous and spiteful.

statement.id: Setinggi 2–3 kaki, topi merah, jaket hijau, menunggang kuda dengan anjing kecil warna pelangi; nakal dan pendendam.
statement.en: 2–3 ft tall, red caps, green jackets, on horseback with rainbow-coloured hounds; mischievous and spiteful.

claims.quote: They live in green hillsides, more especially ancient tumuli. Anyone straying near these on a fine summer's evening would probably hear delightful music

statement.id: Tinggal di lereng hijau dan gundukan kubur kuno; musik indah malam musim panas.
statement.en: Live on green hillsides and ancient tumuli; delightful music on summer evenings.

claims.quote: They are visible to people only when they choose. Some of them are benevolent, curing men of diseases and delivering them from misfortune. Others are malevolent, stealing children, even abducting adults, and bringing misfortune.

statement.id: Terlihat hanya bila mau; sebagian menyembuhkan, sebagian mencuri anak.
statement.en: Visible only when they choose; some heal, some steal children.

claims.quote: Manxwomen would not spin on Saturday evenings, as this was deemed displeasing to the mooinjer veggey , and at every baking and churning a small piece of dough and butter was stuck on the wall for their consumption. Both salt and iron were considered efficacious against malevolent charms.

statement.id: Perempuan Manx (Manxwomen) tak memintal Sabtu malam; api, roti, air untuk mereka; garam dan besi melawan pesona jahat.
statement.en: Manxwomen did not spin on Saturday evenings; fire, bread, water for them; salt and iron against evil charms.

claims.quote: Yn llên gwerin Manaweg,  mae'r Mooinjer veggey yn greaduriaid bach o ddwy i dair troedfedd (600 i 900 mm) o uchder, fel arall yn debyg iawn i feidrolion.

short_description.id: Moroi adalah sejenis vampir atau hantu dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, dalam beberapa versi arwah orang mati yang keluar dari kubur untuk menyerap tenaga orang hidup.
short_description.en: A moroi is a type of vampire or ghost in Romanian folklore, in some versions a phantom of the dead that leaves the grave to draw energy from the living.

long_description.id: Moroi adalah sejenis vampir atau hantu dalam cerita rakyat Rumania; moroi perempuan disebut moroaică. Dalam beberapa versi, moroi adalah arwah orang mati yang meninggalkan kubur untuk menyerap tenaga orang hidup. Moroi sering dikaitkan dengan tokoh lain cerita rakyat Rumania seperti strigoi, vârcolac, atau pricolici, dan ciri-cirinya berbeda menurut sumber.
long_description.en: In Romanian lore a moroi is a kind of vampire or ghost; the female is a moroaică. In some versions the moroi is a dead person's phantom that leaves the grave to sap the energy of the living. It is often tied to other Romanian figures such as the strigoi, vârcolac or pricolici, and its traits vary from source to source.

long_description.id: Moroi juga bisa berarti bayi yang mati sebelum dibaptis. Akademi Rumania menduga istilah ini berasal dari kata Slavonik Kuno mora, "mimpi buruk". Sastra yang berdasar pada cerita rakyat membedakan moroi sebagai vampir hidup dan strigoi sebagai vampir yang bangkit dari kematian, walau perbedaan ini tidak selalu dipegang dalam cerita rakyat Rumania.
long_description.en: Moroi can also mean an infant who died unbaptised. The Romanian Academy thinks the term may come from Old Slavonic mora, "nightmare". Folklore-based literature distinguishes moroi as living vampires from strigoi as vampires risen from the dead, though Romanian folklore does not always keep that line.

statement.en: A moroi is a type of vampire or ghost in Romanian folklore; a female is a moroaică; in some versions it is a phantom of the dead leaving the grave to draw energy from the living.

claims.quote: Moroi are often associated with other figures in Romanian folklore, such as strigoi (another type of vampire), vârcolac (werewolf), or pricolici (werewolf). As with most concepts in folklore, the exact characteristics ascribed to moroi are variable from source to source.

statement.en: Moroi are often associated with other Romanian figures such as the strigoi (another vampire), vârcolac or pricolici (werewolves), and their traits vary by source.

statement.en: Moroi may also mean an infant who died unbaptised; the term's origin is unclear, but the Romanian Academy thinks it may come from Old Slavonic mora ("nightmare").

short_description.id: Ogre adalah raksasa buruk rupa pemakan manusia, terutama anak-anak, dari dongeng Eropa, seperti dalam Puss in Boots dan Hop-o'-My-Thumb.
short_description.en: The ogre is a hideous man-eating giant, especially of children, from fairy tales such as Puss in Boots and Hop-o'-My-Thumb.

long_description.id: Ogre atau ogress adalah monster legendaris berwujud mirip manusia yang besar dan buruk rupa yang memakan manusia, terutama bayi dan anak-anak. Ia berkepala besar, berambut lebat, berkulit warna tak biasa, rakus, dan kuat, dekat dengan raksasa dan kanibal; contoh terkenal ada dalam Puss in Boots dan Hop-o'-My-Thumb, dan tokoh seperti Grendel, Polifemus, dan Humbaba kadang juga disebut ogre.
long_description.en: The ogre or ogress is a legendary monster, a large, hideous humanoid that eats people, especially babies and children. It has a big head, thick hair, oddly coloured skin, a huge appetite and great strength, close to giants and cannibals; famous examples are in Puss in Boots and Hop-o'-My-Thumb, and figures such as Grendel, Polyphemus and Humbaba are sometimes called ogres.

long_description.id: Kata ogre berasal dari bahasa Prancis, dari nama dewa Orcus, dan pertama tercatat dalam Perceval karya Chrétien de Troyes; kata Italia orco sudah dipakai sejak abad ke-13, dan Giambattista Basile pertama menyebut orco perempuan. Di Eropa utara ogre dianggap buas pemakan daging mentah, tetapi juga pemalu dan penakut.
long_description.en: The word ogre is French, from the god Orcus, first attested in Chrétien de Troyes's Perceval; the Italian orco was in use from the 13th century, and Giambattista Basile first spoke of female ogres. In northern Europe the ogre is thought fierce and an eater of raw flesh, yet also shy and timid.

who.en: A man-eating giant.

role.en: Eats children.

famous_for.id: Ogre dalam Puss in Boots.
famous_for.en: The ogre in Puss in Boots.

claims.quote: An ogre (feminine: ogress) is a legendary monster depicted as a large, hideous, humanoid being that eats ordinary human beings, especially infants and children.

statement.id: Ogre (perempuan: ogress) adalah monster legendaris berwujud makhluk mirip manusia yang besar dan buruk rupa yang memakan manusia, terutama bayi dan anak-anak.
statement.en: An ogre (female ogress) is a legendary monster, a large, hideous humanoid that eats people, especially babies and children.

claims.quote: In mythology, ogres are often depicted as inhumanly large, tall, and having a disproportionately large head, abundant hair, unusually colored skin, a voracious appetite, and a strong body. Ogres are closely linked with giants and with human cannibals in mythology.

statement.id: Ogre sering digambarkan sangat besar dan tinggi, berkepala terlalu besar, berambut lebat, berkulit warna tak biasa, rakus, dan bertubuh kuat, serta erat terkait dengan raksasa dan manusia kanibal.
statement.en: Ogres are often shown as hugely large and tall, with oversized heads, thick hair, oddly coloured skin, voracious appetites and strong bodies, closely tied to giants and human cannibals.

claims.quote: Famous examples of ogres in folklore include the ogre in "Puss in Boots" and the ogre in "Hop-o'-My-Thumb".

statement.id: Contoh terkenal adalah ogre dalam Puss in Boots dan Hop-o'-My-Thumb.
statement.en: Famous folklore ogres include those in Puss in Boots and Hop-o'-My-Thumb.

claims.quote: Other characters sometimes described as ogres include the title character from "Bluebeard", the Beast from Beauty and the Beast, Humbaba from the Epic of Gilgamesh, Grendel from Beowulf, Polyphemus the Cyclops from Homer's Odyssey

statement.id: Tokoh lain yang kadang disebut ogre antara lain Bluebeard, si Buruk Rupa dalam Beauty and the Beast, Humbaba dari Epos Gilgamesh, Grendel dari Beowulf, dan Polifemus dari Odisseia.
statement.en: Other figures sometimes called ogres include Bluebeard, the Beast of Beauty and the Beast, Humbaba of the Epic of Gilgamesh, Grendel of Beowulf and Polyphemus of the Odyssey.

claims.quote: The word ogre is of French origin, originally derived from the Etruscan god Orcus. Its earliest attestation is in Chrétien de Troyes's late 12th-century verse romance Perceval, li contes del graal

statement.id: Kata ogre berasal dari bahasa Prancis, dari nama dewa Etruska Orcus, dan pertama tercatat dalam roman Perceval, li contes del graal karya Chrétien de Troyes akhir abad ke-12.
statement.en: The word ogre is French, from the Etruscan god Orcus, first attested in Chrétien de Troyes's late 12th-century romance Perceval, li contes del graal.

claims.quote: The word orco was widely used in Italy at least since 13th century, as attested by Jacomo Tolomei

statement.id: Kata orco sudah banyak dipakai di Italia setidaknya sejak abad ke-13, seperti dicatat Jacomo Tolomei.
statement.en: The word orco was widely used in Italy since at least the 13th century, as Jacomo Tolomei attests.

claims.quote: The Italian author Giambattista Basile (1575–1632) used the related Neapolitan word uerco, or in standard Italian, orco in some of his tales, and first talks of female orcs (e.g. in "Petrosinella").

statement.id: Pengarang Italia Giambattista Basile (1575–1632) memakai kata Neapolitan uerco atau orco dalam dongengnya dan pertama kali menyebut orco perempuan, misalnya dalam Petrosinella.
statement.en: The Italian writer Giambattista Basile (1575–1632) used the Neapolitan uerco, or orco, in his tales and first spoke of female ogres, as in Petrosinella.

claims.quote: Legenda Ogre berawal dari zaman pertengahan di Eropa Selatan, di mana banyak orang barbar yang bersenjatakan pemukul batu yang menyerang wilayah Romawi.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Indonesia, legenda ogre berawal dari Abad Pertengahan di Eropa Selatan, saat banyak orang barbar bersenjata pemukul batu menyerang wilayah Romawi.
statement.en: According to the Indonesian article, the ogre legend began in the Middle Ages in southern Europe, when many club-armed barbarians attacked Roman lands.

claims.quote: 語源としては、古くさかのぼるばあい、ギリシア・ローマ神話の冥府の神オルクスに由来するという説がある。しかし、直接にはイタリア語方言で「悪鬼、怪物」を意味するオルコやオルゴ（イタリア語: Orco, Orgo）に基づくともされる。

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, kata ini mungkin berasal dari Orcus, dewa dunia bawah mitologi Yunani-Romawi, tetapi secara langsung dari kata dialek Italia orco atau orgo, "iblis, monster".
statement.en: According to the Japanese article, the word may go back to Orcus, the Greco-Roman underworld god, but derives directly from the Italian dialect orco or orgo, 'fiend, monster'.

claims.quote: 北ヨーロッパでは凶暴で残忍な性格であり、人の生肉を食べるとされる。一方で、引っ込み思案で臆病という面もある。

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, di Eropa utara ogre dianggap buas dan kejam serta memakan daging manusia mentah, tetapi juga pemalu dan penakut.
statement.en: According to the Japanese article, in northern Europe the ogre is thought fierce and cruel and to eat raw human flesh, yet also shy and timid.

short_description.id: Petermännchen adalah roh rumah kecil yang baik hati penjaga Istana Schwerin, Jerman, yang membawa kunci, menghadiahi orang jujur, dan mengusir pencuri.
short_description.en: Petermännchen is the small, good-natured household spirit guarding Schwerin Palace in Germany, carrying keys, rewarding the honest and driving off thieves.

long_description.id: Petermännchen adalah roh rumah kecil yang baik hati di Istana Schwerin, Mecklenburg. Ia membawa banyak kunci dan berkeliaran di ruang bawah tanah serta terowongan istana. Sebagai penjaga istana ia menghadiahi orang jujur, menghukum pencuri dan penyusup, dan membangunkan prajurit yang tertidur saat jaga agar tidak dihukum.
long_description.en: Petermännchen is a small, good-natured household spirit of Schwerin Palace in Mecklenburg. He carries many keys and roams the castle's vaults and tunnels. As its watchman he rewards the honest, punishes thieves and intruders, and wakes sleeping sentries so they escape punishment.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, ia satu-satunya roh pelayan dewa pagan yang tetap tinggal setelah agama Kristen datang. Richard Wossidlo menafsirkannya sebagai dewa Radegast yang menjadi kobold penjaga harta bangsa Obotrit. Ia konon mengganggu Wallenstein begitu hebat pada malam pertamanya di istana sehingga sang jenderal pergi esok harinya.
long_description.en: Legend makes him the only spirit servant of a pagan god who stayed after Christianity arrived. Richard Wossidlo read him as the god Radegast turned into a kobold guarding the Obotrites' treasure. He is said to have tormented Wallenstein so badly on his first night at the castle that the general left the next day.

long_description.id: Patung Petermännchen karya Heinrich Petters dari sekitar 1856 menghiasi fasad halaman istana.
long_description.en: A statue of Petermännchen by Heinrich Petters from around 1856 adorns the castle courtyard façade.

who.en: A palace-guarding household spirit.

role.en: Guards the palace and drives off thieves.

famous_for.id: Membawa banyak kunci.
famous_for.en: Carries many keys.

description.id: Istana yang dijaga Petermännchen.
description.en: The palace Petermännchen guards.

note.id: Menurut Wossidlo, Petermännchen adalah dewa ini dalam wujud kobold.
note.en: According to Wossidlo, Petermännchen is this god in kobold form.

claims.quote: Petermännchen (English: "Little Peterman"; German: [ˈpeːtɐˌmɛnçən]) is a small good-natured household spirit who is said to live in the Schwerin Palace in Schwerin, Mecklenburg, Germany.

statement.id: Petermännchen ("Peterman kecil") adalah roh rumah kecil yang baik hati yang konon tinggal di Istana Schwerin, Mecklenburg, Jerman.
statement.en: Petermännchen ("Little Peterman") is a small, good-natured household spirit said to live in Schwerin Palace in Schwerin, Mecklenburg, Germany.

claims.quote: The diminutive spirit, maybe only a few feet tall, is often described as carrying many keys, roaming through the vaults and tunnels underneath the castle, unlocking doors as he goes.

statement.id: Roh mungil ini, mungkin hanya setinggi beberapa kaki, sering digambarkan membawa banyak kunci dan berkeliaran di ruang bawah tanah dan terowongan istana sambil membuka pintu-pintu.
statement.en: The tiny spirit, perhaps only a few feet tall, is often described carrying many keys and roaming the vaults and tunnels under the castle, unlocking doors as he goes.

claims.quote: He is also said to be the keeper and watchman of the castle, rewarding those who are honest and good. Conversely the spirit will punish or drive away thieves and intruders.

statement.id: Ia juga penjaga istana yang memberi hadiah kepada orang jujur dan baik, sebaliknya menghukum atau mengusir pencuri dan penyusup.
statement.en: He is also the keeper and watchman of the castle, rewarding the honest and good while punishing or driving away thieves and intruders.

claims.quote: Petermännchen is also said to have woken soldiers who fell asleep on their night-watch in order to save them from being punished.

statement.en: Petermännchen is said to have tormented Wallenstein, granted the Duchy of Mecklenburg by Emperor Ferdinand II in 1628, so badly on his first night at Schwerin Palace that the general left the next morning utterly sleepless.

short_description.id: Pishtaco adalah sosok momok dalam cerita rakyat Andes, terutama Peru dan Bolivia, yang digambarkan sebagai pembunuh yang mengambil lemak korbannya.
short_description.en: The pishtaco is a bogeyman of Andean folklore, especially in Peru and Bolivia, pictured as a killer who extracts his victims' fat.

long_description.id: Pishtaco adalah sosok momok dalam tradisi Quechua dan Aymara di Andes, terutama Peru dan Bolivia: pembunuh mengerikan, biasanya digambarkan sebagai lelaki kulit putih atau mestizo, yang mengambil lemak korbannya. Ia bersenjata pisau panjang untuk memenggal atau memotong korban, tetapi bisa juga tidak meninggalkan luka sama sekali sementara korban meninggal beberapa hari kemudian.
long_description.en: The pishtaco is a bogeyman of Quechua and Aymara tradition in the Andes, especially Peru and Bolivia: a monstrous killer, usually pictured as a white or mestizo man, who extracts his victims' fat. He carries a long knife for beheading or dismembering, but may also leave no wound at all while the victim dies days later.

long_description.id: Namanya di Peru tengah, pishtaco, berarti "penjagal" dalam bahasa Quechua; di Altiplano Bolivia ia disebut kharisiri atau lik'ichiri, "pembuat lemak". Sosok ini diyakini berasal dari praktik penakluk Spanyol yang memakai lemak jenazah penduduk asli Peru sebagai obat.
long_description.en: In central Peru his name, pishtaco, means "slaughterer" in Quechua; in the Bolivian Altiplano he is called kharisiri or lik'ichiri, "fat-maker". The figure is thought to stem from Spanish conquistadors using the corpse fat of Indigenous Peruvians as medicine.

short_description.id: Polevik adalah roh penguasa ladang dalam mitologi Slavia, digambarkan berambut rumput dan dipercaya menyesatkan atau mencelakai orang di ladang.
short_description.en: The polevik is the spirit-master of the fields in Slavic mythology, pictured with grass for hair and believed to lead people astray or harm them in the fields.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, polevik adalah roh ladang. Satu sumber menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk cacat dengan mata berlainan warna dan rumput sebagai pengganti rambut, muncul pada tengah hari atau saat matahari terbenam, berpakaian serba hitam atau serba putih. Cerita rakyat Rusia selatan menyebutnya berambut hijau. Menurut kepercayaan setempat, ia menyesatkan pengembara di ladang, menularkan penyakit, atau menggilas orang yang tertidur dengan kudanya.
long_description.en: In Slavic mythology the polevik is a field spirit. One source describes it as a deformed creature with eyes of different colours and grass in place of hair, appearing at noon or at sunset and dressed all in black or all in white. South Russian folklore gives it green hair. Local belief holds that it leads wanderers astray in the fields, brings disease, or rides over sleepers with its horses.

long_description.id: Pada bangsa Slavia Timur, polevik dianggap roh penguasa ladang, tetapi gambarannya kabur karena kepercayaan tentangnya jarang ditemukan. Ia umumnya digambarkan mirip manusia dengan ciri hewan, tumbuhan, dan iblis, kadang disertai angin kencang dan percikan api. Ada keyakinan bahwa ia menjaga ladang serta memengaruhi kesuburan dan kesejahteraan ternak yang merumput di sana, dan di beberapa tempat orang memberinya persembahan agar panen baik.
long_description.en: In East Slavic tradition the polevik was held to be the spirit-master of the field, though its image is vague because beliefs about it were rare. It is mostly described as human-like with animal, plant and demonic traits, sometimes accompanied by strong wind and sparks. Some believed it guarded the field and influenced its fertility and the well-being of grazing livestock, and in places people brought it gifts for a good harvest.

long_description.id: Sikapnya terhadap manusia umumnya bermusuhan: ia bisa menakut-nakuti, menyesatkan, bahkan membunuh, serta merusak ternak dan tanaman. Orang yang tertidur di ladang setelah minum minuman keras dapat dibunuh olehnya. Untuk menenangkannya, disebutkan perlunya dua butir telur, seekor ayam jantan, seekor kodok, dan seekor gagak yang diletakkan di parit tanpa terlihat orang.
long_description.en: Its attitude to people is mostly hostile: it may frighten them, lead them off the road or even kill them, and harm livestock and crops. A person who falls asleep at work after drinking may be killed by it. To appease it, two eggs, a rooster, a toad and a crow are said to be placed in a ditch when no one is looking.

short_description.id: Vampir Richmond adalah legenda urban dari Richmond, Virginia, tentang vampir yang konon bersemayam di mausoleum W. W. Pool di Pemakaman Hollywood.
short_description.en: The Richmond Vampire is an urban legend from Richmond, Virginia, about a vampire said to lie in the W. W. Pool mausoleum in Hollywood Cemetery.

long_description.id: Vampir Richmond, yang secara lokal juga disebut Vampir Hollywood, adalah legenda urban dari Richmond, Virginia. Warga mengklaim mausoleum W. W. Pool di Pemakaman Hollywood menyimpan jasad vampir yang konon diusir dari Inggris pada abad ke-19. Legenda lisan ini beredar sejak 1960-an, mungkin dipicu arsitektur makam bergaya Mason dan Mesir kuno dengan dua huruf W yang mirip taring, dan populer di kalangan mahasiswa Virginia Commonwealth University di sebelahnya.
long_description.en: The Richmond Vampire, locally also called the Hollywood Vampire, is an urban legend from Richmond, Virginia. Residents claim the W. W. Pool mausoleum in Hollywood Cemetery holds the remains of a vampire supposedly driven out of England in the 19th century. The oral legend circulated by the 1960s, perhaps inspired by the tomb's Masonic and ancient Egyptian architecture with double Ws resembling fangs, and became popular among students of the neighbouring Virginia Commonwealth University.

long_description.id: Sejak 2001 cerita ini digabungkan dengan runtuhnya Terowongan Church Hill pada 1925: konon penggalian membangunkan makhluk berlumur darah bergigi bergerigi yang ditemukan di atas korban. Satu penjelasan menyebut "makhluk" itu sebenarnya juru api Benjamin F. Mosby yang tersiram uap ketel, dan catatan sezaman tidak memuat detail-detail tersebut.
long_description.en: Since 2001 the story has been combined with the 1925 collapse of the Church Hill Tunnel: supposedly the digging woke a blood-covered, jagged-toothed creature found crouching over a victim. One explanation says the "creature" was really fireman Benjamin F. Mosby, scalded when the boiler burst, and contemporary records contain none of these details.

claims.quote: Local residents claim that the mausoleum of W. W. Pool (Dated 1913) in Hollywood Cemetery holds the remains of a vampire. Supposedly Pool was run out of England in the 19th century for being a vampire. Oral legends to this effect were circulating by the 1960s.

statement.id: Warga setempat mengklaim bahwa mausoleum W. W. Pool (bertarikh 1913) di Pemakaman Hollywood menyimpan jasad vampir; konon Pool diusir dari Inggris pada abad ke-19 karena vampir, dan legenda lisan semacam ini sudah beredar pada 1960-an.
statement.en: Local residents claim that the mausoleum of W. W. Pool (dated 1913) in Hollywood Cemetery holds a vampire's remains; supposedly Pool was driven out of England in the 19th century for being a vampire, and oral legends to this effect circulated by the 1960s.

claims.quote: They may be influenced by the architecture of the tomb, which has both Masonic and ancient Egyptian elements, and double Ws looking like fangs. Because this cemetery is adjacent to Virginia Commonwealth University, the story became popular among students, especially from the 1980s onward. It was first mentioned in print in the student newspaper Commonwealth Times in 1976.

statement.id: Legenda ini mungkin dipengaruhi arsitektur makam yang memiliki unsur Mason dan Mesir kuno serta dua huruf W yang mirip taring; karena pemakaman itu bersebelahan dengan Virginia Commonwealth University, ceritanya populer di kalangan mahasiswa terutama sejak 1980-an, dan pertama kali dicetak di koran mahasiswa Commonwealth Times pada 1976.
statement.en: The legends may be influenced by the tomb's architecture, with Masonic and ancient Egyptian elements and double Ws resembling fangs; because the cemetery adjoins Virginia Commonwealth University, the story became popular among students especially from the 1980s, and it first appeared in print in the student newspaper Commonwealth Times in 1976.

claims.quote: According to this newer story, the tunneling awakened an ancient evil that lived under Church Hill and brought the tunnel crashing down on the workers. Rescue teams found an unearthly blood-covered creature with jagged teeth and skin hanging from its muscular body crouching over one of the victims.

statement.id: Menurut versi yang lebih baru, penggalian terowongan membangunkan kejahatan purba yang hidup di bawah Church Hill dan meruntuhkan terowongan itu menimpa para pekerja; tim penyelamat menemukan makhluk berlumur darah bergigi bergerigi dengan kulit bergelantungan dari tubuh berotot, berjongkok di atas salah satu korban.
statement.en: In this newer version, the tunnelling awakened an ancient evil living under Church Hill that brought the tunnel down on the workers; rescuers found an unearthly blood-covered creature with jagged teeth and skin hanging from its muscular body crouching over a victim.

claims.quote: Since 2001, the vampire story has been combined with the collapse of the Chesapeake and Ohio Railroad's Church Hill Tunnel under Church Hill, a neighborhood of eastern Richmond, Virginia, which buried several workers on Friday, October 2, 1925. This part of the story did not show up online until 2001 and was first reported in print in 2007

statement.id: Sejak 2001, cerita vampir ini digabungkan dengan runtuhnya Terowongan Church Hill milik Chesapeake and Ohio Railroad di bawah Church Hill, Richmond timur, yang mengubur beberapa pekerja pada Jumat, 2 Oktober 1925; bagian cerita ini baru muncul daring pada 2001 dan pertama dicetak pada 2007.
statement.en: Since 2001 the vampire story has been combined with the collapse of the Chesapeake and Ohio Railroad's Church Hill Tunnel under Church Hill in eastern Richmond, which buried several workers on Friday, October 2, 1925; this part appeared online only in 2001 and in print first in 2007.

statement.en: The Spanish article describes the Richmond Vampire as an urban legend of the city of Richmond, capital of the state of Virginia, United States (Estados Unidos).

claims.quote: the "creature" that escaped the tunnel collapse was actually the 28-year-old railroad fireman, Benjamin F. Mosby (1896-1925), who had been shoveling coal into the firebox of a steam locomotive of a work train with no shirt on when the cave-in occurred and the boiler ruptured.

statement.id: Menurut penjelasan ini, "makhluk" yang lolos dari runtuhnya terowongan sebenarnya adalah juru api kereta berusia 28 tahun, Benjamin F. Mosby (1896–1925), yang sedang menyekop batu bara ke tungku lokomotif uap tanpa baju ketika runtuhan terjadi dan ketelnya pecah.
statement.en: In this explanation the "creature" that escaped the collapse was actually the 28-year-old railroad fireman Benjamin F. Mosby (1896–1925), who had been shovelling coal into a steam locomotive's firebox shirtless when the cave-in occurred and the boiler burst.

short_description.id: Samodiva, samovila, atau vila adalah peri, nimfa hutan, atau iblis perempuan berbahaya dalam cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan dan Barat.
short_description.en: The samodiva, samovila or vila is a fairy, wood nymph or harmful female demon of South and West Slavic folklore.

long_description.id: Samodiva (jamak samodivi), samovila, atau vila adalah peri, nimfa hutan, atau iblis perempuan yang berbahaya dalam cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan dan Barat. Mereka digambarkan sebagai perempuan cantik berambut panjang pirang atau merah, berbaju putih, dengan kerudung, karangan bunga, atau selempang hijau yang konon memberi mereka kekuatan gaib atau kemampuan terbang; kadang mereka sendiri bersayap.
long_description.en: The samodiva (plural samodivi), samovila or vila is a fairy, wood nymph or dangerous she-demon of South and West Slavic lore. They are pictured as lovely women with long blond or red hair in white dresses, whose veils, wreaths or green sashes are said to give them supernatural power or the power to fly; sometimes they are winged themselves.

long_description.id: Kediaman rahasia mereka berada di tempat tinggi, dekat perairan, atau di hutan, misalnya mata air di gunung atau hutan beech di tepi danau tempat mereka mandi. Orang yang melanggar wilayah mereka, terutama menimba air pada malam hari, bisa ditimpa sakit atau maut. Satu tema yang berulang adalah lelaki yang mencuri kerudung atau karangan bunga samodiva untuk menangkapnya dan memaksanya menjadi pengantin.
long_description.en: Their hidden homes lie on heights, by water or in woodland, such as a mountain spring or a beech grove by a lake where they bathe. Anyone trespassing there, especially to draw water at night, may be struck by sickness or death. A recurring theme is a man who steals a samodiva's veil or wreath to capture her and force her to be his bride.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Bulgaria mereka jiwa perempuan cantik yang tinggal di gua dekat mata air, padang sunyi, atau kincir angin kosong; malam hari mereka mencuci baju putih yang menyimpan seluruh kekuatan mereka, lalu menari hora di padang terbuka. Kadang mereka membantu panen dan pasangan muda, tetapi lebih sering memusuhi manusia, misalnya menahan mata air.
long_description.en: In Bulgarian lore they are the souls of beautiful women living in caves by springs, wastelands or abandoned windmills; at night they wash the white garments that hold all their power and dance the hora in a glade. Sometimes they help with harvests and young couples, but more often they are hostile, for instance stopping up springs.

short_description.id: Sânziană adalah peri lembut dalam cerita rakyat Rumania; bentuk jamaknya, Sânziene, juga nama perayaan tahunan untuk menghormati mereka pada 24 Juni.
short_description.en: Sânziană is a gentle fairy of Romanian folklore; the plural, Sânziene, also names a yearly festival in their honour on 24 June.

long_description.id: Sânziană adalah nama Rumania untuk peri-peri lembut yang penting dalam cerita rakyat setempat; kata itu juga dipakai untuk bunga Galium verum. Dalam bentuk jamak, Sânziene, kata ini menunjuk perayaan tahunan untuk menghormati para peri. Menurut Mircea Eliade, Sânziene berasal dari kultus Romawi bagi dewi Diana, Sancta Diana.
long_description.en: Sânziană is the Romanian word for gentle fairies who matter greatly in local lore, and it also names the Galium verum flower. In the plural, Sânziene, the word refers to a yearly feast held in the fairies' honour. Mircea Eliade traced the Sânziene to a Roman cult of the goddess Diana, Sancta Diana.

long_description.id: Orang di Pegunungan Carpathia barat merayakan Sânziene setiap 24 Juni, yang dipercaya sebagai perayaan pagan titik balik matahari musim panas; menurut Gereja Ortodoks Rumania, adat itu berkaitan dengan kelahiran Santo Yohanes Pembaptis pada tanggal yang sama. Gadis-gadis tercantik desa berbaju putih memetik bunga, termasuk Galium verum, menganyam mahkota bunga, lalu menari mengelilingi api unggun.
long_description.en: People in the western Carpathians mark Sânziene every 24 June, thought to be a pagan summer-solstice rite; the Romanian Orthodox Church links the customs to the Nativity of Saint John the Baptist on that date. The village's loveliest girls, dressed in white, gather flowers including Galium verum, weave crowns and dance around a bonfire.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Rumania, Sânziene adalah peri baik dari golongan iele, tetapi bila hari raya mereka tidak dihormati mereka berubah menjadi seperti rusalii, peri jahat. Di beberapa daerah mereka disebut drăgaice. Dalam lapisan cerita rakyat yang lebih baru muncul peri tunggal, Iana Sânziana, saudari Matahari dalam colinde kosmologis.
long_description.en: In Romanian mythology the Sânziene are good fairies of the iele class, but when their feast is not respected they turn into companions of the rusalii, evil fairies. In some areas they are called drăgaice. Newer layers of folklore have a single fairy, Iana Sânziana, sister of the Sun in cosmological carols.

short_description.id: Tsar Laut adalah raja alam laut dalam dongeng dan bylina Slavia Timur, penguasa semua perairan yang tinggal di istana bawah air dan gemar menari mengikuti musik, terkenal dari kisah Sadko dan Vasilisa yang Bijak.
short_description.en: The Sea Tsar is the king of the sea realms in East Slavic folktales and bylinas, lord of all waters who lives in an underwater palace and loves to dance to music, best known from the tales of Sadko and Vasilisa the Wise.

long_description.id: Tsar Laut adalah tokoh dongeng dan bylina Slavia Timur yang memerintah alam laut. Ia adalah tuan dasar laut, penguasa semua perairan dan para penghuni bawah air, serta pemilik harta tak terhitung. Istananya terbuat dari kristal, perak, emas, dan batu permata, dan letaknya berganti-ganti antara laut biru, sebuah pulau, dan Danau Ilmen.
long_description.en: The Sea Tsar is a character of East Slavic folktales and bylinas who rules the sea realms. He is master of the sea floor, lord of all waters and their underwater dwellers, and owner of countless treasures. His palace is made of crystal, silver, gold and precious stones, and its location shifts between the blue sea, an island and Lake Ilmen.

long_description.id: Ia gemar bersenang-senang: musisi yang tenggelam dipanggil ke istananya untuk bermain, dan ketika ia menari, laut bergolak dan badai pun datang. Dalam bylina tentang Sadko, ia mula-mula membuat Sadko kaya, lalu menuntut Sadko turun ke kerajaannya. Dalam dongeng Vasilisa yang Bijak, ia ingin menahan Ivan-tsarevich, tetapi putrinya Vasilisa kabur bersama sang pangeran dan menyelamatkannya dari kejaran ayahnya.
long_description.en: He loves merrymaking: drowned musicians are summoned to his palace to play, and when he dances the sea storms and a tempest rises. In the bylina about Sadko he first makes Sadko rich, then demands that Sadko come down to his kingdom. In the tale of Vasilisa the Wise he wants to keep Ivan-tsarevich, but his daughter Vasilisa escapes with the prince and saves him from her father's pursuit.

long_description.id: Tsar Laut perlu dibedakan dari roh air vodyanoy. Vodyanoy dalam kepercayaan rakyat adalah makhluk berperut gembung yang tinggal di lubuk dekat penggilingan dan menenggelamkan orang, sedangkan Tsar Laut tinggal di istana mewah dan mencintai musik. Vsevolod Miller menduga gambarannya dipengaruhi dewa laut Finlandia Ahti dan meragukan bahwa ia mencerminkan kepercayaan pagan Slavia Timur kuno; sebagian orang juga menyejajarkannya dengan morski kralj Slavia Selatan.
long_description.en: The Sea Tsar should be distinguished from the water spirit vodyanoy. The vodyanoy of folk belief is a bloated creature living in pools near mills and drowning people, whereas the Sea Tsar lives in rich halls and loves music. Vsevolod Miller suspected that his image was influenced by the Finnish sea god Ahti and doubted that he reflects old East Slavic pagan belief; some also compare him with the South Slavic morski kralj.

statement.id: Artikel Rusia menyebutnya tokoh dongeng dan bylina rakyat Rusia: tuan dasar laut, penguasa semua perairan, raja para penghuni bawah air, dan pemilik harta tak terhitung; ia juga disebut Царь Водяник, Поддонный царь, dan Заморский царь.
statement.en: The Russian article calls him a character of Russian folktales and bylinas: master of the sea floor, lord of all waters, ruler of the underwater dwellers and owner of countless treasures; he is also called Царь Водяник, Поддонный царь and Заморский царь.

claims.quote: Дворец Морского царя, сделанный из хрусталя, серебра, золота и драгоценных камней, помещается неопределённо: то в синем море, то на острове, то в Ильмень-озере. Когда он пляшет и развлекается — на море шторм и поднимается буря.

statement.id: Istana Tsar Laut dari kristal, perak, emas, dan batu permata letaknya tidak tetap: kadang di laut biru, kadang di sebuah pulau, kadang di Danau Ilmen; ketika ia menari dan bersenang-senang, laut bergolak dan badai pun datang.

short_description.id: Shishiga adalah makhluk perempuan penghuni rawa atau hutan dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, mirip roh hutan, yang mengganggu orang dan mendatangkan sial kepada pemabuk.
short_description.en: The shishiga is a female swamp or forest creature of Russian folklore, akin to the wood-goblin, that harasses people and brings misfortune to drunkards.

long_description.id: Shishiga (Rusia: шишига, juga leshenka) adalah makhluk perempuan penghuni rawa atau hutan dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Rusia (Russian), mirip roh hutan. Ia digambarkan putih, telanjang, dan berambut kusut, dan dianggap mengganggu orang serta mendatangkan sial kepada pemabuk. Makhluk yang sama penting dalam mitologi bangsa Komi: ia konon tinggal di Sungai Kama dan sering naik ke tepi untuk menyisir rambutnya, dan siapa pun yang melihatnya akan segera tenggelam atau mati karena sebab lain.
long_description.en: The shishiga (Russian шишига, also leshenka) is a female swamp or forest being of Russian folklore and myth, similar to the wood-goblin. She is pictured white, naked and dishevelled, and is held to pester people and bring bad luck to drunkards. The same creature matters in Komi mythology: she is said to live in the Kama River and often comes ashore to comb her hair, and anyone who sees her soon drowns or dies some other way.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel fr, chichiga digambarkan sebagai makhluk perempuan kecil bungkuk yang tinggal di antara alang-alang, lebih suka anak sungai kecil dan kolam, tidur sepanjang siang dan hanya muncul saat senja; ia juga membawa pergi anak-anak yang terlalu dekat dengan air deras. Menurut artikel ru, dalam mitologi Slavia Timur kata шишига dipakai untuk berbagai roh jahat yang tinggal di balik tungku, di hutan, di rawa, atau di pemandian, dan di Simbirsk setan disebut Shishiga.
long_description.en: According to the fr article the chichiga is a small hunchbacked female creature living among reeds, preferring little streams and ponds, sleeping through the afternoon and appearing only at dusk; she also carries off children who come too close to rushing water. According to the ru article, in East Slavic myth шишига names various unclean spirits living behind the stove, in the forest, the swamp or the bathhouse, and in Simbirsk province the devil was called Shishiga.

short_description.id: Shtojzovalle adalah makhluk kecil yang sangat elok dalam mitologi Albania, tak kasatmata, tinggal di hutan dan padang rumput, serta gemar bernyanyi dan menari.
short_description.en: The shtojzovalle is a small, extraordinarily beautiful being of Albanian mythology, invisible to humans, living in forests and pastures and fond of song and dance.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Albania, shtojzovalle adalah makhluk kecil lelaki dan perempuan yang sangat elok dan berkekuatan gaib. Mereka tinggal di hutan dan padang rumput, menghabiskan waktu dengan bernyanyi dan menari, dapat terbang, dan pada malam hari memintal benang kehidupan manusia. Manusia jarang bisa melihat mereka, kecuali dengan mengangkat selubung tak kasatmata di depan matanya.
long_description.en: In Albanian mythology the shtojzovalles are small male and female beings of extraordinary beauty and supernatural power. They live in forests and pastures, spend their time singing and dancing, can fly, and at night spin the thread of human existence. Humans rarely see them, except by lifting an invisible veil before their eyes.

long_description.id: Hubungan mereka dengan manusia beragam. Kadang terjadi perkawinan, tetapi lelaki hanya bisa mempertahankan istri shtojzovalle jika memberinya pakaiannya sendiri. Rumah yang dibangun di tanah mereka akan dihantui bunyi rantai besi berat, dan orang yang menginjak shtojzovalle bisa dimangsa.
long_description.en: Their dealings with humans vary. Marriages sometimes happen, but a man can keep a shtojzovalle wife only by giving her his own clothes. A house built on their land will be haunted by the rattling of heavy iron chains, and someone who steps on a shtojzovalle may be devoured.

long_description.id: Namanya, hasil perpaduan kepercayaan pagan dan Kristen, berarti "semoga Tuhan menambah tarian mereka". Di kalangan Katolik Albania utara dan Malësia, shtojzovalle dianggap malaikat yang tetap netral ketika Malaikat Agung Mikael melawan Setan. Mereka menangis menyesali kenetralan itu, dan air mata mereka mematikan manusia; dari sinilah ungkapan i ka rënë pika, "setetes jatuh padanya", untuk kematian seseorang.
long_description.en: Their name, a product of pagan and Christian syncretism, means "may God give increase to their dance". Among the Catholics of northern Albania and Malësia, the shtojzovalles are held to be angels who stayed neutral when Archangel Michael fought Satan. They weep in repentance for that neutrality, and their tears are deadly to humans; hence the phrase i ka rënë pika, "a drop fell upon him", for someone's death.

cultural_context.id: Kepercayaan tentang air mata shtojzovalle melahirkan ungkapan Albania i ka rënë pika, yang dipakai sebagai kiasan untuk kematian.
cultural_context.en: Belief in the shtojzovalles' tears gave rise to the Albanian phrase i ka rënë pika, used as a figure of speech for death.

literal_meaning.en: may God give increase to their dance
