learning_questions.id: Bagaimana kepercayaan lama dan agama baru bisa berpadu dalam satu makhluk cerita rakyat?
learning_questions.en: How can older beliefs and a newer religion merge in a single folk being?

claims.quote: In Albanian mythology, the shtojzovalle, also known as shtojzorreshta, shtozote is a small creature with supernatural powers and of extraordinary beauty. They are invisible woodland creatures, which can be seen by humans only on rare occasions and are fond of song and dance.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Albania, shtojzovalle (juga disebut shtojzorreshta atau shtozote) adalah makhluk kecil berkekuatan gaib dan sangat elok; mereka makhluk hutan yang tak kasatmata, jarang terlihat manusia, dan gemar bernyanyi serta menari.
statement.en: In Albanian mythology the shtojzovalle (also shtojzorreshta or shtozote) is a small creature with supernatural powers and extraordinary beauty; they are invisible woodland creatures, rarely seen by humans, fond of song and dance.

claims.quote: The term shtojzovalle derives from the Albanian words shtoj (English: add), zot (English: god, deity) and valle (English: dance), with the term meaning in English "may God give increase to their dance"

statement.id: Istilah shtojzovalle berasal dari kata Albania shtoj (menambah), zot (Tuhan, dewa), dan valle (tarian), sehingga berarti "semoga Tuhan menambah tarian mereka".
statement.en: The term shtojzovalle derives from the Albanian shtoj (add), zot (god, deity) and valle (dance), meaning "may God give increase to their dance".

claims.quote: They live in forests and pastures and spend their time singing and dancing. They have the ability to fly and at night they spin the thread of human existence. They are invisible to humans and a human can see them only if they lift an invisible veil in front of their eyes.

statement.id: Mereka tinggal di hutan dan padang rumput, menghabiskan waktu dengan bernyanyi dan menari, mampu terbang, dan pada malam hari memintal benang kehidupan manusia; manusia hanya bisa melihat mereka jika mengangkat selubung tak kasatmata di depan matanya.
statement.en: They live in forests and pastures, spend their time singing and dancing, can fly, and at night spin the thread of human existence; a human can see them only by lifting an invisible veil before their eyes.

claims.quote: Occasionally humans and shtojzovalles are married, but a human can keep a shtojzovalle maiden only if he gives her his clothes to wear.

statement.id: Kadang manusia dan shtojzovalle menikah, tetapi seorang lelaki hanya dapat mempertahankan gadis shtojzovalle jika ia memberikan pakaiannya untuk dikenakan sang gadis.
statement.en: Humans and shtojzovalles occasionally marry, but a man can keep a shtojzovalle maiden only if he gives her his clothes to wear.

claims.quote: If a human builds their house on lands inhabited by shtojzovalles, the house will be haunted by shtojzovalles shaking heavy iron chains. When people go for a walk and step on a shtojzovalle they may get devoured by it.

statement.id: Jika manusia membangun rumah di tanah yang dihuni shtojzovalle, rumah itu akan dihantui shtojzovalle yang mengguncang rantai besi berat; orang yang menginjak shtojzovalle saat berjalan bisa dimangsa olehnya.
statement.en: If a human builds a house on land inhabited by shtojzovalles, it will be haunted by shtojzovalles shaking heavy iron chains; people who step on a shtojzovalle while walking may be devoured by it.

claims.quote: Albanian Christians and especially the Catholics of northern Albania and Malësia have attributed several Christian characteristics to the shtojzovalles. According to these traditions when Archangel Michael fought against Satan the angels who remained neutral became the shtojzovalles.

statement.id: Umat Kristen Albania, terutama umat Katolik di Albania utara dan Malësia, memberi shtojzovalle beberapa ciri Kristen: menurut tradisi ini, ketika Malaikat Agung Mikael melawan Setan, para malaikat yang tetap netral menjadi shtojzovalle.
statement.en: Albanian Christians, especially the Catholics of northern Albania and Malësia, gave the shtojzovalles Christian features: in these traditions, when Archangel Michael fought Satan, the angels who stayed neutral became the shtojzovalles.

claims.quote: The shtojzovalles weep in repentance for their neutrality and if their tears fall on a human he will die. The Albanian phrase i ka rënë pika (English: "a drop fell upon him"), metaphorically means that someone died and the phrase is derived from this belief.

statement.id: Shtojzovalle menangis menyesali kenetralan mereka, dan jika air mata mereka jatuh ke manusia, orang itu akan mati; ungkapan Albania i ka rënë pika ("setetes jatuh padanya"), kiasan untuk kematian seseorang, berasal dari kepercayaan ini.
statement.en: The shtojzovalles weep in repentance for their neutrality, and a human on whom their tears fall will die; the Albanian phrase i ka rënë pika ("a drop fell upon him"), a figure of speech for someone's death, comes from this belief.

claims.quote: The name shtojzovalle is a product of Pagan and Christian religious syncretism. The alternative term shtojzorreshta means "may God give increase to their rows" in English.

statement.id: Nama shtojzovalle merupakan hasil sinkretisme agama pagan dan Kristen; istilah lain, shtojzorreshta, berarti "semoga Tuhan menambah barisan mereka".
statement.en: The name shtojzovalle is a product of pagan and Christian religious syncretism; the alternative term shtojzorreshta means "may God give increase to their rows".

claims.quote: es una criaturilla danzarina y cantarina de ambos sexos de gran belleza y poderes sobrenaturales de la mitología albanesa. Habita en montes y bosques densos.

statement.id: Artikel Spanyol menyebutnya makhluk kecil penari dan penyanyi dari kedua jenis kelamin, sangat elok dan berkekuatan gaib, dalam mitologi Albania, yang tinggal di gunung dan hutan lebat.
statement.en: The Spanish article calls it a small dancing and singing creature of both sexes, of great beauty and supernatural powers, from Albanian mythology, living in mountains and dense forests.

claims.quote: Shtojzovallet janë krijesa të vogla mashkullore dhe femërore me bukuri të jashtëzakonshme. Ato jetojnë në pyje dhe kullota dhe kalojnë kohën duke kënduar dhe duke vallëzuar.

statement.id: Artikel Albania menyebut shtojzovallet sebagai makhluk kecil lelaki dan perempuan yang sangat elok, tinggal di hutan dan padang rumput, dan menghabiskan waktu dengan bernyanyi dan menari.
statement.en: The Albanian article describes the shtojzovallet as small male and female beings of extraordinary beauty who live in forests and pastures and spend their time singing and dancing.

summary.id: Mereka makhluk hutan berkekuatan gaib dalam mitologi Albania.
summary.en: They are woodland beings with supernatural powers in Albanian mythology.

summary.id: Dalam tradisi Katolik Albania utara, mereka adalah malaikat yang tetap netral saat Mikael melawan Setan.
summary.en: In the tradition of the Catholics of northern Albania they are angels who stayed neutral when Michael fought Satan.

short_description.id: Shubin adalah roh tambang dalam cerita rakyat para penambang Donbas, "tuan tambang" yang biasanya baik dan memperingatkan penambang akan bahaya.
short_description.en: Shubin is a mining spirit of Donbas miners' folklore, the "master of the mine" who is usually kind and warns miners of danger.

long_description.id: Shubin adalah roh tambang dalam mitologi. Legendanya terutama tersebar di kota-kota tambang wilayah Donbas di perbatasan Rusia dan Ukraina. Roh ini biasanya baik, tetapi bisa juga jahat. Dalam cerita rakyat penambang Donbas ia disebut Shubin yang Baik, roh tambang mirip gnome, "tuan tambang" dan pelindung para penambang.
long_description.en: Shubin is a spirit of the mines in folk myth. His legend circulates mainly in the mining towns of the Donbas on the Russia–Ukraine border. The spirit is usually kindly but can turn wicked. Donbas miners' lore calls him Good Shubin, a gnome-like mine spirit, "master of the mine" and patron of miners.

long_description.id: Asal namanya diperdebatkan. Ada yang mengaitkannya dengan julukan seorang penambang yang arwahnya berjalan di dasar tambang memakai mantel bulu sambil membawa obor dan membakar gas tambang; ada yang mengaitkannya dengan mandor kejam bernama Shubin yang membunuh pekerja di bawah tanah; ada pula yang menurunkannya dari bunyi metana, "shu-shu". Tuturan lisan menyebut Shubin yang baik memperingatkan penambang akan bencana, dan bila terdengar batuknya, penambang harus segera lari.
long_description.en: The origin of the name is disputed: some link it to the nickname of a miner whose soul walks the bottom of the mine in a fur coat with a torch, burning off firedamp; some to a cruel mine boss named Shubin who killed workers underground; others to the "shu-shu" sound of methane. Oral lore says good Shubin warns miners of coming disasters, and when his cough is heard, it is time to run.

long_description.id: Pada September 2026, kisah-kisah penambang tentang roh pelindung Shubin dimasukkan ke Daftar Nasional Warisan Budaya Takbenda Ukraina. Kepercayaan tentangnya dicatat oleh penulis Boris Gorbatov dan Leonid Zharikov.
long_description.en: Ukraine added the miners' stories of Shubin, the protective spirit, to its national list of intangible cultural heritage in September 2026. Beliefs about him were written down by the writers Boris Gorbatov and Leonid Zharikov.

short_description.id: Sluagh ("rombongan") atau Sluagh na marbh adalah rombongan arwah orang mati yang tak diampuni dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia dan Skotlandia, yang terbang di udara.
short_description.en: The Sluagh ('host') or Sluagh na marbh are the hosts of the unforgiven dead in Irish and Scottish folklore, flying through the air.

long_description.id: Sluagh (Irlandia Kuno/Old Irish: slúag; Inggris: "rombongan, pasukan, kerumunan"), atau Sluagh na marbh ("rombongan orang mati"), adalah rombongan arwah orang mati yang tak diampuni dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish) dan Skotlandia (Scottish). Menurut folklorist Britania Lewis Spence, di Western Isles Skotlandia Sluagh atau rombongan peri dianggap terdiri atas jiwa orang mati yang terbang di udara, dan pesta orang mati pada Halloween juga perayaan para peri. Nama Gaelik Skotlandia Sluagh berasal dari Irlandia Kuno slúag dan akar Proto-Kelt *slougo-.
long_description.en: In Irish and Scottish folklore the Sluagh, from Old Irish slúag ('host, army, crowd'), also called Sluagh na marbh or 'host of the dead', were bands of the unforgiven dead. The British folklorist Lewis Spence explained that on Scotland's Western Isles this fairy host was believed to consist of dead souls travelling through the sky, and the Hallowe'en feast of the dead was also the festival of the fairies. The Scottish Gaelic name comes from Old Irish slúag and the Proto-Celtic root *slougo-.

long_description.id: Biasanya terbang dalam bentuk bulan sabit seperti kawanan burung, mereka konon dapat mendekati seseorang dari arah mana pun, mengangkatnya, dan membawanya jauh melalui udara dari satu pulau ke pulau lain. Meski kadang menyelamatkan manusia dari celah batu berbahaya, mereka umumnya digambarkan berbahaya bagi manusia. Menurut artikel fr, Sluagh digambarkan sebagai bayangan terbang berputar dengan jari panjang kurus berselaput dan kaki cacat bercakar panjang, dan kawanannya menimbulkan bayangan, bunyi kepakan sayap, serta bau daging busuk. Dalam legenda Irlandia ia menyerang orang sekarat yang masih lemah di ranjangnya.
long_description.en: Usually flying in a crescent like a flight of birds, they could come at a person from any direction, lift him and carry him far through the air from one island to another. Though they sometimes rescued people from dangerous rock clefts, they were generally shown as a danger to mortals. According to the fr article the Sluagh appears as a flying, whirling shadow with long thin webbed fingers and twisted legs ending in long claws, and its flocks bring shadow, the sound of beating wings and a smell of rotting meat. In Irish legend it preyed on the dying still weak in their beds.

short_description.id: Sooterkin adalah makhluk kecil dongeng mirip tikus mondok yang dahulu dipercaya dapat dilahirkan perempuan tertentu, dikaitkan dengan perempuan Belanda yang duduk di atas tungku.
short_description.en: The sooterkin is a fabled small mole-like creature that some women were once believed able to give birth to, blamed on Dutch women sitting over stoves.

long_description.id: Sooterkin adalah makhluk kecil dongeng mirip tikus mondok yang dahulu dipercaya dapat dilahirkan perempuan tertentu. Asal khayalan yang mula-mula bersifat lelucon ini berasal dari abad ke-18, dan sebagian dokter terkemuka masa itu menganggapnya nyata. Ia dikaitkan dengan kebiasaan perempuan Belanda (Dutch) yang sering duduk di atas tungku atau memakai penghangat di bawah rok mereka, yang konon membiakkan hewan kecil yang kemudian tumbuh dan lahir.
long_description.en: Folk belief once held that some women could give birth to a sooterkin, a small mole-like creature of fable. This at-first jokey fancy dates from the 18th century, and some leading physicians of the time took it as fact. It was blamed on Dutch women's habit of sitting on stoves or warming themselves with them under their petticoats, supposedly breeding a small animal that would grow and be born.

long_description.id: Dokter Inggris (English) John Maubray dalam The Female Physician menyatakan perempuan dapat melahirkan sooterkin; ia pendukung teori "maternal impression" dan terlibat dalam kasus Mary Toft, yang tampak membuktikan teorinya dengan "melahirkan" kelinci, meski seluruh perkara itu akhirnya terbongkar sebagai tipuan. Seseorang dengan nama samaran Dr Giovanni lalu menerbitkan The Sooterkin Dissected yang menyatakan percaya padanya adalah kebodohan. Menurut artikel de, John Cleveland pada 1654 menulis bahwa perempuan Belanda konon melahirkan sooterkin "tidak jauh berbeda dengan tikus" bersama anak-anak mereka, dan makhluk ini juga disebut Suyger.
long_description.en: The English physician John Maubray, in The Female Physician, held that women could bear sooterkins; he championed 'maternal impression' and was drawn into the case of Mary Toft, who seemed to prove his theory by 'giving birth' to rabbits, though the whole affair was finally exposed as a hoax. Someone under the alias Dr Giovanni then published The Sooterkin Dissected, calling belief in it stupidity. According to the de article John Cleveland wrote in 1654 that Dutch women were said to bear a sooterkin 'not unlike to a Rat' together with their children, and the creature is also called Suyger.

short_description.id: Strigoi adalah arwah jahat dalam mitologi Romania yang dipercaya bangkit dari kubur, dapat berubah menjadi hewan, dan menghisap tenaga dari darah korbannya.
short_description.en: Strigoi are evil spirits of Romanian mythology believed to rise from the grave, able to turn into animals and to draw vitality from their victims' blood.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Romania, strigoi dipahami sebagai arwah orang mati yang gelisah dan jahat, yang dipercaya keluar dari kubur pada malam hari. Mereka dapat menjelma menjadi binatang atau sosok seperti hantu, bisa menjadi tak kasatmata, dan memperoleh daya hidup dari darah korban. Tujuannya adalah mencelakai orang yang masih hidup.
long_description.en: In Romanian mythology, strigoi are understood as restless, evil souls of the dead believed to leave the grave at night. They can take the shape of an animal or a ghostly apparition, can become invisible, and gain vitality from the blood of their victims. Their aim is to bring harm to the living.

long_description.id: Ada strigoi hidup dan strigoi mati. Strigoi viu adalah strigoi hidup atau tukang sihir, sedangkan strigoi mort, strigoi mati, dianggap paling berbahaya karena keluar dari kubur untuk menyiksa keluarganya sampai mereka meninggal. Menurut kepercayaan, strigoi botak di ubun-ubun, tidak memakan bawang putih dan bawang merah, serta menghindari dupa. Malam mereka adalah malam Santo Andreas (30 November), ketika mereka keluar dari kubur atau meninggalkan tubuhnya.
long_description.en: There are living and dead strigoi. A strigoi viu is a living strigoi or sorcerer, while the strigoi mort, the dead strigoi, is held to be the most dangerous, leaving the grave to torment its family until they die. By belief, a strigoi is bald on the crown, does not eat garlic or onions, and avoids incense. Their night is the night of Saint Andrew (30 November), when they leave their graves or their bodies.

long_description.id: Strigoi dipercaya mengambil susu sapi, sari gandum, dan kekuatan orang, menahan hujan, mendatangkan hujan es, serta membawa kematian bagi manusia dan ternak. Kekeringan di sebuah desa dianggap tanda adanya strigoaică, strigoi perempuan, yang menghalangi hujan. Untuk membunuhnya, kubur orang yang dicurigai dicari, imam membacakan tata doa, lalu jantungnya ditancapi pasak atau ditusuk paku atau pisau supaya ia terikat pada peti matinya.
long_description.en: Strigoi are believed to take milk from cows, the goodness of the wheat and the strength of people, to stop the rain, bring hail and bring death to people and cattle. Drought in a village was read as a sign that a strigoaică, a female strigoi, was holding back the rain. To kill one, the suspect's grave is found, priests read the rite, and a stake is driven into the heart or it is pierced with a nail or knife so that it stays bound to its coffin.

long_description.id: Nama strigoi berakar pada istilah Latin strix atau striga dengan akhiran pembesar -oi, dan berkaitan dengan kata kerja Romania a striga, "menjerit". Salah satu catatan awal tentang strigoi historis adalah kisah Jure Grando Alilović (1579–1656) dari Istria. Dimitrie Cantemir menyebut striga dalam Descriptio Moldaviae, tetapi mengaitkannya dengan penyihir, bukan dengan mayat hidup peminum darah. Kepercayaan ini bertahan lama: pada 2004 keluarga di Marotinu de Sus menggali jenazah kerabat yang dicurigai menjadi strigoi, dan polisi kemudian menangkap enam anggota keluarga itu.
long_description.en: The name goes back to the Latin terms strix or striga with the augmentative suffix -oi, and is related to the Romanian verb a striga, "to scream". The tale of Jure Grando Alilović (1579–1656) of Istria is among the earliest accounts of a real strigoi. Dimitrie Cantemir mentions the striga in Descriptio Moldaviae but links them with witches rather than blood-drinking undead. The belief has persisted: in 2004 a family in Marotinu de Sus dug up a relative suspected of becoming a strigoi, and police later arrested six of the family members.

short_description.id: Trasgu adalah peri rumah usil dari Spanyol utara dan Portugal utara, lelaki kecil pincang bertopi merah dengan tangan berlubang yang membuat keributan malam atau membantu pekerjaan rumah.
short_description.en: The trasgu is a mischievous house goblin of northern Spain and northern Portugal, a limping red-capped little man with a holed hand who makes night mischief or does the housework.

long_description.id: Trasgu, trasgo, atau trasno adalah peri rumah dalam tradisi Galisia, Asturias, Cantabria, dan Portugal utara; namanya mungkin dari bahasa Latin transgredī, "melanggar". Ia lelaki kecil berkulit gelap yang pincang kaki kanan, berpakaian dan bertopi merah, dengan lubang di tangan kiri. Pada malam hari ia membuat keributan dan memindahkan barang, tetapi bila diperlakukan baik ia mengerjakan pekerjaan rumah.
long_description.en: The trasgu, trasgo or trasno is a house goblin of Galician, Asturian, Cantabrian and northern Portuguese tradition; its name may come from Latin transgredī, 'to transgress'. He is a small dark man limping on his right leg, dressed and capped in red, with a hole in his left hand. At night he makes noise and moves things, but if treated well he does the housework.

long_description.id: Ia sulit diusir: dalam sebuah kisah ia ikut pindah sambil membawa lampu yang tertinggal. Cara mengusirnya adalah memberi tugas mustahil, seperti memungut jawawut dengan tangannya yang berlubang. Ia punya banyak nama daerah seperti Cornín dan Xuan Dos Camíos, dan dari Trás-os-Montes mitosnya menyebar hingga melahirkan Saci di Brasil.
long_description.en: He is hard to shake off: in one tale he moves house with the family, carrying the lamp they forgot. The way to expel him is an impossible task, such as picking up millet with his holed hand. He has many local names such as Cornín and Xuan Dos Camíos, and from Trás-os-Montes the myth spread to give rise to the Saci in Brazil.

summary.id: Sebuah keluarga pindah karena trasgu; ketika sang istri bertanya apa yang tertinggal, trasgu yang mengikuti mereka menjawab bahwa ia membawa lampunya.
summary.en: A family moves to escape the trasgu; when the wife asks what was left behind, the trasgu following them says he is carrying the lamp.

claims.quote: The trasgo, trasno or trasgu is a mythological creature present in the tradition of several cultures of what is now northern Spain, especially in  Galician, Asturian and Cantabrian traditional culture, it is also found in legends of North Portugal.

statement.id: Trasgo, trasno, atau trasgu adalah makhluk mitologis dalam tradisi beberapa budaya Spanyol utara, terutama Galisia, Asturias, dan Cantabria, juga dalam legenda Portugal utara.
statement.en: The trasgo, trasno or trasgu is a mythological creature in the traditions of several cultures of northern Spain, especially Galician, Asturian and Cantabrian, and also in legends of northern Portugal.

claims.quote: It is a domestic goblin with a mischievous and nervous character. It is often represented as a tiny man who limps with his right leg; he has dark skin, wears red clothes and a pointy red hat. He has a hole in his left hand.

statement.id: Ia peri rumah yang usil dan gelisah, sering digambarkan sebagai lelaki kecil yang pincang kaki kanan, berkulit gelap, berpakaian merah dan bertopi merah runcing, dengan lubang di tangan kirinya.
statement.en: It is a mischievous, restless house goblin, often shown as a tiny man limping on his right leg, dark-skinned, in red clothes and a pointed red hat, with a hole in his left hand.

claims.quote: Nocturnal noises are attributed to him, and also small pranks like changing the location of objects. He enters homes at night when the inhabitants are asleep.

statement.id: Suara-suara malam dan keusilan kecil seperti memindahkan barang dianggap ulahnya; ia masuk ke rumah pada malam hari ketika penghuninya tidur.
statement.en: Night noises and small pranks such as moving objects are blamed on him; he enters homes at night while the household sleeps.

claims.quote: On the other hand, when he is treated well, he does house chores during the night.

statement.id: Sebaliknya, bila diperlakukan baik, ia mengerjakan pekerjaan rumah pada malam hari.
statement.en: On the other hand, when treated well, he does the housework at night.

claims.quote: In a tale, the inhabitants of a house abandoned it because of the trasgu. On their way to the new house, the woman asks her husband: "Have we left anything?" The trasgu, following them, answers: "You have left the lamp, but I'm carrying it."

statement.id: Dalam sebuah kisah, penghuni rumah pindah karena trasgu; di jalan sang istri bertanya apakah ada yang tertinggal, dan trasgu yang mengikuti mereka menjawab, "Kalian meninggalkan lampu, tapi aku membawanya."
statement.en: In one tale a household moves away because of the trasgu; on the way the wife asks whether they left anything, and the trasgu, following them, answers: 'You left the lamp, but I'm carrying it.'

claims.quote: In order to expel a trasgu it is necessary to request of him an impossible task, like bringing a basket of water from the sea, picking up millet from the floor (it falls through the hole in his hand), and whitening a black sheep.

statement.id: Untuk mengusir trasgu ia harus diberi tugas mustahil, seperti membawa air laut dalam keranjang, memungut biji jawawut dari lantai (yang jatuh lewat lubang di tangannya), atau memutihkan domba hitam.
statement.en: To get rid of a trasgu one must set him an impossible task, such as carrying sea water in a basket, picking millet off the floor (it falls through the hole in his hand) or whitening a black sheep.

claims.quote: In Asturias, the trasgu is known by different names depending on the location. He is known as Trasno, Cornín or Xuan Dos Camíos in western Asturias.

statement.id: Di Asturias trasgu punya nama berbeda menurut tempat, seperti Trasno, Cornín, atau Xuan Dos Camíos di Asturias barat.
statement.en: In Asturias the trasgu has different names by place, such as Trasno, Cornín or Xuan Dos Camíos in western Asturias.

claims.quote: Trasgu or trasno (in Galician and Portuguese) is very common in the folklore of Trás-os-Montes and it was taken by the Portuguese throughout their empire originating similar myths like the Saci in Brazil.

statement.id: Trasgu atau trasno sangat umum dalam cerita rakyat Trás-os-Montes dan dibawa orang Portugis ke seluruh kekaisaran mereka, melahirkan mitos serupa seperti Saci di Brasil.
statement.en: The trasgu or trasno is very common in the folklore of Trás-os-Montes and was carried by the Portuguese across their empire, giving rise to similar myths such as the Saci in Brazil.

claims.quote: Del latín transgredī ('el que transgrede, el que rompe con la ley')  se le denomina trasgo, trasno o tardo en Galicia

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, namanya dari bahasa Latin transgredī, "yang melanggar", dan di Galisia ia disebut trasgo, trasno, atau tardo.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, the name comes from Latin transgredī, 'one who transgresses', and in Galicia he is called trasgo, trasno or tardo.

claims.quote: Тресго наиболее известны в астурийской мифологии. Это домашний гоблин с озорным и нервным характером.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Rusia juga menyebut trasgu makhluk paling terkenal dalam mitologi Asturias, peri rumah yang usil dan gelisah.
statement.en: The Russian article also calls the trasgu the best-known being of Asturian mythology, a mischievous, restless house goblin.

short_description.id: Trenti adalah goblin hutan jahil dalam mitologi Cantabria, berwajah hitam dan bermata hijau, yang suka menarik rok perempuan tetapi diam-diam menolong orang.
short_description.en: The Trenti is a mischievous forest goblin of Cantabrian mythology, black-faced and green-eyed, that pulls women's skirts but secretly helps people.

long_description.id: Trenti adalah goblin hutan dalam mitologi Cantabria yang menjengkelkan tetapi tidak jahat. Ia sulit dilihat karena mirip jamur, daun, dan lumut, wajahnya hitam legam, dan matanya hijau. Ia suka melompat dari semak untuk menakuti pejalan dan menarik rok perempuan.
long_description.en: The Trenti is a forest goblin of Cantabrian mythology, annoying but not malicious. It is hard to see because it looks like mushrooms, leaves and moss, with an all-black face and green eyes. It likes jumping out of bushes to scare walkers and pulling women's skirts.

long_description.id: Diam-diam ia juga menolong manusia, terutama anak-anak, gembala yang kehilangan ternak setelah badai atau ulah Ojáncanu, dan nenek-nenek yang lemah. Ia makan jagung dan buah blackthorn tetapi tidak pernah minum air, yang beracun baginya; musim dingin ia tidur di lubang tanah dan musim panas di bawah pohon.
long_description.en: It also secretly helps people, especially children, shepherds whose flocks were scattered by storms or the Ojáncanu, and frail old women. It eats corncobs and sloes but never drinks water, which poisons it; in winter it sleeps in sinkholes and in summer under trees.

short_description.id: Tzitzimitl adalah dewi langit Aztek yang dikaitkan dengan bintang dan kesuburan, digambarkan sebagai sosok perempuan berwujud kerangka, dan ditakuti saat gerhana matahari.
short_description.en: A Tzitzimitl is an Aztec celestial goddess linked to the stars and fertility, shown as a skeletal female figure and feared during solar eclipses.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Aztek, Tzitzimitl (jamak Tzitzimimeh) adalah dewi langit yang dikaitkan dengan bintang. Mereka digambarkan sebagai perempuan berwujud kerangka yang memakai rok bermotif tengkorak; dalam Codex Magliabechiano roknya berhias kerang. Uraian pascapenaklukan sering menyebut mereka iblis, tetapi sebutan itu belum tentu sesuai dengan fungsi mereka.
long_description.en: In Aztec mythology a Tzitzimitl (plural Tzitzimimeh) is a celestial goddess linked to the stars. They were shown as skeletal women wearing skirts with skull designs; in the Codex Magliabechiano the skirts are edged with shells. Post-conquest accounts often call them demons, but that label does not necessarily match their role.

long_description.id: Tzitzimimeh adalah dewi kesuburan yang dipuja bidan dan perempuan yang akan melahirkan. Pemimpin mereka adalah Itzpapalotl, penguasa surga Tamoanchan. Mereka berperan ganda sebagai pelindung kaum perempuan dan leluhur umat manusia.
long_description.en: The Tzitzimimeh were fertility goddesses worshipped by midwives and women in childbirth. Their leader was Itzpapalotl, ruler of the paradise Tamoanchan. They had a double role as protectors of women and ancestresses of humankind.

long_description.id: Mereka juga ditakuti. Bintang yang tampak saat gerhana matahari ditafsirkan sebagai Tzitzimimeh yang menyerang Matahari dan turun merasuki manusia. Bila upacara api baru di akhir siklus kalender 52 tahun gagal, mereka dipercaya akan memangsa manusia terakhir; mereka juga ditakuti pada lima hari sial Nemontemi.
long_description.en: They were also feared. Stars visible during a solar eclipse were read as Tzitzimimeh attacking the Sun and descending to possess people. If the new-fire rite at the end of the 52-year calendar round failed, they were expected to devour the last people; they were also feared during the five unlucky Nemontemi days.

short_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Slavia, arwah najis adalah orang yang mati secara tidak wajar, tidak menemukan kedamaian, dan dipercaya kembali ke dunia orang hidup sebagai makhluk jahat.
short_description.en: In Slavic folklore the unclean dead are people who died an unnatural death, found no peace, and were believed to return to the world of the living as malevolent beings.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan Slavia, arwah najis adalah orang yang mati secara tidak wajar atau hidup dengan buruk, sehingga jiwanya tidak bisa pergi ke alam baka dan mengembara di bumi. Mereka dipercaya kembali ke dunia orang hidup sebagai makhluk jahat. Yang biasanya digolongkan ke dalamnya adalah korban kekerasan, orang yang bunuh diri, mati karena mabuk atau tenggelam, anak yang belum dibaptis, dukun, dan penyihir.
long_description.en: In Slavic belief the unclean dead are people who died an unnatural death or lived a bad life, so that their souls cannot pass into the afterlife and wander the earth instead. They were believed to return to the world of the living as malevolent beings. They typically included victims of violence, suicides, those who died of drink or by drowning, unbaptised children, sorcerers and witches.

long_description.id: Istilah ilmiah zalozhnye pokoiniki diperkenalkan etnografer Dmitry Zelenin pada awal abad ke-20, karena tradisi-tradisi Slavia tidak punya satu nama bersama untuk mereka. Zelenin mengaitkan kata itu dengan cara penguburannya: jasad diletakkan telungkup dan kuburnya ditutup batu serta ranting. Arwah najis tidak dimakamkan di pemakaman gereja, melainkan di persimpangan jalan, batas ladang, hutan, rawa, atau jurang, karena bumi dipercaya tidak mau menerima mereka.
long_description.en: The scholarly term zalozhnye pokoiniki was introduced by the ethnographer Dmitry Zelenin in the early 20th century, since the Slavic traditions had no single shared name for them. Zelenin linked the word to the manner of burial: the body was laid face down and the grave sealed with stones and branches. The unclean dead were not buried in church cemeteries but at crossroads, field boundaries, forests, swamps or ravines, because the earth was believed to refuse them.

long_description.id: Arwah najis dipercaya mendatangkan bencana. Di Kegubernuran Simbirsk, saat kemarau orang menggali jasad pemabuk dan membuangnya ke rawa agar hujan turun, dan legenda Baturka yang rakus menuntut persembahan dari orang yang lewat agar mereka dan ternaknya tidak jatuh sakit. Di Belarus orang yang melewati tempat kematian karena kekerasan melemparkan batu, ranting, jerami, atau tanah ke sana, dan di tempat lain biji poppy yang diberkati ditaruh di kubur agar si mati tidak mendatangi orang hidup.
long_description.en: The unclean dead were believed to bring misfortune. In Simbirsk Governorate, in a drought, people dug up a drunkard's body and threw it into a swamp to bring rain, and the legend of greedy Baturka demanded offerings from passers-by lest they and their livestock fall ill. In Belarus people passing a place of violent death threw stones, branches, straw or earth onto it, and elsewhere blessed poppy seed was placed in the grave so the dead would not visit the living.

short_description.id: Vahana adalah golongan makhluk, biasanya hewan atau makhluk mitos, yang menjadi kendaraan dewa Hindu.
short_description.en: Vahana denotes beings, usually animals or mythical creatures, serving as Hindu deities' vehicles.

long_description.id: Vahana adalah golongan makhluk, biasanya hewan atau makhluk mitos, yang menjadi kendaraan dewa Hindu. Dewa digambarkan menaikinya atau vahana berada di samping dewa sebagai atribut.
long_description.en: Vahana denotes beings, usually animals or mythical creatures, serving as Hindu deities' vehicles. Deities are depicted riding them or vahanas stand beside deities as attributes.

long_description.id: Akar Sanskerta vah berarti membawa atau mengangkut. Nandi sebagai kendaraan Shiva melambangkan kekuatan; hamsa Saraswati melambangkan kebijaksanaan. Kendaraan ilahi juga dapat melambangkan kekuatan negatif yang ditaklukkan dewanya. Dalam retelling Mackenzie, gajah putih Airavata menjadi tunggangan Indra.
long_description.en: The Sanskrit root vah means to carry or transport. Nandi as Shiva's vehicle symbolizes strength; Saraswati's hamsa symbolizes wisdom. Divine vehicles can also symbolize negative forces overcome by their deities. In Mackenzie's retelling the white elephant Airavata is Indra's mount.

cultural_context.id: Entri pengayaan ini membahas golongan tunggangan ilahi, bukan satu individu bernama Vahana.

short_description.id: Vâlvă adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania yang berjalan di puncak bukit pada malam hari; ada yang baik (Vâlve Putih) dan ada yang jahat (Vâlve Hitam), dan banyak jenisnya menjaga tempat atau harta tertentu.
short_description.en: The vâlvă is a female spirit of Romanian folklore who walks the hilltops at night; some are good (White Vâlve) and some evil (Black Vâlve), and many kinds guard particular places or treasures.

long_description.id: Vâlvă adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania yang dipercaya berjalan di puncak bukit pada malam hari. Ada Vâlve Albe yang baik dan Vâlve Negre yang jahat. Mereka sering tampil sebagai perempuan, tetapi bisa juga muncul sebagai bayangan atau kucing hitam, dan dapat melindungi desa dari badai, hujan es, dan angin topan.
long_description.en: The vâlvă is a female spirit of Romanian folklore believed to walk the hilltops at night. There are the good Vâlve Albe and the evil Vâlve Negre. They often appear as women but may also come as shadows or black cats, and they can protect a village from storm, hail and hurricane.

long_description.id: Vâlve terbagi dalam banyak jenis menurut apa yang mereka jaga. Vâlva Apei melindungi mata air dan pancuran, Vâlva Comorilor menjaga harta dan bisa menunjukkan tempat harta terkubur, dan Vâlva Ciumei menguasai wabah sampar serta penyakit lain. Vâlva Băilor melindungi tambang; kepergiannya menandakan bijih akan habis.
long_description.en: The vâlve fall into many kinds according to what they guard. Vâlva Apei protects water sources and fountains, Vâlva Comorilor guards treasures and can reveal where they are buried, and Vâlva Ciumei controls plague and other diseases. Vâlva Băilor protects mines; her departure signals that the ore is running out.

long_description.id: Ada pula pandangan lain: vâlve adalah anak-anak yang dikandung pada hari raya besar dan lahir dengan semacam topi kecil berwarna merah di kepala. Para solomonar pun konon termasuk Vâlve, orang-orang berbeda yang memiliki kekuatan istimewa.
long_description.en: Another view holds that vâlve are children conceived on great feast days and born with a small red cap on the head. The solomonari, too, are said to be Vâlve, different people with special powers.

short_description.id: Zheuzhyk adalah penjaga sungai dan danau dalam mitologi Belarus, lelaki tua kurus berjanggut merah yang menolong orang dalam kesulitan di air.
short_description.en: Zheuzhyk is the guardian of rivers and lakes in Belarusian mythology, a thin red-bearded old man who rescues people in trouble on the water.

long_description.id: Zheuzhyk adalah makhluk baik dalam mitologi Belarus yang tinggal jauh di dasar danau dan dianggap penjaga sungai dan danau di Belarus. Ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua kurus berjanggut merah panjang dengan lengan dan kaki panjang. Pada siang hari ia berenang di bawah air, dan pada malam hari mengelilingi wilayahnya dengan perahu sambil membelah ombak.
long_description.en: Zheuzhyk is a good being of Belarusian mythology living deep in the lake bed and regarded as the guardian of the rivers and lakes of Belarus. He is pictured as a lean old man with a long red beard and long limbs. By day he swims underwater, and by night he rounds his domain by boat, parting the waves.

long_description.id: Dipercaya bahwa Zheuzhyk pasti datang menolong orang yang mendapat kesulitan di air, dan ia cukup kuat untuk menghentikan angin dan badai. Semua roh air, termasuk Vadavik dan Lazavik, tunduk kepadanya, dan namanya muncul dalam peribahasa tentang kecekatan. Namun sebagai dewa air Belarus kuno, ia digambarkan dan kemungkinan dikarang oleh folkloris Pavel Shpilevsky.
long_description.en: Zheuzhyk is believed to come without fail to rescue anyone in trouble on the water, and is strong enough to stop wind and storm. All water spirits, including the Vadavik and Lazavik, obey him, and his name appears in sayings about nimbleness. As an ancient Belarusian water god, however, he was described and probably invented by the folklorist Pavel Shpilevsky.

short_description.id: Minairó adalah makhluk mungil pekerja keras dari Pyrenees Katalonia yang disimpan ribuan di dalam tabung jarum dan selalu menuntut pekerjaan, membawa kemakmuran bagi pemiliknya.
short_description.en: The minairó is a tiny hard-working being of the Catalan Pyrenees, kept by the thousand in a needle case and always demanding work, which brings its owner prosperity.

long_description.id: Minairó, juga diablorí di Katalonia atau zaingorriak di negeri Basque, adalah makhluk sangat kecil yang di desa-desa Pyrenees disimpan ribuan dalam tabung jarum. Mereka berasal dari St John's-wort yang tumbuh di gua dalam yang dijaga raksasa dan naga dan hanya dapat diambil tengah malam Santo Yohanes. Mereka mendengung seperti lebah atau nyamuk dan begitu keluar menuntut, "Apa yang kita kerjakan? Apa yang kita katakan?"
long_description.en: The minairó, called diablorí by some in Catalonia and zaingorriak in the Basque lands, is a tiny being kept by the thousand in a needle case in Pyrenean villages. They come from St John's-wort, which grows in deep caves guarded by giants and dragons and can only be taken at midnight on St John's Day. They buzz like bees or mosquitoes and on coming out demand, 'What shall we do? What shall we say?'

long_description.id: Pemilik tabung menjadi makmur, tetapi bila pembukanya tidak segera memberi tugas, mereka bisa membunuhnya; banyak hamparan batu longsoran di Pyrenees konon hasil kerja mereka ketika tabung terbuka tak sengaja. Di negeri Basque, roh kecil serupa disebut mamarroak atau galtzagorriak dan melindungi keluarga.
long_description.en: Owners of the case prospered, but if the opener did not give them a task at once they might kill him; many Pyrenean screes are said to be their work when a case was opened by accident. In the Basque Country similar small spirits are the mamarroak or galtzagorriak, who protect the family.

who.en: Tiny working beings.

role.en: Do any work for their owner.

famous_for.en: 'What shall we do? What shall we say?'

claims.quote: A minairó (Catalan pronunciation: [minəjˈɾo], plural minairons), also called manairó, menairó, diablorí in Catalonia or zaingorriak in the Basque country, is a tiny mythological being that some people save enclosed within a needle tube in some villages of the Pyrenees.

statement.id: Minairó (jamak minairons), juga manairó, menairó, diablorí di Katalonia atau zaingorriak di negeri Basque, adalah makhluk mitis mungil yang di beberapa desa Pyrenees disimpan dalam tabung jarum.
statement.en: A minairó (plural minairons), also manairó, menairó, diablorí in Catalonia or zaingorriak in the Basque Country, is a tiny mythical being that some people keep shut in a needle case in villages of the Pyrenees.

claims.quote: The minairons come from the perforate St John's-wort which blooms at the Saint John’s (the summer solstice) night. It grows in very deep caves guarded by giants and dragons and it only can be caught in the point of midnight on St. John’s Day.

statement.id: Minairons berasal dari tumbuhan St John's-wort yang mekar pada malam Santo Yohanes (titik balik matahari musim panas), tumbuh di gua sangat dalam yang dijaga raksasa dan naga, dan hanya dapat diambil tepat tengah malam hari Santo Yohanes.
statement.en: Minairons come from St John's-wort, which blooms on St John's Night (the summer solstice), grows in very deep caves guarded by giants and dragons, and can only be taken at midnight on St John's Day.

claims.quote: Others say that they are as a swarm of tiny mosquitoes, almost invisible. Some people prefer to compare them with the bee, because of the noise they do buzzing when left the needles’ tube or cane.

statement.id: Sebagian orang menyebut mereka seperti kawanan nyamuk kecil yang hampir tak terlihat, yang lain membandingkannya dengan lebah karena dengungnya saat keluar dari tabung jarum.
statement.en: Some say they are like a swarm of tiny, almost invisible mosquitoes; others compare them to bees for the buzzing they make leaving the needle case.

claims.quote: No one doubts, however, that they are so tiny that inside the cane there must be thousands and when one foregrounds, eager demands for work, saying, "What will we do? What will we say?”

statement.id: Mereka begitu kecil sehingga ribuan muat dalam tabung, dan begitu keluar mereka menuntut pekerjaan sambil berkata, "Apa yang kita kerjakan? Apa yang kita katakan?"
statement.en: They are so tiny that thousands fit in the case, and when they come out they demand work, saying, 'What shall we do? What shall we say?'

claims.quote: The legend says that many of the screes of the Pyrenees have been works of these goblins, when his master opened the needle tube by mistake or accident

statement.id: Legenda menyebut banyak hamparan batu longsoran di Pyrenees adalah buatan mereka ketika tuannya tidak sengaja membuka tabung jarum.
statement.en: Legend says many of the Pyrenean screes are their work, made when a master opened the needle case by mistake.

claims.quote: A handful of heirs of the Pyrenees main houses have been, on occasion, owners of the cane, through which the house went up like a mushroom.

statement.id: Sejumlah pewaris rumah besar di Pyrenees konon memiliki tabung itu, sehingga rumah mereka makmur dengan cepat.
statement.en: A few heirs of great Pyrenean houses reputedly owned the case, through which their house rose like a mushroom.

claims.quote: Al abrirse el canuto, los minairones salían y decían: què farem?, què direm? -"¿qué haremos, qué diremos?"- y si la persona que lo había abierto no les ordenaba hacer algún trabajo inmediatamente, lo mataban

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, bila tabung dibuka dan pembukanya tidak segera memberi pekerjaan, minairons membunuhnya.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, when the case was opened, if the opener did not set them work at once, the minairons killed him.

claims.quote: Mamarro ou les mamarroak sont des Ireluak ou génies de petite taille issus de la mythologie basque, ils aident les gens dans leurs tâches quotidiennes et protègent la famille dans laquelle ils vivent.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, padanan Basque-nya, mamarro atau mamarroak, adalah roh kecil yang membantu pekerjaan sehari-hari dan melindungi keluarga tempat mereka tinggal.
statement.en: According to the French article, the Basque counterpart, mamarro or mamarroak, are small spirits who help with daily tasks and protect the family they live with.

claims.quote: Ces petits elfes portent les noms de Galtzagorriak, Prakagorriak, Famerijaleak à Kortezubi, Beharreztanak à Orozko, Aidetikakoak à Sare, Patuak ou Patuek à Ibarruri, Zaingorriak à Ordizia

statement.id: Peri kecil ini juga disebut Galtzagorriak, Prakagorriak, dan Zaingorriak di Ordizia, di antara nama lain.
statement.en: These little elves are also called Galtzagorriak, Prakagorriak and Zaingorriak at Ordizia, among other names.

short_description.id: Babay adalah roh malam (momok) dalam cerita rakyat Slavia yang menurut kepercayaan menculik anak-anak yang tidak tidur atau nakal.
short_description.en: Babay is a night spirit (bogeyman) of Slavic folklore who, by belief, abducts children who do not sleep or misbehave.

long_description.id: Babay adalah roh malam, semacam momok, dalam cerita rakyat Slavia. Menurut kepercayaan, ia menculik anak-anak yang tidak tidur pada malam hari atau berkelakuan buruk. Ia juga disebut Babayka, Babayko dalam bahasa Ukraina, atau Bobo dalam bahasa Polandia.
long_description.en: Babay is a night spirit, a bogeyman, of Slavic lore. He is believed to carry off children who stay awake at night or misbehave. He is also called Babayka, Babayko in Ukrainian, or Bobo in Polish.

long_description.id: Babay jarang digambarkan agar anak-anak membayangkannya dalam wujud yang paling menakutkan bagi mereka, tetapi kadang ia lelaki tua hitam bengkok dengan cacat seperti bisu, tak berlengan, atau pincang, membawa karung dan tongkat. Ia dipercaya tinggal di hutan, rawa, atau kebun, berkeliling jalan pada malam hari, dan memasukkan orang yang ditemuinya ke dalam karung; ia mengintip anak-anak dari jendela dan kadang bersembunyi di bawah tempat tidur.
long_description.en: Babay is seldom described, so that each child pictures him in the form they fear most, but at times he is a black, crooked old man with defects such as muteness, armlessness or a limp, carrying a sack and a cane. He is said to live in the forest, a swamp or a garden, to roam the streets by night stuffing anyone he meets into his sack, to peer at children through windows and sometimes to hide under the bed.

long_description.id: Kata babay kemungkinan besar berasal dari bahasa Turkik dan dari bahasa Tatar berarti "kakek" atau "lelaki tua". Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Polandia, bobo adalah makhluk kecil, buruk rupa, dan jahat yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak; Peregrynacja dziadowska dari awal abad ke-17 menyebut bobo memukul anak-anak dan merusak rumah.
long_description.en: The word babay is most likely Turkic, meaning "grandfather" or "old man" in Tatar. In Polish folk belief the bobo was a small, ugly, spiteful being used to frighten children; the early 17th-century Peregrynacja dziadowska says the bobo beat children and caused damage in the house.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari cerita rakyat Slavia.

role.en: He scares children into sleeping.

short_description.id: Bogle adalah istilah Northumbria, Cumbria dan Skotlandia untuk hantu atau makhluk folklor yang gemar membingungkan manusia.
short_description.en: Bogle is a Northumbrian, Cumbrian and Scots word for a ghost or folk being that exists to puzzle people.

long_description.id: Bogle, boggle atau bogill adalah istilah Northumbria, Cumbria dan Skotlandia untuk hantu atau makhluk folklor, dipakai untuk berbagai makhluk terkait seperti Shellycoat, Barghest, Brag, Hedley Kow, bahkan raksasa. Mereka konon hidup semata untuk membingungkan manusia, bukan untuk benar-benar mencelakai atau melayani. Namanya berasal dari kata Inggris Pertengahan Bugge, asal kata bogey juga.
long_description.en: Bogle, boggle or bogill is a Northumbrian, Cumbrian and Scots word for a ghost or folkloric being, covering related creatures such as the Shellycoat, Barghest, Brag, the Hedley Kow and even giants. Bogles are said to exist simply to baffle people rather than to do them real harm or service. The word comes from Middle English Bugge, the source of bogey as well.

long_description.id: Gavin Douglas, yang dikutip Robert Burns di awal Tam O' Shanter, menulis "Of Brownyis and of Bogillis full is this Buke". Kisah populer Tatty Bogle bercerita tentang bogle yang bersembunyi di ladang kentang untuk menyerang orang atau merusak tanaman, dan digambarkan sebagai orang-orangan sawah. Dalam bahasa Gaelik Skotlandia, padanannya bòcan digambarkan sebagai peri jahat atau hantu.
long_description.en: Gavin Douglas, quoted by Robert Burns at the start of Tam O' Shanter, wrote 'Of Brownyis and of Bogillis full is this Buke'. A popular tale tells of Tatty Bogle, who hid in potato fields to attack careless people or blight the crop and was pictured as a scarecrow. Its Scottish Gaelic counterpart, the bòcan, is described as an evil fairy or ghost.

short_description.id: Pitsen adalah roh penguasa hutan dalam mitologi Tatar Siberia yang dapat membawa keberuntungan atau menyesatkan orang, dan pandai berubah wujud.
short_description.en: Pitsen is the forest spirit-master of Siberian Tatar mythology who can bring luck or lead people astray and is a skilled shapeshifter.

long_description.id: Pitsen adalah roh penguasa hutan dalam mitologi Tatar Siberia, padanan Arçuri dari Chuvash dan Şüräle dari Tatar Volga-Ural. Perannya bertentangan: ia bisa membawa keberuntungan, tetapi juga menyesatkan orang ke belantara. Ia sering menjelma orang tua bertongkat atau hewan seperti kera, tinggal di pondok terbengkalai, dan suka menunggang kuda sambil mengolesi surainya dengan ter.
long_description.en: Pitsen is the forest spirit-master of Siberian Tatar mythology, a counterpart of the Chuvash Arçuri and the Volga-Ural Tatar Şüräle. Its role is contradictory: it can bring luck but also lead people into the wilderness. It often appears as an old man with a staff or as animals such as apes, lives in derelict lodges and likes to ride horses and smear their manes with tar.

short_description.id: Conde Estruch adalah bangsawan Katalan abad ke-12 yang menurut kisahnya menjadi vampir; para sejarawan meragukan bahwa legenda ini benar-benar tradisi lama.
short_description.en: Conde Estruch is a 12th-century Catalan noble said to have become a vampire; historians doubt that the legend is genuinely old.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Katalan, Comte Estruch, juga dikenal sebagai Arnald Estruc atau Wilfred Estruch, adalah bangsawan Katalan abad ke-12 yang menjadi vampir. Kisah ini disebut sebagai salah satu dari sedikit mitos Iberia yang berkaitan dengan vampirisme.
long_description.en: Catalan myth tells of Comte Estruch, also called Arnald Estruc or Wilfred Estruch, a twelfth-century Catalan nobleman who turned into a vampire. The tale is described as one of the few Iberian myths connected with vampirism.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, Raja Alfons II dari Aragon mengirim sang bangsawan tua ke Kastel Llers untuk memerangi paganisme dan sihir, dan ia terbunuh di sana pada 1173. Setelah mati ia mengisap darah penduduk dan menghamili perempuan muda, yang sembilan bulan kemudian melahirkan bayi-bayi mengerikan yang mati saat lahir. Ia akhirnya dibunuh, dalam satu versi oleh seorang biarawati tua, dalam versi lain oleh pertapa Yahudi dengan ritual Kabbalah.
long_description.en: Legend says King Alfons II of Aragon sent the aged noble to Llers Castle to fight paganism and witchcraft, and he was killed there in 1173. After death he drank villagers' blood and got young women pregnant; nine months later they bore monstrous babies who died at birth. He was finally destroyed, in one version by an old nun, in another by a Jewish hermit using rites from the Kabbalah.

long_description.id: Kisah ini dipopulerkan oleh novel Salvador Sáinz, Estruch (1991). Penulisnya tidak pernah membuktikan sumber abad ke-12 yang ia klaim, dan para sejarawan umumnya menolak keaslian legenda ini karena tidak ada jejak sejarah sosok Estruch.
long_description.en: The story was popularised by Salvador Sáinz's novel Estruch (1991). The author never proved the 12th-century source he claimed, and historians generally reject the legend's authenticity, as there is no historical trace of Estruch.

short_description.id: Pearlin Jean adalah hantu yang konon menghantui halaman Allanbank di Allanton, Berwickshire, Skotlandia.
short_description.en: Pearlin Jean is a ghost said to haunt the Allanbank Courtyard at Allanton in Berwickshire, Scotland.

long_description.id: Pearlin Jean adalah nama hantu yang konon menghantui halaman Allanbank di Allanton, Berwickshire, Skotlandia, bekas lokasi rumah janda di tanah milik Blackadder House yang kini sudah dirobohkan. Namanya berasal dari renda "pearlin" yang menutupi tubuhnya menurut para saksi. Menurut legenda ia berasal dari Paris, kekasih Sir Robert Stewart (diangkat Baronet pada 1684). Saat Stewart pulang ke Skotlandia, Jean menghadang keretanya; Stewart menyuruh kusir terus melaju, dan roda kereta melindas dahinya hingga ia tewas. Kata-kata terakhirnya: "Aku akan tiba di Skotlandia sebelum kamu."
long_description.en: Pearlin Jean is the name of a ghost said to haunt the Allanbank Courtyard at Allanton, Berwickshire, Scotland, once the site of a dower house on the estate of the since-demolished Blackadder House. Witnesses gave her the name because she appeared clothed in 'pearlin' lace. Legend makes her a woman from Paris and the lover of Sir Robert Stewart, created a Baronet in 1684. When Stewart left for Scotland she stood in front of his carriage; he told the driver to keep going and the wheels crushed her forehead. Her final words were, 'I'll be in Scotland before you.'

long_description.id: Ketika pertama kali kembali ke tanah miliknya, sebelum 1697, Stewart melihatnya duduk di atas gerbang dengan darah menutupi kepala dan bahunya. Tujuh pendeta setempat gagal mengusirnya. Hantu itu membanting pintu, membuka jendela dan berjalan di rumah siang malam; lama-kelamaan wujudnya menjadi kerangka berbalut renda. Pada abad ke-18 Thomas Blackadder ketakutan saat menemuinya, dan pada 1790 para tamu perempuan terganggu suara langkah kaki. Legendanya diabadikan dalam lagu pada abad ke-19.
long_description.en: On Stewart's first return to the estate, before 1697, he saw her perched above the gateway with blood covering her head and shoulders. Seven local ministers failed to exorcise her. The ghost banged doors, opened windows and roamed the house at all hours, and in time took the form of a skeleton in lace. In the 18th century Thomas Blackadder was terrified on meeting her, and in 1790 lady guests were troubled by pacing footsteps. A 19th-century song preserved the legend.

short_description.id: Dahut adalah putri dalam legenda dan sastra Breton yang dikaitkan dengan legenda kota tenggelam Ys, yang kehancurannya disebabkan olehnya.
short_description.en: Dahut is a princess of Breton legend and literature linked with the legend of the drowned city of Ys, whose ruin she caused.

long_description.id: Dahut, juga dieja Dahud, adalah putri dalam legenda dan sastra Breton yang dikaitkan dengan legenda kota tenggelam Ys. Namanya berasal dari Breton Kuno (Old Breton) da, "baik", dan hud, "sihir". Sebutan tertua tentang Ys dan rajanya Gradlon dari abad ke-15 tidak menyebut Dahut, dan raja sendirilah yang disalahkan; Dahut pertama disebut dalam edisi ketiga Vie des Saincts de la Bretagne Armorique karya Albert Le Grand (1680), sebagai putri "tak tahu malu" yang hendak membunuh ayahnya dan mencuri kunci lambang kerajaannya.
long_description.en: Dahut, also spelled Dahud, is a princess of Breton legend and literature tied to the tale of the drowned city of Ys. Her name comes from Old Breton da, 'good', and hud, 'magic'. The earliest 15th-century mentions of Ys and its king Gradlon leave Dahut out and blame the king himself; her first appearance is in Albert Le Grand's Vie des Saincts de la Bretagne Armorique, in its third edition of 1680, as a 'shameless' daughter plotting to kill her father and stealing the key that stood for his kingship.

long_description.id: Dalam kebanyakan versi, Ys dilindungi tanggul yang kuncinya dipegang Raja Gradlon; Dahut, perempuan muda jahat dan bernafsu, mencuri kunci perak atau emas dan saat bersenang-senang dengan kekasihnya, kadang Iblis sendiri, membuka gerbang sehingga laut membanjiri kota. Gradlon melarikan diri berkuda dengan Dahut di belakangnya, dan begitu Dahut jatuh ke air ia dapat selamat. Dalam beberapa versi Dahut berubah menjadi Mari-morgan atau putri duyung yang nyanyiannya masih terdengar. Menurut artikel fr, Dahut kerap dikacaukan dengan Ahès dan kemungkinan berasal dari sosok perempuan Dunia Lain dalam mitologi Kelt, mungkin dewi ibu atau peri penjaga pintu air.
long_description.en: In most versions Ys is guarded by a dike whose keys King Gradlon holds; Dahut, wicked and lustful, steals the silver or gold keys and, carousing with her lover, sometimes the Devil himself, opens the gate so the sea floods the city. Gradlon flees on horseback with Dahut behind him, and once she falls into the water he escapes. In some versions Dahut becomes a Mari-morgan or mermaid whose singing can still be heard. According to the fr article Dahut is often confused with Ahès and probably comes from an Otherworld woman of Celtic myth, perhaps a mother goddess or a fairy guarding the sluice gates.

claims.quote: In most retellings, the city of Ys is protected from floods by a dike, with King Gradlon possessing the keys to its gate. His daughter, Dahut, is a wicked and lustful young woman. In some versions she has many lovers, whom she murders, until the Devil himself comes to seduce her.

claims.quote: In some versions, Dahut transforms into a Mari-morgan or mermaid who haunts the area and can still be heard singing.

short_description.id: Elemental adalah makhluk gaib dari tradisi okultisme dan alkimia Renaisans, terutama Paracelsus, yang membaginya menjadi gnome, undine, sylph, dan salamander untuk empat unsur.
short_description.en: Elementals are supernatural beings of Renaissance occult and alchemical tradition, above all Paracelsus, who divided them into gnomes, undines, sylphs and salamanders for the four elements.

long_description.id: Elemental adalah makhluk gaib yang dikembangkan dalam karya okultisme dan alkimia Renaisans, terutama oleh Paracelsus pada abad ke-16. Ia membaginya menjadi gnome (tanah), undine (air), sylph (udara), dan salamander (api) dalam bukunya yang terbit pada 1566, dan menganggap mereka makhluk di antara roh dan manusia: tak terlihat tetapi bertubuh, makan, tidur, dan berpakaian.
long_description.en: Elementals are supernatural beings developed in Renaissance occult and alchemical works, above all by Paracelsus in the 16th century. He divided them into gnomes (earth), undines (water), sylphs (air) and salamanders (fire) in his book printed in 1566, and saw them as between spirits and humans: invisible yet bodily, eating, sleeping and wearing clothes.

long_description.id: Artikel bahasa Jerman menelusuri gagasan ini ke Neoplatonisme akhir zaman kuno dan menegaskan bahwa elemental adalah tokoh filsafat dan sastra, bukan cerita rakyat; Paracelsus sendiri tidak memakai istilah elemental. Le Comte de Gabalis (1670) membahas pernikahan dengan mereka, dan kini mereka muncul dalam esoterisme modern seperti antroposofi.
long_description.en: The German article traces the idea to late-antique Neoplatonism and stresses that elementals are figures of philosophy and literature, not folklore; Paracelsus himself did not use the word elemental. Le Comte de Gabalis (1670) discusses marrying them, and today they appear in modern esotericism such as anthroposophy.

who.en: Beings of the four elements.

claims.quote: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being that is described in occult and alchemical works from around the time of the European Renaissance, and particularly elaborated in the 16th century works of Paracelsus.

statement.id: Elemental adalah makhluk gaib mitis yang digambarkan dalam karya okultisme dan alkimia sekitar masa Renaisans Eropa, terutama dikembangkan dalam karya Paracelsus abad ke-16.
statement.en: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being described in occult and alchemical works from around the European Renaissance, especially developed in Paracelsus's 16th-century writings.

claims.quote: According to Paracelsus and his subsequent followers, there are four categories of elementals, which are gnomes, undines, sylphs, and salamanders. These correspond to the four Empedoclean elements of antiquity: earth, water, air, and fire, respectively.

statement.id: Menurut Paracelsus dan pengikutnya, ada empat jenis elemental, yaitu gnome, undine, sylph, dan salamander, yang sesuai dengan empat unsur Empedokles: tanah, air, udara, dan api.
statement.en: According to Paracelsus and his followers there are four kinds of elementals, gnomes, undines, sylphs and salamanders, matching the four Empedoclean elements: earth, water, air and fire.

claims.quote: In his 16th-century work A Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus identified mythological beings as belonging to one of the four elements. Part of the Philosophia Magna, this book was first printed in 1566 after Paracelsus' death.

statement.id: Dalam A Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus menggolongkan makhluk mitologis ke dalam empat unsur; buku ini bagian Philosophia Magna dan pertama dicetak pada 1566 setelah ia wafat.
statement.en: In his Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus assigned mythological beings to the four elements; part of the Philosophia Magna, it was first printed in 1566 after his death.

claims.quote: The concept of elementals seems to have been conceived by Paracelsus in the 16th century, though he did not in fact use the term "elemental" or a German equivalent.

statement.id: Konsep elemental tampaknya diciptakan Paracelsus pada abad ke-16, walau ia sendiri tidak memakai istilah elemental atau padanannya dalam bahasa Jerman.
statement.en: The concept of elementals seems to have been devised by Paracelsus in the 16th century, though he did not actually use the word 'elemental' or a German equivalent.

claims.quote: He regarded them not so much as spirits but as beings between creatures and spirits, generally being invisible to mankind but having physical and commonly humanoid bodies, as well as eating, sleeping, and wearing clothes like humans.

statement.id: Ia menganggap mereka bukan roh semata, melainkan makhluk di antara makhluk jasmani dan roh, biasanya tak terlihat manusia tetapi bertubuh jasmani mirip manusia, makan, tidur, dan berpakaian seperti manusia.
statement.en: He saw them not so much as spirits but as beings between creatures and spirits, usually invisible to humans yet with physical, mostly humanlike bodies, eating, sleeping and wearing clothes like people.

claims.quote: Die Vorstellung von Elementargeistern stammt ursprünglich aus dem spätantiken Neuplatonismus und wurde von frühneuzeitlichen Naturphilosophen wieder aufgegriffen.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, gagasan roh unsur berasal dari Neoplatonisme akhir zaman kuno dan dihidupkan kembali para filsuf alam awal zaman modern.
statement.en: According to the German article, the idea of elemental spirits comes from late-antique Neoplatonism and was revived by early modern natural philosophers.

statement.en: They also play a role in various forms of neopaganism and modern esotericism, such as anthroposophy.

short_description.id: Etiäinen adalah sejenis haltija dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia, bayangan atau kembaran seseorang yang mendahuluinya dan melakukan hal yang kelak ia lakukan.
short_description.en: In Finnish folklore the etiäinen is a kind of haltija, an image or double of a person that goes ahead of them and does what they will later do.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia, semua tempat, benda, dan juga manusia memiliki haltija, roh penjaga masing-masing. Salah satunya adalah etiäinen: bayangan, kembaran, atau sekadar kesan yang berjalan mendahului seseorang dan melakukan hal yang kelak dilakukan orang itu. Misalnya, orang di rumah mendengar pintu ditutup atau melihat bayangan orang yang mereka tunggu, lalu sadar ia belum datang; ketika ia benar-benar tiba, ia mengulangi tindakan etiäinen-nya.
long_description.en: In Finnish folklore every place and thing, and every person, has a haltija, a guardian spirit of its own. One of them is the etiäinen: an image, double or mere impression that goes ahead of a person and does what that person will later do. People waiting at home might hear the door close or see the shadow of the one they expect, then realise that person has not arrived; when they finally come, they repeat what their etiäinen did.

long_description.id: Etiäinen juga bisa berarti firasat bahwa sesuatu akan terjadi, misalnya peringatan akan datangnya tahun yang buruk. Dalam bahasa Finlandia modern, kata ini sudah lepas dari asal-usul syamanistiknya dan berarti firasat. Etiäiset muncul secara spontan, tidak dapat dipanggil, dan kadang tidak diinginkan serta menimbulkan kecemasan seperti hantu.
long_description.en: Etiäinen can also mean a feeling that something will happen, such as a warning of a bad year ahead. In modern Finnish the word has moved away from its shamanistic roots and means premonition. Etiäiset are spontaneous, cannot be summoned, and may be unwanted and cause anxiety, like ghosts.

long_description.id: Seseorang dipercaya mendapat etiäinen pada usia tiga hari, dan etiäinen itu mengikuti watak pemiliknya.
long_description.en: A person is said to receive their etiäinen at three days old, and it follows its owner's character traits.

statement.en: In Finnish folklore all places, things and people have a haltija (guardian spirit); one is the etiäinen, an image, doppelgänger or impression that goes ahead of a person doing what they later do.

claims.quote: In modern Finnish, the term has detached from its shamanistic origins and refers to premonition. Unlike clairvoyance, divination, and similar practices, etiäiset (plural) are spontaneous and cannot be induced. Quite the opposite, they may be unwanted and cause anxiety, like ghosts.

short_description.id: Fetch adalah kembaran gaib atau penampakan orang yang masih hidup dalam folklor Irlandia, yang dianggap pertanda kematian.
short_description.en: A fetch is a supernatural double or apparition of a living person in Irish folklore, taken as an omen of death.

long_description.id: Fetch adalah kembaran gaib atau penampakan dari orang yang masih hidup. Melihat fetch dianggap pertanda pasti, biasanya kematian yang akan datang bagi diri sendiri atau orang tercinta. Fetch digambarkan sebagai kembaran hantu yang persis sama; namun menurut John dan Michael Banim, bila kembaran itu muncul pagi hari dan bukan malam, itu pertanda umur panjang. Ia mirip doppelgänger Jermanik dan beberapa konsep wraith Inggris. Francis Grose mengaitkan istilah itu dengan Inggris Utara dalam Provincial Glossary (1787).
long_description.en: A fetch is a supernatural double or apparition of a living person, and seeing one is taken as a sure omen, usually of coming death for the viewer or someone dear. It is an exact ghostly twin; yet John and Michael Banim say that a double appearing in the morning rather than evening foretells long life. It resembles the Germanic doppelgänger and some ideas of the British wraith. Francis Grose tied the term to Northern England in his 1787 Provincial Glossary.

long_description.id: Etimologinya kabur. Mungkin dari kata kerja "fetch" (menjemput): gabungan "fetch-life", merujuk psikopompos yang menjemput jiwa orang sekarat, tercatat dalam terjemahan Aeneid oleh Richard Stanyhurst tahun 1583. Fetch muncul dalam sastra Irlandia sejak awal abad ke-19, misalnya kisah gotik "The Fetches" karya John dan Michael Banim dalam Tales by the O'Hara Family (1825).
long_description.en: The origin of the word is obscure. It may come from the verb 'fetch': the compound 'fetch-life', for a psychopomp who 'fetches' dying souls, is found in Richard Stanyhurst's 1583 translation of the Aeneid. The fetch entered Irish literature from the early 19th century, as in John and Michael Banim's Gothic tale 'The Fetches' in Tales by the O'Hara Family (1825).

short_description.id: Fext adalah mayat hidup dalam kepercayaan rakyat Ceko dan Slavia, orang kebal peluru yang jasadnya tidak membusuk, dan hanya bisa dilukai peluru kaca.
short_description.en: The fext is an undead of Slavic folk belief known among Czechs, a bullet-proof person whose body does not decay, vulnerable only to glass bullets.

long_description.id: Fext adalah makhluk mayat hidup dalam mitologi Slavia yang asal-usulnya terkait Perang Tiga Puluh Tahun pada abad ke-17. Dalam bahasa Ceko, fext (juga fekst atau fest, mungkin dari kata Jerman fest, "kokoh") adalah sebutan rakyat bagi orang yang jasadnya tidak membusuk setelah mati, hanya mengering dan tetap utuh. Legenda tentangnya terutama berasal dari daerah Rychnov.
long_description.en: The fext is an undead creature of Slavic mythology whose origins are tied to the Thirty Years' War of the 17th century. As a folk term among Czechs, fext (also fekst or fest, probably from German fest, "firm") means a person whose body does not decay after death but merely dries and stays intact. Legends about it come mainly from the Rychnov region.

long_description.id: Fext dipercaya kebal peluru, kecuali peluru kaca, dan beberapa jenderal besar masa itu dijuluki fext karena dianggap tak bisa mati. Menurut sebagian kesaksian, fext lahir dengan selaput ganda yang salah satunya dijahitkan di bawah ketiak bayi; menurut yang lain, kekebalannya didapat lewat sihir atau perjanjian dengan setan. Legenda ini di Eropa hanya dikenal orang Ceko, Slowakia, Jerman, dan Swedia.
long_description.en: The fext was believed invulnerable to bullets except glass ones, and some great generals of the time were called fexts for their supposed immortality. By some accounts a fext was born in a double caul, one of which was sewn under the infant's arm; by others, the invulnerability came from a spell or a pact with the devil. In Europe the legend is known only among Czechs, Slovaks, Germans and Swedes.

short_description.id: Freybug disebut sebagai Anjing Hitam mengerikan dari cerita rakyat Inggris abad pertengahan, khususnya Norfolk, yang menakuti pelancong di jalan desa.
short_description.en: The Freybug is described as a monstrous Black Dog of medieval English folklore, specifically Norfolk, that terrified travelers on country roads.

long_description.id: Freybug dinyatakan sebagai Anjing Hitam mengerikan yang berasal dari cerita rakyat Inggris abad pertengahan, khususnya dari Norfolk. Seperti kebanyakan anjing hitam gaib, ukurannya kira-kira sebesar anak sapi dan berkeliaran di jalan pedesaan untuk menakuti para pelancong.
long_description.en: The first source describes the Freybug as a fearsome Black Dog out of medieval English folklore, tied in particular to Norfolk. As is typical of uncanny black dogs, it stood about as tall as a calf and prowled rural lanes, frightening those who travelled them.

long_description.id: Laurence Saunders, martir Inggris, menyebut Fray-bug dalam surat-suratnya kepada istrinya pada 1555. Kamus sejarah mendefinisikan fray-bug sebagai objek yang ditakuti, yaitu hantu atau momok, dan mengutip kalimat Saunders yang memuat kata itu.
long_description.en: Laurence Saunders, an English martyr, mentioned Fray-bugs in his letters to his wife in 1555. A historical dictionary defines a fray-bug as an object of fear, a bogy or spectre, and cites the Saunders sentence that uses the word.

long_description.id: Gagasan bahwa Fray-bug adalah Anjing Hitam mirip Barghest berasal dari tafsiran John Brand, bukan dari definisi kamus itu sendiri.
long_description.en: The idea that the Fray-bug was a Black Dog like the Barghest comes from John Brand's interpretation, not from the dictionary definition itself.

short_description.id: Gancanagh ("si pembicara cinta") adalah peri lelaki dalam mitologi Irlandia yang terkenal merayu perempuan.
short_description.en: The gancanagh ('love talker') is a male fairy of Irish myth known for seducing women.

long_description.id: Gancanagh (dari Irlandia/Irish gean cánach, "pembicara cinta") adalah peri lelaki dari mitologi Irlandia yang terkenal merayu perempuan. Namanya dieja beragam, termasuk geancánach atau ganconer, dan menurut sumber yang dikumpulkan Irish Folklore Commission di County Meath kata itu juga dapat berarti anak kecil atau anak yang dewasa sebelum waktunya. Pada 1888 W. B. Yeats mencatat bahwa gancanagh tidak ada dalam kamus dan kurang dikenal di Connacht.
long_description.en: The gancanagh (from Irish gean cánach, 'love talker') is a male fairy of Irish myth known for seducing women. The name is spelled many ways, among them geancánach and ganconer, and sources gathered in County Meath by the Irish Folklore Commission say the word could also mean a small or precocious child. In 1888 W. B. Yeats noted that the gancanagh was missing from dictionaries and little known in Connacht.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah tahun 1825 di The Dublin and London Magazine, ganconer adalah sebutan bagi para peri di Irlandia Utara, lelaki kecil yang tinggal di gua dan dipimpin Captain Dearg. long_description.en: In a tale published in The Dublin and London Magazine in 1825, ganconer is a name for the fairies of the North of Ireland, little men living in caves under Captain Dearg. long_description.id: Gjenganger, "yang berjalan lagi", adalah sebutan Nordik untuk mayat hidup, dengan bentuk genganger di Denmark, gengångare di Swedia, dan afturganga di Islandia. Unlike a ghost, it has an entirely bodily form. short_description.id: Habetrot adalah tokoh folklor daerah perbatasan Inggris Utara dan Dataran Rendah Skotlandia yang dikaitkan dengan pemintalan.
short_description.en: Habetrot is a folklore figure of the Border counties of northern England and Lowland Scotland, linked with spinning.

long_description.id: Habetrot (juga Habitrot, Habtrot, Habbitrot) adalah tokoh folklor wilayah perbatasan (Border) Inggris Utara dan Dataran Rendah Skotlandia, yang dikaitkan dengan pemintalan dan roda pintal. Ia muncul dalam dongeng dari Selkirkshire, varian tipe ATU 501 ("The Three Old Spinning Women"): seorang perempuan tua cacat yang tinggal di bawah tanah bersama para pemintal lain yang tubuhnya rusak akibat pekerjaan itu; satu-satunya pemintal lain yang bernama adalah Scantlie Mab.
long_description.en: Habetrot (also Habitrot, Habtrot, Habbitrot) belongs to the folklore of the Border counties of northern England and Lowland Scotland and is tied to spinning and the spinning wheel. She appears in a Selkirkshire tale of type ATU 501 ('The Three Old Spinning Women') as a misshapen old woman dwelling underground among fellow spinners whose bodies the work has deformed; the only other spinner given a name is Scantlie Mab.

long_description.id: Habetrot memintal benang untuk seorang gadis setempat, lalu meyakinkan suami baru gadis itu agar istrinya tidak pernah memintal lagi. Kisah serupa ada di Jerman (The Three Spinners) dan Norwegia (The Three Aunts). Dalam folklor perbatasan, orang yang menginjak makam bayi yang belum dibaptis terkena penyakit "grave-merels"; obatnya hanyalah memakai karung linen yang antara lain dipintal oleh Habetrot.
long_description.en: She spun yarn for a girl of the district and then persuaded the girl's new husband that his wife must never spin again. Comparable stories exist in Germany (The Three Spinners) and Norway (The Three Aunts). Border lore held that treading on the graves of unbaptised infants brought on 'grave-merels', curable only by wearing a linen sack that, among other conditions, had been spun by Habetrot.

short_description.id: Hob adalah roh rumah tangga kecil dalam folklor Midlands Inggris, Inggris Utara dan perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia.
short_description.en: A hob is a small household spirit in the folklore of the English Midlands, Northern England and the Anglo-Scottish border.

long_description.id: Hob adalah sejenis roh rumah tangga kecil dalam folklor tradisional Midlands Inggris, Inggris Utara dan perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia. Mereka bisa tinggal di dalam rumah atau di luar, bekerja di pekarangan pertanian sehingga bermanfaat, tetapi bila tersinggung bisa menjadi pengganggu. Cara biasa mengusir hob adalah memberinya satu setel pakaian baru, yang membuatnya pergi selamanya, walau hob terburuk mungkin tak bisa diusir.
long_description.en: A hob is a kind of small household spirit in the traditional folklore of the English Midlands, Northern England and the Anglo-Scottish border. Hobs might live indoors or out and worked about farmyards, making them useful, though if offended they turned into pests. The usual way to be rid of one was to give it a new suit of clothes, after which it left for good, though the worst hobs could not be shifted at all.

long_description.id: Hob adalah bentuk kecil nama Robin, yang sendiri bentuk kecil Robert, dan kadang dipakai umum untuk goblin, bogle atau brownie. Di utara Inggris kata ini juga terkait dengan Inggris Kuno þyrs dan Norse Kuno þurs ("raksasa"), melahirkan varian hob-thrush dan hob-thrust. Di Yorkshire, hob digambarkan lelaki kecil berbulu dan keriput, baik tetapi nakal; hob terkenal di Runswick Bay tinggal di sebuah hobhole dan dipercaya menyembuhkan batuk rejan anak-anak.
long_description.en: Hob is a pet form of Robin, itself a pet form of Robert, and is sometimes a general word for a goblin, bogle or brownie. In the north of England it is also tied to Old English þyrs and Old Norse þurs, 'giant', giving forms such as hob-thrush and hob-thrust. Yorkshire hobs were small, hairy, wizened men, kindly but mischievous; a famous one at Runswick Bay lived in a hobhole and was believed to cure children of whooping cough.
